News.content:

News.title: Poppy-coloured stamp set honours armed forces
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Royal Mail has revealed images of a set of six new stamps honouring the service of the nation’s armed forces.

The stamps will be issued on Armistice Day, November 11, that this year marks 110 years since the Battle of the Somme, which began on July 1 1916 and became one of the defining battles of the First World War.

The six stamps feature specially commissioned artworks by British artist Matthew Cook that reflect different aspects of remembrance.

open image in gallery The six stamps feature specially commissioned artworks by British artist Matthew Cook (Royal Mail/PA) ( PA Media )

Each has been painted using a colour palette inspired by the red poppy, one of the most recognisable symbols of remembrance.

David Gold of Royal Mail, said: “Remembrance holds a profound place in our national life.

“Through these stamps, we pay tribute to the service and sacrifice of those who have served our country through two world wars and many other conflicts.

open image in gallery Each stamp has been painted using a colour palette inspired by the red poppy (Royal Mail/PA) ( PA Media )

“Matthew Cook’s poignant artworks provide a fitting and powerful way to reflect on the sacrifices made by so many courageous men and women across the generations.”

Cook said: “Remembrance has a very special place in my life, having served as a reservist in the Parachute Regiment and The Rifles and been deployed to Iraq and Afghanistan.

“I was delighted to be asked to illustrate these stamps and to take on the challenge of such a sensitive and significant subject.

open image in gallery The stamps reflect different aspects of remembrance (Royal Mail/PA) ( PA Media )

“It is always a privilege to illustrate stamps for Royal Mail, and this project felt particularly special.”

News.title: Jamie Oliver’s wife Jools says not knowing she had ADHD ‘ruined’ life for 45 years
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Jamie Oliver’s wife Jools Oliver has revealed that she has been diagnosed with autism and ADHD, saying that not understanding her neurodivergence “ruined” her life for 45 years.

Clothing brand owner Jools shared the news during a podcast interview, stating: “I just think it’s quite draining. I think it’s tiring. I think, actually, it’s ruined, so far, 45 years of my life thinking it’s something else. It’s no superpower. It’s just a drain and it’s just really hard work.”

She revealed that she decided to announce her diagnosis to her friends and family via an invitation to her 50th birthday party last year.

open image in gallery Jools Oliver has opened up about neurodivergence on new podcast ( Instagram )

Jools, who suffers from social anxiety, said on Lessons From Our Mothers podcast: “My 50th birthday invite, I decided to come out.” She told her chef husband: “Jamie, I'm going to tell everyone that I’m not normal because I put on such a great act of being really like, ‘Woo,’ and so social. In fact, it’s like my worst night. I’m such an introvert.’”

She said that “a lot of people didn’t come and were turned off”, but she thought to herself: “Well, this is me. I’m afraid this is the new 50. This is it.’”

The 51-year-old went on to say that she is “scared” to take prescribed medication due to her health anxiety. “I’ve got the medication, but I don't want to take it because I’m scared due to health anxiety that something will happen,” she explained, calling it “one ongoing situation”.

Jools said that, following her attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) diagnosis, she decided to get tested for autism after realising that she shares behavioural habits with her children, who were diagnosed with autism.

She said that she “just feels things so deeply”, adding: “I get so dramatic over things and I can be really up and down. And the empathy sometimes is painful.

“I don’t know whether that’s just a personality choice. Sometimes you don’t even know, or is it just the menopause? Am I just going through the menopause and I’m really going bonkers? I think when you do have neurodiversity, menopause is a double nightmare.”

open image in gallery Jools Oliver has been married to chef Jamie since 2000 ( Getty Images for Disney )

Jamie has previously discussed his wife’s neurodivergence, without revealing she had ADHD or autism, during a 2025 appearance on Davina McCall’s Begin Again podcast.

He said: “She's quite in the background and she’s done that on purpose. She’s definitely the rock. She’s got incredible instinct, she’s incredibly kind, very funny. I love her to bits. I can’t really talk for her but she has neurodiversities that make her life really interesting and really challenging.

“Of course, there’s positives, but there’s loads of things that, you know – she makes us the way that we are. And I’m very grateful for Jools.”

The pair, who have four children, met as teenagers in 1993, and have been in a relationship for 33 years, and married since 2000.

NHS England figures shared in 2025 estimate that nearly 2.5 million people in England have ADHD, including those who are undiagnosed. The figures mark the first publicly available estimate of how common the condition is among the population.

Research also found earlier this year that a significant majority of autistic individuals over 40 in the UK are living without an official diagnosis. Researchers at King’s College London’s Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology & Neuroscience (IoPPN) reanalysed 2018 UK healthcare data, estimating that a staggering 91.45 per cent of autistic men and 79.48 per cent of autistic women aged 40 to 59 remain undiagnosed.

It found that 96.29 per cent of men and 97.19 per cent of women with autism over 60 are thought to be undiagnosed, with an overall rate of 96.51 per cent. Symptoms can include having specific and obsessive interests, a reliance on structure and difficulty in understanding social cues.

For more information about autism diagnosis and assessments, visit the National Autistic Society’s website at autism.org.uk.

News.title: What to know about Oleshky as Russia and Ukraine begin Melania Trump-brokered ceasefire
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A regional ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine has come into force to let a humanitarian operation begin in Oleshky, a town in southern Ukraine under Russian occupation.

The ceasefire was agreed in coordination with US First Lady Melania Trump.

Both sides announced the truce on Tuesday, but strikes have continued elsewhere, including in the Ukrainian capital, Kyiv.

The halt in fighting is intended to open the way for aid deliveries and evacuations from the frontline town, which is grappling with acute shortages of food and medicine.

Dmytro Lubinets, the parliamentary commissioner for human rights, confirmed Russia's timing of its halt in a Facebook post: "As head of the Ukrainian negotiating team, I confirm that the Ukrainian side is honouring its commitments,"

open image in gallery A still image taken from an undated drone video released September 12, 2026, shows a destroyed buildings in Oleshky, Kherson Region ( Reuters )

Russia's defence ministry said on Telegram that it stopped shelling in the direction of the city of Kherson from 4 a.m. Moscow time (0100 GMT) to prepare for the effort in Oleshky, which faces Kherson across the Dnipro River.

Mr Lubinets added that the deal was reached with US First Lady Melania Trump in cooperation with Russia's commissioner for human rights, Yana Lantratova.

Where is Oleshky?

Oleshky sits on the eastern bank of the Dnipro in Ukraine's southern region of Kherson, opposite the city of Kherson, which is held by Ukrainian forces.

Russian troops have controlled the town since seizing it during the first days of their February 2022 invasion.

Oleshky map:

White House envoys have spoken to both sides in recent days in an attempt to find a solution, as the US looks to mediate a peace deal to end the war, Europe's deadliest conflict since the World War Two.

On Friday, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said peace negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the United States had agreed to meet at a technical level in the first half of November in Abu Dhabi to continue the talks.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump speaks next to first lady Melania Trump after casting his ballot at the Palm Beach County Supervisor of Elections office, in the 2026 midterm elections in West Palm Beach, Florida, US, October 24, 2026 ( Reuters )

Fighting has continued despite the ceasefire arrangement.

New strikes on Tuesday hit the Southern Bridge and subway infrastructure in Kyiv, forcing a suspension of traffic, city officials said.

A Reuters witness heard explosions in the capital.

A Russian missile attack on Kyiv killed at least one person and injured 15, including students in a dormitory, since Monday evening.

The attacks also killed and injured people in the cities of Kharkiv and Pavlohrad.

On the Telegram messaging app, the Russian defence ministry said it had hit transport infrastructure in Kyiv and a logistics hub in the Kharkiv region.

It also said it had struck industrial facilities and cargo vessels elsewhere that it cited as being put to military use.

A drone attack in the western Russian city of Bryansk, close to the border with Ukraine, killed a man and wounded six people.

In the Russian-controlled part of Ukraine's southeastern region of Zaporizhzhia, a drone hit a bus, killing one person and injuring 30, local officials said.

Reuters could not immediately independently verify the reports.

Russia and Ukraine deny deliberately targeting civilians.

News.title: Adolescence star says prison was ‘one of the best things’ to happen to him
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Ashley Walters has described his time in prison as “one of the best things” to happen to him.

The 44-year-old actor, who played the detective investigating the murder of schoolgirl Katie Leonard in Netflix’s Golden Emmy-sweeping Adolescence, was sentenced to 18 months in a young offenders’ institution in 2002 after being convicted of possessing a firearm.

At the time, he was a member of chart-topping UK garage group So Solid Crew, before going on to establish a successful acting career.

In a new interview with The Guardian, the actor said it was not “a pleasant experience at all” and because of his celebrity name, he was recognised immediately and “all hell broke loose”, with inmates shouting insults and threatening to kill him in the morning.

He said: “I was tried, I was tested, it was pressure, there was loads of fear but I had no choice.

open image in gallery Ashley Walters has described prison as ‘one of the best things that happened to me’ ( AFP/Getty )

“It’s an experience I had to go through, and actually it was one of the best things that happened to me.”

The father-of-eight said the sentence helped him to reflect on his life and hit reset.

He said: “It pushed me to the thoughts I needed to have: who do I want to be? What do I want from life?

“And then, looking around me and seeing my circle of friends and entrusted loved ones, do they reflect that? And the answer was a big resounding no.

“When I came out of prison, I didn’t know what I was going to do with my life and a lot of doors were shut.”

Walters’ acting career began to take off when British filmmaker Saul Dibb wrote a role for him in Bullet Boy, a film about an ex-convict attempting to rebuild his life after returning to his troubled neighbourhood.

He went on to star in successful series including Top Boy and Bulletproof.

In the interview, Walters also reflected on his 15-year struggle with substance abuse, revealing that an argument with his wife, Danielle Isaie, in 2020 prompted him to seek treatment.

open image in gallery Walters played DI Luke Bascombe in Netflix’s ‘Adolescence’ ( Netflix )

He said: “The next morning, my wife dropped me at rehab and I was there for four weeks, came out and I’ve never drunk or drugged since, and it’s coming up to six years in November.

“So, very thankful for that. Sad it took me so long to get there – and there’s a lot of amends to make with family and kids and friends – but one of the best things I’ve ever done.

“In the last six years, it’s no coincidence that my life’s changed, like, amazingly.

“The truth is, nothing started working for me until I was clean and sober.”

Walters is also known for starring in Harlan Coben’s 2025 miniseries Missing You.

He will make his directorial debut with Animol, which follows young inmates in a juvenile detention centre as they navigate their lives and paths to redemption, and stars his Adolescence co-star Graham.

News.title: Amanda Seyfried names the hit film she turned down over fears it would ‘ruin’ her career
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Amanda Seyfried has spoken about her decision to turn down a role in a Marvel blockbuster, admitting she was “wrong” about how the movie would turn out.

The Dropout star, 40, was offered the role of Gamora in Guardians of the Galaxy before it ultimately went to Zoe Saldaña.

At the time, Seyfried thought the space-set superhero adventure — featuring a talking tree and a wisecracking raccoon — could derail her career.

“I think turning down Guardians of the Galaxy was just so obvious to me at the time,” she said during a recent question-and-answer session with the SAG-AFTRA Foundation.

“I’m like: ‘This is not going to be a hit. The tree and the raccoon are talking to each other. And also they’re all in space.’ And I was just like: ‘This will ruin my career if this is bad. And there’s a high chance that this could be bad’.”

open image in gallery Amanda Seyfried admitted she thought starring as Gamora in ‘Guardians of the Galaxy’ might ‘ruin’ her career ( AP )

open image in gallery Zoe Saldaña starred opposite Chris Pratt in the Guardians of the Galaxy franchise ( Marvel Studios )

The movie was a huge hit, becoming the third-highest-grossing film of 2014, and it went on to spawn two successful sequels while the cast also appeared in the Avengers series.

Amanda now admits she was “wrong” about the film, but she doesn’t regret her decision.

She added: “I mean, obviously I was wrong. But I still don’t take back that decision. I made it for myself. I made it for my family that I knew I wanted to have.

“And I just don’t want to spend all the time in the make-up trailer. I just can’t sit still anyway. I really don’t like stunts, and I don’t like heights, and I don’t like pretending the entire world. I need something to hold on to.”

It comes after Saldaña previously confirmed she is walking away from the role of Gamora, but she’s hoping another actor will revive the character in the future.

She told Variety: “I keep saying this time and time again — I can’t wait to see what’s next for Gamora. I hope they’re not done with her, and I hope a woman of color or a woman with special needs can take on the role next. That would be incredible.”

Saldaña also previously told the publication she didn’t fully understand the character until she’d finished work on the films, saying: “I wish I could go back and reshoot what Gamora was going through in the Avengers movies.

“I was not quite understanding what the Russo Brothers [were doing]. They’re excellent filmmakers and the opportunity they gave me was of a lifetime. To highlight Gamora in such a way in their films is something I’ll always be grateful.

“I wish I could go back and redo it so I could push a little harder because it was such a great opportunity to play a daughter having issues with a dad and whether or not she’s having this opportunity to reconciliate or to simply just walk away.

“That would’ve been a great opportunity had I been a little more aware of it then.”

News.title: ByteDance founder Zhang Yiming reclaims top spot in China’s rich list, thanks to his firm's AI push
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

ByteDance founder Zhang Yiming reclaimed the top spot on a list of China’s richest people, driven by his company's push into artificial intelligence.

The rankings released by The Hurun Research Institute on Tuesday reflected that the country's high-tech sectors were rising but others like consumer and real estate were under pressure.

The institute, which has published the list annually since 1999, found a record 1,529 people with more than 5 billion yuan (about $750 million), up 6.6% from last year.

The number of billionaires based on their net worth in U.S. dollars rose to 1,176, up 155 people — 176 more than the U.S. That was slightly below the 1,185 people in 2021.

Zhang topped the list with $100 billion, up 43%, “almost all of it on the back of AI,” Rupert Hoogewerf, Hurun Report chairman, said in a statement. Hoogewerf noted that ByteDance's Doubao is China's most used AI assistant.

ByteDance is also the parent company of popular short-video platforms Douyin and TikTok.

“AI is the biggest single wealth engine on this list: 160 Hurun rich listers — 1 in 10 — now make their money from AI,” he said.

Bottled water magnate Zhong Shanshan fell to second place with $61 billion, down 23%, while Robin Zeng, chairman of CATL, the world’s largest maker of batteries for electric vehicles, came third, Hurun said.

Hurun cross-checked its information with entrepreneurs, regulators, industry experts and others to compile the list, while acknowledging limitations.

Chinese artificial intelligence startup DeepSeek founder Liang Wenfeng, a new face on the list, ranked seventh. AI chipmaker Cambricon chair Chen Tianshi was 10th.

“This year’s gains were polarised — entrepreneurs in AI, semiconductors and robotics surged ahead, whilst those in consumer, real estate and traditional manufacturing saw their wealth shrink — a two-speed economy,” Hoogewerf said.

China last week said its economy grew 4.5% in the July-September quarter from a year ago, fueled by robust exports, moving closer to meeting its official annual growth target for the year. For the whole year, Chinese leaders have set a growth target of 4.5% to 5%, down from last year’s 5% expansion.

While some industries were thriving thanks to government support for technologies such as AI and electric vehicles, owners of small businesses reported tough times as their customers cut back on spending.

China’s domestic demand has been weighed down by a yearslong downturn in its property market.

The Hurun list reflected that too.

Hoogewerf said Lei Jun, chairman of Chinese smart consumer electronics maker Xiaomi, was this year’s “biggest faller,” with his wealth halved to $25.1 billion. Consumer fortunes also fell across the board, Hoogewerf, said.

“Today, for the first time ever, not a single mainland property developer remains in the Top 100 — the only property names left at the top are the Hong Kong landlord families,” he said.

News.title: Harry Kane ends England’s 25-year wait for Ballon d’Or winner
News.content:
The 70th Ballon d’Or ceremony takes place at the London Palladium as England and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane aims to become the first Englishman in more than 20 years to win the award. Michael Owen was the last Englishman to win the award back in 2001.

The choice of London as the host city pays tribute to the award’s inaugural winner, England’s Stanley Matthews, who won it in 1956. This also marks the first time the ceremony will be organised outside France. Kane, who scored over 70 goals for club and country in the relevant year, is among the favourites for this year’s award alongside the likes of Barcelona and Spain’s Lamine Yamal and Real Madrid and France’s Kylian Mbappe.

Kane won the Bundesliga with Bayern Munich whereas Yamal won both La Liga and the World Cup. Yamal won the Kopa Trophy at last year’s ceremony as the best men’s young player.

Last year’s winners were Spain and Barcelona midfielder Aitana Bonmati and France and Barcelona forward Ousmane Dembele. Dembele is aiming to become just the 11th man to win the top prize at least twice, although it would appear to be very unlikely that the Frenchman will be winning the award this evening.

Selected international journalists cast their votes based on the performances of players throughout the season. The panel consists of one representative per country from the top 100 nations in the Fifa men’s world ranking and the top 50 in the women’s world ranking. Each voter ranks their top 10 candidates, with points distributed on a descending scale. They vote based on three factors: individual performance, team achievements, and class combined with fair play.

In total, 13 trophies will be presented across the men’s and women’s game, including the two man Ballon d’Or awards, the best young players and best teams. The awards take into account achievements from August 3, 2025, to July 19, 2026 (August 16 for the women).

The official ceremony begins at 8pm GMT.

News.title: Nurse accused of spreading Ebola murdered by mob
News.content:
A nurse was killed and a teacher badly injured in a mob attack after being accused of spreading Ebola in the water supply in Congo.

The unnamed victims were set upon in Bafwasende territory of Tshopo province after a group of young people accused them of being responsible for the outbreak of the haemorrhagic fever.

The nurse was killed outright and the teacher, who local media reported was close to the health worker, only survived after being rescued by police.

The World Health Organization (WHO) condemned the attack, which is only the latest incident of health workers being attacked by suspicious, scared or angry locals.

Medical workers have been forced to deal with widespread rumours that the outbreak – the world’s second largest – is spread by them.

Other conspiracy theories claim the outbreak is a money-making hoax for aid agencies, or that foreigners are using it as a pretext to grab the country’s minerals.

Strict rules imposed on how to conduct funerals in order to stop mourners becoming infected, have become another flashpoint.

Last month, a Congolese politician was beaten to death in North Kivu after publicly defending the government’s response.

He had been calling on the public to obey response measures, particularly social distancing and hand washing, on a radio show.

News.title: ‘Our world is yellow’: Fears for children as sickening smog blankets Indonesia
News.content:
For two months now, Natanael Undas has opened his curtains not to blue skies, but a sickening sepia haze that blocks out any sunlight. As the relentless fires smoulder nearby, his city looks “more like Mars” than Indonesian Borneo.

“We start our day in yellow, and we end our day in yellow,” the 32-year-old headteacher told the Telegraph. “When you inhale and take a breath, it feels like you’re choking. Your eyes hurt, your nose hurts… when you go outside, it feels like someone is burning dry leaves next to you.”

Palangkaraya, the capital of Central Kalimantan, is on the front lines of an environmental crisis that has cloaked much of Southeast Asia in a toxic haze for months.

According to Nusantara Atlas, an open-access platform that tracks deforestation, fires have torched roughly 1.9 million hectares across the archipelago so far this year – including one million hectares in September alone.

“I’ve seen burning in the city, burning in the forests, burning near the river, burning in the peatlands, burning near the street – it’s devastating,” said Mr Undas. “It’s the longest burning season I’ve seen. Usually the rainy season comes in October, but everything is still on fire.”

News.title: Britain sanctions warlords accused of rape in Sudan
News.content:
The British government is to sanction senior military and militia commanders accused of atrocities, including rape and sexual violence, during the fall of the city of El Fasher in Sudan.

At least 15 commanders from both the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) have been sanctioned after investigations found they used rape as a weapon of war during the brutal siege of the Sudanese city in October last year.

The siege, perpetrated by the RSF paramilitary group who have been battling SAF since 2023, resulted in the massacre of at least 60,000 people.

The fall of the city came after an 18-month blockade in which the city’s population were deliberately starved into submission, according to a report from the UK-government funded think tank the Centre for Information Resilience.

Reports from aid organisations, UN investigators, and eyewitness accounts have previously found that rape was used on a mass scale by both sides.

In one incident, aid workers said at least 54 children were raped or sexually assaulted by RSF fighters while fleeing the city to Tawila, a town 25 miles west of El Fasher.

News.title: Wolff puts ‘tequila on ice’ with Antonelli two points away from title
News.content:
Mercedes had chosen the medium tyres for the start, while Ferrari’s Leclerc and the Red Bulls of Verstappen and Isack Hadjar started on new softs. Antonelli was able to convert that choice into a one-stop race while almost everyone else did two, emphasising his superiority as he finished 16 seconds clear of Leclerc.

A late virtual safety car after Valtteri Bottas’s Cadillac ground to a halt by the side of the track made the final laps rather processional, denying the huge crowds at COTA the opportunity of seeing the fast-closing Hamilton take on Verstappen for the final podium spot.

That might have been fun, with Verstappen having lost his cool with his team midway through the race, furious that they didn’t order team-mate Hadjar out of the way when he came up behind him after stopping: “Thanks guys. Really good strategy there. Stuck in the dirty air.”

Incredibly, his third place finish in Austin means is the first time since the final race of 2020 that Verstappen has been out of title contention.

But it hardly mattered. The day belonged once again to Antonelli who should be champion by the end of next week. Not that he was getting carried away. “It was the result we needed,” he said. “The whole team deserved it so much, bringing this [upgrade] package. It was also the perfect execution with the strategy to do the one stop.”

Asked about the title, he added: “We’re very close, we try to finish on a high and hopefully we can finish it very soon. I mean, the perfect way will be to finish in style and then just enjoy the rest of the season. I’m very aware that it’s very close, but the mindset doesn’t change. I want to finish on a high to go into 2027 with momentum.”

“Yeah, what a boy, no?” Wolff said, admiringly. “I was just saying before, I got a question about whether he was nervous before the race, and I said, ‘Oh, he just sneaked into my office before getting ready and said, ‘I’m just going to enjoy this right now, and it’s weird, I’m not thinking about the championship at all. Isn’t that funny?’”

Wolff added that there would “definitely be a lot of tequila on ice” in Mexico. In hindsight it was always going to be a more appropriate venue to crown the sport’s youngest ever champion. Antonelli is not, after all, old enough to drink yet in the state of Texas.

News.title: Hapless and hopeless Man Utd bring curtain down on out-of-depth Carrick
News.content:
Hapless, hopeless and utterly humiliated. And that has to be that for Michael Carrick. It is surely inconceivable that he will continue any longer as Manchester United’s head coach. A proud club on its knees and a favoured son on his way out.

The former midfielder will carry the can. As managers always do. Even if the fault lines run so deep at United that it feels like they are almost irreparable. Owners – the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe – executives, players. A collective failing of monumental proportions. Although, again, it will be the manager who goes. Carrick knows it and it looked like it at the end. He knows the score, especially after this score.

More than four years ago Ralf Rangnick, the then interim manager, declared that United needed “open heart surgery”. Now there is barely a pulse.

An announcement must be imminent, with United turning to someone else in the fight against Premier League relegation. A joke? No, this abject performance against Bournemouth leaves United in 16th place, just a point above the bottom three, so the priority for the new man will be clear. Save them from the drop. They are 14 points off the top already, but forget that. It is irrelevant given their plight.

News.title: Trafford shows he has credentials to dislodge Pickford as England No 1
News.content:
Goalkeeping is defined by athleticism, physical strength and reflexes, but it is also about decision-making and mental fortitude. The two saves Trafford made to deny Sunderland’s Brian Brobbey in the first half were very different, but equally impressive.

The first was deceptively hard. Although the connection on Brobbey’s shot – back in the Sunderland side and causing chaos as usual – from the edge of the area was not the cleanest and that almost made it harder, as the flight of the ball was difficult to pick up. The bounce just in front of the goalkeeper meant he had to watch it closely, judge the trajectory in the air and spin off the grass and still keep a strong hand, at full stretch, to push it away from danger.

The second was, arguably, even better. Trafford had come off his line as Brobbey ran into the box. He was in a really vulnerable position, well outside his six-yard box in a one-on-one with the Netherlands international. The way he kept calm, stood up and timed when to move for the ball was superb, especially as an error could have led to a penalty.

Trafford may have saved with his feet, but he had cramped Brobbey for room, waited for the centre forward to make a move and timed the moment to dive at his feet perfectly. It was elite-level goalkeeping in a really tricky situation that favoured the striker.

Trafford made two more fine stops in the second half too, both from Nilson Angulo. The first was getting down low to tip another bouncing ball wide, which had flicked off a defender too. The second punching another deflected effort away after a block had taken some of the venom out of the shot.

Sunderland will feel like they shaded the battle, but Robin Roefs also made two decent stops from long-range shots in the second half while substitute Sean Longstaff saw an injury-time effort cleared off the line.

News.title: England pay price for toothless bowling in astonishing defeat by Pakistan
News.content:
Hello and welcome to live, over-by-over coverage of Pakistan v England in Lahore. In the UK, the clocks went back an hour overnight; England would love to wind them back 72 hours and have another go at defending 429 against Sri Lanka. That unfathomable defeat in Rawalpindi has left them on the brink in this tri-series.

England won’t be mathematically eliminated if they lose to Pakistan today, but it would leave them needing snookers if they are to reach Saturday’s final. Realistically, they need to win the last two group games, and there’s a chance even that might not be enough.

“It’s my first tri-series and it replicates World Cup styles and pressures,” said the England all-rounder Will Jacks. “You can’t replicate that in training or a bilateral series. In World Cups you have to bounce back. I remember in 2019 when England lost a couple of games in the group and they had to win their last two and they were able to do that to take the momentum forward.

“I’m not saying it’s the same thing but it’s a mini version of that and hopefully we can win on Sunday and move on. We have the opportunity to play in two must-win fixtures. Sometimes you learn more in losses than you do in wins.”

Jacks’ Surrey team-mate Sam Curran suffered the most against Sri Lanka, conceding an eye-watering 103 from his nine overs.

“They were incredibly hard conditions to bowl in and he bowls a lot of pressure overs – that’s his role in the team,” said Jacks. “He’s been so successful with that for England over a number of years. There are some days where it doesn’t quite work.”

Curran has kept his place in the side – but Josh Tongue is replaced by Henry Crocombe, who makes his international debut. And there’s no recall for Adil Rashid. We’ll have the toss and full team news in a moment.

SPAIN star Nico Williams revealed he snubbed the chance to join Arsenal.

The winger was a target for the Gunners in 2024, while he was also being tracked by Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain.

Sports.title: How a new manager could SAVE Man Utd with Howe, Conte and Nagelsmann circling as Carrick stares down barrel at sack
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED are in total disarray under Michael Carrick following another tactical disaster in their 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth.

The Red Devils hierarchy, led by Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada, face a monumental decision with Carrick staring down the barrel of the sack.



SunSport’s tactical expert Dean Scoggins broke down the candidates on Tactics Exposed to see who could step in and save United’s season.

Former Bournemouth and Newcastle boss Eddie Howe has emerged as the leading contender to take over after catching the eye of director of football Jason Wilcox.



Dean said: “Start with the favourite, which is Eddie Howe.

“He’s climbed the ladder in English football. He’s intense. He goes into details.



“He does favour a similar setup to what United have been playing under Michael Carrick. That becomes more of a 3-2-5 shape.

“Where I struggle with it, with Eddie Howe, in this intensity, high press, is the full-backs. Have they got the full-backs there to do it straight away? We’re two months out of a transfer window.

“He will drop a team into a very, very compact 4-5-1 shape off the ball. And from there, you can then counterattack.

“He’s got to come in there and get a team singing from the same sheet that currently isn’t.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“At the moment, you need a safer pair of hands. He’ll come with a plan. He’ll galvanise some of those players. They won’t go down under Eddie Howe.”

United could also opt for an alternative approach with ex-Chelsea boss Antonio Conte, with his trademark back-three system demanding an instant tactical overhaul.

Dean added: “Eddie Howe might put out the fire. Antonio Conte is going to start a fire.



“This is not vibes. This is not freestyling. This is automatic tactical change. He makes the players suffer and they have to suffer to play in his system. But wherever he goes, it’s success.

“And this is what will put off Manchester United fans. It’s the back three and it’s wing backs.

“Are Manchester United going to go down that route? He’s not got time like he had with Marcos Alonso and Victor Moses to turn people into that.

“Conte is too big a risk and is extremely combustible. And it could be another Mourinho or Conte at Tottenham scenario.”

Former Germany boss Julian Nagelsmann offers a long-term coaching project that could unlock the squad’s attacking potential.



Head of recruitment Christopher Vivell is a huge believer in Nagelsmann’s tactical pedigree, making the German another interesting option.

Dean said: “He’s the intriguing one of the group.

“He pushes into that 3-1-6 in attack. He was a prodigy when he first came through. Everybody knows he’s extremely tactically astute.



“Nagelsmann likes to overload that central area. So it’s fast balls in there and then little interchanges around that area.

“He likes crossing over wingers who are high and attackers who pin full backs over on one side. That would absolutely suit a Manchester United style of play as well.

“It just feels like there’s got to be so much that has got to change within different player roles. And this would be sort of an evolution under someone like Nagelsmann.

Sports.title: Harry Kane enjoys best moment of career as Bayern Munich’s ‘greatest ever signing’ is handed Ballon d’Or
Sports.content:
Next

HARRY KANE spent most of his career waiting for trophies, awards and accolades – and now they keep on coming.

At his home in Grunwald, south of Munich, there is a gleaming new arrival to his collection which will now take pride of place: a golden ball measuring 31cm x 23cm and weighing 7kg.



No one can deny Kane, a true professional on and off the pitch, the greatest individual moment of his career by being presented with the Ballon d’Or.

And in a few weeks there will be another extraordinary night for the 33-year-old when he breaks Peter Shilton’s appearances record for England by earning his 126th cap.



That game against Croatia is on November 12 at Wembley and equally, it was fitting last night’s ceremony also took place in London.

Sir Stanley Matthews, Sir Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan (twice) and Michael Owen are the other Englishmen to have won this award.

Charlton won in 1966 after inspiring the nation to World Cup glory so in terms of success, he is ahead of Kane.

But Kane’s numbers are frankly ridiculous compared to the Manchester United legend. In the eyes of the 100 journalists who vote for this award, his 73 goals for Bayern Munich and England topped anything else achieved by the great and good of world football — and they were dead right.

During those loan periods at Leyton Orient, Millwall, Norwich and Leicester, when he struggled to convince, this special moment on stage at the London Palladium seemed utterly impossible.

Yet although he appears to be a mild-mannered and relaxed individual, Kane is an extremely determined and driven professional who has always thrived on sticking two fingers up to his many doubters. And he has done it again.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Although Kane’s club boss, Vincent Kompany, is still recovering after collapsing, there was a huge delegation from Bayern.

Apart from picking up Fifa’s Golden Boot for finishing top scorer at the 2018 World Cup, Kane had won little and suffered only heartbreak during his years at Tottenham.

But in 2023, Kane made the best decision of his life by tearing himself away from his beloved Spurs to link up with Bayern.

Although Kane was ridiculed at the end of the first season as Xabi Alonso’s unbeaten Bayer Leverkusen won the title, he got his hands on his first Bundesliga crown in 2025.



Kane then won a domestic double last season during which everything he touched ended up in the net.

He fired four hat-tricks in the Bundesliga, including one on the final day of the season to reach 36 league goals.

Bayern cruised to the title, winning by 16 points. He also scored another hat-trick in the 3-0 win over Stuttgart in the German Cup final.

So in total, he netted 61 times for Bayern with another 12 for England, including six at the World Cup.

Always hungry for success

These 73 goals made it the second-highest goalscoring season by any footballer in the 21st century, trailing only Lionel Messi’s 82-goal haul in 2011-12. Kane was Europe’s top domestic goalscorer for the second time in his career.



And for the third successive year, he was the top scorer in German football. The trophy is a cannon, which is hilarious given the dislike Arsenal fans have for him.

Bayern’s honorary president Uli Hoeness claims Kane is the club’s greatest ever signing, which is some statement. There is, however, the argument that Kane has not delivered in the big games for England.

But a strong counter is that the rest of the team have not been good enough against the top sides to give him the ammunition. Kane won a bronze medal at this summer’s World Cup after the third place play-off win over France in Miami.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

However, that was little consolation to the captain, who was still hurting after the 2-1 late loss to Argentina in the semi-finals. Already, he is looking forward to Euro 2028 which England will co-host as one of the favourites.

But right now, his focus is on a third successive Bundesliga title and a first Champions League success. And never happy and always hungry for success, he will also be looking to win a second Ballon d’Or crown.

Sports.title: Ex-England star Paul Merson hit with £1,600 bill after driving untaxed car for six months in ‘honest mistake’
Sports.content:
Next

BUNGLING ex-England football ace Paul Merson must stump up more than £1,600 after forgetting to pay his road tax.

The Sky Sports pundit apologised to magistrates for his “honest” mistake, but was still handed the stinging financial penalty.



His £20,000 VW Touareg was flagged for being untaxed for six months by an ANPR camera in Cardiff in March.

The 58-year-old, from Teddington, South West London, told JPs in Croydon, South London: “I honestly thought I’d done it.



“I’m very sorry.”

The double title winner with Arsenal was banned for six months in 2024 for speeding three times in a month in the same car.



He also received a 14-month ban in 2011 after falling asleep at the wheel and crashing into a lorry on the M40 motorway, near Warwick.

Court documents showed the £20,000 VW’s tax had expired six months earlier.

Merson pleaded guilty to using a vehicle without a valid vehicle licence under the Single Justice Procedure.

He won the league twice with Arsenal in 1989 and 1991 and secured an FA Cup and League Cup double in 1993.



Merson, who was praised for going public over his battle with alcohol, drugs and gambling addictions, won 21 England caps.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick in limbo as Man Utd draw up succession plan after Ratcliffe joins crisis talks and Howe obstacle emerges

MANCHESTER UNITED chiefs left Michael Carrick in a state of limbo on Monday night after hours of crisis talks over his job.

A stung Old Trafford hierarchy is refusing to pull the trigger on a sacking until they have a clear plan in place.



Carrick’s job is in serious doubt ten months after replacing Ruben Amorim following a day of emergency talks at the club’s Carrington training base.

Director of football Jason Wilcox and CEO Omar Berrada were locked in discussions on Monday with co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and co-chairs Avram and Joel Glazer dialing in via video link.



It could mean Carrick takes training when United’s players report back on Tuesday morning following a standard day off after a match.

As things stand, Carrick expects to lead training to begin preparations for their next game at Chelsea on Saturday, unless he is dragged in before then.



Carrick spent three hours at United’s Carrington training base on Monday afternoon to watch the reserves draw 2-2 against Hull City in a behind-closed-doors friendly.

Former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and ex-Bayern and Germany manager Julian Nagelsmann are among the options should Carrick be sacked.

United’s top brass are well aware of the embarrassment of appointing a third manager this year after six defeats in 12 matches, and a fourth since Ratcliffe took charge of football operations in February 2024.

Sunday’s shameful 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth left the club just a point above the drop and the Amazon documentary could find themselves covering a relegation scrap this season.

It emerged on Monday that United would have to pay a few million in compensation to land Howe under the terms of his exit from Newcastle in July.

The 48-year-old had several years left on his contract at St James’ Park when he stepped down in the summer.

The Toon brought in a degree of protection in the event that he ended up at a rival in the months that followed.

Unai Emery and Fabian Hurzeler have admirers at Old Trafford but it would be expensive to prise them away from Aston Villa and Brighton, respectively

Former Chelsea and Spurs manager Antonio Conte is open to returning to football after leaving Napoli in June.



Carrick signed a two-year contract after guiding the club back into the Champions League in May.

The Stretford End hurled a tirade of abuse at the Glazers, Ratcliffe and board between spells of singing Carrick’s chant loudly and booing the players.

Sports.title: Arsenal stars back 4-year-old cancer patient’s £339k appeal for life-saving treatment
Sports.content:
Next

ARSENAL football aces have boosted a four-year-old cancer patient’s push to raise £339,000 for life-saving treatment.

Gunners fan Zach Fleming was just two when diagnosed with rare stage 4 neuroblastoma.



To boost his fundraising drive, the Premier League champions invited Zach to Saturday’s 2-0 win against Everton at the Emirates Stadium.

He and brother Alex, 11, met players Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze, plus boss Mikel Arteta and club great Ian Wright.



Zach was given a signed shirt which will be auctioned as part of his appeal.

Mum Edwina, 40, of Hackney, North London, told The Sun: “The support that me and my family have received in regards to Zach’s diagnosis has been amazing.



“I can’t put into words the experience that Zach and his brother received on Saturday.

“They couldn’t do enough to assist us and make sure we had one of the most magical days that my kids could ever imagine. I’d like to say a massive, massive thank you to the Arsenal fans for all their support and heartfelt messages.”

Stage 4 neuroblastoma affects about 100 UK children each year.

It occurs when cells from the tumour spread to distant parts of the body.



Zach had 18 months of extensive treatment at Great Ormond Street Hospital but has relapsed, forcing him to pull out of school.

His parents hope that the CAR T-cell therapy offered in Italy’s capital Rome will help him see off the cancer and give him back his life as a happy, active child.

So far, Zach’s family has raised about £100,000 through a JustGiving page.



The campaign is supported by Solving Kids’ Cancer UK.

The family wrote: “Before he became ill, Zach was an active little boy who loved running around and playing with his brother. Through it all, he has never stopped being Zach.”

Sports.title: Ballon d’Or audience groan at Kate Scott as star-studded crowd endure lengthy delay before Harry Kane crowned winner

KATE SCOTT was met with groans from the star-studded Ballon d’Or audience during Monday night’s ceremony.

The popular presenter was hosting the prestigious awards alongside former Arsenal legend Thierry Henry at London’s Palladium.



The ceremony was badly delayed, with many in the packed auditorium having been forced to sit and wait patiently for the event to get going.

So when Scott revealed proceedings would be interrupted by a commercial break, they let their feelings be known.



The announcement went down like a lead balloon, with an audible groan sweeping across the auditorium as some of football’s biggest names were forced to wait even longer.

Scott was forced to announce another break later in proceedings which was also met with audible frustration.

The reaction to the ad breaks was just one of many incidents on a chaotic evening, with the ceremony delayed by 45 minutes after heavy traffic and huge crowds outside the venue disrupted arrivals.

Fans watching from home were equally unimpressed, with one writing on social media: “Not the entire room groaning at an ad break lol.”



Another sarcastically complained: “There’s some random awards in my commercials can they fix this”, while a third joked: “Damn this whole event could have been an email.”

The interruptions came as football’s biggest stars gathered for the 70th edition of the Ballon d’Or, being held in London for the first time to commemorate Sir Stanley Matthews winning the inaugural award in 1956.

CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Barcelona wonderkid Lamine Yamal was among the early winners, collecting the men’s young talent award for the third consecutive year.

His Barcelona team-mate Vicky Lopez scooped the women’s equivalent for the second year running.

Spain boss Luis de la Fuente was crowned men’s coach of the year after guiding his country to World Cup glory, while Barcelona manager Pere Romeu claimed the women’s award.



Spain goalkeeper Unai Simon and Barcelona’s Cata Coll were also recognised for their performances between the sticks.

Arsenal star Bukayo Saka received the Socrates Award for his humanitarian work, while Barcelona were named women’s club of the year and Paris Saint-Germain took the men’s prize.

And the winner of the biggest prize of the evening was Harry Kane, who won the Ballon d’Or.

He is the first English winner since Michael Owen won the award in 2001.

Eddie Howe gets Ratcliffe backing

INEOS boss Ratcliffe is reportedly in favour of Eddie Howe getting the nod to take over the reins next. That's despite stating his intent to "take a break" from football after his time at Newcastle came to an end in the summer.

The i Paper has said United's part-owner is in favour of ensuring United has an English manager in charge. There is evidence to support that notion after Ratcliffe previously spearheaded a push to recruit ex-England chief Gareth Southgate to the position.

It's claimed there is currently a divide between United's board members as to whom should get the job if Carrick is fired. Director of football Jason Wilcox reportedly has his sights set on Howe, while head of recruitment Christopher Vivell wants to link up with former Germany and Bayern Munich boss Julian Nagelsmann.

And it seems Ratcliffe is leaning towards siding with Wilcox. However, there are also concerns among fans regarding Wilcox's long-term future after Lisandro Martinez's recent rant criticising the director for not recruiting properly in the summer.

Howe's free-agent status makes him an attractive target in that he would come at minimal cost. His achievements at Newcastle speak for themselves, namely landing the club its first major title in 70 years, though there may be doubt as to whether he'd have the same freedom financing his project as he did in the north-east.

Howe to insist on coaching staff

View 2 Images Eddie Howe will reportedly insist on bringing his coaching staff with him to Old Trafford if appointed (Image: PA)

One potential prerequisite for Howe signing on at Old Trafford would be for the manager to bring his coaching staff with him. Howe has long demonstrated a fierce loyalty to those he knows well and has turned down work in the past over that same issue.

Howe, 48, was previously linked with the Celtic job in 2021 when he insisted on naming his own coaching team. In the end, Celtic's reluctance to do so resulted in the proposed move collapsing.

"I felt that if I was to come into a pressured job like [Celtic], I needed to go in with a sense of stability," he told The Athletic in 2022.

"I could have recruited new staff, but then you're working each other out and there's a transition process where it probably takes three, four, five months. That's five months too late. I needed my staff with me and we couldn't get them together."

Howe's former Newcastle assistant, Jason Tindall, has something of a reputation for being active on Premier League sidelines. Tindall previously worked under Howe at Bournemouth before reuniting at St. James' Park five years ago.

Other long-term fixtures under Howe at Newcastle include Graeme Jones, Stephen Purches and Simon Weatherstone.

Harry Kane claimed the Ballon d'Or, ending a 25-year wait for an English winner, as the Bayern Munich ace saw off Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal.

‌

The former Tottenham striker was able to claim the award in his hometown with London hosting the event. This was the most competitive Ballon d'Or race in years and that was summed up by the quality of the top ten.

‌



Mbappe would finish second as his wait for a Ballon d'Or goes on despite a stellar year with Real Madrid and France. World Cup winner Lamine Yamal was in third.

Sports.title: Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or win bucks the trend and is fitting for a humble superstar
Sports.content:
Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or win bucks the trend and is fitting for a humble superstar

Harry Kane claimed the Ballon d'Or after a sensational year for the Bayern Munich ace - who became the first Englishman to claim the award in a quarter of a century

View 3 Images Harry Kane is a credit to English football and his stellar year saw him win the Ballon d'Or

No-one deserves this more than Harry Kane - and this is the fulfilment of a lifelong dream to be considered an all-time great with the likes of Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo.

‌



‌



Bayern Munich superstar Kane has made no secret of how much winning the Ballon d’Or means to him and his family. It is a recognition of his life’s work, his determination and ambition to become England’s greatest-ever goal scorer and one of the best players in history.

‌



Kane has been defined by his remarkable 73 goal season for club and country last year. His goals were spectacular, his performances are getting better and he is evolving as a player.

‌



The England captain broke records, helped Bayern win a domestic Treble and led his country to the semi finals of the World Cup. They eventually finished third and that is England’s best-ever finish on foreign soil.

But in a World Cup year, the coveted Ballon d’Or normally always goes to a player for his achievement in the tournament.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

The script is normally written for a World Cup winner to also be crowned the Ballon d’Or winner. Luka Modric being a notable exception in 2018 but even he won for helping Croatia reach the final. However, Kane has bucked the trend because his performances have been so good, so impressive and so spectacular.

‌



Yes, you could look to Lamine Yamal for his performances for Barcelona and also in helping Spain win the World Cup. Or Spain captain Rodri because he was magnificent in helping his country win the World Cup in the United States last summer.

But neither matched Kane’s achievement from an individual perspective because the Bayern striker has been so consistent, so prolific and, despite his award being about individual success, he has an incredible team ethic.

‌



Last week, Kane became only the second player in Champions League history to find the net in ten consecutive matches when he scored against Arsenal last week.

View 3 Images Harry Kane enjoyed the best season of his career (Image: Alex Grimm/Getty Images)

‌



The only other player was five-time Ballon d’Or Ronaldo winner who scored in 11 successive matches for Real Madrid between June 2017 and April 2018. Kane's goal against Arsenal last week also took his tally to 156 in 158 appearances since joining Bayern Munich from Tottenham in 2023.

Bayern legend Uli Hoeness, the club’s honorary president, has described Kane as their “best-ever signing” which is really saying something.

‌



This is the player who, let’s not forget, had to fight to succeed. Released by Arsenal as a kid, loaned out to Leyton Orient, Norwich, Millwall and Leicester, he struggled to make it at Tottenham. When he was told he was not quick enough, he worked endlessly on his speed and acceleration with resistance training. When he realised he needed to improve his technique, he spent endless sessions on his finishing and control.

Now he is not just a great finisher - and England’s record scorer - but also an all-round player because of his ability to drop deep, pass and provide assists. This is a player at the top of his game. But he has worked to get there. Back in 2017, a few columnists poked fun at Kane when, still at Tottenham and only 24, he talked about trying to emulate the achievements of Messi and Ronaldo.

‌



“A football career is a short career, so you have got to make the most of every day,” he said. “I use it as inspiration. “With social media these days it’s difficult to stay away from it. I want to be one of the best players in the world, so when people put it up and I see I am close to those players, it is a great incentive to get closer and go to the next step.”

View 3 Images The striker reached the World Cup semi-final in the summer

‌



Kane went from strength to strength at Tottenham. He scored goals, helped revive the club and earned himself a move to Bayern Munich. His goals there have been spectacular. One, in particular, stands out. It was against Inter Milan in April 2025 when he fought, battled and then wriggled past two defenders before digging the ball out to fire into the top corner.

That epitomizes Kane - and his determination. Nothing will stop him. He is a national treasure who deserves to be remembered as one of English football’s all-time greats. It is fitting that he has become the first English player since Michael Owen in 2001 to win this award.

‌



We should also respect the parameters of the award. Individual performances, decisive and impressive character. Collective performances and titles won. Class and fair play. That is Kane. He is a class act. A great leader. He has his own Foundation which champions mental health conversations, wellbeing, good health and to build resilience in young people.

Kane deserves this. More than anyone else. I even loved the fact that he said last week how nervous he is and how his wife Kate wanted to know in advance. She knows how important this is to him. And that in itself is another good reason to reward the humble superstar.

Sports.title: Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or as England star crowned world's best footballer
Sports.content:
Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or as England star crowned world's best footballer

England captain Harry Kane was among the favourites for the Ballon d'Or ahead of Monday evening's glitzy ceremony in London and he finally claimed the award

View 2 Images Harry Kane claimed the Ballon d'Or in London on Monday (Image: Getty Images)

Harry Kane has become the first English player to win the Ballon d'Or in 25 years after being crowned the world's best footballer.

‌



‌



Kane, 33, was among the favourites to claim the gong for the first time in his career following a sensational season with Bayern Munich. He scored 61 goals in 51 outings for the German side last term, helping them to yet another Bundesliga crown, as well as a German cup.

‌



Kane continued that form for England and the World Cup as he scored six goals for the Three Lions as they finished third under Thomas Tuchel.

‌



And that form was enough to see him become the first Englishman since Michael Owen in 2001 to claim the award, as well as the Striker of the Year gong.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Speaking after claiming his award, Kane said: "I am almost speechless. Being here in London has made it extra special. Made it a good omen for me tonight. Thank you to everyone who voted for me. I can imagine it was tough this year.

"Some world-class players in the room tonight. Congratulations to all the winners and nominees tonight and impressive showing determination and hard work can really achieve."

‌



He added: "Without you guys [Bayern Munich team-mates] and the rest of the team it wouldn't be possible, the way you guys push me, the way we compete. So thank you very much. To Vinny [Vincent Kompany]. I know he is at home or still in the hospital. Wishing you well. I hope this gave you a bit of energy. To all the staff we way train and the way you push us it is a credit to yourself.

"Since I have been with you I have improved as player, improved as a person and a leader. Thanks to your leadership. An honour to play for Bayern Munich. To represent you is a real privilege. Glad to be bringing this trophy back to Bayern Munich.

‌



View 2 Images Kane also secured the Gerd Muller Trophy (Image: Getty Images)

"To my England team-mates, again the same. We had a special year. It wasn't the perfect year, but we had a load of great moments. We built a great bond together. The togetherness in the hotel in the World Cup. An honour to captain you and lead you. It makes me extremely proud. This one is for all of us for sure. Thomas Tuchel and the staff at England, again the leadership the way you drive us, the way you push standards is something to be admired."

‌



Kane had faced serious competition for the award from Barcelona's Lamine Yamal. The teenager scored 24 goals and notched 18 assists for the Spanish giants last term, while he also shone for the Spanish national team as they secured their second World Cup crown in the USA.

Elsewhere, Kane's England colleague Jude Bellingham ended up finishing outside of the top ten in 11th place following another standout year for both Real Madrid and England. Declan Rice in the meantime only accumulated enough votes to finish 15th.

Sports.title: Man Utd told to STRIP Bruno Fernandes of captaincy after Michael Carrick outburst
Sports.content:
Man Utd told to STRIP Bruno Fernandes of captaincy after Michael Carrick outburst

Bruno Fernandes was left on the bench by Man United boss Michael Carrick during the Red Devils’ defeat to Bournemouth following his explosive comments and the club have been told to take the armband from him

View 2 Images Fernandes was named as an unused substitute vs Bournemouth (Image: Getty Images)

Ian Holloway has demanded that Bruno Fernandes be stripped of the Manchester United captaincy. The Red Devils skipper hit out at the side’s approach under Michael Carrick during their heavy Champions League defeat to Como in midweek.

‌



‌



And that appeared to have had some serious consequences for Fernandes, who was named as an unused substitute in Sunday’s reverse at the hands of Bournemouth.

‌



Former Blackpool and Crystal Palace boss Holloway has now offered his take and suggested that the Portuguese playmaker should have the captain’s armband taken from him.

‌



Speaking on Football Uncensored, he said: “Your club captain should be a leader and Man United used to have fantastic ones and they were big enough to take it. This lad is a good player, a very, very good player but as a person, I've seen him cheat time and time again.

“I've seen him kick someone, get him sent off… No Man United captain should ever do any of that, honestly, he doesn't deserve that shirt.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

“The fact is he came in and he managed to play well for that football club, which a lot of people can’t. They don't wear that shirt. They're not strong enough to wear that shirt. The expectation that it brings but he is not captain material, not in a million years. He will not lead anyone. He throws his arms in the air and he blames everyone.”

‌



Holloway added: “Yeah, he should be. I'd rip it off him. I'm not saying he's not a good player…The manager should not be undermined by players who aren't trying hard enough.

“And how can you not try hard enough when you pull on a Manchester United shirt? Do you not take into consideration how lucky you are to be even breathing in that air that was Man United?

‌



View 2 Images Fernandes hit out at Carrick's tactics vs Como (Image: Getty Images)

“You had to earn that shirt years ago. All of these people, honestly, they wouldn't have got in any one of the squads that Sir Alex built.”

‌



Carrick spoke out on the situation at the weekend and claimed his decision to leave Fernandes out was purely for footballing reasons.

He said: "He's fit and available but we decided to pick the team that we did today. Unfortunately for everyone we didn't manage to get the right result. We want to push forward and create more, we could've done certain things but not enough really and that's pretty clear."

Sports.title: Arsenal face Carabao Cup nightmare at club with 10 parking spaces as EFL reality hits home
Sports.content:
Arsenal face Carabao Cup nightmare at club with 10 parking spaces as EFL reality hits home

Arsenal will play in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday night when they take on League Two outfit Fleetwood Town, whose facilities are very much limited, which could pose problems for the Premier League giants

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta is aiming to win the Carabao Cup for the first time (Image: David Price, Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Arsenal will face Fleetwood Town in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup on Tuesday night with their usual luxuries certainly not afforded to them.

‌



‌



The Gunners went back level at the top of the Premier League at the weekend with a victory over Everton, and their next assignment sees them head to Highbury, the ground that shares the name with their former home.

‌



Fleetwood are currently sitting 18th in League Two and Arsenal will fly to Blackpool before making the short trip to Fleetwood, but when they arrive their usual travelling fleet of three buses and six vans may struggle for parking. The stadium boasts just ten spots.

‌



The Times reports that the Fleetwood players usually leave their cars on nearby streets in and around Highbury, which leaves Arsenal facing some parking challenges before they've even begun their journey to the north west of England.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Fleetwood boss Matt Lawlor is English football’s seventh-youngest manager and has overseen only 40 professional games. Last season he was at Waterford and narrowly kept them in the League of Ireland.

The Fishermen boss said on the challenge of facing the champions of England: “Me and Mikel are doing the same job, aren’t we? But obviously at different ends of the professional pyramid and different pressures. Hopefully in my career it becomes a more regular occurrence, doing stuff like this.

‌



“That’s the dream, that’s the hope of any young manager. For me to go through a year ago to that, it is amazing. But I’ve worked my socks off to be in the position that I am in today at Fleetwood Town."

View 2 Images Fleetwood's Highbury Stadium is Arsenal's next destination

‌



Arsenal are poised to ring the changes and, again, showcase their depth of squad. They've already been able to shuffle their ranks earlier the tournament when they saw off Ipswich at Portman Road with teenage sensation Max Dowman grabbing a brace. He is again expected to get minutes.

The Gunners have endured several near misses in the Carabao Cup, which under its previous names has been missing from the Arsenal trophy cabinet since 1993. It eluded Arsene Wenger throughout his tenure and last term Arteta was beaten in the final by Manchester City. The year prior to that he was undone in the semi-final.

Sports.title: Jim Ratcliffe's Man Utd blunders could see Red Devils eye-watering bill increase to £36m
Sports.content:
Jim Ratcliffe's Man Utd blunders could see Red Devils eye-watering bill increase to £36m

Manchester United are facing another very difficult decision over the future of their manager Michael Carrick following a dismal start to the new Premier League season

View 2 Images Sir Jim Ratcliffe has not been afraid to move managers on at Man United (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United's managerial mistakes could see the club end up paying nearly £40m in various compensation packages. Current boss Michael Carrick is clinging to his job following a disastrous start to the season that reached new lows with a 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth over the weekend.

‌



‌



Carrick has been at the centre of crisis talks with United chiefs on Monday, with a decision yet to be taken over his future. And should he leave Old Trafford, that could see the Red Devils fork out yet another considerable severance package.

‌



As of yet, it is not known how much United would have to pay out should they choose to sack Carrick. Any amount of compensation would add considerably to the amounts that the club have been forced to fork out under Sir Jim Ratcliffe since he seized control.

‌



United paid around £11m to sack former boss Erik ten Hag and his staff during the INEOS boss' first year at the helm. He then paid out another chunk of £11m to buy Ruben Amorim out of his deal with Sporting Lisbon.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



The Portuguese coach's stint at the club was a disaster, with Ratcliffe and his club colleagues paying out a further £8.2m to sack him. Another hefty bill could potentially be on the way with a new manager.

Ex-Newcastle boss Howe is among the frontrunners but one issue remains regarding a move for his services. When he left St James’ Park in the summer, Howe still had a number of years left to run on his deal, with a compensation package thought to be worth around £6m written into it, according to the Daily Telegraph, bringing the amount that the club have paid to hire and fire managers to around £36m before any severance package heading Carrick's way.

‌



It is suggested that Howe would listen to an approach from the Red Devils but would need some convincing to return to the dugout so soon. Links with Howe come at the same time that some of his previous comments about his demands in a job have resurfaced.

View 2 Images Eddie Howe could potentially replace Michael Carrick (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Speaking in 2022, he said: "I felt that if I was to come into a pressured job like [Celtic], I needed to go in with a sense of stability.

"I could have recruited new staff, but then you're working each other out and there's a transition process where it probably takes three, four, five months. That's five months too late. I needed my staff with me and we couldn't get them together."

‌



Howe is not the only name that has been mentioned as a potential Carrick replacement. Former Chelsea and Tottenham boss Antonio Conte is an obvious candidate, while Julian Nagelsmann is also available, having left his role as Germany boss after a disastrous World Cup campaign.

Meanwhile, Carrick appeared to suggest that his job could be under threat after the defeat to Bournemouth. He said: "Listen, it's a tough situation. There's no hiding from it. What it looks like, what's next, I really don't know. But I'll always do what's best for this football club.

Article continues below

“I've said it all along. I don't change that now. I love what I do, I love the position I'm in and I feel the responsibility, but we'll have to wait and see.”

Sports.title: FIFA issue statement as England walk off pitch at U15 World Cup after alleged racism
Sports.content:
FIFA issue statement as England walk off pitch at U15 World Cup after alleged racism

England players gathered at the side of the pitch following the alleged incident during their Under-15 World Cup match against the Republic of Ireland

View Image England's U15 World Cup match was abandoned following alleged racist incident

FIFA are investigating an allegation of racist abuse by a Republic of Ireland player that led to the abandonment of England's Under-15 World Cup match. The incident took place during Monday's match in Azerbaijan, when an England player was seen approaching the touchline to inform his coaching staff of the alleged abuse, before the complaint was brought to the referee's attention.

‌



‌



England's coaching staff then instructed their players to leave the pitch, with the Republic of Ireland leading 4-1 heading into the final minute of the match. FIFA have since confirmed they are investigating the incident and gathering reports to establish the circumstances surrounding the allegation.

‌



"Fifa is aware of an incident at the U-15 World Cup and Festival match between England and the Republic of Ireland," a spokesperson said. "The match was abandoned by the referee following England's refusal to continue.

‌

Sports.title: 'Lots to take away' - Hamilton reveals area he's 'lost out' to Leclerc
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton has revealed he's "lost out" to Charles Leclerc through the set-up of his Ferrari car in recent races.

Hamilton was outqualified by Leclerc at the United States Grand Prix and was unable to match his team-mate's impressive pace in the race on his way to fourth, while Leclerc finished second behind race-winner Kimi Antonelli.

At the previous race in Singapore, Hamilton looked strong in qualifying until Q3 when he was beaten by Leclerc, and a similar pattern occurred in Austin where the seven-time world champion topped final practice, only to qualify fifth.

"I lost a lot of points in the last five races or so," Hamilton, who is one point behind second-placed George Russell in the Drivers' Championship, told Sky Sports F1.

"I think it has come from set-up, not perfect, the set-up. That's something I really have to get on top of. That's where I have lost out. Performance-wise I feel like I've been driving well and the last [race] stint [in Austin] was good. The first two stints there was nothing I could do about that.

"Definitely lots to take away. The team did a great job to bring an upgrade. Charles got a second place. We have got good performance. Hopefully when we go to Mexico, we can improve on where we have gone wrong on that setup."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 United States Grand Prix

Ferrari continued to be the benchmark team in most corners at the Circuit of the Americas but lacked straight-line speed compared to Mercedes and Red Bull.

But, Hamilton was unhappy with the car's low-speed balance in the first two stints of the Grand Prix which put him out of the podium fight.

"I lost so much time. I couldn't turn the car in the low-speed particularly - Turn 1, Turn 11, Turn 12, Turn 13, 14, 15. Massive understeer so the [other] cars pulled away when I was adjusting my settings," he said.

"By the time we got to the last stint, we got closer to the balance but we should have started with that balance at the beginning. Lots of learnings. The team did a great job with pit stops and strategy."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton revealed that his Ferrari had 'massive' understeer, which cost him a fourth-place finish at the United States Grand Prix

Could Leclerc have won United States GP?

Leclerc qualified fourth but had a superb start by overtaking Isack Hadjar and Max Verstappen in the first sector, only for Verstappen to overtake the Ferrari driver at the end of the first lap.

Ferrari opted for a two-stop strategy with Leclerc which saw him charge past Verstappen and Lando Norris, who did a one-stop race, in the closing stages but he ultimately finished 13 seconds behind Antonelli.

Leclerc believes his qualifying position cost him a chance at victory but even if he had less traffic to contend with in the race, Antonelli was "just too quick".

"If you look at FP1, FP2 and FP3, we were very strong. If you look at qualifying, at the end of the day in Q3, it was extremely difficult to bring the tyres up to temperature, and we probably lost a shot at the victory there," said Leclerc.

"But Kimi was very strong, so, as a whole weekend, I think we're just not robust enough."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton topped final practice in Austin from Max Verstappen

Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur believes Leclerc could have won the race in different circumstances.

"The race went well - the racing went well, the pace was OK, we were aggressive with the strategy because we had to overtake," Vasseur told Sky Sports F1.

"Overall, if we missed something it was the last two laps in Q3. That was the most important laps of the weekend and that's where we had the issue.

"Overall, I want to take the positive of the weekend that the pace was there from FP1 to the last lap of the race. Without the VSC it would have been a double podium but let's try to do a better qualifying in Mexico and win the race."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charles Leclerc makes two great overtakes on Lando Norris and Max Verstappen

Can Ferrari win another race in 2026?

Five rounds remain in the 2026 season with the Mexico City Grand Prix up first this weekend, where altitude will be a factor given the track is 2,200m above sea level.

The performance of the Ferrari power unit at altitude will dictate if they can challenge for victory at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, which features lots of twisty corners which the SF-26 should enjoy.

"It's such fine margins, and it also depends on what the upgrade plans of the others are in upcoming races. But the feeling with the car is getting better and better," said Leclerc.

"These cars are very specific and unique, and I feel like, over the last two or three races, I've unlocked something again in terms of driving, and particularly setup with my driving. Just both together, we've taken a step forward, and I just feel much more comfortable with the car.

"I hope that this will result in a win soon. Whether it's in Singapore or in Austin, we were quite close, so I'm confident that we'll have a shot to win a race before the end of the season."
