"You definitely have to take the job, but I'm saying I'm taking it. But you know what? I want the control that Unai Emery's got at Aston Villa. I want the whole package.

3 Howe is a leading candidate to replace Carrick at Old Trafford Credit: Shutterstock Editorial



"I want promises that in January that I can buy this, this and this. These idiots that are in the squad, put them in the Under-10s, let them train with the kids.

"Give me everything I want and I'll take the job. If you don't get that Eddie Howe, stay clear of it."

Agbonlahor's comments come after Jeff Stelling urged Howe to steer clear of the job.

Meanwhile, Carrick's imminent departure comes after he dropped Bruno Fernandes for the visit of Bournemouth.



The Red Devils captain was an unused substitute against the Cherries.

It was a move which followed Fernandes' criticism of the tactics in the defeat to Como.

3 Carrick is expected to be sacked by the Red Devils Credit: Getty

As for Howe, he is currently without a club after leaving Newcastle in July.

The 48-year-old spent almost five years in charge at St. James' Park.

During that time, he twice qualified for the Champions League as well as winning the Carabao Cup.



That triumph ended the club's 70-year wait for a major domestic trophy.

Sports.title: Martin Keown and Alex Crook in heated clash live on air over Man United crisis
Sports.content:
Martin Keown and Alex Crook in heated clash live on air over Man United crisis

Manchester United's ongoing crisis prompted a fiery exchange live on talkSPORT on Monday morning.

The Red Devils' problems deepened on Sunday as they were beaten 3-0 by Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

4 Chief Football Correspondent Alex Crook clashed with Martin Keown live on air amid United's ongoing crisis Credit: talkSPORT

United are now winless in eight matches and talkSPORT understands dressing room insiders expect Michael Carrick to be sacked as manager.

Amid the issues facing the club, talkSPORT's chief football correspondent Alex Crook joined Sam Matterface, Martin Keown and Dean Ashton on air.

Crook and Keown clash amid United crisis

Having provided an update on Carrick's future, though, he quickly became embroiled in a heated back-and-forth with Keown.

The exchange stemmed from the former Arsenal defender asking Crook about his status as a United supporter.

Keown said: "Alex, not to blow your cover, but you’re a Manchester United fan, aren’t you?"

"Why are you not in the camp of the fans applauding Carrick off the pitch?"

Carrick was applauded off the pitch at Old Trafford by the home crowd, who had booed the United players at half-time and full-time on Sunday.

Crook replied: "I am. How do you know I'm not?" before Keown added: "Well, you just want change. You want him out."

In response, Crook said: "I didn't say that," only for the former England international to continue: "You implied that."

As their back-and-forth raged on, Crook reiterated: "I said my information as a journalist is there’s going to be a change, whether I think that’s the right or wrong decision, I think it’s inevitable."

4 Keown questioned Crook's stance on Carrick's United future Credit: talkSPORT

When asked what he thinks United should do next, he explained: "I don’t think Michael Carrick is the biggest issue at Manchester United.

"I don't think the manager has ever been the biggest issue at Manchester United.

"I think the Stretford End conducted themselves with great dignity yesterday, making their feelings towards a club legend, someone who clearly has put his all into this job, very clear and also voicing their disdain for a group of players who week in, week out, let them down, not just the fans, but the manager himself as well.

"He won’t say it, Michael Carrick, because he’s too much of a diplomat. He still cares too much about the football club. He will feel hurt by the performance of this season.

"How can you go from beating everybody around you last season to qualify for the Champions League to turning in the tripe that they are this season, that lack of effort, that lack of endeavor, that lack of accountability?"

Keown was not finished, though, as he responded: "So you’re separating the manager.

4 Crook accused Keown of 'putting words' in his mouth during their exchange Credit: talkSPORT

"You’re looking at the iconic player and not looking at the manager that you see before you now."

Crook then hit back, saying: "Why are you putting words into my mouth, Martin? I’m not going to say that."

The exchange then concluded with Keown adding: "But you are. That’s what it seems like.

"If we’re in the dressing room, taking you into the dressing room, it’s not an us and them situation.

"If we win, we all get the credit. If we lose, then it’s all of our fault. Everybody."

Latest on Carrick's future

As of Monday evening, Carrick has not been sacked by the Red Devils.

4 Carrick is expected to be sacked by United Credit: Getty

However, club officials expect the former United midfielder to be relieved of his duties just five months after signing a two-year deal.

His squad had a day off on Monday following their heavy defeat to the Cherries, with no training session held at Carrington.

Boardroom talks were expected to take place in the morning, with a decision not yet communicated to the manager regarding his future.

Carrick was present at the training ground, though, attending an Under-21s fixture against Hull City.

He was joined by assistant manager Steve Holland and Under-18s boss Darren Fletcher.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso committed cardinal sin against Tottenham, but calls for Chelsea sack are baffling
Sports.content:
There is a tacit agreement that every Chelsea manager, head coach or interim appointment must respect - you don't lose to Tottenham.

A London rivalry that had its first fixture in 1909, the mutual loathing really kicked off in 1967 when Spurs beat the Blues 2-1 in what was the first ever FA Cup final between two teams from the capital.

6 Chelsea lost to Spurs at Stamford Bridge in the Premier League for just the second time in 35 seasons Credit: Getty

Eight years later, Chelsea were relegated from the First Division soon after a 2-0 loss at White Hart Lane, whose residents avoided the drop by one point.

But the power eventually shifted and the Kings of the King's Road are top of their head-to-head table with 83 wins from 182 meetings, and the Lilywhites are on 56.

Chelsea have dominated since the turn of the millennium having won 41 of 69 matches, though the most recent clash on Saturday was one to forget.

Blues lose Bridge battle

Cole Palmer was sent off at Stamford Bridge as Spurs left with three points in a 2-0 victory, which is only their second away from home in the Premier League since it began in 1992.

Overseeing a Chelsea performance lacking effort from players who seemed to be unaware of the occasion's importance was manager Xabi Alonso, who made an error with his game plan before kick-off.

Joao Pedro picked up an injury the day before and was replaced by Geovany Quenda, the 19-year-old starlet who has so much potential but struggled out wide on what was his first league start.

Morgan Rogers appeared to be the focal point in attack whilst the natural striker Danny Welbeck sat on the bench until Spurs scored their second goal, by which time it was too late to make an impact.

Chelsea had just 31.3 per cent of possession, a woeful amount of time on the ball for a team who were playing at home, and a total of seven shots that their visitors bettered by eight.

During the full-time lap of applause, Levi Colwill was met with some choice words from supporters in the West Lower and encouraged to walk away from the fury by Welbeck.

It was the club's third Premier League defeat of the season and, even though they are fifth in the table and remain in the European race during Alonso's opening weeks, some fans aren't happy with him.

6 Alonso got it wrong against their London rivals and missed an opportunity to go third in the Premier League Credit: Getty

A quick search on social media will present numerous posts calling for the Spaniard to be dismissed as manager.

Some made the demand soon after the defeat to Spurs, and others believe anything but a win against a crisis-hit Manchester United this Saturday lunchtime, live on talkSPORT, is enough for the sack.

Whilst those who follow Chelsea from afar and express their views via social media are absolutely entitled to do so, they can sometimes fall into the trap of rash discourse.

Shock defeats, poor performances and questionable decisions are all catalysts for off the cuff outpourings that may be caught in clouds of emotion shortly after a full-time whistle has blown.

This can also be the case in the stands at Stamford Bridge, with those shouting at Colwill a prime example, but Alonso will have the backing of a myriad of fans who frequent the SW6 stadium for matches.

Again, those in the 'Alonso out' camp are certainly allowed to think in this way and communicate their opinions, yet a simple question must be asked for balance - what on earth would happen next?

6 Chelsea fans were furious and Colwill (right) took some of the heat, with Alonso also facing some baffling calls for the sack Credit: Getty

Calls for Alonso sacking are purely hasty

For a club who have made five permanent appointments in the head coach or manager role since BlueCo became custodians in May 2022, another change would further damage the fan-owner relations.

Thomas Tuchel was sacked in September 2022 despite winning the Champions League a year prior, Graham Potter couldn't make the step up from Brighton and ex-Spurs boss Mauricio Pochettino did not win over the fanbase.

Whilst Enzo Maresca sabotaged the 2025/26 season by throwing his toys out the pram to eventually replace Pep Guardiola at Manchester City, his successor Liam Rosenior was out of his depth.

Having finished in the bleak position of tenth, Chelsea were able to deliver a managerial coup with the hiring of Alonso.

The World Cup winner with Spain and ex-Liverpool midfielder made waves in the Bundesliga at Bayer Leverkusen as they won the 2023/24 title unbeaten, the DFB-Pokal and DFL-Supercup.

Winning one of the top five leagues in Europe cannot be overlooked, especially when there is not a single loss and the success comes in a first full season at senior management level.

6 Alonso boasts a highly impressive win record across the three clubs he has managed, especially at Madrid

Alonso was rewarded with the job at Real Madrid, where he spent five seasons as a player but taking charge at the world's biggest club is a huge leap and he left in January, despite winning 24 of 34 matches.

A 71 per cent win record is nothing to scoff at, even if his exit came off the back of Madrid's 3-2 Supercopa de Espana defeat to their bitter rivals Barcelona.

Just two months have passed since they commenced their campaign and Alonso has developed a front three of Palmer, Rogers and Pedro into a strong attacking force with a combined 13 goals and ten assists.

Chelsea are only two points outside the top four, and will be boosted towards a Champions League spot if City are to be given a massive points deduction for financial charges following their guilty verdict.

However, let's imagine a scenario where the club did decide to send Alonso packing for whatever reason - it's difficult to argue that any realistic replacements are available.

Pep Guardiola is taking a break from management and unlikely to be a candidate after spending a decade at rivals City, and Arne Slot won the league at Liverpool but had a poor title defence.

6 Julian Nagelsmann is one of the top managers currently without a club, but has already rejected a move to Chelsea Credit: Getty

Gareth Southgate has dismissed future Premier League management after reaching two Euros finals with England, whilst ex-France boss and World Cup winner Didier Deschamps is also an implausible choice.

Julian Nagelsmann turned down the Chelsea job in 2023 and is one of a number of options for United, whose targets to potentially replace Michael Carrick would most likely not come into the Blues' thinking.

Eddie Howe won the League Cup at Newcastle but is arguably a step down from Alonso, Antonio Conte left Chelsea on bad terms in 2018 and Fabian Hurzeler would be yet another hire from Brighton.

Unai Emery has gained plaudits for his work at Aston Villa but is not likely to leave, and the same can be said for Luis Enrique at Paris Saint-Germain, Hansi Flick at Barcelona and Jose Mourinho at Madrid.

Whilst the options for Chelsea look slim given the aforementioned, yet hypothetical, names are unrealistic, various fans in the 'Alonso out' camp have pointed to Cesc Fabregas as the answer.

Fabregas reunion is a no-go

He won two Premier League titles as a midfielder for the west London club from 2014 to 2019, and the 'Fabregas is magic' chant that takes aim at his ex-side Arsenal is still sung at the Bridge today.

6 Fabregas has really impressed at Como and is likely to be linked with Chelsea in the future but, in the here and now, Alonso must be backed Credit: Getty

Now at the beginning of his managerial career, the Spaniard is eyed as one for the future thanks to immense success with Como.

Fabregas not only got them promoted to Serie A in 2024, 21 years after relegation from the Italian top flight, he masterminded their first ever qualification for the Champions League.

After three games in their competition debut, Como are ninth in the league phase with two wins - 4-1 victories over RB Leipzig and United.

Chelsea naming Fabregas as their manager is not a situation that is out of the realms of possibility, whilst his fellow former employers Arsenal and Barcelona are also potential destinations in the future.

However, the 39-year-old is still relatively inexperienced and so, if he was to return to Chelsea and have a poor tenure in the dugout, then his popular reputation amongst the fans could be tarnished.

Furthermore, the club will find themselves back at square one once again, an avoidable outcome that must also be shunned in the present day.

Yes, Chelsea manager Alonso broke the tacit agreement and lost to Spurs, but relieving him of his duties so early on in his spell would be a real drop of the ball.

Sports.title: England Under-15s walk off pitch during World Cup match after racism allegation
Sports.content:
England Under-15s walk off pitch during World Cup match after racism allegation

England's Under-15s walked off the pitch during their match against the Republic of Ireland after a player was allegedly racially abused.

The Young Lions' fixture at the FIFA Under-15 World Cup and Festival was abandoned on Monday.

3 England Under-15s walked off the pitch during the final minute against Ireland Credit: DAZN

Head coach Matt Thorpe withdrew his players in the final minute of the match following the incident.

England player alleges racist comment

According to the Daily Mail, an England player claimed an opponent had made a racist comment towards them.

It followed an altercation which saw the England youngster push a rival in the back.

After the allegation was made, a member of the Irish coaching team reportedly shouted: "No, he didn't," prompting the England player to protest back.

An argument subsequently broke out between members of staff from both benches.

Thorpe and his coaches were then approached by the accuser, who waited on the touchline whilst his manager spoke to an official.

Before the match could restart, the England boss ordered his players off the pitch.

As a result, the clash was abandoned in the final minute with Ireland leading 4-1.

FIFA statement

FIFA have since launched an investigation into the incident.

In a statement, a FIFA spokesperson said: "FIFA is aware of an incident at the FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival match between England and the Republic of Ireland.

3 An England player alleged a racist comment had been made towards them Credit: DAZN

"The match was abandoned by the referee following England’s refusal to continue.

"The official reports are being gathered, and the matter will be referred to the independent Disciplinary Committee who will decide in due course."

It is yet to be confirmed whether the result from the match at the time it was abandoned will stand.

Ireland currently sit a point clear of England at the top of Group C following their meeting.

The Young Lions conclude their group stage schedule against Zimbabwe on Monday, with England winning 2-0 at the time of writing.

Thorpe's side began their campaign with a 4-0 win over Nicaragua on Saturday.

3 The inaugural FIFA Under-15 World Cup and Festival is taking place in Azerbaijan Credit: Getty

They subsequently beat Montenegro and Cambodia 2-1 and 10-0, respectively on Sunday.

As it stands, England will advance to Tier B of the tournament stage.

This week's tournament in Baku, Azerbaijan, marks the inaugural edition of the FIFA Under-15 World Cup and Festival.

The event is set to run until Friday having started on Saturday.

Matches are eight-a-side and consist of two 20-minute halves.

Sports.title: 2026 Ballon d’Or winner ‘leaks’ cause fan meltdown hours before official announcement
Sports.content:
2026 Ballon d’Or winner ‘leaks’ cause fan meltdown hours before official announcement

The winner of the 2026 Ballon d'Or was announced early on the award's official website...

However, fans were left confused after France Football published that Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal had all won the prestigious gong. The posts have since been deleted.



3 Kane was announced as the Ballon d'Or winner... along with Mbappe and Yamal Credit: Getty

This year's recipient is set to be officially announced on Monday night in a ceremony at the London Palladium.

The ceremony is expected to begin at 8pm, with the winner's press conference scheduled for 10:30pm.

Kane, Mbappe and Yamal are the three leading contenders for the Ballon d'Or.



The trio are amongst 30 players nominated for their performances during the 2025/26 season.

Those nominees are being placed from 30th to fourth ahead of this evening before the top three discover their fate.



talkSPORT understands Mbappe will be named as the winner of the Ballon d'Or.

Ballon d'Or winner leaked

Prior to the awards ceremony, articles appeared on the Ballon d'Or website for each player, claiming they had 'won' the award.



An article detailing Kane's 61 goals for Bayern Munich titled 'Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d'Or' was amongst those to appear online.

The England captain won the European Golden Shoe as he fired the German giants to a league and cup double last term.

Kane also scored six goals for the Three Lions as they finished third at the World Cup, their best performance since 1966.

3 Mbappe is nominated for the award alongside Kane and Yamal Credit: Getty



He is aiming to become the fifth Englishman to win the award and the first since Michael Owen 25 years ago.

Who are Kane's Ballon d'Or rivals?

However, Mbappe's 'consistency personified at the very highest level' saw him win the Ballon d'Or, according to another article that was published on the official website.

The Real Madrid forward won the World Cup golden boot after becoming the tournament's all-time leading scorer with 10 goals this summer.

Mbappe also finished as the top scorer in both LaLiga and the Champions League last term.



Across all competitions, the France international scored 42 goals in 44 appearances for Real Madrid.

As for Yamal, the 19-year-old became a World Cup winner with Spain as well as winning LaLiga for the third time in four seasons.

3 Yamal is aiming to become the youngest-ever winner of the Ballon d'Or Credit: Getty

Having finished as runner-up last year, the teenager is aiming to become the youngest ever winner of the Ballon d'Or.



The current record is held by Ronaldo, who was 21 years and 96 days old when he received the award for the first time in 1997.

Yamal has previously won the Kopa Trophy, awarded to the world's best Under-21 player, in each of the last two years and talkSPORT understands he will win it again this year.

Sports.title: Nicolas Jackson is one of top three strikers in Premier League – he starts for Arsenal
Sports.content:
Nicolas Jackson is one of top three strikers in Premier League – he starts for Arsenal

Is Nicolas Jackson a top three striker in the Premier League?

talkSPORT's Gabby Agbonlahor thinks so, with the Aston Villa frontman scoring four in his last four league games.

3 Jackson has instantly hit form for Aston Villa, scoring seven goals in his first 11 appearances since joining from Chelsea Credit: Getty

Jackson, who signed for Villa from Chelsea for a club record £65million in the summer, has hit the ground running.

In 11 appearances in all competitions for his new side, he has already scored seven goals, with four strikes coming in the top flight.

His double against Manchester City on Saturday showcased just how good he can be - and after that game, Agbonlahor made a bold claim.

He asked on talkSPORT's GameDay Phone-In: "Nicolas Jackson - give me three better centre forwards in the Premier League?"

Agbonlahor firmly put him in among the best and disregarded any inclusion of Brentford's Igor Thiago in the conversation.

The ex-striker also stated that Jackson would start for Arsenal, putting him in their side over Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz.

Is Jackson one of the best three strikers in the Premier League?

After those comments, talkSPORT Breakfast host Jeff Stelling agreed with statement, saying: "I think he [Agbonlahor] is right on current form.

"Erling Haaland and Alexander Isak yeah, but who else can you argue? It's very hard to argue the case for anybody else."

Co-host Ally McCoist then added: "He [Jackson] has got a lot more composure than he's had. He can still be doing with a little more calmness in front of goal.

"But there are not a lot of strikers that are top class that really enjoying playing the role themselves and he's perfect for it, he's been terrific. Gabby's right!"

3 Agbonlahor, Stelling and McCoist all agree that Jackson is one of the best three strikers in the Premier League Credit: Getty

Jackson has found 'a natural home'

Jackson's career in England appeared to be in doubt after struggling at Chelsea and being sent out on loan last season.

He spent last term as Harry Kane's understudy at Bayern Munich, scoring 11 goals in 34 appearances in all competitions.

The Senegal international was then sold to Villa on his return to the Premier League and he is now in impressive form.

Arsenal legend Martin Keown believes Jackson lost his way at Chelsea and that now, working under Unai Emery for the second time after his spell at Villarreal, he has found a 'natural home'.

Keown said: "He worked with him [Emery] before and I think this Villa team is now unrecognisable now from the start of the season.

"Jackson, for me, is a nightmare to play against. He's robust, dynamic and he punishes you with pace.

3 Back working under Emery, Jackson appears to be finding his best form Credit: Getty

"I think the Villa faithful are delighted he's now playing for them and maybe this is a natural home for him.

"I thought he was losing his discipline at Chelsea a little bit... he was getting sent off, getting involved in silly things, he wasn't loved.

"But he has the full love now of the manager and the club and I think it's the perfect place for him."

Sports.title: Harry Kane wins the Ballon d'Or: England captain sends poignant message after emotional speech as he was named the world's best and beat Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal
Sports.content:
Harry Kane has won the Ballon d'Or, becoming the first English player in 25 years to be crowned the world's best player, edging out Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to the award.

The most prestigious awards night on the footballing calendar descended into chaos hours before it even got underway as the Ballon d'Or's official website published three separate articles announcing Kane, Mbappe and Yamal as winners of the main award and fights broke out outside between fans and security.

But Bayern Munich striker Kane, who scored 61 goals for the German giants last season, was unruffled by the time he was crowned the victor on a night which left him ‘speechless’.

The 33-year-old, who was supported by wife Katie Goodland at the London Palladium on Monday night, shared the poignant message: 'Work hard in silence. Let success be your noise' on social media after being named as the winner.

While Yamal went on to win the World Cup in the summer, defeating Lionel Messi’s Argentina in the final, and Mbappe became the leading scorer in World Cup history, Kane’s magnificent goalscoring season separated him from his peers.

En route to winning the double with Bayern Munich, as well as guiding England to a third-placed finish at the World Cup, Kane scored 73 goals.

Harry Kane has been crowned as England's first Ballon d'Or winner since 2001

Kane received the award from legendary Brazil forward Ronaldo after beating Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe to the honour

The England captain had to fight back tears as he thanked his parents for their support

His 61 goals for Bayern Munich saw Kane become the first player to hit that total in a single season since Cristiano Ronaldo scored 61 for Real Madrid in 2014-15.

That total was 19 more than any other player across Europe’s top five leagues and his complete total, adding his 12 goals for England, saw him finish with 73. Mbappe would wrap up with 58 and Yamal finished with 25.

Adding assists, Kane’s total goal involvements last season came to a staggering 81.

'Wow, wow, wow,' Kane said after receiving the honour. I am almost speechless. Being here in London has made it extra special. Made it a good omen for me tonight.

'Thank you to everyone who voted for me, I can imagine it was tough this year.

Kane was emotional on stage as he thanked each of the managers and coaches he has played under, while also tearing up as he spoke of the importance of his parents in helping him to the crowning moment of his career.

'Mum and dad, what a moment. All those years, the sacrifice, the support you gave me. Taking me to training, coming to watch me play. No matter where it was, even to this day you're there,' Kane said.

'All those traits you have given me have allowed me to be successful and be here tonight.

"My kids back home watching - it is past your bedtime! You're the reason I do this. This one is a special one. I can't wait to see you and celebrate with you. I love you very much.

'My wife Kate, my best friend, you're my biggest supporter. We have done it. You always want the best for me. You sacrifice yourself to help me achieve my reams. It wouldn't be possible without you.'

Work hard in silence. Let success be your noise. 🏆 — Harry Kane (@HKane) October 26, 2026

Kane thanked his wife Kate, describing her as his 'best friend' and 'my biggest supporter'

Harry Kane scored 156 goals for Bayern Munich since moving to Germany in 2023

Kane continued: 'Without you guys [Bayern Munich team-mates] and the rest of the team it wouldn't be possible, the way you guys push me, the way we compete, so thank you very much.

'To Vinny [Vincent Kompany]. I know he is at home or still in the hospital. Wishing you well. I hope this gave you a bit of energy. To all the staff we way train and the way you push us it is a credit to yourself.

'Since I have been with you I have improved as player, improved as a person and a leader. It is an honour to play for Bayern Munich, to represent you is a real privilege and I am glad to be bringing this trophy back to Bayern Munich.'

'To my England team-mates, again the same, we had a special year. It wasn't the perfect year, but we had a load of great moments.

'It is an honour to captain you and lead you. It makes me extremely proud. This one is for all of us for sure, Thomas Tuchel and the staff at England, again the leadership the way you drive us, the way you push standards is something to be admired.'

There was also special mention to his former team Tottenham Hotspur.

‘I want to say thank you to Tottenham Hotspur as well,’ an emotional Kane said.

‘I wouldn’t be where I am today without Tottenham for sure. I was there from 11 years old.

Kane also drew level with Peter Shilton on a record 125 caps for England during the recent Nations League fixtures

‘You allowed me to live my dream so without all those ups and downs along the way, that journey has led me to this moment today.

'To all the fans, Bayern, England fans, Spurs fans and all my fans around the world. I love you in this room tonight.

'I remember being a fan not long ago and what it means to play football. It was a dream of mine. Any time I can give back to you guys is an honour and privilege to do so.'

Kane’s success on Monday night means that he has become the first Englishman to win the award since Michael Owen was crowned the world’s best player in 2001.

Since then, Ronaldo (Brazil), Pavel Nedved (Czech Republic), Andriy Shevchenko (Ukraine), Ronaldinho (Brazil), Fabio Cannavaro (Italy), Kaka (Brazil), Cristiano Ronaldo (Portugal), Lionel Messi (Argentina), Luka Modric (Croatia), Karim Benzema (France), Rodri (Spain), and Ousmane Dembele (France) have all won it.

Kane’s victory means he is also the first player from the Bundesliga to win the award since Matthias Sammer of Borussia Dortmund, won it in 1996.

The Football Association lit up Wembley in honour of Kane's accomplishment on Monday evening, as England boss Thomas Tuchel congratulated his captain.

‘Congratulations Harry on a deserved Ballon D’Or,' Tuchel said.

'I ran out of superlatives to describe your performances a long time ago, but I’m delighted to see that you have now been formally recognised by the football world.

'To become the first Englishman to win this huge honour in 25 years makes it extra special and we are lucky to have you as our leader. I know you will enjoy this moment with your loved ones and then get back to doing what you do best – scoring goals and winning football matches.’

Kane had been the bookmakers’ favourite for the award for some time and he has had to contend with plenty of noise around whether he will end England’s 25-year wait for a winner.

Since 2024, organisers France Football made the executive decision not to reveal the winner in advance in a bid to build suspense, although leaks in previous years led to the likes of Real Madrid’s Vinicius Jr boycotting the award after hearing Rodri was to be crowned the victor instead.

Kane with wife Katie at Oktoberfest in Munich last month

Kane was never going to miss Monday night’s iconic event, even if his family have had a hard time trying to stop stressing.

‘I think my wife would prefer to know and my family, it's very stressful for everyone,’ Kane said last week.

‘From my point of view, of course, I'd love to know to just kind of see and not have to wait throughout the whole night. But it is their decision, I can't control that. We'll have to just enjoy it and try not to stress out too much.

‘I try not to think about it. Obviously it is hard not to. There are always rumours flying around and you try to stay away from it.’

In the end it was elation, rather than despair, for the Kane family as the suited up striker received the applause and recognition from his illustrious peers.

Sports.title: Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or triumph was vindication for a superstar brimming with quiet excellence who swerves flashy controversy, writes OLIVER HOLT - and a win for English football
Sports.content:
It is July 10 2024, a couple of hours after goals from Harry Kane and Ollie Watkins have taken England past the Netherlands in Dortmund and into the final of Euro 2024. In the Dorint Hotel, the other side of a dual carriageway from the Westfalenstadion, a group of fans, some in England shirts, are sitting in the lobby bar.

They see a couple of us sitting by ourselves at another table and invite us over. It is Kane’s wife, Katie Goodland, and her family, her sister, her parents. They talk about Kane’s life in Munich and their lives in Essex, their favourite pubs, favourite places to eat. They talk a little about some of the criticism Kane is attracting but they hold no bitterness. They are lovely people. It is two hours well spent.

I thought of them when I got around to seeing Dear England, the play written by James Graham, which won rave reviews for its portrayal of Gareth Southgate as football’s answer to Jesus Christ but whose characterisation of Kane as a dolt and a bore was so crass and crudely drawn that it spoilt the play.

I thought of them when I saw Kane criticised for making the move from Spurs to Bayern Munich and then failing to win the Bundesliga in his first season. I thought of them when people laughed that he would never win a trophy.

I thought of them a few weeks ago when I read that Lamine Yamal had dismissed Kane’s claims to winning the Ballon d’Or, the sport’s most prestigious individual honour, and had fed into the star culture that pervades the game by saying the battle for it should be between him and Kylian Mbappe.

‘I honestly believe there are two of us who are the best in the world, and this year I’d deserve it because of what I’ve won,’ Yamal said in an interview clip shared by Spanish streaming platform Movistar. As far as I’m concerned, Mbappe and I are the two best in the world. It’s clear to me, and everyone who watches the matches knows it.’

Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or triumph is a success story for football's humble superstars

The Bayern Munich and England star is a model professional as well as a superb goal-scorer

Kane thanked his wife Kate, describing her as his 'best friend' and 'my biggest supporter'

But most of all, I thought of them late on Monday night when I sat in the audience at the London Palladium in the heart of London’s West End and watched Kane walk up to the stage to take that prize ahead of both Yamal and Mbappe and become the first Englishman for 25 years to be named the best footballer in the world.

Because that moment was Kane’s vindication. It was the moment that justified the way he has conducted himself throughout a career that started with him scrapping his way through loan spells at Leyton Orient, Millwall, Norwich City and Leicester City before he nailed down a place in the Spurs first team.

‘My journey has not been a straightforward one,’ Kane said on that stage in front of an audience of yelling kids and raucous fans. 'For any young boy wanting to achieve their dreams, and hoping to learn through resilience, determination and self-belief, I hope this can give you inspiration.'

It was a pitch-perfect speech that combined the emotion that spilled out when he thanked his parents and his wife and the care and the loyalty that came with a heartfelt thank you to Tottenham for ‘believing in me and my dreams.’

It was the moment that told him that he had been right to dedicate himself to the game completely and that all the years of being a fine role model to young players in the sport and to fans who idolised something they saw in him had been worth it.

It was the moment that said that football is capable of handing the highest honours to men like him, who have not sought the limelight or courted controversy or abused their fame or hired performers with dwarfism to decorate your 18th birthday party, as Yamal is alleged to have done, but have dedicated themselves to a career of quiet excellence.

Work hard in silence. Let success be your noise. 🏆 — Harry Kane (@HKane) October 26, 2026

He received the award from Brazil icon Ronaldo after beating Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe

Kane, pictured embracing Women's Ballon d'Or winnger Alexia Putellas, justified the way he has conducted himself throughout his career by winning football's top individual prize

And it was the moment that told him that scoring a remarkable 61 goals for Bayern in a single season, leading England to the brink of a World Cup final and extending his astonishing goalscoring record with his country so that he now boasts 91 goals in 125 caps counts for what it should.

It is not a win for the Premier League because Kane plies his trade in the Bundesliga now but it is a win for English players. It asks more questions about Thomas Tuchel’s attempt to pin the blame on England’s World Cup exit on the poor technique of English players. In Kane and Jude Bellingham, England have players with Rolls-Royce technique.

And it is a win for English football because Kane is the ambassador for our game in the way Sir Bobby Charlton was the ambassador for our game. He is a player admired for more than just his football. He is admired for what he stands for on and off the pitch. He is a player who plays the game with respect and dignity as well as sublime skill.

‘The Ballon d’Or,’ its rules suggest, ‘is awarded based on three criteria, in order of importance: 1. Individual performances, decisive and impressive character. 2. Collective performances and titles won. 3. Class and fair play.’ Those criteria are rich justification for Kane’s win.

The truth is that for everything he has achieved, Kane has been underrated for much of his career. Because the truth is also that he is, alongside Jimmy Greaves, the greatest goalscorer England has ever produced but also a player who proves again and again that he is far more than a goalscorer.

Kane is the complete centre forward, a man who scores and scores and scores for Bayern, but whose passing ability and brilliant technique makes him stand out amid his competitors. He and Jude Bellingham drove England on and on at the World Cup in Mexico, Canada and the US last summer.

And now he is in rare company. He is the first Englishman to win the Ballon d’Or since Michael Owen in 2001. Only four of his compatriots, Sir Stanley Matthews(1956), Sir Bobby Charlton(1966), Kevin Keegan(1978 and 1979), and Owen, have been awarded the honour. Denis Law(1964) and George Best(1968), are the only other British players to have won.

Kane was warned when he left Spurs that the move would cost him his shot at immortality because it would end his chances of overhauling Alan Shearer’s mark of 260 goals that makes him the leading scorer in Premier League history.

The striker’s move to Bayern Munich from Tottenham in 2023 has paid off handsomely

Kane is the first Englishman to win the Ballon d’Or since Michael Owen (right) in 2001

Those warnings may have been right but think of what Kane has gained. Think of how much he has been rewarded for that move. Maybe the chance of the league record has gone but Kane’s name is now written in football history alongside Lionel Messi, Cristiano Ronaldo, Franz Beckenbauer, Johan Cruyff and Zinedine Zidane.

Kane’s victory is a victory for a player who has done things the right way, a player who is not a raging narcissist like Ronaldo, a player who is understated and unassuming, a player who is the ultimate professional, who has done everything to maximise his talents and devote himself to the game and who is now reaping the rewards.

It is a victory for Spurs, it is a victory for English football, which created and nurtured him. And it is a victory for his family, whose pride in their husband, son, father and brother is something we can all share.

Sports.title: Why Mikel Arteta is so impressed by Ceadach O'Neill, Arsenal's prolific 18-year-old vying for his first-team debut against Fleetwood - and how he's justifying Gunners' new recruitment drive
Sports.content:
There's a good reason why Arsenal are especially keen for Ceadach O'Neill to be a success story.

The 18-year-old, who is vying to make his competitive debut in the Gunners' Carabao Cup fourth-round tie at Fleetwood Town on Tuesday night, is the first rising star to emerge from their raid on Scottish and Northern Irish academies, which began in 2024 and was influenced by Brexit rules.

If the teenager can either make a name for himself at Arsenal, or one day be sold for a worthwhile fee, the club's recruitment pivot to a UK strategy will have paid dividends.

And Mikel Arteta likes what he sees. So do Northern Ireland, for whom O'Neill made his senior debut in June. And so do the Republic of Ireland, but we'll come back to that.

O'Neill was involved in the Gunners' pre-season preparations, featuring in friendlies against Girona and Real Betis in August, as well as scoring in a behind-closed-doors fixture against MK Dons. He was also on the bench for Arsenal’s 3-0 Champions League victory over Lille earlier this month.

This followed a fruitful 2025-26 campaign where he finished as the club’s top goalscorer in the academy with 18 goals in 30 games across three age-group levels.

The 18-year-old Ceadach O'Neill is vying to make his competitive debut in Arsenal's Carabao Cup fourth-round tie at Fleetwood Town on Tuesday night

The attacking player (right) has taken part in first-team training alongside Bruno Guimaraes, Declan Rice and Andre Harriman-Annous

The versatile forward typically operates on either wing or as a false nine and with Bukayo Saka sidelined and Christos Tzolis still making his way back from injury, Arsenal are not blessed with options out wide.

O’Neill's profile is an exciting one. He's 5ft 11in with tight dribbling skills and constantly looks to take opponents on and get into goalscoring positions. He's also two-footed, reflected by his ability to play off both flanks.

O’Neill’s long-term position remains a work in progress, though, Arsenal having also played him as an attacking midfielder.

Born in Kilrea, County Londonderry, O’Neill made his senior debut for Linfield in the Irish Premiership aged just 15 against Ballymena United in November 2023. Weeks later he was on trial at Arsenal, and travelled to Brazil with the Under 16s in December 2023 for the Flamengo Adidas Cup – a baptism of fire for a teenager trying to win a contract.

O’Neill impressed in the tournament before officially joining the Gunners in March 2024, later signing his first professional contract with the club in April 2025.

He has flourished ever since and become the embodiment of Arsenal's bid to tap into the best talents across the UK borders, bringing in other young prospectsfrom Scotland and Northern Ireland after Brexit made it harder to sign players from Europe.

Callan Hamill, 17, signed an agreement in the summer of 2024 which allowed him stay at Scottish Premiership side St Johnstone while also splitting his time with Arsenal, before officially joining in July 2025.

The versatile forward typically operates on either wing or as a false nine and with Bukayo Saka sidelined and Christos Tzolis still out, Arsenal are not blessed with options out wide

Evan Mooney, 18, moved from St Mirren in February 2026 for a fee the Scottish club described as ‘substantial... with potential for significant future add-ons and a sizeable sell-on clause’. As for Northern Ireland, Daniel McCarron, 16, joined from Dungannon Swifts in July 2026.

The Gunners’ pivot to the UK stems from Brexit. Before these rules changes, English clubs could recruit eligible 16 to 18-year-olds from EU countries.

After Brexit, that was no longer allowed. So non-EU Northern Ireland and Scotland were seen as fertile areas for Arsenal to explore further. For example, Arsenal are having to wait for Victor Ozhianvuna to turn 18 in January 2027 before he officially joins them from Shamrock Rovers due to him coming from EU member, the Republic of Ireland.

Most academy prospects have enough to worry about when it comes to whether they will make the grade or not. Yet O’Neill has had other matters to navigate too – the tug of war between Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland over his international allegiance.

Having represented Northern Ireland at youth level, he earned his first two senior caps in friendlies against Guinea and France in June 2026.

But that summer, the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) approached him about switching to the Republic, thrusting the youngster into an international eligibility saga that dominated local headlines, despite him not having made his competitive debut for the Gunners.

O'Neill represented Northern Ireland at youth level and earned his first two senior caps in friendlies against Guinea and France in June 2026. But that summer, the Republic of Ireland approached him about switching allegiances

‘I've been really impressed with him,’ said Mikel Arteta of O'Neill. ‘For his age, he's really mature, really focused, and he has tremendous quality'

Northern Ireland manager Michael O’Neill met the youngster in London in September before selecting him for the UEFA Nations League. O’Neill earned his third and fourth senior caps against Georgia and Ukraine on September 25 and October 2, effectiely ending the prospect of a switch under FIFA’s eligibility rules – you can’t switch allegiances after representing your country four times at senior level.

With the saga behind him, O’Neill’s focus is now on impressing at Arsenal. After the summer Betis defeat, Arteta praised O’Neill when asked about the player by a throng of excited Irish journalists in the mixed zone.

‘I've been really impressed with him,’ said Arteta. ‘For his age, he's really mature, really focused, and he has tremendous quality. He's a player that we have big hopes with and we just need to develop him in the right way.’

The challenge for O'Neill now is to turn that promise into first-team minutes – and, in doing so, become the clearest sign yet that Arsenal’s post-Brexit recruitment strategy is paying off.

Sports.title: Stars arrive for glitzy Ballon d'Or bash in London: Game of Thrones star Sophie Turner, Jorja Smith, and Kate Scott join sporting legends Gary Lineker and Ronaldo... with England captain Harry Kane hoping to land top prize
Sports.content:
Stars arrive for glitzy Ballon d'Or bash in London: Game of Thrones star Sophie Turner, Jorja Smith, and Kate Scott join sporting legends Gary Lineker and Ronaldo... with England captain Harry Kane hoping to land top prize

Stars of football were pictured on the red carpet ahead of the glitzy Ballon d'Or ceremony at the London Palladium.

England captain Harry Kane, Spain and Barcelona star Lamine Yamal and Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe are viewed as the frontrunners to land the top prize on the night.

Game of Thrones star Sophie Turner was among those from the showbiz world taking to the red carpet ahead of one of the biggest nights in the football calendar.

Turner was followed by British singing superstar Jorja Smith and presenter Kate Scott.

Scott, who is set to host the ceremony with football legend Thierry Henry, shared a kiss with her husband Malik Scott on the red carpet.

Football legends including Gary Lineker and former Brazil forward Ronaldo also arrived ahead of the ceremony, along with Alan Shearer, Figo and Jamie Carragher.

England captain and Ballon d'Or contender Harry Kane was among one of the last arrivals on the red carpet alongside his wife Kate

Presenter Kate Scott shard a kiss with her husband Malik Scott on the red carpet ahead of hosting the Ballon d'Or ceremony

French superstar Kylian Mbappe led Real Madrid's delegation at the ceremony as the Spanish giants ended their two-year boycott of the event

Actress Sophie Turner and singer Jorja Smith were among those from the showbiz world in attendance

Lamine Yamal is hoping to make history on Monday night and looked sharp in a floral suit

The leading names bidding to land the men's award were among the later arrivals ahead of the ceremony getting underway.

Kane is hoping to become the first English man to win the award since Michael Owen back in 2001.

Owen will be among those in the crowd, with the former England forward set to watch the event with his wife Louise.

Mbappe, who is hoping to land the award for the first time, will lead a Real Madrid delegation in London after the Spanish club ended a two-year boycott.

The Spanish giants dramatically pulled out of attending the 2024 award ceremony at the last minute after it emerged Vinicius Jr was not expected to claim the top prize.

Rodri was insisted announced as the winner over the Brazilian star.

Real Madrid continued their boycott last year, with only Caroline Weir travelling to the event after she had been nominated for the women's prize.

Sports.title: Boxing world champion Adrien Broner back in hot water as video shows him being handcuffed and hauled into police car in Beverly Hills
Sports.content:
Adrien Broner, the troubled former boxing champion once seen as the future of the sport, had another run-in with police over the weekend in Beverly Hills.

Now more than two years removed from his last fight, the 37-year-old Broner was among a group of men recording content on the streets of Beverly Hills for the social media platform, Kick, when local police arrived.

Viral footage from the incident shows the group recording what appears to be a music video involving both Broner and his fellow content creator, Deen The Great.

A separate clip shows Broner with his arms raised and walking backwards towards a pair of officers, who ultimately placed him in handcuffs. Broner is seen trying to poke fun at the situation by doing a funny walk for the officers' benefit, but they did not seem amused.

'Broner was detained during a traffic stop as part of an investigation into a large street gathering in a residential area,' Beverly Hills police told TMZ in a statement. 'He was released from the scene and a citation was not issued.'

The Daily Mail has sought further information from Beverly Hills police.

Adrien Broner dancing while getting put in handcuffs by the police 💀 pic.twitter.com/h9SZlIYfdM — Happy Punch (@HappyPunch) October 26, 2026

Viral footage shows the group recording what appears to be a music video involving both Broner (center, open gray sweatshirt) and his fellow content creator, DeenTheGreat

A separate clip shows Broner with his arms raised and walking backwards towards a pair of officers, who ultimately placed him in handcuffs on the streets of Beverly Hills

Adrien Broner and Deen The Great attend the Internet Ball on August 19, 2026

Broner is currently among several defendants being sued in Los Angeles County over allegations of sexual battery, battery and assault.

'Plaintiff alleges that Broner repeatedly pressured Plaintiff for sexual activity after repeated refusals, attempted to isolate Plaintiff, repeatedly pressured Plaintiff while intoxicated, attempted unwanted physical contact, publicly humiliated Plaintiff, and made false sexual statements about Plaintiff to a livestream audience,' read the complaint, obtained by The Daily Mail.

Broner has denied any wrongdoing in the case.

Previously, in September of 2025, Broner was kicked off rapper Cam'ron's popular podcast after ignoring the host's warnings to stop flirting with his on-air co-host.

Sporting a greying beard and speaking in an increasingly raspy voice, Broner repeatedly interrupted the interview to make passes at Treasure 'Stat Baby' Wilson, who co-hosts It Is What It Is with Cam'ron and Ma$e.

Adrien Broner and Deen The great attend Sold Out Saturdays on August 15, 2026 in Atlanta

Adrien Broner punches Gavin Rees during their WBC Lightweight Title fight at Atlantic City Boardwalk Hall in 2013. Broner won the WBO Super Featherweight title at just 22 in 2011

At one point, Broner responded to a question about boxing's welterweight division by telling Wilson: 'Stat, I love you.'

Things ultimately boiled over during a discussion about Sunday's NFL action when Broner appeared to stop himself from making another comment about Wilson: 'I can't talk… You told me to stop.'

Cam'ron took the moment to end his interview with Broner.

'Hey, we going to have to ask you to go, my n*****,' Cam'ron said before pulling a stack of cash out of a small bag to give to his guest.

'I don't have no problems with you, but I'm gonna pay you for your time,' the rapper said, adding: 'You can't violate, bro.' Cam'ron went on to explain that Wilson's boyfriend was on set.

A native of Cincinnati who won the WBO Super Featherweight title at just 22 in 2011, Broner enjoyed a meteoric rise in the boxing world before his career was derailed by a series of arrests, upset defeats and mental health issues.

Sports.title: Ireland and Lions rugby star Tadhg Furlong faces lengthy ban after being accused of grabbing opponent's genitals
Sports.content:
Ireland and Lions rugby star Tadhg Furlong faces lengthy ban after being accused of grabbing opponent's genitals

Ireland and Lions star Tadhg Furlong faces the potential of a long ban after he was cited for allegedly grabbing the groin area of Munster’s Gavin Coombes.

Prop Furlong started his Leinster team’s 24-18 win over Irish derby rivals Munster at Dublin’s Aviva Stadium on Saturday night.

In the first half, Coombes told referee Andrew Brace of the incident.

But the television match official could not find any video evidence to back up his claim.

Initially, Furlong was not mentioned with the allegation made against an unnamed Leinster player.

Juste après le match Gavin Coombes s'est plaint d'un joueur du Leinster qui aurait attrapé l'aine du numéro 8 du Munster. Voici l'action en question. Sur ce ruck c'est Tadgh Furlong qui est l'auteur du geste. Il n'aurait pas dû être sur le terrain après cela...#LEIvMUN pic.twitter.com/pH8PlqyDeK — Ed Sarraf 📝 (@Edsarraf) October 25, 2026

Ireland and Lions star Tadhg Furlong (No 3) faces the potential of a long ban after he was cited for allegedly grabbing the groin area of Munster’s Gavin Coombes

Furlong, 33, was cited for an act of foul play and could miss a significant period of action

But on Monday, the 33-year-old was named in a statement by the United Rugby Championship (URC) which cited him for an act of foul play under the league’s rule which states ‘a player must not do anything that is against the spirit of good sportsmanship including but not limited to grabbing, twisting or squeezing the genitals.’

The URC said the disciplinary process arrangements will be made in due course.

Furlong, a three-time Lions tourist and one of Ireland’s most important players, would almost certainly miss his country’s home November Tests with Argentina, Fiji and South Africa and the finals weekend of the Nations Championship in London if found guilty.

Should Furlong end up missing Ireland's autumn matches, their head coach Andy Farrell would have to turn to Finlay Bealham as the man to start in the No 3 jersey. While Furlong's Test class is undisputed, Bealham is not only also an established Irish international, but a Lion to boot having been part of the successful 2025 summer tour to Australia.

Farrell's Ireland will go into the autumn as the highest-ranked northern hemisphere team in World Rugby's table in third place, with only New Zealand and leaders South Africa above them.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick left in limbo as vilified chiefs Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox meet for crisis summit at Carrington: Inside Man United's day of reckoning after humiliating Bournemouth defeat
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick is in limbo as Manchester United head coach following a day of crisis talks between the club’s owners and senior executives over his future at Old Trafford. Carrick remains under huge pressure after Sunday’s home defeat to Bournemouth left United one point above the Premier League relegation zone. Chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox were at the club’s Carrington training ground on Monday and are understood to have held conference calls with minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and co-chairmen Joel and Avram Glazer. It is unclear if United have reached a final decision over whether to sack Carrick or if he will take training on Tuesday morning when the players report back to Carrington to prepare for their next game at Chelsea on Saturday lunchtime. The squad had Monday off after losing 3-0 to Bournemouth, but Carrick turned up at the training ground to watch a behind-closed-doors game against Hull City while Berrada and Wilcox discussed his future in another part of the complex. It isn’t known if the 45-year-old spoke to them during the three hours he spent there. Carrick arrived at 1.50pm Monday, 10 minutes before the game involving a mixture of fringe players and youth-teamers kicked off. He watched it with his assistant Steve Holland and Under-18s boss Darren Fletcher before leaving the training ground shortly after Wilcox. Michael Carrick arrived at Carrington to watch the under-21s - with his bosses deciding his fate Carrick's future at Old Trafford is in jeopardy after Sunday's awful 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth To add to the intrigue, Bruno Fernandes was also at Carrington for treatment along with Benjamin Sesko, Patrick Dorgu and Manuel Ugarte, 24 hours after Carrick had dropped his captain for Sunday’s game and left him on the bench. Although Carrick insisted that his decision was purely for football reasons, it felt like he was punishing Fernandes for criticising United’s tactics in a television interview after the Champions League defeat to Como in Italy last week. The Portugal star seemed to respond with a veiled dig at Carrick on Sunday night when he liked a cryptic Instagram post that read: ‘Never push a loyal person to the point where they no longer care.’ Carrick’s job is hanging by a thread after losing half of his 12 games this season. United have made their worst start to a league campaign in 40 years, and have failed to win in eight games for the first time since 2015. Carrick was visibly emotional after the defeat to Bournemouth when the fans gave him a rousing show of support while directing their fury at the Glazers, Ratcliffe, Wilcox and the players. The former United midfielder appeared to say farewell to supporters afterwards, although he later insisted that was not the case. It followed a heartfelt five-minute monologue to reporters at the start of his pre-match press conference on Friday, two days after he approached the travelling fans in Como to apologise for a 4-1 defeat. After playing away in Spain and Italy over the last fortnight, United have a free week because they were knocked out of the Carabao Cup by Brighton and aren’t in action again until Saturday’s trip to Stamford Bridge. Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada met for crunch talks as Carrick spent time with the youth team Carrick has 18 months left on the two-year contract he signed in May after guiding the club back into the Champions League. If United decide to change head coach again, Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann – both currently out of work and able to take over immediately – are the leading candidates after bookmakers stopped taking bets on Carrick being sacked. Although Howe is available after leaving Newcastle in the summer, it’s understood that United would still owe his old club around £3million in compensation as well as having to pay off Carrick and his coaching staff.

Sports.title: Ballon d'Or plunged into CHAOS as esteemed event announces Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal ALL as winners on official website just hours before the ceremony
Sports.content:
Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal were all bizarrely listed as winners of the Ballon d'Or on the organisers' website hours before the ceremony began in London.

The trio have all been viewed among the leading candidates to land football's biggest individual prize for the first time.

Prior to the event at the London Palladium, the Ballon d'Or's official website appeared to mistakenly publish three separate articles announcing them individually as the winner.

Daily Mail Sport alerted the organisers to the mistake at 5.23pm and it triggered a series of frantic phone calls and WhatsApp messages.

Shocked organisers have since launched an investigation, with articles announcing Kane and Mbappe as winners subsequently being removed.

The article listing Yamal as the winner was still live on the website over 30 minutes after organisers were informed by Daily Mail Sport.

Ballon d'Or organisers published three articles announcing different winners of the Ballon d'Or, including England captain Harry Kane

Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe were also listed as winners on the website, with shocked organisers only becoming aware after being alerted by Daily Mail Sport

A Ballon d’Or statement read: 'Portraits of some Ballon d’Or nominees prepared by were inadvertently published online.

'These articles had been prepared in advance for all nominees in the event of a win.

'They DO NOT, in any way, reveal the podium, which remains unknown to everyone at this time.'

Kane's article featured the headline 'Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d’Or: Here are his best and most meaningful strikes from a 61-goal season.'

The article examined Kane's stunning year as he helped Bayern Munich win a domestic Treble, as well as reaching a century of goals for the German side in record time.

'A record-breaking welter of league and cup goals in 2025/26 has propelled Harry Kane to Ballon d’Or success. Here we identify his most iconic and greatest finishes in what has been a bountiful year,' the article stated.

Another announced Yamal as the Ballon d'Or winner, stating that the Barcelona and Spain star had set an 'unprecedented record' by becoming its youngest winner and labelling him as the 'new king of football'.

'In fact, at just 19 years of age, Lamine Yamal has just become the youngest winner in the history of the Ballon d'Or, which was established in 1956,' the article read.

'To truly appreciate the scale of his achievement, one need only recall that not even Lionel Messi – the record holder for the most trophies – had managed to win the Ballon d'Or at that age.

'The Argentine star won it for the first time in 2009, when he was 22 years and 160 days old.

'The all-time record for the youngest winner, until this magical evening in London, belonged to Ronaldo Nazário, who won the Ballon d'Or at the age of 21 years and 92 days.

All three articles were subsequently taken down, with Yamal's last to be removed from the website over 30 minutes after organisers were informed of the error

'Now, this historic record belongs to the new king of football and the brand-new winner of the most prestigious trophy on the planet.

'It belongs to Lamine Yamal Nasraoui Ebana.'

The third stated Mbappe as the winner, lauding him as 'consistency personified at the very highest level'.

'A record-breaking World Cup and another welter of goals for Los Blancos has brought Kylian Mbappe his first Ballon d'Or triumph,' the article read.

'Here we celebrate the French star's consistency, not just last season, but every season since first emerging as a true phenomenon.'

The error took place ahead of official coverage of the ceremony, which will be headlined by the winner of the Ballon d'Or.

England captain Kane is bidding to become the first English player to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001.

Yamal and Mbappe are also hoping to claim the gong for the first time, with the pair having had best finishes of second and third respectively.

Sports.title: Man Utd's 7 biggest social media tantrums as Bruno Fernandes joins Sancho and Garnacho
Sports.content:
Man Utd's 7 biggest social media tantrums as Bruno Fernandes joins Sancho and Garnacho

Bruno Fernandes has taken out his Manchester United frustrations on social media, but he's far from the first player to do so

View 8 Images Bruno Fernandes appears to have taken a sly jab at Manchester United on social media (Image: Getty)

Bruno Fernandes seems to have vented his frustration on social media after being dropped for Manchester United's 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth. Yet the club concerningly has a rich recent history of their stars spitting dummies out online.

‌



‌



United are in a rut. Under Michael Carrick, their season has started abysmally and they have just one Premier League win to their name. They're out of the Carabao Cup after losing to Brighton and their most recent European venture saw them battered 4-1 by Como.

‌



On Sunday, they needed to show some spine against the Cherries but lost 3-0 in the latest damning result of the season. But skipper Fernandes played no part. He had spoken out against his boss in the week and was dropped to the Old Trafford bench - though Carrick insisted this was purely a sporting decision.

‌



United perhaps could have used their Portuguese talisman as they were humiliated by Marco Rose's side, but Fernandes was an unused substitute. In the wake of the loss, his social media activity - liking a specific post - is being treated as him passive-aggressively throwing his toys out of the pram.

Jamie Carragher picks who must replace Michael Carrick as next Man Utd manager READ MORE :

Bruno Fernandes hints he DOESN'T CARE about Man Utd after Michael Carrick snub READ MORE :

But the 32-year-old father of two is not the first United star to use social media as a vessel for public agitation and he won't be the last. Mirror Football takes a look at seven times United players and those associated with them have thrown online tantrums in recent years.

Bruno Fernandes (2026)

To be specific, the benched captain's official Instagram account liked a reel that has the caption: "Never push a loyal person to the point where they no longer care." This occurred not long after Sunday's loss.

‌



View 8 Images Fernandes liked the reel (Image: Instagram)

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



In the reel, a Sisyphus-esque rock monster is depicted protecting a city from a giant boulder. The citizens then turn on him, at which point he lets the boulder he was holding back destroy the city in its entirety.

Fernandes might just be a fan of the animation, or maybe the reel's backing tune, Macarena. However, it's still likely that this cryptic bit of online activity represents how he's feeling at this current stage.

‌



Kobbie Mainoo's brother (2025)

Just last year, some more social media rumblings caused a stir at United - though this time it wasn't a player directly creating them. Under Ruben Amorim, the promising Kobbie Mainoo had had his minutes cut down dramatically.

Amorim made it clear he wasn't part of his plans, despite having shown potential in United's midfield and for England at Euro 2024. Fans disagreed, but the Portuguese coach stood firm. Mainoo requested a loan move away last summer, but this never materialised. He must have been frustrated, though it was not he who took action. It was his half-brother, Jordan Mainoo-Hames.

‌



View 8 Images Mainoo's half-brother Jordan uploaded the pictures online (Image: Instagram/@jxrdan)

During a match against none other than Bournemouth in December 2025, Mainoo's brother was snapped in the Old Trafford stands wearing a plain black t-shirt with "FREE KOBBIE MAINOO" on it in large, white writing. He immediately uploaded these pictures to his Instagram account and both he and Mainoo came under scrutiny.

‌



Amorim responded quite diplomatically, saying: "It was not Kobbie that wore the t-shirt. He is not going to start because of the t-shirt or go to the bench because of it. He is going to play if he is the right player to play." Eventually, Amorim was given the boot and Mainoo returned to first-team contention.

Alejandro Garnacho (2024)

Like Fernandes, ex-United star Alejandro Garnacho found himself in hot water after liking specific posts with his official account. In April 2024, the Argentine was hauled off at half-time during a match away at… Bournemouth. Who knew the Cherries could cause such head loss?

‌



View 8 Images Ten Hag clashed with Garnacho (Image: Getty)

The game ended 2-2 and Garnacho was visibly annoyed with manager Erik ten Hag for taking him off. So much so that on X, his account liked two posts by fan content creator Mark Goldbridge.

‌



One post read: "Ten Hag subtly blaming Garnacho in the post-match press conference... Not a good look throwing a 19-year-old under the bus who has actually delivered for you this season." The other branded the substitution as "a joke."

Garnacho later unliked these posts and Ten Hag confirmed that he had apologised. He was eventually frozen out under Amorim before being sold to Chelsea in August 2025 for £40million. He is currently on loan at Aston Villa.

‌



Jadon Sancho (2023)

Perhaps the most infamous and damaging outburst on this list came from Jadon Sancho. In September 2023, the winger, who had cost United £73m just two years earlier, was completely excluded from Ten Hag's squad that travelled to Arsenal for a 3-1 defeat.

The player was not injured and Ten Hag stated that he was not selected because of his performance in training. This angered the Englishman, who took to X and damningly stated: "Please don't believe everything you read!

‌



View 8 Images Sancho claimed he was being used as a scapegoat (Image: Getty)

"I will not allow people saying things that was entirely untrue. I have conducted myself in training very well this week... I have been a scapegoat for a long time which isn't fair!"

‌



Sancho pinned this post to the top of his profile for a week before deleting it. He refused Ten Hag's demand to make an internal and public apology, was banned from using the club's facilities and shipped out on loan to Borussia Dortmund four months later.

The two did draw a line under the feud when he returned, but the truce was short-lived: Sancho was loaned out to Chelsea then Villa before his United contract expired this summer. He is still without a club at 26.

‌



Jesse Lingard and his brother (2022)

Both Jesse Lingard and his brother Louie Scott had a pop in 2022. That January, the attacker had sought a move to Newcastle after falling out of favour with interim boss Ralf Rangnick. However, the move was blocked and in a press conference, Rangnick said Lingard was absent from an FA Cup tie against Middlesbrough because he'd asked for days off to "clear his mind."

View 8 Images Lingard's brother did not think he was given a proper farewell (Image: Getty)

‌



The player immediately contradicted this by posting on Twitter (now X): "The club advised me to have time off due to personal reasons! But my headspace is clear and I'll always be professional when called upon and give 100 per cent."

An acrimonious departure soon followed the February 2022 public spat, as Lingard's contract expired. United beat Brentford 3-0 in the final home game of the season and whilst Juan Mata, Nemanja Matic and Edinson Cavani all made farewell appearances, Lingard did not.

‌



He was an unused substitute and left months later for Nottingham Forest. Lingard's brother did not take kindly to this and posted on his Instagram story: "20 years of blood sweat and tears, four domestic trophies, three cup final goals, not even a farewell. No wonder it's Conference League next year."

Anthony Martial (2022)

Rangnick seemingly attracted online controversy in 2022 and Lingard and his brother were not the only ones who felt aggrieved - so did Anthony Martial. In January, Rangnick named his team to face Aston Villa and Martial was nowhere to be seen.

‌



View 8 Images Martial vented online (Image: Getty)

Asked why, the manager stated: "He didn't want to be in the squad. He would have been in the squad normally, but he didn't want to and that was the reason why he didn't travel with us yesterday."

‌



Martial, like Lingard, then directly batted this back online, stating on his Instagram story: "I will never refuse to play a match for Man United. I've been here for seven years and I never disrespected and will never disrespect the club and the fans."

Rangnick quickly chalked this interaction down to miscommunication and he wasn't kept on after a short spell as interim boss. Martial left the club in 2024 and is currently a free agent after spells at AEK Athens and Monterrey.

‌



Sergio Romero's wife (2020)

Two years before Rangnick's discord, the wife of goalkeeper Sergio Romero made her feelings crystal clear on social media. The Argentine shot-stopper was third-choice at United in the summer of 2020 and sought an exit.

View 8 Images Romero's partner was not best pleased (Image: John Peters)

Article continues below

Everton reportedly launched a deadline-day loan bid, but United refused the deal. Romero's wife, Eliana Guercio, was furious and she tore into the club on Instagram. The goalkeeper was effectively frozen out for the entire season until his contract expired in the summer of 2021. He then headed to Italian side Venezia.

His wife posted: "Sergio Romero worked hard for his club. Last trophy they won, they lifted it with him. He helped the team reach four finals/semi-finals and then he was left on the bench only to lose them all. It is time for them to return the opportunity and let him go. RESPECT FOR ONCE!"

Arsenal news: Julian Alvarez January transfer decision and offer for target confirmed

Arsenal are busy preparing for a trip to League Two side Fleetwood Town in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup

View 3 Images Julian Alvarez has two goals in his last two games (Image: Getty Images)

Arsenal are aiming for another unbeaten week in all competitions, starting with the Carabao Cup. The Gunners have two away trips, firstly to Highbury Stadium where Fleetwood Town await in the fourth round, before heading to Anfield to face Liverpool in the Premier League.

‌



‌



Mikel Arteta is ready for the challenges ahead and is pleased with his team's results for the most part. Speaking after the Everton win on Saturday, the Spaniard explained: "We just have to focus on what we can do, and we’re very pleased with 90% of the performances and results - apart from the Brighton game, I would say."

Fleetwood face the mammoth task of hosting the reigning Premier League champions. While there are 66 league places between the two clubs, Arteta will not take this Carabao Cup clash lightly.

‌



Here, Mirror Football has the latest coming out of the red side of north London.

Unseen footage sparks Arsenal Declan Rice injury concern after Everton win READ MORE :

Ju lian Alvarez transfer decision

Atletico Madrid have reportedlt insisted they will not allow Julian Alvarez to leave in January, ending Arsenal's hopes of signing the Argentinian striker this season. TEAMtalk reports that the Gunners had kept in contact with Alvarez's agents in the hopes that he would be open to a move to England in the next transfer window.

The forward had major desires to move to Barcelona but Atleti were strict on their decision to block this transfer in its entirety. Arsenal had kept a close eye on the move and were set to be the frontrunners for his signature in January.

View 3 Images Atletico are not planning on selling Julian Alvarez in January (Image: Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

However, new reports have emerged that Alvarez will not be permitted to exit Madrid during the current season. It also looks like the striker has gone back on his public desire to leave after apologising to fans following their win over RC Deportivo.

Alvarez scored the winning goal and told Movistar Plus that he regrets speaking out about potential transfers. He said: "I'd like to apologise to our fans for what I said at the World Cup; it was a mistake in terms of how I said it and the timing. I understand why the fans are angry. If I were a fan, I'd be angry too. Especially given how they've supported me since I arrived."

Offer for target confirmed

Arsenal have submitted an offer for teenage sensation Gilberto Mora ahead of the January transfer window in a bid to get ahead of their Premier League rivals, it's been claimed. Suarez believes Mora needs a move to Europe to boost his career after an exciting campaign at the World Cup for Mexico. He said: "The truth is that Gil Mora’s situation is unique - the kind that comes along once in a very long while.

"He’s extraordinary, both because of his age and the entire development path he’s been on since Juan Carlos Osorio gave him his debut. If it were up to me, I’d let him go.

‌



"He needs to head to Europe to start gaining that kind of experience. It wouldn’t be the end of the world if things didn’t go well -though I personally believe he’ll do very well. It’s just a matter of finding the right club - somewhere he can adapt quickly and where he’ll be well supported."

The 18-year-old has 18 goal contributions in 63 appearances for Tijuana and is also off the mark for his country. He appeared in four of Mexico's five World Cup games this summer and also helped them win the Gold Cup against the United States last year.

Sports.content:
The 2026 Ballon d'Or ceremony takes place in London on Monday evening, with Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal the frontrunners for the men's award

England captain Harry Kane has been crowned the world’s best footballer at the 2026 Ballon d’Or awards.

The eyes of the footballing world descended on the West End tonight as the London Palladium hosted the prestigious ceremony.

And Three Lions and Bayern Munich striker Kane won the top award, becoming the first English player since Michael Owen in 2001 to do so.

Former Tottenham forward Kane said: “I am almost speechless. Being here in London has made it extra special.

“Made it a good omen for me tonight. Thank you to everyone who voted for me. I can imagine it was tough this year.”

Kane spearheaded Bayern's Bundesliga title and England's run to the World Cup semi-final in North America, and beat off competition from the likes of France forward Kylian Mbappe and Spain youngster Lamine Yamal to win the award.

London City Lionesses and Spain star Alexia Putellas, meanwhile, won the women's prize.

Michael Carrick says he 'takes responsibility' as position hangs in balance

Michael Carrick's future at Manchester United is hanging by a thread after the Reds suffered a humiliating 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth on Sunday.

Carrick, 45, had come into the game against the Cherries under huge pressure following a dismal start to the season, with the Reds winning just TWO in 11 fixtures across all competitions.

Mikel Arteta fires Arsenal stars Fleetwood warning and makes Viktor Gyokeres admission

FLEETWOOD TOWN vs ARSENAL: Mikel Arteta's side head to Highbury Stadium looking to book their place in the fifth round of the Carabao Cup on Tuesday evening

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta's Arsenal are bidding to avoid a Carabao Cup upset vs Fleetwood Town

Mikel Arteta has ordered his Arsenal stars to "respect" Fleetwood Town - or risk being embarrassed in an almighty Carabao Cup giant-killing.

‌



‌



With strong winds and awkward playing conditions anticipated in the North West, Highbury Stadium - against the Premier League champions of all teams - would be a rather fitting place to stage an unlikely upset.

‌



Arteta, who was an unused substitute when the Gunners were eliminated 3-2 on penalties in the quarter-finals by Bradford City back in December 2012, wants his players to handle business professionally.

‌



When asked how his team approach the potential banana skin, he replied: "Show them the Arsenal shirt and what we represent and that's it. We need to go there and win the game. That's it. It's very simple.
