Sports.title: Christian Mbilli Tests What Canelo Alvarez Has Left
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez faces Christian Mbilli in Riyadh with sharp questions hanging over what remains in the Mexican superstar’s tank. Veteran boxing insider Dan Rafael views Alvarez’s mileage, ring age, and recent outings as unmistakable signs that the veteran is drifting further from his peak.

Rafael argues that a prime Canelo would have systematically broken Mbilli down. Heading into Saturday, however, Mbilli brings youth, stamina, and relentless pressure, making the outcome far harder to forecast.

“A lot younger. He’s fresher. I mean, it’s a crapshoot at this stage of Canelo’s career,” Rafael said on About Boxing. “This is the type of guy that in his best days he would completely pick apart and probably just do damage to for 12 rounds or maybe stop him. But the reality is Canelo hasn’t had a stoppage in a long time.”

Rafael pointed to Canelo’s defeat against Terence Crawford alongside his decisions over Jaime Munguia and Edgar Berlanga as clear proof of decline. Alvarez turned pro at 15, and more than two decades in the ring have built up heavy wear and tear.

Canelo hasn’t stopped an opponent since halting Caleb Plant in 2021. While he has managed to keep winning most nights, the emphatic dominance that fueled his run to the top of the sport has largely vanished.

When a fighter has one flat performance, people call it an off night. When it stretches across four straight outings as we’ve seen with Canelo in his last four fights, it is an unmistakable pattern. The public senses it, which explains why the energy around this Riyadh card feels muted.

Mbilli’s relentless work rate presents a serious operational hurdle. Canelo can still punish mistakes off the back foot, and Mbilli’s aggression will present openings. Yet it remains uncertain whether Alvarez can match that output and maintain his gas tank across 36 minutes against a hungry titleholder.

Surviving Mbilli is step one. An emphatic showing keeps Canelo primed for another lucrative main event. Turki Alalshikh could look toward Hamzah Sheeraz next, a fight Alvarez could handle comfortably. It seems doubtful anyone will push him into the ring with a destructive puncher like Osleys Iglesias anytime soon.

A disputed decision on the cards might protect Canelo’s status contractually, but it would hammer his standing with fans. If observers feel Mbilli got robbed, friendly judges will not quiet Rafael’s warnings about the veteran’s fading reflexes.

Mbilli also carries pressure into the ring, looking to rebound after battling Lester Martinez to a draw on the Canelo Crawford undercard. Both enter this meeting off identical layoffs.

Rafael declined to pick the outright upset. Still, he expects Saturday to deliver a clear verdict: Canelo either proves he still belongs at elite championship caliber, or the final bell on his career draws noticeably closer.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury’s 10-Fight Plan Could Lead to More Losses
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury already has his eyes on the future, tossing out the idea of signing another 10-fight contract once his current deal wraps up. That talk might hit a brick wall fast if Anthony Joshua takes care of business on December 11 in Cardiff.

A rough beating at Principality Stadium would leave the 38-year-old stuck in no-man’s-land, stuck weighing genuine ring threats against matchups nobody wants to pay to see.

Walking away does not seem to be anywhere on Fury’s radar. He has walked away and come back enough times that even a lopsided loss might not force his exit.

“I’m going to continue,” Fury told WSVN Miami, brushing off exit talk. He mentioned having two bouts left on his current deal before adding, “I’ll finish the contract off and then probably sign another 10-fight deal. Who knows?”

The Gypsy King tossed in a reality check, noting the cash must make sense and the schedule needs to move fast given his age.

That is a wild roadmap for someone who has logged 39 pro outings, survived a brutal three-bout war with Deontay Wilder, and dropped consecutive decisions to Oleksandr Usyk. He grabbed comeback wins over Arslanbek Makhmudov and Mariusz Wach earlier this year, but Joshua delivers power on a whole different level.

A bad knockout loss would trigger alarms that go way past whether he can hang with top-tier champions. Depending on the damage taken, even a hungry fringe contender who brings steady heat, works the body, and presses the action could become an unnecessary hazard.

Fury spent his prime dominating with slick movement, massive reach, and smothering upper-body weight. Those attributes fade in a hurry when reaction times dip against fresh heavyweights. Joshua owns the raw dynamite to reveal exactly how much punch resistance Fury has left when shots start landing clean inside.

The Fury brand will always sell tickets at home. British fans backed him through long layoffs, fake retirement posts, and the Usyk defeats. A tune-up bout against an easy touch would pull numbers in the short term.

Selling a full ten-round tour against soft touches is an entirely different hustle. The Wach bout worked as a quick warm-up. Stacking up multiple dates against fading veterans or clear underdogs will simply drain fan interest.

Promoters will cut checks as long as Fury wants to put gloves on. The real headache will be finding guys he can handle without boring the crowd to tears.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Shamelessly Pushes for Fighter of the Year Over O’Shaquie Foster
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia is continuing his campaign for Fighter of the Year, staying on the attack since last Sunday by taking aim at O’Shaquie Foster’s resume and dismissing his win over Raymond Ford. Foster quickly fired back, asking if Garcia stopping Conor Benn actually tops beating a proven former world champion.

While Garcia praised Foster for handling Emanuel Navarrete on Saturday, he brushed Ford aside as “not a standout fighter.” That remark directly targets half of Foster’s case for the award.

Foster went to X to set the record straight, insisting Ford possesses far more championship pedigree than Benn:

“Ford was a ex world champion, what was Benn other than a big name? Skill for skill he not f***in wit Ray being honest!!! Neither one of your wins compare to mines dude!!”

Ryan made his intentions unmistakable on Sunday, October 25, kicking off a brazen social media campaign for 2026 Fighter of the Year. Responding to talk surrounding O’Shaquie, Garcia flatly declared, “You lost your mind – I’m the fighter of the year,” before posting self-congratulatory notes boasting about wanting to screenshot the faces of critics once the award is handed out.

The sudden push came just twenty-four hours after Foster dominated Emanuel Navarrete. Ryan clearly saw the public momentum swinging toward Foster and decided to counter it by flooding the timeline.

When you place the resumes side by side, it is not particularly close. Foster earned a tough majority decision against Ford in May, then produced a clinic on October 24 against Navarrete. He sent the three-division champion to the canvas twice in round twelve, unifying three major belts at super featherweight.

Garcia picked up the WBC welterweight strap against Mario Barrios before blowing through Benn. Those victories carry weight, yet Foster holds the upper hand on opponent quality, championship hardware, and divisional supremacy. Garcia never referenced Fighter of the Year directly in his latest post, but picking apart the Ford win serves his self-promotion perfectly. Downplaying Foster’s first victory helps clear an easier path to the trophy.

Ryan knows exactly what he is doing by trying to erase the Ford win. If he can convince the casual audience that Foster only had one real fight this year, his own two-fight run looks respectable by comparison. It is shameless PR, but in modern boxing, guys with twenty million followers are used to controlling the narrative regardless of what actually happened in the ring.

Sports.title: Brian Norman Jr. Risks Another Setback Against Abel Ramos
Sports.content:
Brian Norman Jr. could face a dangerous test against Abel Ramos on the December 19 Devin Haney–Liam Paro card, with a loss threatening to undo his progress since surrendering the WBO welterweight title to Haney last November.

Boxing journalist Dan Rafael reports that Top Rank is planning Norman vs. Ramos for the card, which is expected to take place in San Francisco. The bout would be the 25-year-old Norman’s second fight since his defeat to Haney.

Rafael reports that Top Rank also plans to feature welterweights Tiger Johnson and Rohan Polanco. But Norman has the most to lose if the Ramos fight comes together: he’s a former champion trying to regain ground, and his proposed opponent has already shown this year that he can upset a younger fighter’s plans.

Ramos (29-6-3, 22 KOs) is 35 and has six losses on his record, but those numbers don’t tell the whole story. In February, he rallied to defeat previously unbeaten Tahmir Smalls by split decision. Smalls was supposed to be the rising fighter. Ramos turned the fight into a long night and left him with his first loss.

Norman is a more established fighter than Smalls, having already held a world title, but that doesn’t make Ramos a safe opponent. The veteran can pressure, take punishment, and keep working when a younger fighter expects him to fade.

For Norman, the danger is getting drawn into a fight at close range and spending too much time looking for one big punch. He has the power to hurt Ramos, but he’ll need to put his shots together and keep the veteran from setting the pace. If he lets rounds slip away while waiting for a knockout, Ramos could make the scorecards uncomfortable.

The setting would add another layer. Norman lost his WBO title to Haney by decision in Riyadh last November, and now he could return on the undercard while Haney fights Paro in a reported title unification.

That gives Norman a chance to put on a strong performance in front of an audience watching the man who beat him. It also gives him a direct comparison with his former opponent: Haney will be fighting for two belts while Norman takes on a hard veteran to keep his own title hopes moving.

A victory over Ramos would help Norman make his case for another major fight. A loss would be far more damaging, raising questions about where he fits among the leading welterweights after the Haney defeat.

Norman–Ramos remains a planned matchup, according to Rafael, rather than an officially announced fight. If it happens, Norman will have to get past an opponent who has already ruined one prospect’s unbeaten record this year.

Sports.title: Frazer Clarke Agrees To Joseph Parker Fight On Fury vs Joshua Undercard
Sports.content:
Joseph Parker could make his ring return against Frazer Clarke on the Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua undercard on December 11 in Cardiff, risking his remaining standing among the heavyweight elite after a lengthy layoff.

Clarke confirmed he agreed to the matchup, though communication has quieted recently and organizers have not officially announced the bout.

Parker has remained inactive since Fabio Wardley stopped him in October 2025. Facing Clarke provides immediate visibility on a massive stage, yet it offers zero margin to shed ring rust.

That defeat to Wardley halted an impressive career resurgence. Parker had forced his way back into title contention through disciplined, mobile performances against Deontay Wilder and Zhilei Zhang, frustrating both power punchers over the distance.

Those past achievements offer little protection here. Clarke possesses the size to impose himself physically, alongside an extensive amateur foundation to punish any hesitation if Parker starts slowly.

The central uncertainty centers on Parker’s sharpness. His previous run required sustained concentration across twelve grueling rounds. Following a stoppage defeat and over a year outside the ropes, replicating that form against an ambitious opponent represents a serious hurdle.

Their history stretches back to 2010, when Parker defeated Clarke in the amateur ranks in India. Clarke aims to avenge that loss, calling Parker a huge name and a great fighter in an interview with The Sun.

Clarke recently snapped a two-fight skid with an August stoppage of Lamah Griggs. Upsetting Parker would instantly elevate his profile and secure invitations to major events.

Parker’s time away also involved outside complications, including a backdated three-month suspension following a failed test for a cocaine metabolite. UK Anti-Doping subsequently cleared him for competition.

Fighting in Cardiff delivers the ultimate platform for Parker to re-establish momentum. That spotlight carries severe consequences, because a sluggish showing or another defeat under the eyes of the boxing world could permanently close the door on future world championship opportunities.

Sports.title: Vasily Lomachenko Targets Charly Suarez for Ring Return at 130.
Sports.content:
Vasiliy Lomachenko is eyeing Charly Suarez for his return at super featherweight, yet defeating the Filipino contender will not settle the core mystery surrounding his comeback: How much elite ability remains after a prolonged absence at age 38?

Suarez is under consideration for his ring return. Lomachenko intends to test his reflexes under real fire prior to chasing premier targets.

“My next step, it will be a fight with a guy, maybe with a guy from the Philippines, Suarez,” Lomachenko said to Fight Hub TV. “It will be my first fight after rest, and after that, we’ll see how I feel.”

Lomachenko has remained inactive since halting George Kambosos Jr. in May 2024. He has not stepped inside the ropes at 130 pounds since 2017, introducing another variable after more than two years on the shelf.

Sharing the ring with Suarez guarantees rounds against an established contender, though any verdict requires scrutiny. Suarez is also 38 years old. Outpointing him offers limited insight into how Lomachenko handles younger, sharper champions across a full championship distance.

Lomachenko built his legendary status on dazzling footwork, spatial control, and split-second precision. He famously pivoted into blind spots, unloading clean punches before opponents could reset. If his reflexes have eroded or his legs can no longer maintain that tempo, fighters who once swung at air might suddenly connect with ease.

Taking on someone like O’Shaquie Foster represents a far steeper hazard. Foster’s slick mobility and sharp counterpunches would force Lomachenko to spend considerable energy establishing range. Looking sharp against Suarez is positive, yet it does not guarantee Lomachenko can cut the ring on Foster or match his pace over 36 minutes.

Lomachenko clearly recognizes the reality in front of him. When questioned regarding matchups with Gervonta Davis or Naoya Inoue, he urged the interviewer to pump the brakes.

“I want to do slowly, slowly, slowly,” Lomachenko noted. “I need to check my body in the real fight.”

Hitting 130 pounds again presents its own physical hurdle. After spending several years up at lightweight, dropping back to a weight class he exited almost ten years ago takes a heavier toll on an older fighter. How comfortably he makes the scale could tell us just as much as his performance under the lights.

The veteran southpaw admitted the ticking clock motivated him to lace up the gloves again instead of letting time slip away.

“One day I wake up and thinking, hey, now I’m 38 years old, and we need to try one more time,” Lomachenko said. “If it will be after two more or three years, then I will be 40, 41 years old. It will be too late.”

His team is scheduled to sit down with Bob Arum to map out the business side of the ring return. Neither a date nor an opponent has been made official.

Suarez offers a workable starting point, though Lomachenko must deliver more than just a victory to prove he still belongs among the division elite. Hand speed, foot mobility, and gas tank over the championship stretch will tell the real story.

Sports.title: Devin Haney Faces Liam Paro In San Francisco
Sports.content:
Devin Haney’s new DAZN deal is getting a favorable launch: a welterweight unification against Liam Paro in San Francisco, with the Australian traveling to Haney’s home region for the opening fight of that agreement.

Mike Coppinger of The Ring reports that the WBO and IBF titleholders will meet December 19 at Chase Center. The fight has yet to receive an official announcement.

It is a legitimate unification. It also puts Haney in the more comfortable position before either man throws a punch. DAZN gets to introduce its newly signed fighter to a Bay Area audience, while Paro arrives with a belt that could make that investment look better by the end of the night.

Paro’s job is to wreck the launch.

He has done something similar before. In June 2024, he traveled to Puerto Rico and beat Subriel Matias by unanimous decision for the IBF light welterweight title. The champion’s reputation and home support failed to intimidate him.

But using that victory as proof he can beat Haney would overlook the harder comparison. Matias came forward and gave Paro opportunities to land while moving. Haney can force him to become the pursuer, making the Australian create openings rather than wait for an opponent to supply them.

That is where this fight could become frustrating for Paro. Following Haney around the perimeter would allow the American to jab, move and make relatively quiet rounds look like his rounds.

Paro needs to attack the body when Haney moves, work when they get close and avoid letting every clinch become a break from the pressure. He cannot afford to spend the first half studying a target that keeps leaving.

Haney has an obligation here, too. A new broadcast deal and two belts will generate promotion, but they cannot substitute for a performance that makes people want his next fight.

Winning narrowly while limiting the action would collect another title. Taking command against a fellow champion would give DAZN something stronger to sell.

The homecoming is arranged around Haney. Whether the night belongs to him depends on how much fighting Paro forces him to do.

Sports.title: Alberto Puello Rematch Is The Only Move That Makes Sense For Dalton Smith
Sports.content:
Dalton Smith kept his WBC light welterweight strap in Sheffield, but his reputation took a beating against Alberto Puello.

Eddie Hearn is already talking up a stadium blockbuster against Shakur Stevenson. That talk conveniently skips past the reality left inside the ring: Smith did not convince viewers he solved the man in front of him.

Domestic rival Adam Azim quickly called out the verdict, backing fans who saw the split decision as generous. Two judges handed Smith 115-113 cards, while the third had Puello cruising 116-112.

“Puello won by one round, in my opinion,” Azim told RS Boxing TV, pointing directly to Smith’s lack of urgency.

The deeper issue was how Smith faded down the stretch. Once Puello timed him, Smith went into a shell. His output cratered because every attack opened him up to clean counters.

Instead of building on early rounds, Smith spent the championship rounds fighting in a safety-first manner. He was getting outboxed right when a champion needs to close the show.

Normally, that kind of performance demands an immediate rematch. Matchroom is instead trying to fast-track Smith straight into a massive event with Shakur. The commercial angle makes sense while Smith still holds the belt, but a stadium fight cannot answer the tactical problems Puello exposed.

If Puello made Smith freeze, Shakur’s precision and defensive discipline would make every mistake punishing. Saturday showed zero evidence Smith is ready for that jump. Winning a controversial decision was not the performance Smith needed for Hearn to campaign for a fight with Shakur.

A rematch with Puello is the fight that makes sense. It offers Smith a chance to adjust, keep his work rate up, and earn an undisputed result.

Hearn can sell the official victory, but the ring tells the truth. The belt stayed in Sheffield, while the performance wrecked the case for throwing Smith in with Shakur.

Ghana News.title: Ghana faces possible US$50 million default judgment at ECOWAS Court over alleged human rights violations
Ghana News.content:
Toh You Kang, Ashie Moore, and Attorney General Dominic Akuritinga Ayine

By Isaac Yeboah

The Republic of Ghana faces a possible default judgment at the ECOWAS Community Court of Justice in Abuja, Nigeria, following its alleged failure to file a defence in a US$50 million human rights lawsuit brought by Singaporean businessman and investor, Toh You Kang.

The businessman, through his lawyer, Cephas Boyuo, Esq., is seeking the cedi equivalent of US$50 million in compensatory damages over alleged violations of his fundamental human rights, including unlawful arrest and detention, denial of fair hearing, infringement of his freedom of movement, and failure by state institutions to protect his rights.

The case arises from a series of events involving Mr You Kang, Emmanuel Nii Ashie Moore, the Greater Accra Regional Chairman of the ruling National Democratic Congress (NDC), and certain officers of the Ghana Police Service.

According to the originating application filed before the ECOWAS Court, Mr You Kang travelled to Ghana in May 2025 to resolve outstanding business and financial matters arising from transactions involving Mr Moore.

Alleged business transactions and financial dispute

Court documents indicate that Mr You Kang, an investor and shareholder of Ghanaian-registered NSG Innovation Limited, was introduced to Mr Moore, who allegedly presented himself as a politically connected businessman with the capacity to facilitate government-related business opportunities in Ghana.

The applicant alleges that, relying on these representations, he transferred US$100,000 and subsequently provided an additional US$700,000 in connection with purported contracts for the supply of electrical cables to the Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG).

He further claims to have supplied approximately US$1.5 million worth of campaign paraphernalia for the 2024 general elections.

According to the application, disagreements subsequently arose over the transactions, prompting Mr You Kang to travel to Ghana in May 2025 to seek a resolution.

However, what was intended to be a business engagement allegedly took a dramatic turn when he was taken to a private residence, where armed men led by Mr. Emmanuel Ashie Moore allegedly demanded US$3 million from him.

Mr You Kang alleges that when he refused, he was assaulted before being handed over to the Ghana Police Service, which subsequently arrested and prosecuted him on a charge of defrauding by false pretences.

High Court quashes criminal proceedings

The applicant contends that the criminal proceedings instituted against him were unlawful because the alleged transactions forming the basis of the charges allegedly occurred outside Ghana.

He maintains that the Dansoman Circuit Court lacked jurisdiction to entertain the matter.

Following his arraignment on May 30, 2025, the Circuit Court remanded him into custody. He subsequently obtained bail from the High Court but remained subject to restrictions on his movement.

On September 4, 2025, the High Court granted an application for certiorari, quashing the proceedings before the Circuit Court and prohibiting that court from continuing with the criminal case.

The High Court also made consequential orders concerning personal belongings allegedly retained following his arrest.

Mr You Kang argues that the circumstances surrounding his arrest, detention and prosecution constituted violations of his rights guaranteed under international human rights instruments.

Allegations against Police and Immigration authorities

Beyond the criminal proceedings, Mr You Kang accuses certain officers of the Ghana Police Service of failing to act on complaints he lodged against Mr Moore concerning alleged assault, threats and the retention of his personal property.

His application references a report by the Police Professional and Standards Bureau (PPSB), which he contends supports aspects of his allegations concerning the conduct of police officers involved in the matter.

He further alleges irregularities in the handling of his travel documents upon his arrival at Kotoka International Airport.

According to the court documents, his passport was taken by Mr. Ashie Moore without he going through arrival formalities by the Immigration Service of Ghana, and it was subsequently discovered that the document did not bear the required Ghanaian entry stamp.

The applicant says correspondence from the Ghana Immigration Service acknowledged the irregularity and sought to rectify it at a time he had already undergone the bad treatment of alleged unlawful detention in Ghana.

Mr You Kang eventually departed Ghana for Singapore on September 12, 2025.

Ghana allegedly fails to defend US$50 million suit

Mr You Kang, acting through his lawyer, Cephas Boyuo, Esq., has filed an application requesting the ECOWAS Community Court of Justice to enter judgment by default against the Republic of Ghana.

The application, filed in December 2025, is grounded on Ghana’s alleged failure to respond to the substantive human rights action despite having been duly served.

According to an affidavit supporting the application, the originating processes were electronically served on November 13, 2025, on the Attorney-General, Deputy Attorney-General, Solicitor-General and other authorised legal officers of the Republic.

The applicant maintains that Ghana failed to file a defence within the period prescribed by the Rules of the ECOWAS Court.

Lawyer Cephas Boyuo relies on Article 35 of the Court’s Rules of Procedure, which provides for the filing of a defence within 30 days of service.

He also invokes Article 90(1), which permits an applicant to seek judgment by default where a respondent, having been duly served, fails to lodge a defence within the prescribed period.

The application accordingly invites the Court to enter judgment against Ghana and grant the substantive reliefs sought by Mr You Kang.

These include declarations that Ghana violated his fundamental human rights and an order directing the Republic to pay the cedi equivalent of US$50 million in compensatory damages, together with legal costs and fees.

Press of ECOWAS Court for hearing date

Meanwhile, Mr You Kang’s lawyer, Cephas Boyuo has formally written to the Registry of the ECOWAS Community Court of Justice requesting that a hearing date be fixed for the pending application for judgment by default.

In a letter dated April 13, 2026, counsel drew the Court’s attention to an earlier communication from the Registry dated March 6, 2026, indicating that arrangements were being made for the issuance of a hearing notice.

The lawyer expressed concern that approximately one month had elapsed without the issuance of the hearing notice or communication of a hearing date.

He consequently urged the Registry to expedite the necessary administrative processes to enable the application to be heard without further delay.

Responding in a letter dated April 14, 2026, the Chief Registrar of the ECOWAS Community Court of Justice, Yaouza Ouro-Sama, acknowledged receipt of counsel’s correspondence.

The Chief Registrar explained that the matter was awaiting a directive from the judges and assured counsel that the process was being monitored.

He further indicated that the hearing notice would be communicated to the parties once issued.

US$50 million claim awaits judicial determination

The legal action raises questions concerning Ghana’s obligations under regional and international human rights instruments, particularly regarding the protection of foreign nationals from arbitrary arrest, unlawful detention and alleged abuses by state officials.

Mr You Kang maintains that the actions and omissions of Ghanaian state institutions caused him substantial financial losses, reputational damage, emotional distress and interference with his personal liberty and business interests.

Through his lawyer, he is asking the ECOWAS Court to hold the Republic of Ghana accountable for the alleged violations and award the compensation sought.

Ghana News.title: Ebola fight: Misinformation is our worst enemy — GHS boss
Ghana News.content:
The Director-General of the Ghana Health Service (GHS), Dr Samuel Kaba Akoriyea, has warned that misinformation could undermine Ghana’s efforts to prepare for a possible Ebola outbreak, urging journalists and social media users to verify information before publishing or sharing it.

He has appealed to the media, content creators and users of platforms such as TikTok and WhatsApp to rely on official sources for updates on the disease, cautioning that inaccurate or misleading reports could complicate public health communication at a time when clear, credible information is critical.

“Our worst enemy is misinformation,” Dr Akoriyea said on Joy News’ PM Express on Monday, October 26.

He urged the public to cross-check claims with the Ghana Health Service and the Ministry of Health before circulating them.

“Ghana Health Service website is there, the Ministry of Health website is there, the Minister is there, I'm there, we have PROs, cross-check before you come out,” he appealed.

The GHS Director-General said the speed at which information circulates online made verification especially important, as people could easily misrepresent health developments or spread claims that had not been confirmed.

“In this era, people miscommunicate a lot,” he added.

Dr Akoriyea said Ghana had intensified its preparedness measures to strengthen its ability to respond if an Ebola case were detected, although the true test of readiness would come when the country had to manage an actual case.

“We have increased our preparedness to make sure that we tighten all the knots,” he said.

“Until we get a case, we might not be able to prove our readiness and even no matter how ready you are, no matter how ready you are, when you get a case, it's a different story.”

He said it was nevertheless better for the country to prepare thoroughly before a possible outbreak than to be caught unprepared.

“But it's better to be prepared, right, and get a case and do commit very few errors than not to be prepared at all,” he said.

The Director-General cited Ghana’s experience during the COVID-19 pandemic as an important foundation for strengthening its response to future health emergencies.

He said the availability of the Ga East Municipal Hospital and the University of Ghana Medical Centre (UGMC) had been an advantage during the pandemic, adding that lessons from that period were informing efforts to improve the country’s preparedness.

“I remember we were extremely prepared, and we're so fortunate as a country during COVID that we had Ga East already built, we had UGMC already built, and we are building on that to make sure that whatever we have done or we had done, now we can even make it better,” he said.

Trusted information critical

The appeal comes amid heightened concern over Ebola and the need for countries to strengthen surveillance, preparedness and public communication as outbreaks are reported in parts of Africa.

Ebola is a severe viral disease that can spread through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person who is showing symptoms, or with contaminated materials.

Prompt identification, isolation and appropriate care of suspected cases, alongside effective contact tracing and infection prevention, are important to containing transmission.

Public health authorities also rely on accurate information to explain risks, clarify what is known about an outbreak and communicate recommended precautions. False claims can fuel fear, undermine trust in health authorities and encourage people to act on advice that has not been medically verified.

Ghana News.title: Meghan to co-host Junior MasterChef Australia
Ghana News.content:
The Duchess of Sussex has been confirmed as a co-hostof the new season of Junior MasterChef Australia.

Meghan will join the 2027 series as a "special guest" with fellow host Poh Ling Yeow, according to Australia's Channel 10.

The Duchess said she "can't wait" to join the programme after appearing as a guest judge on MasterChef Australia last year. The show drew its largest Sunday audience since 2023, according to a statement from Paramount ANZ.

The announcement comes as Meghan faces increased scrutiny due to her father Thomas Markle being accused of child sexual abuse. He denies the allegations.

The BBC understands Meghan broke contact with her father last year, telling him she and authorities knew he had abused young girls.

Markle has strongly rejected the accusations as "lies" used to destroy his reputation.

Meghan's return to Australia follows a four-day tour of the country she and Prince Harry undertook in April.

Meghan's MasterChef debut was announced on the second day of the tour, a Wednesday when the Duchess was notably absent from public appearances. That evening, it was revealed she had been filming an episode.

It is understood she was not paid for her appearance. Australia's Network 10, which airs the series as part of Paramount ANZ, did not respond to a question from the BBC about whether Meghan would be paid for the Junior MasterChef season.

"I love cooking with my own kids, so seeing what these young stars create in the kitchen is going to be a lot of fun," Meghan said in a statement.

In August, the Sussexes announced they were moving back to the UK from California. The couple left the UK and stepped back from their royal duties in early 2020, before settling in California in March that year.

They launched media careers that included a high-profile interview with Oprah Winfrey and deals with Netflix and Spotify.

Meghan's lifestyle and cookery show on Netflix, With Love, Meghan, ran for two series and a Christmas special but did not perform well with audiences.

She also launched lifestyle brand As Ever, which includes a food range, but in March it ended its partnership with the streaming platform.

Last year, she registered her trademark in more than a dozen product categories in Australia, including cookware and table linen.

Ghana News.title: Awula Serwah urges Mahama to reaffirm mining licence requirements
Ghana News.content:
The Executive Director of Eco-Conscious Citizens, Awula Serwah, has urged President John Dramani Mahama to publicly reaffirm the legal requirements governing mining, warning that recent comments by Ghana Gold Board Chief Executive Officer Sammy Gyamfi risk sending the wrong signal to small-scale miners.

She says the government must make it clear that no one is permitted to undertake mining without the appropriate licence and other regulatory approvals, amid ongoing efforts to clamp down on illegal mining.

Awula Serwah warned that any suggestion that miners could operate without the necessary authorisation could weaken the work of the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) and other groups fighting irresponsible mining.

She said illegal mining continues to pose serious threats through the pollution of water bodies, destruction of forest reserves and loss of agricultural land.

She also stressed that a mining licence is essential to ensure operators work only in approved areas, adding that securing one does not necessarily mean all other regulatory conditions have been met.

Depending on the operation, miners may also require permits from the Environmental Protection Agency and approvals from relevant water authorities.

Speaking to Channel One TV on Monday, October 26, she said the President should assure the public that the government was not endorsing unlawful mining.

“The President should come out and let Ghanaians know that they are not encouraging lawlessness, and anybody who wants to mine must first obtain a licence,” she said.

She further cautioned that encouraging mining without a licence could amount to a criminal offence, insisting that the law must be respected as the country intensifies efforts to address the environmental damage caused by illegal mining.

Ghana News.title: Cheaper DStv: 4 new packages take effect November 5
Ghana News.content:
Canal+ and MultiChoice Ghana have introduced cheaper DStv subscription packages to make pay television more affordable and discourage pirated services and illegal digital boxes.

The existing six DStv packages will be replaced with four — Starter, Select, Sports and Ultimate — priced at GH¢50, GH¢100, GH¢250 and GH¢570 a month respectively.

Canal+ and MultiChoice Ghana agreed on the new subscription rates after engaging with the government through the Ministry of Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations.

It is intended to lower the cost barrier to legitimate television content ahead of a planned government crackdown on piracy, while giving subscribers broader access to entertainment, news, movies and sports at significantly reduced prices.

The parties announced details of the agreement at a joint press conference in Accra on Monday, October 26, 2026, where they outlined the new subscription structure and measures to tackle piracy in the pay television ecosystem.

Interest of Ghanaians

The Minister of Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Samuel Nartey George, said the government's engagement with MultiChoice and Canal+ was driven by the need to protect Ghanaian consumers' interests by making television content more affordable.

"I think that for us, when we began this journey with MultiChoice and now, Canal+, the question had been very simple. How do we put content in the hands or in the homes of Ghanaian families at an affordable price? The Ghanaian consumer is our ultimate interest," he said.

He added that the government was awaiting an opinion from the Attorney-General's Department before launching a major crackdown on illegal television streaming and ghost boxes.

He said the National Communications Authority and the Cyber Security Authority had already reviewed the proposed technical solutions and found them viable for tackling piracy, including measures involving the blocking of IP addresses used for illegal streaming.

Mr George said the government wanted to ensure it addressed all legal implications before enforcement began, adding that a committee comprising the ministry, NCA, MultiChoice, National Security, Customs, and other relevant institutions would continue to coordinate the exercise and protect consumers.

Not a promo

MultiChoice Ghana's Country Chief Executive Officer, Alex Okyere, said the new structure would simplify DStv's offerings from six packages to four while expanding the content available to subscribers.

He said the GH¢50 Starter package would offer 90 channels, including selected entertainment, movie, children's and free-to-air channels as well as all La Liga matches, while the GH¢100 Select package would provide 123 channels.

The GH¢250 Sports package would carry the company's entire football offering, including the Premier League and UEFA Champions League, compared with GH¢563 currently required to access the full football offering.

Ultimate, which replaces the current GH¢854 Premium package, would cost GH¢570 and include additional premium sports such as Formula One, golf, tennis, MotoGP and rugby.

"This is not a promo. These are the new packs, new prices that are here to stay. These are the new packs, new prices that are here to stay. So, I think that answers the question," Mr Okyere said.

Piracy effects

The Executive Vice-President of Public Affairs for Rest of Africa at Canal+, Dr Keabetswe Modimoeng, described the agreement as a product of sustained engagement between the company and the government and an example of the benefits expected from the Canal+ and MultiChoice merger.

He said piracy remained a major threat to the creative industry because illegal consumption of content deprived people across the production value chain of income, including producers, actors, costume designers and make-up artists.

Dr Modimoeng said Canal+ was therefore encouraged to make combating piracy a priority, stressing that protecting content ultimately meant safeguarding livelihoods.

He added that the country's macroeconomic and currency stability also made it easier for the company to run the projections and cost modelling needed for sustainable pricing.

Ghana News.title: UCC-UTAG demands clearer boundaries for GTEC’s regulatory role
Ghana News.content:
The University of Cape Coast (UCC) Chapter of the University Teachers Association of Ghana (UTAG) has admonished the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC) to refrain from interfering in university affairs and focus on its core mandates.

It noted that GTEC has been a useful ally in the education space but has often overstepped its boundaries, undermining academic freedom and disrupting other university activities.

The Association made the call at the UTAG Experts’ Forum 2026, held on the theme: “Rethinking Autonomy, Power and Oversight: GTEC’s Regulatory Authority and the Politics of Academic Freedom in Ghanaian Universities.”

Professor Philip Ebow Bondzi-Simpson, a Senior Member of the Faculty of Law, UCC, noted that beyond being a regulator, the GTEC was, by law, an advisor, coordinator, and accreditor, a mandate he said the Commission had failed to execute effectively and efficiently.

Prof Bondzi-Simpson noted that by executing its core mandates, including regulation, the GTEC would have less time to veer into matters outside its remit, stressing that the GTEC’s Director-General and staff were legally required to operate within their defined mandates and implement decisions of the Commission’s governing council.

He argued that any exercise of authority must be grounded in a clear mandate, warning that actions outside that scope would be unlawful.

“So, a Chief Executive whose mandate is set out by law does not go hovering around all manner of tertiary institutions to see what they are doing right or wrong. Any such thing should be in furtherance,” he said.

“The mandate must always precede the assertion of authority, and if that is not done, the exercise by the director general or a deputy director general or any director or staff on his behalf is ultra vires,” he added.

On other concerns, Prof Bondzi-Simpson objected to the GTEC’s membership of University Councils, arguing it contravened the law.

He said: “Nowhere in the GTEC law does it require membership on a university council. It is not in the letter of the law, nor does it conform to the spirit of the law. Because a regulator cannot be sitting on council; council is a governing council that makes decisions about the university, participating in the process while wearing one hat.

“Then in the next hat, it will go and negate or undermine those decisions. If you are part of it, you are bound by the decision. A referee or regulator cannot employ you, your staff, determine the policy.”

“A referee cannot choose the coach and the players and the captain or the general captain and then come and referee the game. So the letter of the law does not allow it. The spirit of the law does not allow it,” he stressed.

It was also the case of Prof Bondzi-Simpson that the Commission’s “policeman” posturing stemmed from its frequent description as a regulator in public discourse, adding that emphasising its roles as an adviser, coordinator and accreditor could help change their approach.

He called for stronger collaboration between tertiary institutions and GTEC.

Sharing similar concerns, Prof Denis Worlanyo Aheto, the Vice Chancellor of UCC, reiterated the call for GTEC to respect universities' autonomy.

He called for a regulatory framework that strengthens accountability and academic standards without the Commission unnecessarily interfering in legitimate academic decisions.

Turning to the institutions, he challenged universities to embrace accountability, stressing that academic freedom must be exercised responsibly with strict adherence to sound governance, ethical conduct and institutional integrity.

“Our goal should not be to weaken GTEC or diminish the authority of universities. Rather, we should build a relationship of constructive engagement in which regulatory authorities and universities understand their respective mandates and work collaboratively towards excellence in higher education,” the Vice Chancellor stressed.

For her part, Dr Cynthia Sena Kpeglo-Freiku, the Executive Secretary of the Vice Chancellors Ghana (VCG), among other disquiet, expressed concern about regulatory directives affecting staff appointments, internal organisational structures, retirement arrangements and academic programme development.

She said excessive interference delayed recruitment, created teaching gaps, increased administrative costs and disrupted academic delivery.

She called for a review of overlapping legal mandates, meaningful consultation with affected institutions, transparent regulatory procedures and a permanent mechanism for dialogue and dispute resolution.

“Strong universities require effective regulation. Effective regulation requires institutional trust, and institutional trust requires accountability on both sides,” Dr Kpeglo-Freiku stated.

Prof Kwadwo Appiagyei-Atua, the Regional Director of the African Coalition for Academic Freedom, suggested that GTEC’s regulatory powers must be checked against the Constitution.

He called for legislative instruments jointly developed by government, academic unions, and students through broad stakeholder consultations to prevent arbitrary directives and protect university autonomy.

Prof Appiagyei-Atua further argued that GTEC’s Board composition must be reviewed to ensure balanced representation, calling for the inclusion of academic unions and student representatives to limit excessive executive influence and promote democratic decision-making in university regulation.

“My recommendation is that it should not be done by the Minister alone. It should involve academic unions like UTAG, CETAG, and student representatives so that we all sit around the table, consult among ourselves, and agree on the details of the law,” he said.

Professor Jerry Opoku Ansah, the UCC UTAG President, explained that the forum, organised over the years, provided a platform to discuss local, national, and global matters objectively, offer informed policy alternatives, and contribute to development at all levels.

Speaking to the theme of this year’s forum, he emphasised that universities had a responsibility to maintain academic standards freely and produce well-trained graduates, but acknowledged the need for regulation to safeguard quality and public confidence.

He, therefore, called for a more collaborative relationship between tertiary institutions and GTEC.

Ghana News.title: TOR unveils a sweeping four-year transformation agenda
Ghana News.content:
The Tema Oil Refinery (TOR) has announced a sweeping four-year transformation agenda to quadruple its refining footprint, diversify its asset base, and embed social infrastructure in its revival story.

Mr Edmond Kombat, TOR's Managing Director, unveiled the “Restoration and Legacy Projects” programme for 2026 to 2029 at the Government Accountability Series Press Conference at the Presidency in Accra.

He described it as a blueprint that “looks further ahead” than routine maintenance and positions the national refiner for long-term strategic relevance.

He reiterated that the programme's core was a major capacity expansion.

Mr Kombat disclosed that TOR proposed a brownfield expansion of the existing refinery from 45,000 barrels per stream day (bpsd) to 85,000 bpsd.

In addition, TOR would develop a new greenfield refinery with a capacity of 115,000 bpsd, bringing its total processing capacity to 200,000 bpsd.

“This is not merely an upgrade; it is a re-industrialisation of TOR,” Mr Kombat said.

“The combination of brownfield and greenfield investments will position the refinery to meet Ghana’s growing petroleum product demand while creating opportunities for export and value addition.”

Mr Kombat emphasised that the restoration agenda extended beyond industrial infrastructure.

The programme includes building a Specialist Hospital with a Burns and Trauma Centre, a facility he said would ensure that “TOR’s revival leaves behind something that serves people as well as plants.”

The Hospital, he said, was expected to address a critical gap in Emergency and Burns Care within the Tema industrial enclave and the wider Greater Accra Region, where industrial accidents and thermal injuries require specialised attention.

To tackle accommodation challenges within the Tema enclave, the MD said TOR is working closely with the Ghana Home Ownership Fund to build a staff housing project on existing TOR land.

Mr Kombat said the initiative would ease workers' housing burden and support the broader development of the industrial city.

“Our people are our greatest asset. A restored TOR must also mean a better quality of life for those who keep the plant running,” he said.

The Managing Director reaffirmed TOR’s commitment to pursuing the programme with discipline, transparency, and partnership.

“We will pursue these projects with the urgency and seriousness they deserve. The Restoration and Legacy Projects are about securing TOR’s future and leaving a lasting legacy for Ghana,” Mr Kombat stated.

Ghana News.title: SAWA Program: Agri-Impact, PwC Ghana partner to strengthen consortium firms
Ghana News.content:
Agri-Impact Ltd has signed a four-year agreement with PwC Ghana to strengthen the institutional capacity of consortium partners implementing the Sustainable Aquaculture for Women Advancement (SAWA) Program.

Signed on October 26, 2026, at Agri-Impact’s office, the agreement builds on three years of collaboration under the Harnessing Agricultural Productivity and Prosperity for Youth (HAPPY) Program, through which PwC supported Agri-Impact’s institutional development.

The partnership will help participating agribusiness firms strengthen their organisational systems, improve performance, and scale operations to create more dignified, fulfilling work opportunities for young women under the SAWA Program, a Mastercard Foundation initiative in partnership with Agri-Impact.

SAWA Program seeks to unlock 60,000 dignified and fulfilling work opportunities for young women aged 18 to 35, including young women with disabilities in Ghana's aquaculture sector.

Speaking at the signing ceremony, Agri-Impact’s Chief Executive Officer, Dr. (h.c.) Daniel Fahene Acquaye, said the decision to extend institutional strengthening support to other consortium partners followed the benefits his organisation had gained from working with PwC.

He said the support had enhanced Agri-Impact’s visibility and capacity to manage large-scale agricultural and agribusiness projects in Ghana and the Caribbean, unlocking more opportunities for youth.

“We have seen the benefits and importance of institutional strengthening, especially for local and indigenous companies,” Dr Acquaye said.

He explained that Agri-Impact had proposed to the Mastercard Foundation that it extend similar support to other private sector partners, noting that stronger businesses were better positioned to grow and create more employment opportunities for young people.

“The more we strengthen the private sector, the more opportunities we create for young people,” he said.

Dr Acquaye emphasised that PwC’s role would be collaborative, helping participating firms build the capacity to expand and become more competitive rather than focusing on audits.

He expressed hope that the four-year engagement would produce stronger indigenous agribusiness brands with improved scale, quality, performance and resilience.

For his part, PwC Ghana Partner Hayfron Aboagye said the partnership aligned with the firm’s purpose of building trust in society and helping solve important problems.

He said PwC is committed to supporting indigenous agribusinesses to build on the sector's already recorded growth.

“We are excited to partner with Agri-Impact and the Mastercard Foundation for this great support. We believe that, at the end of the four-year journey, we will be seeing big brands coming out of this intervention,” Mr Aboagye said.

Other members of the SAWA consortium are expected to sign their respective agreements in the coming days.

About the SAWA Program

The Sustainable Aquaculture for Women Advancement (SAWA) Program is a four-year Mastercard Foundation initiative, in partnership with Agri-Impact Ltd, running from 2026 to 2030.

It aims to address systemic constraints in Ghana’s aquaculture sector while expanding inclusive economic opportunities across the tilapia and catfish value chains.

The program seeks to create 60,000 dignified, fulfilling jobs for young women aged 18 to 35, including 3,000 young women with disabilities.

Agri-Impact leads implementation with Newage Agric Solutions Ltd, AgroKings Limited, the Fisheries Commission, CEL and TechnoServe. Anchor partners Aglow, Afrigem Global, and Naple Betta, along with the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), provide additional support. PwC serves as the program’s institutional strengthening partner.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
