World.title: Italy’s Young Protesters Return to the Streets
World.content:
Demonstrators across Italy on Saturday protested economic inequality and the political establishment. A heavy police presence throughout the country aimed to prevent the looting and violence that occurred during protests last weekend.

Young people demonstrated across Italy on Saturday amid a heavy police presence to prevent the looting and violence that occurred during protests last weekend.

The demonstrations echoed student protests in France that have unleashed a nationwide groundswell of frustration there, sparking the country’s worst rioting in decades.

Italy’s marches on Saturday were largely peaceful, though protesters clashed with the police in Turin, Padua, Bologna and Rome, where a small group of demonstrators stormed the Colosseum. The police arrested just nine people nationwide and reported 87 to prosecutors, the Italian news agency ANSA reported.

In Milan, the site of last week’s largest and most violent demonstrations, some 10,000 people hit the streets, the police estimated — five times as many as had marched the previous weekend.

Throngs of young people chanted about their frustration with the high cost of living and Italy’s political establishment. They held hand-drawn signs denouncing low wages, high rents, economic inequality and Italy’s financial support of Israel, whose war in Gaza is deeply unpopular with Italians.

Protesters said that the country’s sluggish job market and a government they saw as more focused on military spending than on investing in young people had set their generation up to fail.

“I look for work abroad every day of my life,” said Ilaria Carrozza, 27, a design engineer. “And that’s not fair: This is my country, I want to stay here. But I can’t live like this.”

Manfredi Cacioppo, a 26-year-old sales assistant from Sicily, said he was demonstrating in solidarity with truckers and farmers in southern Italy, who had recently blockaded roads and ports to protest high fuel prices caused by the war in Iran.

“It all comes from the same issue: money being spent on war,” he said. “That money would be better to invest in health, education, transport, the housing crisis and help for the workers.”

Last weekend’s demonstrations took Italy’s northern cities by surprise. In Milan, groups of masked young people set fires, looted stores and lobbed projectiles at the police, causing an estimated $1.1 million in damage, according to a local business association. Fifty-one people, most of them minors, were arrested.

Milan’s left-wing mayor accused the national police of “having underestimated the moment” and posting too few officers to the scene. Italy’s right-wing interior minister accused the mayor of pandering to the left.

Giorgia Meloni, Italy’s prime minister, called an emergency meeting on Monday and announced tougher penalties for violent protesters. A cabinet member, Matteo Salvini, said that the government would send 500 soldiers to Milan this weekend to “defend” the city against “criminals.”

On Saturday, army vehicles and police vans dotted many of Milan’s main squares, and numerous stores in the city’s shopping district boarded up their windows. Throughout the city, plainclothes police officers stopped groups of young people to check their identification documents.

For many protesters, the first challenge was figuring out where to go.

A social media account that helped organize the protests was supposed to post a meeting place at 2:30 p.m. But shortly before then, the Milan police said they had detained the account’s owner. The announcement never came.

Image Protesters in Rome on Saturday. Credit... Remo Casilli/Reuters

That left many demonstrators unmoored. In bars and online chat rooms, they argued over where, and whether, to show up.

“We were lost and confused,” said Caterina Sironi, a 23-year-old university student. “We ran all over the whole city.”

Ruggero Lorenzi, 19 and a high school student, crisscrossed Milan on three trains and a tram in search of a demonstration. “On Telegram, on Instagram, in metro stations, everyone was fighting over where to go,” he said.

After several false starts — “ten people over here, ten people over there,” he said — he found about 500 protesters gathered near a subway stop in the city center.

As Mr. Lorenzi’s protest snaked through the city to the Politecnico di Milano, Milan’s oldest university, its ranks swelled.

Many protesters said they were eager to keep the demonstration peaceful, hoping their message would be heard. The police used tear gas and water cannons against protesters in other cities on Saturday, but not in Milan, where they reported that there had been no violence or damage.

“We’re trying to emulate the French protests,” said Joshua Flores, 21, who is unemployed. “I hope this protest continues in a positive way.”

World.title: Lula wins fourth term in dramatic Brazil election comeback
World.content:
Brazil's President Luiz InÃ¡cio Lula da Silva has won a fourth term in office in a dramatic comeback over his right-wing challenger FlÃ¡vio Bolsonaro.

Left-wing leader Lula took 51.79% of votes, becoming the first president since Brazil's return to civilian rule in 1985 to be elected after losing the first round of voting.

Lula told jubilant crowds his victory was a "loss for negativity, lies", adding "long live democracy".

FlÃ¡vio Bolsonaro, the son of convicted former president Jair Bolsonaro, has so far refused to recognise the result and called for it to be annulled. World leaders have congratulated Lula on his re-election.

Bolsonaro's rejection comes as no surprise to observers. His father did the same.

But a challenge appears unlikely to succeed.

Firstly, it seems to centre on the unprecedented decision by the Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin to extend voting nationwide by two hours. Some Bolsonaro fans are pointing out that Zanin was once Lula's lawyer and alleging bias.

But both teams had requested an extension to voting times - Lula's had argued that voters in SÃ£o Paulo and Bahia could not get to the polling stations because of a lack of buses, while Bolsonaro's campaign cited heavy rain in some areas in the south of the country and in SÃ£o Paulo as their reason.

Both knew every vote would count and did not want their side to miss out.

The president of the Supreme Electoral Court KÃ¡ssio Nunes Marques â appointed by Jair Bolsonaro â confirmed Lula's victory and said that the voter extension did not change the outcome of the race.

The sheer gap between the two candidates' tallies - 4.4 million votes - makes the result more difficult to challenge.

World.title: Ex-FBI chief James Comey faces federal charges for third time
World.content:
Federal prosecutors have taken steps to charge ex-Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Director James Comey with leaking national defence information, according to a court filing.

It marks the third time the justice department has moved to bring criminal charges against Comey, a longtime critic of President Donald Trump.

Few details are provided about the two counts in the three-page filing, but Comey's lawyers said in separate court papers that the case stemmed from an alleged disclosure of classified information to the New York Times in October 2016, while he was head of the FBI.

Comey denied any wrongdoing in a video posted on Substack on Monday, calling the charges an "appalling abuse".

"It would almost be funny if it weren't such an appalling abuse of the department of justice, one that we cannot become numb to," he said in the clip.

"Nothing's changed with me - I'm still innocent, I'm still not afraid of these people and I still believe in the independent federal judiciary."

Comey was charged in Washington DC through a criminal information, which is a formal written charging document filed directly by a prosecutor.

This is different to a criminal indictment, which must be approved by a grand jury, a group of citizens sworn in to review if evidence is strong enough to prosecute.

Comey's lawyer, Patrick Fitzgerald, said in a statement that two different teams of prosecutors had investigated the alleged disclosure to the New York Times a decade ago during the first Trump administration.

"Both times the Government determined that no charges should be brought against anyone," he said.

The attorney said the court filing "purports to charge Mr Comey with crimes that he did not commit".

His legal team has filed a motion to dismiss the charges.

Former federal prosecutor Glenn Kirschner told the BBC that the case may have exceeded the 10-year statute of limitations, giving the motion to dismiss the charges "a very good chance of being granted".

Kirschner said it seemed like the charges against Comey were a "revenge-fuelled attempt by Donald Trump to have his Department of Justice find something that might stick".

World.title: Jordan carries out deadly strike in Syria in retaliation for church attack
World.content:
Jordan has struck what its military says were "terrorist organisations" in Syria in retaliation for an attack on a Christian funeral last week that killed nine people.

Syrian health officials told state media five people, including women, children and an elderly man, were killed in the strike on a village in the southern Daraa province. Jordan said its fighter jets had killed and wounded "several terrorists", without giving further details.

Jordan said it had co-ordinated with the Syrian government. Syria said it had not been notified of Monday's attack.

It comes after a nine people were killed and 34 injured in a shooting at a funeral in a Greek Orthodox church in Karak on Friday.

World.title: Meghan to co-host Junior MasterChef Australia
World.content:
The Duchess of Sussex has been confirmed as a co-host of the new season of Junior MasterChef Australia.

Meghan will join the 2027 series as a "special guest" with fellow host Poh Ling Yeow, according to Australia's Channel 10.

The duchess said she "can't wait" to take part in the programme after an appearance as a guest judge on MasterChef Australia last year. It was the show's largest Sunday audience since 2023, according to the statement from Paramount ANZ.

The announcement comes as Meghan faces increased scrutiny due to her father Thomas Markle being accused of child sexual abuse. He denies the allegations.

The BBC understands Meghan broke contact with her father last year, telling him she and authorities knew he had abused young girls.

Markle has strongly rejected the accusations as "lies" which are being used to destroy his reputation.

World.title: Jay-Z to perform at Super Bowl half-time show
World.content:
Rapper Jay-Z will perform at the Super Bowl half-time show in February, the NFL has announced.

Jay-Z's company Roc Nation has produced the half-time show since 2019, and he plays a key role in selecting each year's performer but he has not performed before at the NFL championship game.

"Anticipation as to who Jay-Z might have guest star at halftime for the big game will now kick off," the NFL said in a statement. "Of course, his wife, BeyoncÃ©, will be atop the list."

Next year's Super Bowl LXI will take place on 14 February near Los Angeles.

The hip-hop star will follow in the footsteps of other recent half-time performers including Bad Bunny, Kendrick Lamar, Usher, Rihanna and The Weeknd.

The musical performance draws global attention while the sport is watched by tens of millions of people in the US.

Kendrick Lamar's 2025 performance was the most watched Super Bowl half-time show in history and won the Emmy award for outstanding music direction.

The announcement was made after Jay-Z, whose real name is Shawn Carter, performed two shows last weekend at the Los Angeles stadium where the Super Bowl will be played.

The LA shows were part of a tour to celebrate the 30th anniversary of his debut album Reasonable Doubt.

"From 'Reasonable Doubt' to standing on the Super Bowl halftime stage, this has been a journey," said Jay-Z, whose real name is Shawn Carter.

"Thirty years of music, work, and culture on the world's biggest stage. This run continues to be a dream come true."

NFL commissioner Roger Goodell said he "couldn't be more excited for fans around the world to experience the artistry, creativity and cultural impact he will bring".

"When we first reached an agreement with Roc Nation to produce the show, I had just one request: that Jay-Z take the stage himself one day, whenever the moment felt right to him," Goodell said.

The star's accolades include being the first rapper inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame, 25 Grammy awards and being inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2021.

World.title: Opposition leader María Machado returns from exile to a Venezuela reshaped by Trump
World.content:
Driving down roads lined with jubilant supporters from the western state of Lara to the capital Caracas, Maria Corina Machado's return to Venezuela could hardly have been more different to her exit 10 months earlier.

Colourful, loud, open and defiant, it stood in stark contrast to the way the Venezuelan opposition leader slipped out of the country in the dead of night in December last year to receive the Nobel Peace Prize in Oslo.

She had been unable to make it back to her homeland until now, thwarted on several occasions by the Venezuelan government - and by the Trump administration, which insisted the "time wasn't right" for her return.

Now, it appears, it is.

"Maria Corina is the indisputable leader of Venezuela," says 20-year-old Gregory Noriega, wearing a sweatshirt emblazoned with the logo of the opposition movement Vente Venezuela. "Her return represents hope."

World.title: Celebrations in Serbia after veteran ruler Vučić loses election to student-led protest movement
World.content:
Serbia's long-standing leader Aleksandar VuÄiÄ has admitted defeat to a student-led protest movement in snap parliamentary elections.

Celebrations erupted as crowds descended on the centre of Belgrade, Novi Sad and other cities.

The student movement was formed less than two years ago in response to a railway station disaster blamed on corruption and negligence, but fought the election with candidates from a cross-section of Serbian society.

"It is clear we have lost these elections," right-wing populist leader VuÄiÄ said as he conceded. With 97% of polling stations counted, Serbia's election commission said the students had won 2.25 million votes and the former ruling party 1.67 million.

The students had secured 52.7% of the vote, while VuÄiÄ's Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) was on 39.2%, according to its preliminary figures late on Monday morning.

VuÄiÄ had spent two terms as president and could not seek a third term, so was leading his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) with the aim of returning to the post of prime minister, which he left in 2017.

He called the snap elections after two years of protests triggered by the collapse of a canopy in front of Novi Sad station which killed 16 people.

World.title: Trump administration illegally fired James Comey's daughter, judge rules
World.content:
The US justice department illegally fired Maurene Comey, the daughter of former Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) director James Comey, a federal judge has ruled.

Comey, who lost her job as a federal prosecutor in New York in July 2025, sued the government, arguing she was unlawfully fired because of her father, a critic of US President Donald Trump, and because of her perceived political affiliations.

Judge Jesse Furman ruled on Monday that the Trump administration must reinstate her and that she must be given back pay.

A spokesperson for the justice department said in a statement that it disagreed with the decision and "will appeal in due course".

In his ruling, Judge Furman said Comey's dismissal violated the US Constitution as well as her right to a fair legal process.

He said the US attorney general can fire federal prosecutors but only "in a particular manner and only for certain reasons".

Furman noted that in Comey's role, "she was assigned some of the country's highest profile cases and consistently received the highest accolades from supervisors and peers alike".

Comey has worked on cases against the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, his accomplice Ghislaine Maxwell, and hip-hop mogul Sean "Diddy" Combs, who was convicted on prostitution-related charges involving his two ex-girlfriends last year.

Furman ordered that Comey be given back pay from July until December 2025, when she accepted a new job.

In a statement, Comey's lawyers said: "This hard-earned victory belongs to Ms Comey, to all civil servants, and to all fighting for the rule of law."

Comey had previously said the only reason she was told about her firing was that it "came from Washington".

A complaint filed by her lawyers in September 2025 stated that they believed Comey had been fired "solely or substantially because her father is former FBI Director James B Comey, or because of her perceived political affiliation and beliefs, or both".

The justice department said in court filings that the decision was made by former Attorney General Pam Bondi.

The Trump administration has twice brought charges against James Comey, including for allegedly lying to Congress, but that case was dismissed by a judge who said the prosecutor who brought the case was unlawfully appointed.

Earlier this year, the justice department charged Comey with knowingly and wilfully making a threat to take the life of, and to inflict bodily harm, on the president. He has denied any wrongdoing.

The case stems from a 2025 Instagram post shared by Comey that contained a photo of seashells on a beach arranged to read "86 47".

"Eighty-six" is a slang term for "get rid of", and prosecutors allege it encourages violence against Trump.

World.title: Gunmen kill Islamic cleric Sheikh Masussuka in Katsina
World.content:
The Katsina State Police Command has confirmed the killing of an Islamic cleric, Sheikh Yahaya Masussuka, who was shot by suspected gunmen outside his residence in Dutsin-Ma Local Government Area on Monday night.

DW Hausa reported that the police confirmed the killing to its correspondent, adding that the attackers were riding a motorcycle when they opened fire on the cleric.

The incident reportedly occurred at about 9 p.m. near the entrance to his residence.

Several local news platforms reported that another person was shot during the attack, although accounts differed over the person’s identity and whether he survived.

Photographs circulating on social media purportedly showed residents gathered outside the cleric’s residence following the shooting. PREMIUM TIMES has not independently verified where or when the images were taken.

The circumstances surrounding the attack and the identities of those responsible remain unclear.

The spokesperson for the Katsina State Police Command, Abubakar Sadiq, acknowledged enquiries from journalists in a police WhatsApp group at 10:44 p.m. on Monday, saying he would respond to their calls as soon as possible.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He had not provided further details to PREMIUM TIMES at the time of filing this report.

Who was Sheikh Masussuka?

Mr Masussuka was an Islamic preacher based in Dutsin-Ma, Katsina State, although he was originally from Bauchi State.

He was known for his Quran-centred teachings, particularly his rejection of certain Hadith traditions, which brought him into disagreement with other Islamic scholars. His sermons also attracted considerable attention on social media.

In April 2024, he established Qur’an TV/Radio and Masussuka International School in Dutsin-Ma. The school was designed to provide both Qur’anic and conventional education.

He also advocated peaceful coexistence between Muslims and Christians. In June 2025, the Network for Good Governance and Transparency honoured him with a Peace Ambassador award at an event in Katsina.

In November 2025, the Katsina State Government summoned the cleric following complaints that some of his teachings contravened Islamic principles.

The government also acknowledged receiving complaints from Masussuka that members of Jama’atu Izalatul Bidia were insulting him and threatening to attack him.

The matter was referred to the Katsina Emirate Council, where both sides were invited for discussions. Governor Dikko Radda subsequently directed the cleric to respond to the allegations before a committee of Islamic scholars.

There is no evidence at this stage linking the earlier religious dispute or the reported threats to Monday’s killing.

World.title: JIBWIS disowns viral video preaching violence, religious intolerance; demands probe
World.content:
The Jama’atu Izalatil Bid’ah Wa Iqamatis Sunnah (JIBWIS) has distanced itself from a viral video of a group in its First Aid Group uniform chanting threats to Christians.

In the video, the leader of the group is heard soliciting assault rifles to carry out mass killings in churches in Enugu and Plateau states.

The National Chairman of JIBWIS, Abdullahi Bala-Lau, condemned the footage and urged the State Security Services (SSS), the Nigeria Police Force, and other security agencies to launch an immediate investigation, unmask those behind the recording, and prosecute anyone found culpable.

Mr Bala-Lau stated that the inciting remarks and calls for violence are entirely foreign to the core values, teachings, and objectives of JIBWIS.

He cautioned that merely wearing the organisation’s First Aid Group uniform or standing among members does not confer official representation or authority to speak on behalf of the body.

Expressing concern about the video’s timing and nature, the cleric noted that the incident might be a calculated effort by external actors to smear the organisation’s image and undermine national peace.

He pointed to JIBWIS’s peacebuilding track record, citing its recent international conference in Abuja, which convened Christian leaders, scholars from Islamic denominations, and international delegates to foster interfaith harmony and religious tolerance.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Read below the full statement by JIBWIS

The National Chairman of Jama’atu Izalatil Bid’ah Wa Iqamatis Sunnah (JIBWIS), Sheikh Abdullahi Bala Lau, has strongly condemned a viral video showing a man dressed in the uniform of the organisation’s First Aid Group, participating in a jogging exercise and chanting provocative statements calling for AK-47 rifles to be given to them to enable them to travel to Enugu on Sunday and carry out an attack.

Reacting to the disturbing development, Sheikh Bala Lau called on the Department of State Services (DSS), the Nigeria Police Force and other relevant security agencies to immediately investigate the incident, identify those responsible and ensure that anyone found culpable is brought to justice in accordance with the law.

The National Chairman categorically dissociated JIBWIS from the inflammatory statements, stressing that such expressions of violence, intimidation and threats against any community are completely alien to the principles, teachings and objectives upon which the organisation was established.

He emphasised that wearing the JIBWIS First Aid Group uniform or appearing among its members does not automatically mean an individual is acting on behalf of the organisation or with its authorisation.

Sheikh Bala Lau further expressed concern that the incident could represent a deliberate attempt by individuals or external interests to misrepresent the organisation and damage its longstanding reputation. He therefore urged security agencies to thoroughly investigate the circumstances surrounding the video, including the identity, affiliation and possible motives of those involved.

The Chairman recalled that JIBWIS recently organised an international conference in Abuja, bringing together Christian leaders, Muslim scholars from different Islamic schools of thought, prominent personalities and participants from different parts of the world, with the central objective of promoting interfaith dialogue, mutual understanding, religious tolerance and peaceful coexistence.

He questioned how an organisation that has consistently invested its resources, leadership and institutional efforts in building bridges across religious and ethnic divides could reasonably be associated with statements advocating violence against fellow Nigerians.

For approximately 48 years since its establishment, JIBWIS has remained committed to the propagation of authentic Islamic teachings, the promotion of the Sunnah of Prophet Muhammad (SAW), moral reformation, education, humanitarian services and the peaceful coexistence of people irrespective of their religious, ethnic or geographical backgrounds.

World.title: Police arrest two suspects over alleged murder of step-brother
World.content:
The police in Cross River State have arrested two suspects for allegedly killing their step-brother in Yakurr Local Government Area of the state

In a statement on Monday, the police spokesperson, Sunday Eitokpah, said the suspects, Omini Ibiang, 28, and Emmanuel Ibiang, 26, allegedly attacked the deceased, Bassey Ibiang, over claims that he stole their elder sister’s bag.

According to the statement, a complainant, who reported the case to the police, said, “The deceased was allegedly tied by his hands and legs and inflicted with a deep machete wound to the head.

“He was subsequently taken to Ugep General Hospital, where he was confirmed dead, and his body was deposited in the hospital mortuary,” the statement said.

Police said they were informed of the incident on Sunday, after which they arrested the suspects.

“Police operatives visited the scene and commenced preliminary investigations to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and the respective roles of those involved,” the statement added.

The Commissioner of Police, Ajo Ordue, warned residents against resorting to violence over allegations of theft or other disputes.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He urged members of the public to report suspected offences to the police and allow the law to take its course.

Recent killings in Cross River

The arrest comes amid other reported cases of killings in Cross River linked to alleged disputes and violence.

PREMIUM TIMES recently reported the arrest of a man accused of stabbing a 42-year-old man to death over a N500 gift.

The newspaper also reported police investigations into the deaths of two men allegedly attacked by a mob, as well as the arrest of a man over the alleged murder of his stepdaughter, whom he accused of witchcraft.

In another case, a pastor was sentenced to death by hanging for killing his daughter.

World.title: Police arrest 35-year-old man over alleged rape of 11-year-old girl
World.content:
The police in Cross River State have arrested a 35-year-old man over the alleged rape of an 11-year-old girl in Yala Local Government Area of the state.

Police said the suspect, Okputu Bright, was arrested after the victim’s father reported the incident at the Okpoma Divisional Police Headquarters on 24 October.

In a statement on Sunday, police spokesperson Sunday Eitokpah said the alleged incident occurred on 18 October.

According to the police, the father alleged that Mr Bright lured the girl and sexually assaulted her before leaving her at a location within the community.

The police said the child had been referred to a general hospital for medical examination, while the suspect was arrested and detained.

“The Command has directed that the investigation be concluded promptly and the case file transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID) for further investigation, in accordance with established procedures,” the statement said.

Police warn against exposing victim

The Commissioner of Police in the state, Ajo Ordue, reiterated the command’s commitment to protecting children and other vulnerable persons.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Ordue urged residents to report suspected sexual offences promptly and assured the public that the allegations would be handled professionally, with due regard for the child’s welfare and confidentiality.

The police also warned against circulating information or images that could identify the child or expose her to harm further.

“The Command emphasises that the suspect remains presumed innocent unless proven guilty by a court of competent jurisdiction,” the statement added.

One in many cases

The arrest comes amid other reported cases of sexual offences involving minors in Cross River.

In August, PREMIUM TIMES reported the arrest of two men, aged 68 and 70, over the alleged attempted rape of a 12-year-old girl in Calabar. The police said the girl’s father reported the incident.

In June, a Family Court in Calabar sentenced 41-year-old Endurance Sandy to life imprisonment for raping an 11-year-old girl. The case commenced in 2021.

In May, the Family Court in Calabar sentenced 27-year-old Edidiong Nyojole to life imprisonment for raping a 13-year-old girl. The court also ordered him to pay the victim N1 million in compensation.

World.title: Delta extends retirement age for clinical health workers
World.content:
Governor Sheriff Oborevwori of Delta State has approved an extension of the retirement age for skilled clinical health professionals in government hospitals from 60 to 65 years.

The policy also extends the maximum length of service from 35 to 40 years, whichever comes first.

Mr Oborevwori announced the development in Asaba on Monday.

He said the initiative aimed to address manpower shortages, retain experienced medical personnel and strengthen healthcare delivery in the state.

The governor also said the policy covers 26 categories of skilled clinical health professionals actively engaged in clinical services in government hospitals.

According to him, these include medical officers, nursing officers, pharmacists, medical laboratory scientists, physiotherapists, radiographers, optometrists, psychologists, dental officers, community health officers and audiologists.

Others include dieticians, medical laboratory technicians, pharmacy technicians, X-ray technicians, dental technologists, dental therapists, prosthetic and orthoptists, among others.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Oborevwori said the extension followed appeals by the Delta Council of the National Association of Nigeria Nurses and Midwives and the state chapter of the Nigerian Medical Association.

“The associations have sought the adoption of the policy in Delta following its approval at the federal level,” he said.

The governor explained that eligible officers seeking the extension must apply through their respective chief medical directors six months before attaining 60 years of age or completing 35 years in service.

“Applicants are also required to present medical certificates of fitness, while chief medical directors are expected to forward applications to the Ministry of Health for screening and approval by the commissioner,” he added.

Mr Oborevwori clarified that the policy does not cover skilled clinical health professionals serving in ministries and extra-ministerial departments.

He said the extension was specifically designed for personnel actively engaged in clinical practice in government hospitals.

He expressed confidence that retaining experienced and medically fit personnel would help preserve professional expertise and institutional knowledge within the state’s public hospital system.

The governor added that the policy took effect from the date of approval, subject to the prescribed application, screening and approval procedures.

(NAN)

World.title: Ballon d’Or: Kane, Putellas crowned world’s best footballers in London
World.content:
Harry Kane has ended England’s 25-year wait for the men’s Ballon d’Or after winning the prestigious individual award at Monday’s ceremony in London.

The Bayern Munich striker became the first Englishman since Michael Owen in 2001 to be named the world’s best male footballer.

The England captain claimed the honour ahead of a strong field of nominees, including France’s Ousmane Dembélé and Kylian Mbappé, Norway’s Erling Haaland, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Argentina’s Lionel Messi and Spain’s teenage sensation Lamine Yamal.

The 2026 ceremony, organised by France Football, recognised outstanding individual and team performances across men’s and women’s football.

The award represents a major milestone for Kane, who has established himself among Europe’s leading forwards through his goalscoring consistency and performances for club and country.

Meanwhile, Spain and Barcelona midfielder Alexia Putellas won the women’s Ballon d’Or for the third time, equalling the record set by her former teammate Aitana Bonmatí.

Putellas was rewarded for an outstanding 2025-26 campaign in which she captained Barcelona to four major trophies: the Spanish Liga F, Copa de la Reina, Spanish Super Cup and UEFA Women’s Champions League.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Her achievements also included playing a key role in Spain’s Nations League triumph.

After receiving the award, Putellas thanked her teammates and acknowledged the quality of the other nominees.

“I think anyone here could have fairly won this trophy and be giving this speech here right now,” she said.

The ceremony also celebrated emerging talents, coaches, goalkeepers and clubs that distinguished themselves during the season.

Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal won the men’s young player award, while Vicky López claimed the corresponding women’s honour.

Barcelona Femeni and Paris Saint-Germain were named the women’s and men’s clubs of the year, respectively.

Spain’s Pere Romeu and Luis de la Fuente received the women’s and men’s coach of the year awards, while goalkeepers Cata Coll and Unai Simon won the corresponding prizes in the women’s and men’s categories.

Kane also claimed the men’s top scorer award, with Mexico’s Charlyn Corral receiving the women’s equivalent.

England forward Bukayo Saka received the Socrates Award, which recognises humanitarian work and social initiatives.

The ceremony brought together leading figures in world football to celebrate individual excellence and achievements across the game.

World.title: Ebola: How much have Nigerian states allocated to emergency preparedness?
World.content:
Nigeria’s first confirmed case of Ebola in more than a decade has raised questions about how prepared state governments are to detect and contain the virus before it spreads through their communities.

The World Health Organisation said on 20 October that Nigeria had recorded an imported case of Ebola caused by the Bundibugyo virus. The patient is the wife of a Swiss diplomat based in Abuja. She arrived in Nigeria on 3 October after travelling from Uganda and developed symptoms a few days later. The patient and her spouse were later evacuated to Switzerland on Monday while health authorities identified 53 contacts and began monitoring them.

The confirmation followed weeks of warnings from the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) about the risk of the virus entering Nigeria from an outbreak that began in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

Health authorities are identifying people who may have been exposed, tracing their movements, testing suspected cases, protecting healthcare workers and preventing further transmission. Much of this work depends on coordination across states, local government areas and health facilities, where people live and seek treatment.

A PREMIUM TIMES review of states’ 2026 approved budgets shows differences in allocations for disease surveillance, infection control, emergency operations and infectious disease facilities.

Some states made substantial provisions for health emergencies, while others allocated smaller sums to specific disease-control activities. Some budgets provide for preparedness under general health emergency headings, while others identify particular diseases, facilities or surveillance programmes.

The allocations do not establish how much money is available for an immediate Ebola response or whether the systems funded are operational. They show what state governments have provided for in their 2026 budgets, offering a basis for examining their stated priorities for public health preparedness.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The NCDC (Establishment) Act 2018 provides the statutory foundation for the agency’s work in preventing, detecting and controlling diseases of public health importance. The agency coordinates disease surveillance, provides technical support to subnational authorities and supports responses to public health emergencies.

The International Health Regulations (2005), a legally binding international framework, also requires countries to develop and maintain the capacity to detect, assess, notify and respond to public health risks.

The National Health Act 2014 provides another part of the framework. Section 11 establishes the Basic Health Care Provision Fund to support essential health services, particularly at the primary healthcare level. Although the fund is not a substitute for state emergency-response budgets, primary healthcare facilities play an important role in early detection, referral and disease reporting.

These frameworks do not prescribe a uniform amount that every state must earmark specifically for Ebola. They nevertheless underscore the need for functional public health systems capable of identifying and responding to infectious disease threats.

In May, the NCDC warned that the risk of Ebola being imported into Nigeria was high. It cited international travel, population movements and the difficulty of distinguishing early Ebola symptoms from common illnesses such as malaria. The agency urged states and the Federal Capital Territory to strengthen their preparedness and ensure they could detect and contain suspected cases promptly.

The subsequent confirmation of an imported case has made those preparations more urgent.

On Monday, the World Health Organisation said Nigeria currently has no active Ebola case after the country evacuated its index patient to Switzerland. The WHO Regional Director for Africa, Mohamed Janabi, said this in a post on X, shortly after Nigeria’s Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate, confirmed the patient’s evacuation from Nigeria.

Billions budgeted for state’s preparedness

Among the largest provisions identified in the 2026 approved state budgets are Delta’s N37.28 billion for emergency operations centres, Zamfara’s N20 billion for a health emergency response fund and Lagos’s combined N17.79 billion for two infectious disease research facilities.

Delta’s 2026 budget also provides N590 million for integrating national disease surveillance, N100 million for the control and management of infectious diseases and N50 million for communicable diseases.

Zamfara’s N20 billion allocation for a health emergency response fund could provide substantial funding for public health crises. Its effectiveness will depend on how the money is released and deployed.

Lagos’s combined N17.79 billion allocation comprises N15.27 billion for a public health epidemics and infectious disease research institute and N2.52 billion for an infectious disease research institute at Mainland Hospital, Yaba. The facilities could strengthen the state’s capacity to respond to outbreaks such as Ebola, although their contribution will depend on their completion, staffing, diagnostic capabilities and recurrent funding.

Meanwhile, Ogun provides N2.5 billion for a medical emergency preparedness and response project and N4.8 billion for national disease surveillance. Akwa Ibom allocated N1 billion for upgrading statewide emergency health interventions and N100 million for upgrading its health emergency operations centre.

These allocations show the amounts the states have provided for emergency preparedness in their 2026 budgets. They do not, on their own, establish how much funding has been released or which systems are ready for immediate use.

An operational emergency operations centre with trained staff, reliable communications and established response procedures may be more useful in the early hours of an outbreak than a facility still under construction. Similarly, a functioning surveillance system may detect a suspected case before a large emergency allocation translates into operational capacity.

Funding for surveillance, hospitals and infection control

The 2026 approved budgets show different approaches to health security, ranging from hospital rehabilitation and emergency equipment to disease surveillance and community-level prevention.

Cross River allocated N350 million to upgrade the abandoned tuberculosis hospital in Obubra into an infectious disease hospital, N300 million for a disease-control and partners complex, and N20 million for communicable disease prevention and control. The combined allocation is N670 million for infrastructure and disease-control activities.

Enugu’s 2026 budget includes N129.33 million for communicable diseases, N100 million for medical equipment intended to strengthen health security, N20 million for furniture and information technology equipment for a health sector command centre or public health emergency operations centre, and N10 million for fencing an infectious disease hospital. The four provisions total N259.33 million.

Kaduna allocated N179.69 million for monitoring and tracking public health emergencies and N620.68 million for the Kaduna State Centre for Disease Control. Together, the two provisions amount to N800.37 million.

Kebbi allocated N410.37 million for disease surveillance tools, equipment and essential emergency drugs for its emergency operations centre. Kwara set aside N301.5 million for integrated national disease surveillance, while Plateau provided N25.7 million for the same general purpose.

Kogi allocated N500 million for health security involving emergency preparedness, response and disease control, alongside N3.02 million for controlling emerging public health diseases. Benue provided N19.38 million for infection control and community awareness.

Other states made provisions for surveillance vehicles, emergency response systems and outbreak management. Taraba allocated N107 million for disease surveillance and response vehicles, in addition to N27.37 million for establishing and maintaining a responsive public health emergency system.

Adamawa’s 2026 budget includes N10 million for communicable diseases, N2 million for emergency response to rural outbreaks and N27.8 million for chemicals used in fumigation and decontamination.

In the North-east, Bauchi allocated N500 million for surveillance and disease outbreak prevention, N100 million for medical equipment for communicable diseases, N100 million for rehabilitating the infectious disease hospital at Bayara and N300 million for renovating another infectious disease hospital.

Gombe provided N35 million for disease surveillance under its public health emergency system, N10 million for emergency operations centres and N3 million for communicable diseases. Yobe allocated N1.09 billion for health emergency services, while Borno earmarked N35 million for research on communicable diseases.

In the North-west, Jigawa allocated N135 million for renovating its infectious disease hospital in Dutse. Kano’s 2026 budget includes N92.7 million for integrated disease surveillance, N115 million for coordinating communicable disease activities in primary healthcare, N20 million for coordinating public health emergencies at local government level and N54.67 million for strengthening its communicable disease prevention task force.

Katsina provided N50 million for an infectious disease fund and another N50 million for communicable disease control. Sokoto allocated N500 million as counterpart funding for health emergencies, N73 million in recurrent funding for the Infectious Disease Hospital in Amanawa and N75 million for an ambulance for the hospital. The budgets also contain provisions for equipment and community-level prevention.

In the South-east, Abia allocated N4.5 million for research on vaccine hesitancy and disease burden, N4.5 million for an electronic surveillance system for communicable diseases and N10 million for distributing buckets with taps to 903 primary healthcare centres.

Anambra provided N90 million for a disease control and surveillance centre, N10 million for controlling emerging communicable diseases and N15 million for surveillance and epidemic response equipment.

Ebonyi allocated N15 million for equipment for emergency response to epidemic disease control. Imo’s N500 million provision is specifically for operational funding for its COVID-19 emergency operations centre. The existing centre could potentially support an Ebola response, depending on its capacity and readiness.

In the South-west, Ondo’s appropriation includes N95 million for disease outbreak monitoring, response and free health commodities, N60 million for emergency preparedness and disease surveillance, and N13.6 million for procuring 10,000 personal protective equipment items. Osun allocated N119.7 million for communicable diseases, while Oyo provided N38 million for a responsive public health emergency preparedness system.

Bayelsa budgeted N30 million for research and development into early warning systems and integrated national disease surveillance. Niger State’s 2026 budget includes N860 million for a USAID grant-related consortium programme focused on universal health coverage, malaria and other communicable diseases.

Nasarawa allocated N590 million for vehicles, an ambulance, isolation ward equipment, oxygen and medical air plants, and other infrastructure at the state’s Infectious Diseases, Diagnosis and Research Centre in Lafia. The budget also includes N4 million for communicable diseases and N7 million for disease surveillance, prevention and control.

This review did not identify a relevant emergency allocation in Ekiti’s approved 2026 budget. The state may have provisions for health emergencies under other headings, but the review could not identify an allocation for that purpose. The 2026 approved budgets for Rivers State and the Federal Capital Territory were not publicly available for this review.

Why the money must translate into operational capacity

The NCDC’s preparedness guidance identifies several requirements for responding to Ebola, including early detection, isolation and referral, laboratory diagnosis, contact tracing, infection prevention and control, risk communication, and protection for health workers.

These activities require more than construction projects. They depend on trained surveillance officers, functioning reporting systems, reliable transport, protective equipment, access to testing and facilities capable of safely managing suspected cases.

Nigeria’s experience in 2014 illustrates the importance of these systems. After an infected traveller arrived in Lagos, cases were subsequently recorded in Port Harcourt. Nigeria recorded 20 cases and eight deaths before transmission was interrupted.

The outbreak demonstrated the importance of quickly identifying exposed people, tracing their contacts, isolating cases and coordinating public health action across jurisdictions.

The recent Ebola case has not been reported to have spread across Nigeria. Preparedness measures are designed to prevent an imported infection from developing into sustained community transmission.

Koko Udo, a director of Bestway Initiative for Health, Education and Self Sufficiency, who holds a PhD in virology, said the immediate question for state governments was whether the systems provided for in their budgets were operational and accessible when needed.

“A state may have a designated infectious disease hospital, but do they have trained staff, suitable isolation arrangements, adequate protective equipment and the ability to refer patients safely?” he said.

Mr Udo said an emergency operations centre should be assessed on its staffing, communications, surveillance links and capacity to coordinate a response, rather than its mere inclusion in a budget.

“There is need for states to learn from the 2014 Ebola and Covid-19 outbreak. The state governments need to release money for these preparations immediately,” he said.

Mr Udo said surveillance funding should translate into health workers who could recognise suspected cases, report them promptly and receive support to investigate alerts. He also called for clear procedures for releasing emergency funds to prevent avoidable administrative delays in procurement and deployment.

He urged the NCDC and federal health authorities to publish state-by-state preparedness assessments identifying gaps and the support needed to address them. Such assessments, he said, would help the public distinguish states with functioning emergency systems from those whose provisions existed only on paper.

The legal and policy frameworks provide a basis for coordinated disease surveillance and response. The 2026 approved budgets show how state governments have chosen to fund parts of that responsibility. Neither the frameworks nor the allocations establish that the systems are working.

As Nigeria responds to its latest Ebola threat, the test is not simply which governor has announced the largest allocation or which state has budgeted for the most expensive infectious disease facility.

It is whether a health worker who encounters a patient with symptoms consistent with Ebola knows what to do, whether the alert reaches the relevant authorities promptly, whether a response team can arrive without delay, and whether the state can isolate and refer the patient safely while protecting other patients and health workers.

This is because while Nigerians need to know what their governments budgeted for health emergencies, they also have to know what those funds have made possible.

World.title: Diri unveils AI robotic tutors in Bayelsa medical university
World.content:
Governor Douye Diri of Bayelsa State has unveiled Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered robotic tutors and other digital learning innovations at the Bayelsa Medical University (BMU), Yenagoa.

The News Agency of Nigeria reports that the initiative is part of the government’s efforts to advance medical education, research and technological development in Bayelsa.

The innovations were unveiled alongside the university’s 2025–2029 Strategic Plan on Monday in Yenagoa.

Mr Diri described the initiative as a significant step towards modernising medical education, saying that the digital tools must complement human instruction and make learning more interactive.

He urged the institution to deploy technology to improve teaching, learning and research without replacing physical classroom interactions and the mentorship role of lecturers.

He also challenged the university’s management to translate its strategic plan into measurable improvements in academic standards, research, infrastructure and the quality of graduates.

The governor reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to supporting BMU’s ASPIRE Agenda, which focuses on academic excellence, sustainability, partnerships and engagement, innovation and technology, as well as research excellence among others.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He commended the Vice-Chancellor, Dimie Ogoina, and the university management for developing a roadmap for institutional growth, charging them to collaborate with the state’s Ministries of Education and Health to achieve its objectives.

Mr Diri said his administration was strengthening science, technical and vocational education to equip young people with practical skills for employment, entrepreneurship and self-reliance.

He expressed confidence that the science-oriented schools being established across the state would provide qualified candidates for BMU and other tertiary institutions.

According to him, this will help the state to produce more doctors, nurses, pharmacists, radiologists, engineers and other professionals.

The governor acknowledged the late governor Diepreye Alamieyeseigha, who initiated the development of the former 500-bed hospital where the university is located, and his successor, Seriake Dickson, who revived the project and transformed it into the medical university.

He disclosed that the university’s campus at Sampou was nearing completion and would provide additional space for its expansion.

Mr Diri also inspected facilities at the newly established Bayelsa Medical University Teaching Hospital and expressed confidence in the institution’s capacity to provide advanced diagnostic services.

He said the teaching hospital was equipped to conduct x-rays and advanced scans, including Computed Tomography (CT) scans, which use x-ray technology and computer processing to produce detailed images of internal body structures.

The governor said the availability of such facilities would improve access to specialised diagnostic services and reduce the need for Bayelsans to travel outside the state for certain medical procedures.

Mr Diri also undertook a tour of facilities at the Bayelsa Emergency Medical Services and Ambulance System.

My vision for the university – VC

Earlier, the Vice-Chancellor, Mr Ogoina, said his vision was to transform the school into a globally recognised institution for medical education, research and innovation, driven by technology and sustainability.

He explained that the ASPIRE Agenda was being implemented through institutional teams and initiatives designed to improve academic quality, accountability, innovation and student welfare.

The vice-chancellor disclosed that the university had secured accreditation for nine academic programmes while its nursing science students recorded a 96 per cent pass rate in their professional examinations.

He also revealed that the university’s College of Medicine had attained full membership of the Consortium of Medical Schools of Africa while BMU was selected as one of 18 medical schools in Nigeria for a high-impact intervention programme.

On digital innovation, Mr Ogoina said the university had established a virtual reality, artificial intelligence and mixed-reality studio, expanded digital connectivity and introduced a “Talk to the VC” application to enable students and staff communicate directly and confidentially with the university leadership.

He added that the institution was strengthening simulation-based learning through its clinical skills laboratory and pursuing plans to develop a smart campus, improve internet connectivity and increase internally generated revenue.

“The BMU is developing a Centre of Excellence for Digital Health and Biomedical Innovation, alongside the Niger Delta Centre of Excellence for Health, Environment and Development to address regional health and environmental challenges,” he said.

World.title: 2027: FOOG women DG urges Nigerians to support Tinubu’s re-election bid
World.content:
Chief (Mrs) Esther Orighomisan Okotie-Eboh, Director-General of FOOG Women Support for Tinubu, has called on Nigerians to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027, urging critics of the administration to present credible alternatives to its policies.

Okotie-Eboh said those opposing the Tinubu administration should go beyond criticism and explain how their proposed policies would improve the lives of Nigerians.

She argued that political opponents had a responsibility to provide concrete reasons for rejecting the government’s programmes and demonstrate what they would do differently if elected.

According to her, critics should be able to present at least five to 10 clear reasons for their positions, rather than engage in endless consultations and political discussions without offering practical solutions.

She maintained that Nigerians deserved constructive political engagement backed by workable policies and measurable commitments.

The FOOG Women Support for Tinubu director-general also cautioned against comparing the Tinubu administration directly with previous governments, arguing that each administration faced peculiar challenges that required different approaches.

According to her, differences in prevailing circumstances, economic realities and governance challenges should be taken into consideration when assessing the performance of successive administrations.

She maintained that the Tinubu administration should be assessed within the context of the challenges confronting it and the policies being implemented to address them.

Okotie-Eboh likened governance to building a house, stressing that a solid foundation and a clear plan were necessary to achieve lasting results.

“Governance is like building a house. You must first lay a solid foundation and have a clear plan before you can complete the building,” she said.

She added that abandoning a project halfway through could undermine the desired outcome, arguing that the Tinubu administration should be given the opportunity to implement its policies and deliver on its promises.

Okotie-Eboh further maintained that governments needed sufficient time and space to execute their programmes and address the challenges confronting their countries.

Citing developments in other parts of the world, including the United States and efforts to resolve the Russia-Ukraine war, she argued that governance required continuity and sustained efforts to achieve meaningful progress.

She warned against what she described as a tendency to move backwards by constantly disrupting the process of governance, insisting that elected administrations should be assessed based on their performance and tangible results.

According to her, Nigerians should critically examine the alternatives being proposed by opposition politicians before deciding whether to support a change of government.

“The question Nigerians should ask is simple: what are the alternatives being offered by those criticising the government? Let them tell us what they intend to do, how they plan to do it and how their proposals will improve the lives of ordinary citizens,” she said.

She stressed that anyone seeking the mandate of Nigerians must be prepared to articulate clear policies and demonstrate how such policies would translate into better governance.

Okotie-Eboh maintained that the country needed issue-based political engagement rather than rhetoric, adding that Nigerians deserved concrete policies, clear explanations and measurable results from those seeking public office.

She therefore called on Nigerians to support Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027, saying continuity would give the administration the opportunity to pursue its programmes and work towards achieving its objectives.

End

World.title: 2027: APC dismisses NDC’s allegation of blocking venues, billboards for campaign
World.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi, Cynthia Alo & Kafayat Kokumo

ABUJA — The Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, has accused the All Progressives Congress, APC, of frustrating its campaign preparations ahead of the 2027 general elections by allegedly denying it access to event venues and billboards.

National Publicity Secretary of the NDC, Osa Director, made the allegation during an interview on ARISE TV yesterday, insisting that the party will not be intimidated or prevented from exercising its democratic rights.

He said the party had encountered difficulties securing venues despite making payments, adding that its latest venue was the fourth it had attempted to use for its planned activities.

“This is the fourth venue we are paying for. We kept this one under wraps until just a few hours ago when we issued the press release, only for us to be called that the political marauders have come and said they are the owners of the land, so we should take back our money,” he said.

He added that the party will proceed with its activities, despite the alleged restrictions, insisting that no individual or political party owned the country.

“Nigeria belongs to us all. Nobody owns Nigeria. We fought, we used our life and sweat and blood to fight for this democracy we are enjoying today. So who is that person to tell me that I will not have a right to exercise my freedom of speech and freedom of assembly?” he said.

The NDC spokesman also alleged that the party had been denied access to billboards but maintained that such restrictions would not prevent it from reaching voters.

Speaking on the party’s campaign preparations, Director dismissed suggestions that the NDC was starting late, saying its presidential candidate had already held several town hall meetings across the country.

He said the party had held at least four meetings and had nearly completed its engagements across the zones, arguing that its approach differed from campaigns focused on rallies, music and public displays.

The party was scheduled to inaugurate its national campaign council, commission its newly acquired national secretariat in Jabi, Abuja, and present certificates of return to its candidates yesterday,

the spokesman said the certificates were part of a formal process, adding that the candidates had already been uploaded to the Independent National Electoral Commission’s portal.

He also announced that the party would publicly present a statement of its finances and challenged the APC to do the same, saying Nigerians would be surprised by the figures.

He defended the party’s anti-defection oath, adding that it was intended to address political defections and what he described as irresponsible politicking.

Osa Directoralso said members dissatisfied with the outcome of party primaries had the constitutional right to seek redress in court.

Director dismissed allegations that the party’s National Leader, Senator Seriake Dickson, was working for the ruling party, describing the claims as baseless.

He further claimed that Peter Obi was the preferred candidate of many Nigerians. And warned that any attempt to restrict the political space could force some democracy advocates to return to the kind of guerrilla journalism practised under military rule.

APC rejects NDC’s claim of blocked campaign venues as baseless

Reacting to the allegation, the All Progressives Congress, APC, dismissed it, asking whether Nigerians were in kindergarten to be treated to such baseless allegations.

The official, who spoke anonymously, said the NDC had not said which state or which ministry was involved.

“You want us to be responding to such baseless allegations? The party will not. Are we in kindergarten? Which state? Which ministry denied them the use of facilities?” he queried.

World.title: NYSC, UNN disowned ex-minister Uche Nnaji’s certificates, ICPC witness tells court
World.content:
An investigator with the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC), Yakubu Ibrahim, on Monday, told a Federal High Court in Abuja that both the University of Nigeria (UNN) and the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) disowned the degree and discharge certificates presented by former Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology, Uche Nnaji, to the Senate for his ministerial screening in 2023.

The witness, Suprintendent of Police, Yakubu Ibrahim, testified as the first prosecution witness in the trial of Nnaji, who is facing a six-count charge marked FHC/ABJ/CR/389/2026, bordering on alleged corruption, fraud, conferring corrupt advantage and providing false information through the alleged presentation of forged university degree and national service certificates.

The investigator, who was led in evidence by the prosecution counsel, J. A. Mumini (SAN), said he was part of the ICPC team that investigated two petitions against the defendant.

The witness said his team was assigned to investigate the matter after the commission received two separate petitions alleging certificate forgery against Nnaji.

He said the Chairman of the Special Task Force directed an investigation, prompting the commission to request relevant documents from the National Assembly, the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), University of Nigeria, Nsukka and the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC).

He told the court that the team wrote to UNN to authenticate the Bachelor of Science certificate in Microbiology/Biochemistry allegedly submitted by Nnaji to the Senate.

According to him, the university responded that it did not issue the certificate to the governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Enugu for the 2027 election.

The witness added that the team also contacted the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) over a discharge certificate 15th May 1986, but the NYSC equally disowned it, maintaining that it did not issue any such certificate to the ex-minister.

Ibrahim further told the court that UNN supplied the investigators with the defendant’s academic records, including a notice of withdrawal issued over his failure to obtain the required grade in a course.

When shown copies of the correspondence between the ICPC and the two institutions, the witness identified the documents, following which the prosecution sought to tender them in evidence.

Defence counsel, Wole Olanipekun (SAN), said he would allow the documents to be admitted at that stage but reserve his objection until later.

On the steps taken to interview the defendant, Ibrahim said the head of his section issued an invitation, but investigators could not locate his address.

He said a copy of the invitation, dated May 5, 2026, was subsequently sent to the defendant’s email address and WhatsApp number.

According to the witness, after Nnaji failed to honour the invitation, the ICPC liaised with the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) to effect his arrest on July 1.

He added that the defendant was questioned and made statements dated July 1 and 2.

During cross-examination by Olanipekun, the witness admitted that he did not visit UNN during the investigation and did not know the faculty to which the defendant had been admitted.

He, however, said members of the investigating team interviewed the university’s Registrar.

Asked whether the team established where the alleged certificates were forged, Ibrahim said he did not know.

He also said the defendant made no comment on the allegations when questioned by investigators.

On whether the team investigated where Nnaji undertook his national service, the witness said it did not because the NYSC had stated that it did not issue the certificate.

“The NYSC said the certificate was not issued by it, which was why we didn’t inquire where he served,” he told the court.

The witness also confirmed seeing a notice of withdrawal supplied by UNN. When asked to identify it, he identified the document, marked Exhibit C, dated November 7, 1984.

He said the university explained in its letter the policy governing the grades required for the award of a certificate saying if one failed four times, the person was not qualified.

Ibrahim said Nnaji failed at two stages and did not write the examination at the third stage for medical reasons.

“The witness said, “the defendant went ahead to write the supplementary examination for which he did not register.”

Ibrahim further testified that UNN confirmed that the BSc certificate in Microbiology and Biochemistry attributed to the defendant was not issued by the university.

Olanipekun suggested that a subsequent letter dated March 18, 1985, rescinded the earlier withdrawal notice. Ibrahim agreed, adding that the withdrawal notice related to a course in General Microbiology.

The witness also told the court that investigators did not establish the number of years a student studying Microbiology was expected to spend at the university.

At the conclusion of cross-examination, the prosecution did not re-examine the witness, following which Justice Joyce Abdulmalik discharged him and adjourned further hearing until November 3.

Meanwhile, it is recalled that Nnaji, who resigned as minister following the certificates forgery scandal did not include the controversial degree certificate in his Independent National Electoral Commissioner (INEC) filing ahead of the 2027 election in which he flies the flag of the PDP.

World.title: El Niño: What it means and how Nigerians should prepare
World.content:
By Sekinat Osundiji

Nigeria may experience increased heat and changing rainfall patterns as a strengthening El Niño event raises concerns about its potential effects on agriculture, water supply, electricity generation and public health.

The World Meteorological Organisation (WMO) said in September 2026 that El Niño was expected to strengthen into a very strong event and persist into early 2027. The Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet) has also warned that the phenomenon could affect rainfall patterns, including the length of the rainy season and when it ends.

But what is El Niño, how could it affect Nigeria, and what can the country do to prepare?

What is El Niño?

El Niño is a natural climate phenomenon that occurs when surface waters in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean become warmer than average.

This warming affects atmospheric circulation, changing weather patterns around the world. Depending on the region, it can contribute to higher temperatures, reduced or excessive rainfall, and shifts in seasonal conditions.

El Niño is part of the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), a climate pattern that also includes La Niña, its cooler phase, and neutral conditions.

According to the WMO, El Niño typically occurs every two to seven years and lasts between nine and 12 months. Although it develops thousands of kilometres from Nigeria, its influence on global atmospheric circulation can affect weather in West Africa. However, its effects vary by location and do not automatically mean drought or extreme heat everywhere.

What does El Niño mean for Nigeria?

NiMet’s August 2026 seasonal climate update identified the onset of a strong El Niño event and outlined possible implications for rainfall, agriculture, water resources and energy.

For August to October 2026, the agency forecast normal to above-normal rainfall across much of northern Nigeria, while parts of the South-West and Cross River State were expected to experience normal to below-normal rainfall.

These projections highlight the possibility of different weather outcomes across the country.

1. Higher temperatures and health risks

One major concern is the possibility of increased heat. In October 2026, the Climate Impact Lab projected that Nigeria could record an additional 31,400 heat-related deaths between September 2026 and February 2027, compared with an average year.

The figure is a model-based estimate of potential excess deaths, not a confirmed death toll or a certainty that those deaths will occur.

Extreme heat can cause dehydration, heat exhaustion and potentially fatal heatstroke, particularly among children, older people and outdoor workers.

Health authorities should strengthen public awareness campaigns, issue timely heat warnings and prepare health facilities for heat-related emergencies. Residents should drink water regularly, seek shade, limit strenuous outdoor activities during the hottest hours where possible, and check on vulnerable relatives and neighbours.

2. Agriculture and food production

Changes in rainfall can disrupt planting schedules and crop development. Prolonged dry spells or an early end to the rainy season could reduce yields, while excessive rainfall may cause flooding and damage farms.

NiMet has identified possible agricultural risks in areas expecting below-normal rainfall, including parts of Borno and Yobe.

Farmers should monitor updated forecasts, consider early-maturing or drought-tolerant crop varieties where appropriate, and seek advice from agricultural extension officers. In areas expecting heavier rainfall, maintaining drainage channels can help limit damage.

Government agencies should also improve farmers’ access to timely weather information and agricultural advice.

3. Water supply and electricity generation

Prolonged rainfall deficits can reduce river flows, reservoir levels and groundwater recharge, putting pressure on domestic water supplies and irrigation.

Hydropower generation could also be affected if water inflows into dams decline. NiMet has identified reduced water availability and lower reservoir inflows as potential risks, although these do not confirm nationwide water shortages or electricity disruptions.

Water authorities should monitor reservoirs and groundwater conditions, identify vulnerable communities and develop contingency plans. Residents can help by repairing leaking taps and avoiding unnecessary water waste.

4. Food prices and household expenses

Adverse weather could reduce agricultural output, damage farms and disrupt transportation, placing pressure on food supplies and prices.

However, El Niño alone does not mean food prices will rise nationwide. Harvests, storage, transport costs and wider market conditions will also influence prices.

The government should monitor food supplies, support farmers in vulnerable areas and strengthen storage and distribution systems to reduce avoidable losses.

How should Nigeria prepare?

Preparation requires coordinated action by government agencies, state authorities, farmers, health workers, businesses and residents.

NiMet should continue issuing updated, location-specific forecasts and ensure warnings reach rural communities and farmers, including those without reliable internet access.

Health authorities should educate the public on heat-related illnesses and strengthen emergency responses, particularly for vulnerable populations.

Agricultural ministries and extension officers should provide advice on planting dates, crop selection, irrigation and drainage based on current forecasts.

Water agencies should monitor dams and reservoirs, reduce distribution losses and plan for communities that may face shortages. Authorities must also prepare for heavy rainfall and flooding rather than focus exclusively on drought.

Government agencies, broadcasters and journalists should communicate climate information clearly, distinguish projections from confirmed events and update the public as conditions change.

Does El Niño mean Nigeria is heading for disaster?

Not necessarily. El Niño increases the likelihood of certain climate-related impacts but does not determine precisely what will happen in every state.

The WMO has emphasised that even a very strong event does not produce equally severe effects everywhere. Local weather patterns and other climate drivers can alter its influence.

Nigeria’s priority should be to identify areas most vulnerable to heat and rainfall changes and prepare accordingly. Following NiMet’s updates and taking practical precautions can help reduce risks to public health, agriculture, water resources and electricity generation.

Ultimately, the challenge is not simply how strong El Niño becomes, but how effectively Nigeria prepares for its potential consequences.

World.title: Ifeanyi Okoye emerges 12th President of MAN
World.content:
By Yinka Kolawole

The Manufacturers Association of Nigeria (MAN) has elected Dr. Ifeanyi Okoye, Chief Executive Officer of Juhel Nigeria Limited, as its 12th President .

He succeeds Otunba Francis Meshioye, who completed his four-year tenure at the recently-concluded 54th Annual General Meeting of the association held on 7th October 2026 in Lagos.

A statement by Director General of MAN, Segun Ajayi-Kadir, noted that Okoye holds a Bachelor’s degree in Pharmacy from the University of Ife (now Obafemi Awolowo University) with a Bachelor’s degree in Pharmacy and an M.Sc. and PhD in Pharmaceutical Technology and Industrial Pharmacy from the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, graduating as the best student in his class.

He established JUHEL Nigeria Limited in 1987, a wholly indigenous pharmaceutical manufacturing company with headquarters in Enugu, Enugu State, and moved to its permanent site in Emene, Enugu, in 2001 with facilities expanded to include syrups and capsules. In 2010, JUHEL opened a major parenteral manufacturing facility in Awka, Anambra State.

Okoye is a Fellow of the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria and an alumnus of Harvard Business School in Boston, USA. He attended the National Institute for Policy and Strategic Studies in Kuru, Plateau State, and was conferred the national honour of Officer of the Order of the Federal Republic (OFR) in 2012.

He has served on several committees, including the Ministerial Committee on the Establishment of World-Class Hospitals and Diagnostic Centers from 2013 to 2015; Member of the Governing Council of the Standard Organization of Nigeria (SON) – 2009 to 2022.

Before he was elected President, Okoye served MAN in various capacities, including as Chairman of the Enugu, Anambra and Ebonyi States Branches from 1998 to 2005, and as Vice President from 2006 to 2010.

World.title: Oil spill in Odidi: Is an end finally in sight?
World.content:
•It’s serious, 216 communities affected — Gov Oborevwori •Orders Health Commissioner to deliver medicare •Says Heritage Energy must keep to October deadline

By Jimitota Onoyume, Assistant News Editor

Has an end finally come for the nearly nine-month crude oil spill in Odidi community, Warri South-West Local Government Area of Delta State?

That is the question on the lips of many residents and natives of the area following Governor Sheriff Oborevwori’s charge to Heritage Energy Operational Services Limited, HEOSL, to ensure that the company keeps its promise to redress the devastating situation this October.

General Manager, Operations Integrity, HEOSL, Nelson Wilbert, had assured that the company was committed to bringing the spill to an end, saying it would work with relevant stakeholders to achieve this. Wilbert spoke when Governor Oborevwori visited the community for an on-the-spot assessment of the situation.

What the governor said he saw during the visit while addressing the community appeared far worse than the information he had earlier. After touring the affected areas, Oborevwori expressed shock at the magnitude of the pollution and the economic devastation it had caused.

He said he had initially been briefed that about 86 communities were affected, only to discover that the pollution had spread to as many as 216 communities along the coastal lines.

“We have come here to see and not just to get report in the office. The thing is spreading. When it started, it was 89 communities. Today from your record, you said 216 communities. We believe there are small small villages that are affected and not captured,“ the governor said.

Deeply moved by compassion, he immediately directed his Commissioner for Health, Dr. Joseph Onojaemo to provide urgent medicare for residents of the affected communities, stressing that the intervention of his administration would go beyond the distribution of relief materials, given the severity of the situation.

“We have to take this matter seriously. Once you see what is happening, you realise that it is a very big issue. We don’t want our people dying at this time. We cannot afford to lose our focus or waste time. We have to act quickly and decisively,” he said.
