The governor also directed Heritage to provide medical support services in the affected areas, insisting that residents should be medically examined to determine the possible health implications of prolonged exposure to the pollution.

He ordered the Commissioner for Health, Dr. Onojaemo to immediately deploy and coordinate medical teams to the affected communities and ensure that necessary medications are made available.

Oborevwori further warned that the state government would not sleep over the matter until the company fulfilled its promise to redress the problem this month, instructing his Commissioner for Environment, Hon. Moses Ogodo, to keep his eyes on development in the area .

He also called for genuine dialogue between the company and the host communities to resolve the crisis and prevent further tension.

For the governor, the crisis goes beyond compensation. It is about restoring the environment, protecting lives and rescuing the livelihoods of people whose economic activities depend largely on the waters.

The spill, which according to community folks started in February from the Trans-Forcados Trunkline, has brought economic activities in Odidi and surrounding communities to a near standstill. Long before the governor’s visit, residents who spoke with Vanguard described the situation as a prolonged nightmare, saying their lives had been turned upside down by the heavily polluted waters.

Aquatic life, they said, had been severely affected, while farms had also not been spared. Fishermen, women who trade in fishes and other seafood, and others whose livelihoods depend on the waterways said they had been left with little or nothing to do.

“The spill has forced us to remain at home in the last nine months. No river to fish or even periwinkle to pick,” Agnes and others told Vanguard. Residents also alleged that a sexagenarian died few months ago after slipping and hitting her head on hard ground while attempting to walk across a surface stained with the crude oil.

“We don’t know what we can call this. Our people are dying; we can’t breathe. Recently, we lost one of our aunties. She fell and couldn’t breathe again because of the pollution. We need the federal, state and local governments to come to our aid,” a woman in the area said.

“Life has not been the same in the community in the last nine months,” a woman identified as Timi said.

Timi said she eventually relocated to Warri in search of something to do after waiting endlessly for the situation to be resolved.

Amid the prolonged crisis, residents have also raised concerns over alleged oil theft around the affected oil facilities.

Some community members alleged that oil thieves may have taken advantage of the situation to siphon crude, although they admitted that they could not confirm the allegation or identify those allegedly involved.

One resident, who spoke on condition of anonymity, alleged that boats sometimes come to the area to evacuate crude under the guise of protecting the environment.

“They come there with boats to remove crude oil; where do they take the crude to?” he asked as he gazed into the air as though the answer was visibly there.

The allegation, whether eventually established or not, has added another layer of concern to an already troubling situation and heightened calls for greater transparency around activities at the affected facilities.

For the people of Odidi and the other affected communities, however, the immediate concern is simple: they want the oil to stop flowing and their lives to begin again.

They say Heritage’s promise to end the spill will only become something to celebrate when the pollution is actually stopped, the affected environment is properly remediated and efforts are made to restore the aquatic life on which thousands depend.

Now, with October fast coming to an end and the governor demanding action, the question is no longer merely when the promise will be fulfilled. Will October finally bring an end to Odidi’s agonising oil-spill nightmare, or will the month slide away with the promise being yet another chapter in a crisis that has already lasted almost nine months?

World.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, October 27, 2026
World.content:
Trading in Nigeria’s foreign exchange market opened with the local currency displaying subtle fluctuations against the United States dollar across both official and unofficial channels.

At the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), the naira opened around N1,339.93 to the dollar, reflecting minor adjustments during early morning trading. This follows recent sessions where the official rate navigated pressure from elevated dollar demand, lingering near the N1,330 to N1,360 threshold.

In the parallel market, currency operators in major hubs like Lagos and Abuja continue to quote wider spreads due to immediate liquidity needs. Independent dealers reported buying rates floating around N1,370 per dollar, while selling rates averaged between N1,380 and N1,385 per dollar.

Market participants note that overall liquidity conditions remain tied to foreign capital inflows and central bank intervention strategies. Although foreign reserves maintain a stable buffer above $55 billion, ongoing demand from importers and domestic businesses keeps pressure steady across all FX segments.

World.title: At Economic Summit, Tinubu Says the Nigerian Story is Being Rewritten
World.content:
• Oyedele unveils policy framework to ring-fence economic policies against reversals

•Abubakar Bagudu: Tinubu won’t reverse economic reforms

• Chukwuma Soludo: lack of local patronage costs Nigeria 10 million jobs, says 12% annual growth needed to achieve $1 trillion economy, 8% acceleration to address poverty

Deji Elumoye and James Emejo in Abuja





President Bola Tinubu yesterday said his government was rewriting Nigeria’s decades-long story of economic underperformance through far-reaching reforms designed to dismantle structural barriers, unlock the nation’s enormous potential, and deliver jobs, productivity, and shared prosperity.

Tinubu said rewriting the story of a nation that had performed below its potential for far too long was what the administration came into office to achieve:

The president spoke in Abuja while formally declaring open the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit (NES#32), with the theme, “Growth that Works: Delivering Jobs, Productivity and Shared Prosperity.”

At the summit, Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Mr. Taiwo Oyedele, presented the Nigerian Economic Policy Framework, which he described as a national economic doctrine establishing how Nigeria made economic decisions and measured real progress.

Oyedele said the blueprint aimed at curbing arbitrary policy changes.

Minister of Budget and Economic Planning, Senator Abubakar Bagudu, ruled out a return to petrol subsidy, insisting that the Tinubu administration will sustain its economic reforms, despite mounting pressure on households and businesses.

Bagudu told the conference that reversing reforms would undermine efforts to address longstanding distortions.

Governor of Anambra State, Professor Chukwuma Charles Soludo, said lack of local patronage of Made-in-Nigeria products had robbed the country of 10 million potential jobs, adding that everyone has a role to play in boosting growth.

Soludo said the economy needed between seven and nine per cent annual growth rate to address multidimensional poverty.

Tinubu, who was represented at NES#32 by Vice President Kashim Shettima, stated that his government began on a difficult note because there was no shortcut to economic growth.

He stated, “Distinguished ladies and gentlemen, we came to rewrite the story of a nation that has performed below its potential for far too long. But there is no shortcut to economic growth. This is why we began with a difficult reset. For us, rescuing the economy means rescuing livelihoods and transforming the fortunes of young jobseekers, farmers, manufacturers, entrepreneurs and innovators.

“We cannot harness the immense opportunities offered by our growing population without first stabilising the economy. We must also create the conditions for the public and private sectors to invest, expand and generate productive employment.”

Tinubu observed that the summit’s theme, “Growth That Works: Delivering Jobs, Productivity and Shared Prosperity,” built on the ambition of the previous edition of the annual event to achieve a prosperous and inclusive Nigeria by 2030.

He stated that his administration had “since set in motion a series of reforms to dismantle the structural barriers that have prevented our abundant human and natural resources from yielding prosperity”.

The president said, “These reforms are restoring confidence, strengthening our economic foundations and laying the groundwork for sustainable growth.”

He added that the administration was encouraged by what it had accomplished so far.

Acknowledging that creating jobs was only half the task, the president stressed the need to “improve the quality of work, reduce underemployment and harness the potential” of the country’s underutilised workforce.

He stated, “Our pursuit of prosperity demands greater productivity from every worker, enterprise and investment. We must judge infrastructure by the economic activity it generates and education by the skills and productivity it delivers.

“We must judge industrial policy by the competitiveness of our firms and investment incentives by the capital, technology, exports and jobs they attract.”

Tinubu outlined the achievements of his administration’s reforms, saying they have been well documented. He cited figures from the National Bureau of Statistics indicating that Nigeria’s inflation-adjusted GDP grew by 3.89 per cent in the first quarter of 2026, compared with 3.13 per cent a year earlier.

On economic diversification, he stated that “non-oil activities accounted for 96.08 per cent of GDP, while manufacturing grew by 3.29 per cent and the oil sector by 2.57 per cent”.

He emphasised that the gains had reinforced his administration’s confidence in the path of recovery and diversification.

The president stated, however, that his administration’s ambition must go beyond favourable statistics, even as the development narrative was changing and investor confidence was returning.

Outlining the administration’s gains so far, he said, “In the first quarter of 2026, our capital importation reached $10.37 billion, an increase of 83.83 per cent over the corresponding period in 2025. This comprised both portfolio and foreign direct investment. We will, therefore, continue to ease regulatory burdens, strengthen transparency and policy predictability, and expand access to finance.

“Our tax reforms seek to build a modern, equitable system that finances development and gives businesses certainty. This discipline must guide our investments in all sectors of the economy, including energy, agriculture and solid minerals. We are reforming the electricity market to improve supply and attract investment in generation, transmission, distribution and alternative energy.”

On agriculture, Tinubu said the administration was connecting farms to storage facilities, processing centres, and markets, while expanding irrigation, mechanisation, finance, and rural infrastructure.

He added that the government was also seeking “to move beyond extraction into domestic processing, industrial production and exports” in the solid minerals sector.

The president, however, stated that despite the gains of his administration’s economic reforms, the task remained far from finished, even as young Nigerians had demonstrated their capacity to compete globally in technology, financial services, and the creative industries.

Oyedele unveils framework to guard against policy reversals

Oyedele, at the summit, presented the Nigerian Economic Policy Framework, saying it is a national economic doctrine that establishes how Nigeria makes economic decisions and measures progress.

He said the plan aimed to curb arbitrary policy reversals, reduce uncertainty for businesses, and ensure economic reforms delivered measurable improvements in jobs, household incomes, and productivity.

He said the economic doctrine was intended to outlive successive administrations.

The minister stated that Nigeria’s persistent development challenges stemmed not from a shortage of economic plans but from inconsistent policymaking, weak implementation, and the tendency of successive governments to reverse or undermine previous reforms.

According to him, policy uncertainty imposes an invisible cost on businesses, discourages investment, raises the cost of capital and prevents potential employment opportunities from materialising.

Oyedele said, “Governments will come. Governments will go. But Nigeria’s economic horizon must outlive every electoral calendar.”

The proposed framework is intended to establish enduring principles for economic decision-making, rather than serve as another development plan, catalogue of government projects, or manifesto of an administration.

Oyedele said the document was being released for public consultation and had not yet received government approval.

The consultation, which runs until November 27, 2026, will seek public input on 17 core questions through the Ministry of Finance’s website. Following validation, the framework will be presented to the Federal Executive Council (FEC) for approval and the National Economic Council (NEC) for endorsement.

A central feature of the proposal is a mandatory policy impact assessment for major economic interventions, including tax adjustments, tariff changes, regulatory restrictions and incentives.

Under the proposed arrangement, policymakers would be required to establish the problem a measure seeks to address, provide supporting evidence, identify its beneficiaries and those bearing its costs, and specify the conditions under which it would expire.

The framework also proposes an annual National Economic Scorecard, to be published on or before October 1, to track whether real wages are rising, productive employment is expanding, and poverty is declining.

Oyedele maintained that headline economic growth and investment announcements alone were insufficient measures of success, stating that economic performance must translate into tangible improvements in living standards.

He outlined seven interconnected priorities for the framework: stability, productivity, enterprise, capital, people, markets and institutions.

The minister identified private enterprise as the principal engine of economic growth, with government responsible for providing public goods, maintaining the rule of law, correcting market failures, and protecting vulnerable citizens.

He also advocated competitive markets, warning against using industrial policies and tariffs to shield inefficient businesses indefinitely from competition.

On coordination, Oyedele said government institutions must assess the cumulative burden of their policies on businesses instead of pursuing isolated departmental

The minister invited members of the Nigerian Economic Summit Group (NESG) and private sector experts to make valuable contributions to the development of the framework by rigorously critiquing the draft proposal with facts and figures.

He said the principles underpinning the framework included enterprise, open but fair markets, and whole-of-government coherence.

Bagudu Rules Out Return to Petrol Subsidy, Says Tinubu Won’t Reverse Reforms

Minister of Budget and Economic Planning, Senator Abubakar Bagudu, ruled out a return to petrol subsidy, insisting that the Tinubu administration will sustain its economic reforms, despite mounting pressure on households and businesses.

Bagudu, at NES#32, said reversing the reforms would undermine efforts to address longstanding economic distortions and stabilise the economy.

“For those of us serving under the president and vice president, the instruction has been clear: we must stay the course,” he said.

His position came amid opposition calls, including from the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, for the restoration of petrol subsidy to ease the rising cost of living.

Bagudu, however, acknowledged that sustaining the reforms would require improved implementation, responsive policy adjustments, and targeted interventions to cushion vulnerable Nigerians.

He said the government was focused on translating economic gains into jobs, higher productivity, and improved living standards, while strengthening domestic production and attracting investment.

The minister stated that increased revenue accruing to federal, state and local governments presented an opportunity to expand infrastructure and improve public services, stressing the need for stronger coordination among the three tiers of government.

He also reiterated Nigeria’s ambition to build a $1 trillion economy by 2030, saying this would require higher productivity, expanded industrial capacity, stronger private-sector participation, and a more competitive business environment.

Bagudu identified agriculture, manufacturing, digital technology, and human capital development as key drivers of the administration’s growth strategy.

He said the Renewed Hope Ward Development Plan would unlock productive opportunities across Nigeria’s 8,809 wards through targeted interventions based on local economic strengths, including agriculture, fishing, livestock, and textiles.

On agriculture, Bagudu highlighted the need for improved access to financing, mechanisation, irrigation, processing, storage and markets to boost production, reduce post-harvest losses, and improve food affordability.

He also cited the Nigeria Industrial Policy 2025 and Nigeria First Policy as initiatives aimed at strengthening local manufacturing and supply chains.

Bagudu highlighted a proposed 90,000-kilometre fibre-optic infrastructure initiative, being pursued with the European Union and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, to expand broadband connectivity.

He called for improved access to finance for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, including through a proposed credit guarantee framework, while urging public- and private-sector stakeholders to mobilise investment to close Nigeria’s development financing gap.

Soludo: Poor Patronage of Local Products Costs Nigeria 10m Jobs

Soludo said limited local patronage of Made-in-Nigeria products was costing the country about 10 million potential jobs.

The former CBN governor said while the current stability must not be take for granted, the country should not be carried away by the euphoria of massive huge currency appreciation.

He said the current growth was not sufficient to eliminate poverty, adding that the economy needs to grow between seven and nine per cent per annual to address poverty.

Among other things, he said growth needed to average 12 per cent annually to achieve the proposed $1 trillion economy by 2030.

According to him, the average Nigerian still lives on less than $1 per day, urging coordination and collaboration between federal and states governments to rein in inflation and attract investments into the country.

Rabiu Seeks 100 More Major Industrial Firms, Cites FX Reforms

Rabiu commended the economic reforms of the Tinubu administration, saying they have begun to address longstanding challenges confronting Nigerian businesses.

He acknowledged the difficulties experienced by ordinary Nigerians but stated that improvements in access to foreign exchange had created a more predictable environment for businesses.

He called for policy consistency, affordable long-term financing and improved infrastructure to accelerate industrialisation, warning that uncertainty in the business environment can undermine investments requiring decades to deliver returns.

He stressed that the success of Nigeria’s economic reforms would depend on the government’s ability to create conditions that enable businesses to expand production, create jobs, and compete effectively.

“We cannot expect businesses to make 20-year investments if they cannot plan with confidence beyond the next few years,” he said.

The industrialist identified high borrowing costs and limited access to long-term capital as major constraints preventing small businesses from evolving into large-scale manufacturing concerns.

He explained that industrial investments typically required substantial upfront spending on land, factories, equipment, workforce development, and production, often years before businesses begin to realise significant returns.

“You cannot build a strong industrial economy primarily with expensive short-term finances,” he said.

Rabiu said the next phase of reform must focus on expanding productive capacity and building more big Nigerian businesses capable of competing internationally.

He said foreign-exchange reforms had eased a major constraint for industrialists, who previously had to lobby the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) for dollar allocations even when they had the naira to pay for imports.

Businesses can now obtain foreign exchange through the market, he said, describing the change as a significant improvement for companies seeking machinery and industrial inputs.

The BUA chairman cited the cement industry’s transition from heavy dependence on imports to domestic self-sufficiency and net exports as evidence of what sustained investment and local production could achieve.

He challenged Nigeria to develop 100 more major industrial companies across critical sectors, like manufacturing, agriculture, mining, technology and other sectors, stating that such businesses would generate jobs, support local suppliers and increase exports.

However, he identified expensive financing as a major obstacle, saying industrial projects often require 10 to 20 years to mature and could not be sustainably financed with costly, short-term loans.

He called on pension funds, insurance companies, banks, development finance institutions, and capital markets to channel more long-term funds into productive investment.

Rabiu also urged the government and private sector to agree on a new economic accord anchored on policy consistency, infrastructure, human-capital development, and shared prosperity.

He said, “For many years, one of the greatest challenges facing businesses was access to foreign exchange. You could have all the naira but be unable to obtain the foreign exchange needed to buy raw materials and machinery.”

Amina Mohammed Urges Consolidation of Economic Reforms

United Nations Deputy Secretary-General, Dr. Amina Mohammed, assessed the reforms implemented under the Tinubu administration, acknowledging the gains, while urging their urgent consolidation and stabilisation, as well as the effective management of expectations among citizens and other stakeholders.

Mohammed applauded the African Development Bank (AfDB) for its new financial architecture for development across the continent, particularly its prioritisation of financing programmes that targeted impactful development.

Dercon: Nigeria Must End Business Protection, Boost Non-Oil Exports to Drive Sustainable Development

In his keynote, Professor of Economic Policy at the University of Oxford/former Chief Economist for the UK’s Department for International Development, Stefan Dercon, said macroeconomic stabilisation must be followed by a credible growth strategy capable of raising incomes and expanding economic opportunities.

Dercon stated that Nigeria’s income per capita remained around its 2010 level, stressing that the country needs a broader development bargain linking government, businesses, and citizens around measurable economic objectives.

He advocated stronger non-oil exports, lower trade barriers, and time-bound incentives that reward firms for becoming competitive rather than protecting them indefinitely.

He said Nigeria should aim to at least double non-oil exports by the end of the next administration, while warning that import tariffs could also raise costs for exporters who depend on imported inputs.

Dercon urged the federal government to double the non-oil exports by the end of the next administration, warning that economic stabilisation alone cannot deliver sustainable growth, jobs and poverty reduction.

He commended the Tinubu administration for unifying the exchange rate, curbing monetary financing of the budget and implementing tax reforms.

However, he said Nigeria must move beyond stabilisation to fundamentally restructure its economy, which he said remained constrained by an elite bargain centred on sharing oil revenues rather than creating broad-based prosperity.

He stated that income per capita had barely improved since 2010, despite previous reform efforts, while oil output per capita had declined by about 60 per cent since 2000.

According to him, Nigeria needs a new development compact that prioritises productivity, competitiveness and job creation over the distribution of economic rents.

Flour Mills MD Seeks Incentives to Boost Private Sector Exports

Group Managing Director/Chief Executive, Flour Mills of Nigeria Plc, Mr. Omoboyede Olusanya, promised significant investment by the private sector to drive exports if government provided the needed incentives.

Olusanya said infrastructure remained a major challenge for businesses in the country.

He stressed the need to deal with supply chain challenges, tackle the inflationary environment, and cut interest rate.

NESG Chairman Urges Shift from Policy Consensus to Practical Solutions

Earlier, in his welcome address, Chairman of NESG, Mr. Olaniyi Yusuf, said participation at the 32nd summit reflected stakeholders’ commitment to contributing to inclusive and impactful growth, while acknowledging the federal government’s efforts to improve the ease of doing business in the country.

Yusuf said although the reforms of the Tinubu administration might have introduced significant changes to Nigeria’s economic structures, the task before economic experts at the summit and beyond was to ensure stabilisation rather than seek a reversal of the policies.

He added that the 32nd edition of the summit must help Nigeria move from policy consensus to a framework that resolved practical issues, stating that deliberations would be guided by proposals for job creation, improved productivity, and shared prosperity.

ADC Campaign Replies Shettima Over Atiku’s Education

Meanwhile, African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council criticised Vice President Kashim Shettima for mocking former Vice President Atiku Abubakar’s educational background, challenging Shettima to explain alleged discrepancies in President Bola Tinubu’s academic records.

The council, in a statement yesterday by its Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, accused Shettima of diverting attention from the country’s cost-of-living crisis by questioning Atiku’s attendance at the Kano School of Hygiene.

The reaction followed Shettima’s remarks at the opening of the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit in Abuja, where he reportedly questioned Atiku’s qualifications and suggested that he lacked the skill set required to govern a modern Nigeria.

Countering the vice president’s criticism, the ADC campaign council stated that Atiku’s educational journey was not a legitimate basis for ridicule, particularly at a time when Nigerians were grappling with rising living costs.

“What, exactly, is shameful about Atiku’s education?” Shaibu asked.

He added, “He completed secondary school, pursued further training and built a life through work. Millions of Nigerians have travelled the same road.”

Shaibu stated, “Their parents sacrificed to get them into the schools they could afford; they studied, worked and rose. Shettima looked at that struggle and saw something to laugh at.”

The campaign council subsequently turned its attention to Tinubu’s academic history, citing what it described as an inconsistency in documents associated with his education at Chicago State University in the United States.

“If Shettima wants to examine school records, he should begin with the man he serves,” Shaibu said.

He alleged that a document in Tinubu’s Chicago State University records listed him as having graduated from Government College Lagos in 1970, although the school was established in 1974.

“Shettima should explain how a man graduates from a school before it exists, instead of mocking Atiku for attending a school whose doors were open,” the statement said.

The council also raised questions about the name on a National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) certificate Tinubu submitted to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), alleging that it bore the name “Tinubu Bola Adekunle”.

According to Shaibu, Atiku had challenged the discrepancy in court.

“Shettima cannot ridicule Atiku’s documented schooling while refusing to address questions about the name on his principal’s certificate,” Shaibu added.

The campaign council maintained that Tinubu’s Chicago State University documents remained the subject of litigation in the United States, stating that questions surrounding documents submitted in connection with his election should be addressed on their merits.

It also referenced the documented 1993 forfeiture involving Tinubu in Chicago, which arose from a narcotics investigation, saying the issue continued to attract public attention.

The allegations and interpretations in the statement were advanced by the ADC campaign council as part of its political response to Shettima’s remarks.

ADC Says Economic Hardship Deserves Priority Over Political Attacks

Beyond the controversy over academic qualifications, the council stated that the exchange had diverted attention from the economic difficulties confronting households and businesses.

Shaibu cited World Bank estimates, as presented in the statement, that nearly seven in 10 Nigerians would live below its lower-middle-income poverty line in 2026, while 35 million people faced acute food insecurity.

“Shettima says Atiku wants Nigerians to ‘backslide into penury’. Back from where?” he asked.

Shaibu said, “Poverty is not a future threat to these families. It is the life they are struggling through today.”

He added that Nigerians forced to choose between transport costs and feeding their families did not need lectures about poverty from government officials.

“A parent choosing between transport to work and food for the children does not need Shettima to explain penury,” Shaibu said, accusing the administration of being disconnected from the daily realities of ordinary Nigerians.

The statement also challenged the federal government to respond to Atiku’s proposal for a targeted, capped and independently audited subsidy tied to petrol refined in Nigeria.

“If Shettima thinks it cannot be funded, he should show his figures and offer a better way to lower prices,” Shaibu said.

“Insulting Atiku will not fill a cooking pot, pay a bus fare or put fuel in a tank.”

The council maintained that Atiku had no reason to be ashamed of his educational background, stating that his experience reflected the circumstances of many Nigerians who had pursued education through the opportunities available to them.

It accused Shettima of choosing personal attacks over an explanation of the administration’s economic policies and their effects on citizens.

Looking ahead to the 2027 general election, the campaign council said Nigerians would have an opportunity to express their views on the administration’s performance at the ballot box.

“Nigerians will answer the Vice-President’s mockery and his boss’s record with their votes,” Shaibu said.

The statement concluded with a direct political challenge to the president and his deputy, asserting that voters would hold the administration accountable for its policies and record.

World.title: NUPRC: Domestic Refiners Got 127 Million Barrels in 9 Months Amid Improved Supply
World.content:
• FG assures Nigeria’s four refineries won’t be left stranded

•NMDPRA expands gas supply access with new network code

• Targets 9 fuel laboratories nationwide by 2027

•Authority, NNPC to pilot national strategic fuel reserve

Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja and Peter Uzoho in Lagos





The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) has disclosed that domestic refineries received more than 127 million barrels of Nigerian crude oil and condensate between January and September 2026, reflecting improvements in the implementation of the Domestic Crude Supply Obligation (DCSO).

Also, the federal government has said it is pursuing a more rigorous, commercially sustainable approach to rehabilitate and reposition the four national refineries in Port Harcourt, Warri and Kaduna to prevent them from becoming stranded assets.

In the same vein, the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority, (NMDPRA) has signed and unveiled Revision II of the Nigerian Gas Transportation Network Code (NGTNC), aimed at expanding gas supply access to power, fertiliser plants, shippers and investors.

The NURPC Chief Executive, Mrs. Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan, who spoke yesterday in her speech at the OTL Africa Downstream Energy Week 2026 in Lagos, restated that the commission was also consulting producers, refiners and other stakeholders on a domestic crude swap framework.

Speaking on the theme: ‘’Secure Energy, Shared Prosperity’’, the NUPRC boss, who was represented by the Assistant Director, Operations, Mr. Prosper Omonedo, said the commission’s intervention had improved crude oil deliveries after commercial disagreements between producers and refiners affected supplies in the first quarter.

“We engaged producers and refiners, and in the second and third quarters, 53.7 and 45.1 million barrels of crude oil and condensate were supplied to domestic refineries, an overall performance of 97.4 and 76.2 per cent, respectively.

“From Q1–Q3 of 2026, more than 127 million barrels of Nigerian crude went to Nigerian refineries,” she said. Under Section 109 of the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) 2021, the NUPRC allocates crude oil to domestic refineries before export.

The NUPRC chief executive said the NUPRC was also consulting producers, refiners and other stakeholders on a domestic crude swap framework.

“Under it, a refiner could receive crude from the nearest suitable production or export point instead of moving an allocated grade over long distances, which could take an estimated three to four dollars off the cost of every barrel,” he added.

On production, Eyesan said Nigeria recorded an average of 1.717 million barrels per day of crude oil and condensate in September, a 2.34 per cent increase over August. Crude oil production alone averaged 1.53 million barrels per day, marking the fifth consecutive month the industry met or exceeded its quota.

She attributed the improvement to better asset integrity, enhanced security of evacuation infrastructure, stronger collaboration with operators and sustained regulatory efforts to restore shut-in production.

On the 2026 Licensing Round, she said the 40 blocks on offer would be subjected to a transparent evaluation process, with published criteria and mandatory disclosure of beneficial ownership.

The NUPRC boss added that the commission was enforcing the drill-or-drop principle to discourage speculative holding of licences, noting that 22 recent awardees were expected to contribute at least 250,000 barrels per day within five years.

She reaffirmed the commission’s commitment to meeting the Domestic Gas Delivery Obligation and working with the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) to align refinery demand with crude supply planning, ensuring that upstream gains translate into tangible benefits for households, industries and power generation.

At the event, the federal government said that it was pursuing a more rigorous, commercially sustainable approach to rehabilitate and reposition the four national refineries in Port Harcourt, Warri and Kaduna to prevent them from becoming stranded assets.

Permanent Secretary, Federal Ministry of Petroleum Resources, Mrs Patience Oyekunle, in her remarks, said the government remained committed to ensuring existing national refining assets run by the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) were not lost, supported by technical assessment, stronger partnerships and improved operational discipline.

“At the same time, the government remains committed to ensuring that existing national refining assets are not allowed to become stranded investments. We are pursuing a more rigorous, commercially sustainable approach to the rehabilitation and repositioning of our refineries, supported by technical assessment, stronger partnerships and improved operational discipline,” she said.

She said the 20th anniversary of OTL was a testament to resilience and relevance, commending the platform for bringing government, investors, operators and regulators together.

The government noted that Nigeria is transforming from import dependence to domestic refining, private investment and regional competitiveness under the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA).

“Today, we are beginning to see the results. Nigeria’s crude oil production has been strengthened significantly,” she explained.

She said Nigeria has maintained its compliance with the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) quota for the fourth consecutive month, owing to the rise in the nation’s crude oil production as shown by October output which surpassed 1.7 million barrels per day including condensates.

She said increasing production was only one part, with greater emphasis on value addition at home through refining, petrochemicals, gas processing and manufacturing.

“The emergence of large-scale private refining capacity represents an important turning point. The Dangote Refinery has reached its 650,000 barrels-per-day nameplate capacity, strengthening Nigeria’s prospects of becoming a net exporter of refined petroleum products,” the government said.

On gas, the federal government said Nigeria with over 215 trillion cubic feet of proven reserves must move from resource-rich to value-creating economy, citing the Gas Master Plan 2026 targeting 10 billion standard cubic feet per day by 2027 and 12BCF/d by 2030.

“Gas will power industries, support electricity generation, expand CNG and LPG utilisation, strengthen LNG exports and provide feedstock for petrochemicals,” she said.

She warned that the era of extracting value without building value was changing, with expectations on local content, technology and host-community development.

On its part, the NMDPRA said the new Network Code will deepen domestic gas utilisation and guarantee open, fair access

Authority Chief Executive, Rabiu Umar, who signed and unveiled the code with partners comprising power generation plants, fertiliser plants, shippers and investors at the OTL opening, said the code is the rulebook for shared pipelines.

“The Network Code basically is the rulebook for gas transportation. As we know, there’s one pipeline that different producers put their gas into. And for there to be equity, there needs to be a code, or if you like, rules of engagement on how you put your gas inside, how the gas is measured, and how you nominate gas,” Umar said.

“The pipelines deliver their full value only when access to them is open and fair. It is therefore a pleasure to announce that the Authority has officially launched revision 2 of the Nigerian Gas Transportation Network Code,” he explained.

Umar said about three-fifths of gas processed in September went to power plants, factories, NLNG and West African Gas Pipeline, while cooking gas demand outstrips supply. He said the Obe-Obiafu-Obrikon (OB3), the Escravos-Lagos Pipeline System (ELPS) midline compressor and the Ajaokuta-Kaduna-Kano (AKK) pipeline at over 80 per cent completion will double transport capacity from 2.2 to 4.4 BCF/d, linking the south to north.

“Since Revision I, more shippers have come onto the network, and the imbalance on the Western network has fallen by about 30 per cent Revision II builds on these gains,” he said, noting clearer provisions on Shrinkage Factor and initial rules for Trans-Saharan and Trans-African pipelines.

On downstream stability, Umar said three in four litres of petrol last month were refined domestically compared to over half imported a year ago, showing energy security built at home.

Although, he noted that much supply still came from one large refinery (Dangote Refinery) above nameplate in September, requiring diversity via modular and state refineries and competitive imports on merit-based licences.

Umar disclosed that NMDPRA is in advanced talks with NNPC to pilot strategic stock at National Pipeline and Storage Company Limited (NPSC) depots in Ibadan, Enugu and Suleja to cushion against external shocks, after eight months of Gulf war pushing crude to $100.

He announced the first of nine fuel laboratories launched recently in Port Harcourt, two more by year-end, all nine by second half 2027, in partnership with Bureau Veritas and Ace Energy and Power Solutions towards a National Reference Laboratory.

Chairman of OTL Africa Advisory Board, Mr Adetunji Oyebanji, in his welcome address, said 20 years of OTL mirrors Africa’s downstream evolution from securing imports and managing administered prices to shaping own supply arrangements, with private refining changing possibilities.

“When OTL began in 2007, much of Africa’s downstream discussion centred on securing imports. Those concerns have not disappeared. But the continent’s capacity to shape its own supply arrangements has strengthened,” Oyebanji said, citing Ghana’s 2015 price liberalisation, Dangote refinery, Kenya’s Mombasa-Nairobi pipeline, Egypt’s Mostorod upgrade, South Africa’s Lesedi terminal and Angola’s Cabinda refinery.

He warned of Middle East conflict, shipping route insecurity and Russian supply disruptions still pressuring diesel availability and freight costs, requiring dependable feedstock, efficient operations and clear rules to sustain confidence.

World.title: Alleged N582m Fraud: Judge Threatens Arrest of NNPC Coop Society’s Ex-President, Ogunbayo over Absence in Court
World.content:
Alex Enumah in Abuja





A High Court of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja, has threatened to order the arrest of a former President of the Nigeria National Petroleum Company (NNPC) Staff Multi-Purpose Cooperative Society, Olalekan Ogunbayo, over his failure to appear in court and take his plea in an alleged N582 million fraud charge.

Justice Lesley Wike issued the threat on Monday following complaints by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) that Monday’s proceedings was the third time Ogunbayo refused to appear in court for arraignment on the alleged financial misappropriation of the society’s funds.

When the matter was called, prosecution counsel, R. U. Adagba informed the judge that only the 2nd defendant, Abolade Nurudeen was in court.

The lawyer complained that Ogunbayo was granted administrative bail but jumped the bail and that all efforts to locate him for service of the charge have been unsuccessful.

The EFCC stated that Ogunbayo had stalled the arraignment twice due to absence in court and applied that bench warrant be issued against him to facilitate his arrest and production in court.

Adagba cited Sections 35, 113, 114 of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act (ACJA) 2015, arguing that the court has the power to order arrest of the defendant.

However, counsel to the defendants, Innocent Adoo, opposed the arrest warrant application, arguing that arraignment in a criminal trial could not proceed without proper service of the charge on the defendant.

He submitted that a defendant must be informed of the allegations against him and given adequate opportunity to prepare his defence, adding that service could not be waived by any party.

Adoo told the court that Ogunbayo was still on administrative bail and was unaware of the scheduled arraignment.

He explained the defence had used the information available to it to communicate with Ogunbayo who was said to be in Warri and unable to secure a flight to Abuja for today’s proceedings.

The defence counsel consequently urged the court to adjourn the matter to enable both defendants to appear and take their pleas in the interest of justice.

Reacting, Justice Wike held that in the interest of justice, the matter be adjourned to enable the first defendant made himself available for arraignment.

The judge, however, warned the court would take the necessary steps if Ogunbayo fails to appear on the next adjourned date.

She subsequently adjourned until November 23 for arraignment.

The anti-graft agency had filed an eight-count criminal charge bordering on alleged criminal misappropriation, abuse of office, corrupt practices and obtaining money by false pretence over the sale of the cooperative society’s property at Plot 50, Karsana North, Abuja.

The prosecution alleged that Ogunbayo, the society’s president, and Nurudeen, who operates under the name and style of Abolade Nurudeen & Co., conspired in January 2024 to misappropriate proceeds from the transaction.

In one of the counts, the defendants were accused of dishonestly misappropriating N582 million realised from the sale of the property.

Ogunbayo was also accused of allegedly receiving N100 million, N10 million and N50 million through different bank accounts in connection with the transaction.

The prosecution further alleged that Nurudeen received N180 million into an account belonging to his firm after representing that the property had been sold for N1 billion.

Both defendants were also accused of involvement in an alleged N160 million corrupt transactions.

World.title: Oborevwori, Dafinone, Guwor Mourn Okonjo-Iweala’s Mother, Prof Kamene, 96
World.content:
Sylvester Idowu in Warri





Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, Senator Ede Dafinone, and Speaker of Delta State House of Assembly, Hon. Emomotimi Guwor, have mourned the death of Professor Kamene Okonjo, mother of Director-General of World Trade Organisation (WTO), Dr. Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala.

They described the deceased as an accomplished scholar, revered matriarch, and community builder.

Kamene, who died on Friday at the age of 96, was the wife of the late Professor Chukwuka Okonjo, a former traditional ruler of Ogwashi-Uku Kingdom in Aniocha South Local Government Area of Delta State, and mother of the kingdom’s current monarch, Obi Ifechukwude Okonjo II.

Oborevwori, in a condolence message by his Chief Press Secretary, Sir Festus Ahon, described the late professor as a distinguished scholar whose contributions to the academia, women’s empowerment, and society would remain indelible.

The governor said Kamene’s remarkable achievements in scholarship and advocacy for women’s rights had earned her recognition beyond Nigeria, while her humility, compassion, and commitment to service distinguished her as a woman of exceptional character.

He also acknowledged her invaluable contributions to her family and society, stating that her legacy as a mother, grandmother, and great-grandmother would continue to inspire generations.

Dafinone also extended his condolences to Okonjo-Iweala and the Okonjo family of Ogwashi-Uku Kingdom over the death of their matriarch, Kamene.

Dafinone described Kamene as a woman who lived a remarkable life of purpose and impact, distinguished by her contributions to scholarship, women’s empowerment, and service to humanity.

He stated that Kamene’s legacy of excellence, compassion, and devotion to family would continue to inspire generations, adding that her passing is a profound loss to her family and society.

The senator particularly sympathised with Okonjo-Iweala, His Royal Majesty, Obi Ifechukwude Okonjo II, and other members of the Okonjo family over the loss.

According to him, although the family would deeply feel Kamene’s absence, there is comfort in the knowledge that she lived a fulfilled life and left enduring footprints in society.

Guwor, for his part, described the late nonagenarian as a distinguished matriarch whose life was defined by intellectual accomplishment, service, and an enduring commitment to her family and community.

In a statement by his Chief Press Secretary, Mr. Nkem Nwaeke, the speaker said Kamene’s death was a painful loss not only to the Okonjo family and Ogwashi-Uku Kingdom but also to Delta State and Nigeria.

He stated that Okonjo was more than the mother of a globally recognised figure, describing her as an accomplished academic, a revered traditional queen, and a community builder whose influence extended beyond her immediate family.

Guwor said the deceased had made lasting contributions as a scholar, served her community with dignity, and raised children whose achievements had brought pride to Delta State, Nigeria and Africa.

World.title: NDC Discloses N8.5bn Income, N2.4bn Spending in Seven Months
World.content:
• Cleopas: Members deserve to know how party funds are managed

•Party unveils campaign council, commissions national secretariat

•Umeh seeks greater funding for state chapters as chairman pledges reconciliation

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja and Sunday Ehigiator in Lagos





The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) on Monday disclosed that it generated N8.529 billion from nomination forms, membership dues, levies and contributions within its first seven months of operation, while spending N2.402 billion on primaries, publicity, staff salaries and other activities.

The party presented the financial figures at its National Executive Committee (NEC) meeting in Abuja, where its National Chairman, Senator Moses Cleopas, said the disclosure was intended to promote transparency and accountability in the management of the party’s resources ahead of its first anniversary.

The NEC Meeting was attended by the National Leader of the party, Senator Henry Seriake Dickson; the Presidential Candidate of the party, Mr. Peter Obi; his Vice, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso; serving and former members of the National Assembly and other notable leaders of the party, among others.

Cleopas said the party decided to account for its finances before the statutory deadline for submitting its audited accounts to the relevant government institutions, insisting that members had a right to know how funds entrusted to their leaders were being managed.

He said the decision was not prompted by allegations or criticisms on social media but reflected the party’s commitment to accountability and responsible leadership.

According to him, the party’s leadership considered it necessary to provide members with an early account of its financial position, even though the NDC had yet to complete its first year of operation.

He said, “One of the critical instruments that destroys leadership or communal living, as I have been taught, is the management of public funds. When you have a responsibility to sit over a public forum, you also owe the people who entrusted you with that privilege an obligation to be open to them.

“They must know what you are doing from time to time. Any attempt to foreclose that will lead to suspicion and give room for people to say what is not true.

“When you find yourself in a leadership position, accountability must be your sense of duty, especially when it has to do with common wealth.

“That is what Nigeria is suffering from. Nigeria is so blessed. We cannot say that we do not have resources in this country. The question we are asking is: where are our resources? What are our resources being used for that will bring relief or blessings to Nigerian citizens?”

The national chairman said the NDC would submit its properly audited financial statement to the constitutionally authorised institutions when the appropriate reporting period ended.

He explained that the party’s financial management process involved a committee comprising the national chairman, national secretary, financial secretary, treasurer and auditor, with the party’s legal adviser co-opted when necessary.

The National Treasurer, Dr Peter Onigah, presented the financial statement at the meeting, outlining the funds received and expenditure incurred during the period under review.

The disclosure comes as the NDC intensifies preparations for the 2027 general election, with the party also inaugurating its presidential campaign council, present certificates of return to its candidates and commission its national secretariat at the Jabi Area of Abuja.

Cleopas said the activities were part of efforts to strengthen the party’s structures and demonstrate its readiness for the forthcoming elections.

He said the inauguration of the presidential campaign council followed consultations aimed at identifying people willing to commit their time and resources to the party’s electoral project.

“It is not a matter of rushing to announce a campaign council. It is a matter of getting people who are committed, people who are ready to serve this nation in that capacity,” he said.

The chairman also cautioned party members against interpreting the initial list of campaign council appointments as a complete representation of all those who would eventually be involved.

“Some are calling to ask, ‘Why is my name not there? Why is my name not there?’ We are not finished. Let them wait for us,” he said.

Cleopas said the party presented certificates of return to its candidates to prevent individuals who did not win its primaries from parading themselves as candidates and misleading voters.

He described the NDC as a party intended to outlive its founding leaders, urging young Nigerians to identify with it and prepare for future leadership responsibilities.

Cleopas said, “This party is intended to be a generational party for as long as we remain on earth. This party is intended to outlive us. And if that is the vision we have, there is a particular set of people we must target.

“We have the youth to target in this country. The reason is that they must be prepared for leadership. So, this is a party of mentorship,” he said.

Umeh Seeks Funding for State Chapters

At the meeting, Senator Victor Umeh, representing Anambra Central, commended the party’s leadership for making its financial position available to members, describing the disclosure as an important step towards building public confidence.

Umeh said providing financial information would help members understand the party’s operations rather than rely on speculation.

He, however, called on the national leadership to ensure that state chapters received an appropriate share of the funds generated through their activities.

Responding, Cleopas said the issue of funding for state chapters was already under consideration, assuring members that the party would address the matter in line with its constitution and organisational objectives.

The chairman also disclosed that the party’s reconciliation committee had visited the six geopolitical zones to engage aggrieved aspirants and other members dissatisfied with the outcomes of its primaries.

He said the national secretariat was holding regular meetings to resolve outstanding disagreements and prevent internal disputes from undermining the party’s preparations for the elections.

Cleopas urged candidates, party leaders and supporters to put aside their differences and work collectively for the success of all NDC candidates.

He said the party could not afford to allow personal disagreements to weaken its electoral prospects, particularly when its presidential and vice-presidential candidates would require the support of lawmakers and other elected representatives to implement their programmes if elected.

The chairman argued that supporting only the party’s presidential candidate while abandoning its candidates for governorship and legislative seats could undermine the party’s ability to govern effectively.

He said, “Don’t you also know that they need a majority, if not all, in the National Assembly from our party? If you don’t know so, how will they get the president they want? How will they get the Senate president or the speaker of their choice?

“You may not like the face of the candidates, but they are your party’s candidates. We must work together so that we can have the Nigeria of our dreams.”

NDC Insists on Candidate Compliance, Vote Protection

The NEC meeting also heard updates from party officials on preparations for the 2027 elections, including efforts to resolve disputes involving candidates and strengthen the party’s grassroots structures.

The National Vice-Chairman for the North-east, Dr Dallamiya Nzukumbe, said preparations were progressing, although the party had encountered some disagreements between candidates and party leaders in certain areas.

He said the leadership was working to resolve the disputes and ensure that the party’s structures remained focused on the elections.

Nzukumbe also urged Nigerians to reject the notion that their votes would not count, calling on voters to remain at polling units after casting their ballots to ensure that votes were counted and results properly documented.

“We will vote, we will wait, and we will escort,” he said, stressing that the party wanted an electoral process in which votes cast at polling units were accurately reflected in the final results.

He said voters in the North were particularly concerned about insecurity, the disruption of farming activities and attacks on schools, adding that residents wanted to return to their farms, travel safely and send their children to school without fear.

“The children in the North must go to school,” he said.

Another party official, speaking on preparations in the southern part of the country, said the party was working to resolve outstanding disputes arising from its primaries and restore harmony among members.

He said the NDC was intensifying voter education and sensitisation on electoral responsibilities, particularly the need for voters and party agents to protect their votes after voting.

According to him, the party was documenting its agents and working with candidates at different levels to ensure adequate representation at polling units and collation centres.

He urged voters not to leave polling units immediately after casting their ballots but to remain until the votes were counted and the results properly recorded.

Cleopas, in his closing remarks, also addressed concerns over the omission of some candidates’ names from the relevant electoral processes.

He said the party was pursuing both administrative and legal avenues to address the matter and expressed confidence that candidates who had fulfilled the requirements of the law would be able to contest the elections.

“The party is not folding its hands. The party is interfacing on administrative fronts and legal fronts,” he said.

He added that the leadership was conscious of its responsibility to candidates who had completed the required processes and would continue to pursue the matter.

The NDC chairman urged members to remain united as the party moved from internal preparations to the next phase of its electoral activities.

He said the party’s immediate priorities included commissioning its national secretariat, inaugurating the presidential campaign council, presenting certificates to its candidates and resolving outstanding grievances before the 2027 general election.

World.title: Court Orders el-Rufai to Enter Defence on Alleged Wiretapping Trial
World.content:
Alex Enumah in Abuja





Justice Joyce Abdulmalik of a Federal High Court, Abuja, on Monday ordered the immediate past governor of Kaduna State, Nasir El-rufai to enter his defence if he so desires in his ongoing trial on bugging the telephone communications of the National Security Adviser (NSA), Nuhu Ribadu.

Justice Abdulmalik made the order shortly after dismissing the no-case submission filed by El-rufai, in response to the prosecution’s case.

In her ruling on the no-case submission, the judge held there is sufficient evidence by the prosecution to warrant the court to call on the defendant to enter his defence if he so desires.

She subsequently adjourned till November 25 for the former governor to open his defence.

The African Democratic Congress (ADC) chieftain is standing trial on a five-count criminal charge brought against him by the Department of State Services (DSS).

At the no-case submission hearing on September 22, the prosecution, represented by Oluwole Aladedoye (SAN), objected to the submission and urged the court to dismiss it and order the defendant to enter his defence.

According to Aladedoye, the defendant failed to address Exhibit “B”, which the prosecution claimed contains El-rufai’s admission in relation to the tapping of Ribadu’s phone.

He contended that since the prosecution has effectively established a prima facie case against El-rufai, through its two witnesses, the defendant is required by law to enter a defence.

Defence lawyer, Akinyemi Aremu, while adopting his client’s no-case submission, argued that the prosecution failed to establish a prima facie case against the ex-governor to require him to be called upon to enter a defence.

Aremu urged the court to uphold the no-case submission and discharge his client.

El-rufai opted for a no-case submission after the prosecution closed its case upon calling two witnesses – an operative of the DSS and a lawyer, Deji Adeyanju.

Adeyanju, who testified as a subpoenaed witness, told the court that the ex-governor admitted during a television interview that he wiretapped the NSA’s phone lines.

World.title: Atiku’s Aide Demands Answers over Seven SUVs Displayed by APC Youth Leader
World.content:
Chuks Okocha in Abuja





Paul Ibe, media adviser to former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, has demanded an explanation from the All Progressives Congress over seven 2026 Toyota Prado SUVs reportedly displayed by the party’s National Youth Leader, Dayo Israel.

Ibe, in a statement on Monday, questioned the source of funding for the vehicles and whether public resources were involved in their purchase or distribution.

He said Israel had displayed the vehicles, thanked First Lady Remi Tinubu for her support and later deleted the post.

However, Ibe argued that removing the pictures did not resolve questions about the vehicles’ ownership, funding and intended beneficiaries.

“Deleting the pictures does not erase the questions,” he said.

Ibe criticised the development against the backdrop of rising living costs, unemployment and poverty, arguing that the reported distribution of luxury vehicles to party operatives contrasted with the economic difficulties facing many Nigerians.

He also questioned the call for Nigerians to make sacrifices amid reports of luxury vehicles being made available for political activities.

“Is sacrifice only for the poor?” he asked.

The former vice-president’s aide called on the First Lady, Israel and the APC to disclose the total cost of the seven vehicles, identify their purchasers and explain the sources of the funds used to acquire them.

He also demanded the identities of the donors and beneficiaries, evidence of payment and details of the purpose for which the vehicles were provided.

Ibe further asked the party to clarify whether any funds or assets belonging to the Federal Government, the Office of the First Lady or government agencies were used in the transaction.

He called on the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission and the Independent National Electoral Commission to examine the funding arrangements and determine whether public resources were used for partisan activities or whether applicable campaign-finance rules were breached.

“The Nigerian treasury is not the APC’s campaign purse, and the Presidency must not become the ruling party’s election-financing machinery,” Ibe said.

He maintained that deleting the social media post should not end scrutiny of the reported vehicle distribution.

“Deleting the post cannot delete the demand for accountability,” he added.

The statement did not provide independent evidence that public funds were used to acquire the vehicles or establish the circumstances surrounding their purchase.

World.title: N76bn Fraud Trial: EFCC Witness Calls Arik Air Receivership Scam
World.content:
• Insists airline owes Union Bank nothing, court admits AMCON board resolutions

Wale Igbintade





Director of the Lagos Zonal Directorate 2 of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), Bawa Usman Kaltungo, yesterday described the receivership of Arik Air as fraudulent, insisting that the airline is not indebted to Union Bank of Nigeria Plc.

Kaltungo, the fourth prosecution witness in the ongoing trial of former Managing Director of Asset Management Corporation of Nigeria (AMCON), Ahmed Kuru, and others over an alleged N76 billion ($31.5 million) fraud, told the Special Offences Court in Ikeja that the purported bad debt that formed the basis for the receivership did not exist.

The witness, who testified before Justice Mojisola Dada, said his investigation into a petition concerning the airline revealed that the basis for appointing a receiver-manager over Arik Air was faulty.

In a significant development, however, the court admitted AMCON board resolutions tendered by Kuru’s counsel, Uyi Giwa-Osagie, to challenge the prosecution witness’ assertion that the former managing director had unilaterally approved the receivership.

The documents were admitted despite the prosecution’s objection to their relevance.

The court held that they emanated from AMCON’s board as a corporate body and had been duly certified in accordance with Section 104 of the Evidence Act.

During cross-examination by Giwa-Osagie, counsel to the second defendant, Kaltungo, said he headed the EFCC team that investigated the petition concerning Arik Air.

He told the court that he had informed AMCON’s top management at a meeting that the airline was not indebted to Union Bank and that the appointment of a receiver-manager to take control of the company was defective.

The witness said, “The foundation for the appointment of a receivership over Arik Air was fraudulent and faulty. There was no bad debt; it does not exist.”

The testimony came amid allegations surrounding the handling of Arik Air’s loan obligations, its takeover by AMCON, and transactions involving the airline’s assets.

During the cross-examination, Kaltungo maintained that Kuru, in his capacity as AMCON’s Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, had extensive powers and had unilaterally sanctioned the appointment of a receiver-manager over Arik Air.

Giwa-Osagie challenged the account by tendering AMCON board resolutions intended to demonstrate that the receivership decision was taken at the corporate level rather than solely by Kuru.

The prosecution objected to the admissibility of the documents, arguing that they were too remote to the issues before the court.

However, Giwa-Osagie argued that the documents were relevant to determining his client’s culpability in the alleged offences.

He submitted that Kuru was not standing trial over the propriety of AMCON’s powers to appoint a receiver-manager but over the specific allegations contained in the charge sheet.

The defence counsel maintained that the board resolutions were necessary to establish the circumstances surrounding the decision and challenge the witness’s account of Kuru’s role.

He further argued that the documents were public records that could properly be tendered from the Bar.

In her ruling, Dada upheld the relevance and admissibility of the documents, holding that they emanated from AMCON’s board as a corporate body and had been duly certified in accordance with Section 104 of the Evidence Act.

The admission of the resolutions provides the defence with documentary evidence to challenge the prosecution witness’s assertion that Kuru acted unilaterally in approving the receivership.

However, their admission does not, in itself, determine the legality of the receivership or resolve the allegations against the defendants.

EFCC instituted the case following a petition by human rights activist and lawyer, Femi Falana, SAN, on behalf of Arik Air’s promoters and shareholders over the airline’s receivership and related transactions.

The defendants are Kuru; Kamilu Alaba Omokide, a former receiver-manager of Arik Air; Captain Roy Ilegbodu, the airline’s chief executive officer; Union Bank of Nigeria Plc; and Super Bravo Limited.

They are facing a six-count charge bordering on conspiracy, stealing and abuse of office.

The prosecution’s case includes allegations concerning the handling of Arik Air’s loan obligations, the transfer of its debt exposure to AMCON and the alleged conversion of N4.9 billion belonging to the airline for the benefit of NG Eagle Limited.

The dispute also raises questions about the exercise of AMCON’s statutory powers and the responsibilities of a receiver-manager appointed to take control of a distressed company.

Section 553(2) of the Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020 requires a receiver-manager to act in the company’s best interests, including preserving its assets and furthering its business objectives.

The defendants were arraigned on January 20, 2025, and they pleaded not guilty to all the charges.

One of the counts reads, “That you, Union Bank of Nigeria Plc, sometime in 2011 or thereabouts, in Lagos, within the jurisdiction of this Honourable Court, with the intention of causing and/or inducing the unwarranted sale of Arik Air loans and bank guarantees with Union Bank, made false statements to the Asset Management Corporation of Nigeria (AMCON) regarding Arik Air Limited’s performing loans, following which you transferred a bogus figure of N71,000,000,000.00 (Seventy-One Billion Naira) to AMCON.”

Another count reads, “That you, Ahmed Lawal Kuru, Kamilu Alaba Omokide (as Receiver-Manager of Arik Air Limited), and Captain Roy Ilegbodu (Chief Executive Officer of Arik Air Limited in Receivership), sometime in 2022 or thereabouts, in Lagos, within the jurisdiction of this Honourable Court, fraudulently converted to the use of NG Eagle Limited the total sum of N4,900,000,000.00 (Four Billion, Nine Hundred Million Naira only), property of Arik Air Limited.”

World.title: BIG changes to public transport operating licences until April 2027
World.content:
After airing grievances, requirements for public transport operating licences in Gauteng are temporarily suspended. Image: AI generated, for illustrative purposes only

Three requirements for public transport operating licences are temporarily suspended by the Gauteng Department of Roads and Transport (GDRT). As such, this gives operators a six-month grace period, until 30 April 2027, to get their affairs in order …

This temporary amendment to the Gauteng Public Transport Regulatory Information System (GPTRIS) follows an airing of concerns by operators. These include scholar transport, metered taxis and e-hailing industry. The Gauteng National Taxi Alliance (GNTA) and South African National Taxi Council (Santaco) also asked for a period consultation.

PUBLIC TRANSPORT OPERATING LICENCES

As such, the temporarily scrapped requirements until the end of April 2027 are:



Police clearance certificates : Applicants for public transport operating licences won’t have to submit one.

: Applicants for public transport operating licences won’t have to submit one. Labour law compliance : You don’t need to submit a formal undertaking that you’ll comply with the Labour Relations Act.

: You don’t need to submit a formal undertaking that you’ll comply with the Labour Relations Act. Professional driving permits (PrDPs): Business/operating licence owners don’t need one.

Public transport operating licences will be facilitated by the admin board (TOLAB) without the above requirements.

WHAT’S NOT SUSPENDED

Gauteng government insists operators use this time to get compliant with the various requirements. Image: File

However, the Gauteng government stressed that the suspension is strictly limited to these requirements. “It does not constitute a general suspension of any other public transport operating licences,” a spokesman confirmed. As such, the department says it will use the six months to standardise a single set of application requirements for operating licences across all public transport modes. And, after 30 April 2027, the temporary suspensions will lapse. The department says it will: “Strictly monitor and enforce compliance across all modes of public transport.”

WHAT OPERATORS CAN DO ABOUT IT

Gauteng government recommends operators should use this grace period to:

Gather all police clearance certificates, labour compliance documents and PrDPs where needed.

Apply/renew through your TOLAB now and keep all records for reference.

Watch for further GDRT notices.

For the country’s richest and busiest province, six months gives operators breathing room and the department time to settle on workable rules. What it doesn’t do is remove the requirements entirely, which Santaco and GNTA may wish were the case …

But what do you think of these temporary changes to public transport operating licences in Gauteng? Please share your thoughts in the comments section below …

World.title: Zimbabwean striker faces new challenge after sensational AmaZulu start
World.content:
Zimbabwean striker Thandolwenkosi Ngwenya faces a new challenge at AmaZulu after his impressive start to the 2026/27 season attracted increased attention from opposition defenders.

Ngwenya has scored 10 goals in as many matches for Usuthu, establishing himself as a key attacking figure.

However, the forward believes rival teams are now working harder to contain him as they look to limit his influence on matches.



Speaking to SABC Sport, Ngwenya admitted that the increased attention from defenders is forcing him to reconsider his approach in front of goal.

“Everyone is preparing for me but it’s gonna give others a chance to score because everyone is coming for me,” he said.

The Zimbabwean acknowledged that he must find alternative ways to penetrate opposition defences, particularly as opponents become more familiar with his movements and scoring methods.

“It’s a bit demanding now because I have to find another way to penetrate because everyone is looking for how I’m scoring, so I must find another way to score,” Ngwenya added.

Ngwenya faces a test of adaptability

The striker’s comments highlight the challenge that can accompany a prolific start to a campaign. While scoring regularly can boost a player’s confidence, it can also make them a primary target for opposition defenders.

For Ngwenya, maintaining his scoring form could depend on how quickly he adapts to the increased attention and varies his approach in attacking situations.



The forward also recognised that his teammates could benefit from opponents concentrating on stopping him, potentially creating opportunities for other AmaZulu attackers.

However, turning that possibility into a consistent advantage will require Usuthu to make the most of the space and chances available when opposition defences focus on Ngwenya.

AmaZulu coach Arthur Zwane has also stressed the importance of the striker improving certain aspects of his game.

Zwane highlights areas for improvement

Ngwenya was unable to find the net when AmaZulu defeated Kruger United 1-0 in the Carling Knockout at Mbombela Stadium on Sunday.

Hendrick Ekstein scored from the penalty spot to secure Usuthu’s place in the quarter-finals, while Ngwenya struggled to make his opportunities count.

Zwane explained that the striker tends to perform better when he scores early in a match, pointing to two early opportunities against Kruger United that Ngwenya failed to convert.

The coach also criticised his reactions in those situations and offered advice on how he should approach challenges from defenders.

“You can’t push the ball and expose your ball to the right when the defender is coming from the right side. Put it to your left and put your body across,” Zwane explained.

The coach’s assessment underlines the importance of decision-making and composure as Ngwenya looks to maintain his impressive scoring record.

With opposition teams increasingly focused on containing him, the Zimbabwean’s ability to adapt could prove crucial to sustaining his strong start and helping AmaZulu remain competitive throughout the campaign.

World.title: Buskers, beer and zombies: The best SA festivals this weekend
World.content:
In a group or solo, these four festivals are guaranteed to keep you entertained as October dips out. Images via Canva @MoonstoneImages/@leolintang

The last weekend of October is packed with plenty of festivals, and South Africans are ready to bid goodbye to the spooky season in style.

If you’re looking to have fun solo or with your family and friends, there’s no shortage of entertaining events to choose from!

Here’s our pick of the best festivals happening this weekend across Mzansi:



1. V&A WATERFRONT BUSKER FESTIVAL – CAPE TOWN

Soak up the sunshine and vibes at the inaugural Busker Festival. Image via Facebook @WhatsoninCapeTown.EventsGuide

The V&A Waterfront is set to become entertainment central from 30 October to 1 November 2026, from 12:00 to 19:30.

Forty local and international buskers – from musicians and dancers to magicians and face-painting – will showcase their talents across 11 locations at the iconic waterfront, including the Amphitheatre. It’s a guaranteed good time, and it will certainly keep the kids entertained and full of wonder.

Entrance is completely free, and you’re strongly encouraged to show your appreciation to buskers by leaving a gratuity in their designated tip boxes.



2. ZOMBIE WALK – CAPE TOWN

A spook-tacular staple on Cape Town’s social calendar, Zombie Walk makes its grand return to Cape Town on 31 October 2026, from 17:00 to 18:00.

As per tradition, you and the rest of the horror-loving horde will limp your way from Government Avenue, through the CBD and finish at Albertus Street.

To book your place in the Zombie Walk, you can register for free at www.zombiewalk.co.za. Tickets for the afterparty (18+ only!) start from R100 and are available to purchase from www.quicket.co.za.



3. JOHANNESBURG PRIDE 2026 – JOHANNESBURG

Celebrate South Africa’s LGBTQIA+ community by joining Johannesburg Pride 2026 on 31 October 2026, from 12:00 until midnight.

This year’s theme is “Proudly African, Authentically You”, so you, your family and friends are highly encouraged to show up and show out as your authentic selves and lift each other up. There’ll be plenty of live entertainment, food vendors and market stalls – in other words, there’s something for everyone!





Plus, there’s the Pride march, which starts at 14:00. You will walk from Sandton City on 5th Street and finish at Pride Village, Katherine Street. Admission is free, though you must register at www.howler.co.za. VIP tickets are also up for grabs for R250.

4. OKTOBERFEST 2026 – GQEBERHA

Experience a taste of Germany as Oktoberfest 2026 descends on Gqeberha on 31 October, from 17:00 until midnight.

At the German Club, expect beer upon beer when you order from the 50-metre bar, bust out your best moves on the dancefloor to the tunes of a live oompah band and indulge in German cuisine from the food court.
