Tickets cost R200 each and can be purchased at www.quicket.co.za. Note that under-18s are not allowed, and you need to have your ID on hand.

WHICH FESTIVAL WILL YOU BE ATTENDING?

If you’re looking to end October on a high note, then these festivals are certainly the place to be!

Let us know in the comments below which one you’ll be attending this weekend.

World.title: WSAR tackles record-breaking seven incidents on Table Mountain
World.content:
Wilderness Search And Rescue (WSAR) saw a record number of mountain incidents being recorded in a single day. Image: Pexels

Wilderness Search And Rescue (WSAR) were hard at work this past weekend, responding to seven incidents across Table Mountain in a single day.

According to the Western Cape-based organisation, rescue teams worked throughout Saturday, 24 October 2026, to provide much-needed assistance to hikers in distressing situations.

WSAR TO THE RESCUE

One of the seven incidents involved a 56-year-old American visitor, who collapsed while hiking Platteklip Gorge. A Western Cape Government Health and Wellness EMS paramedic was lowered down from a helicopter to assist the visitor, who was subsequently airlifted to safety and taken to a waiting ambulance.



In another incident, WSAR technical teams rescued a 24-year-old male hiker, who was injured after falling four metres while attempting to climb up a break in the cliffs above Union Ravine.

Left stranded on a small ledge, the hiker contacted WSAR for help. The responding teams subsequently abseiled down the cliffs to him, assessed his injuries and administered medical care. They then raised him approximately 130 metres to the top of Table Mountain.

HUGE INCREASE IN RESCUE NUMBERS, SAYS WSAR

Worryingly, noted WSAR in a Facebook post, these seven mountain incidents mark a new year-to-date record. This equals WSAR’s busiest day on record for only the third time in their history.

What’s more, it has already surpassed the previous high recorded in 2024 by 17.5%. October 2026 saw 235 incidents; in comparison, October 2024 saw 200 at that point.

“We don’t share these numbers to suggest that people are becoming more careless, or that anyone should think twice about asking for help,” the post reads. “There are many possible reasons why rescue numbers have increased, and the figures alone don’t tell us what those reasons are.”

WSAR relies on volunteers to carry out rescue operations. Image: Pexels

The post continues: “But they do tell us something important. More people are needing assistance, and we’re asking more of the volunteers, specialist teams and partner agencies who respond. Behind every one of those 235 incidents is someone who needed help. And behind every response are people who put their own plans aside to provide it.



“We want to extend our sincere appreciation to every volunteer rescuer, paramedic, helicopter crew member, technical specialist, law enforcement officer, ranger and support team who contributed to Saturday’s operations.”

SAFETY FIRST

Hiking is a beloved pastime in Cape Town, home of many beautiful hiking trails. Like most outdoor activities, however, hiking comes with its own set of dangerous risks.

If you’re planning a hike, WSAR advises to taking the following steps:

Prepare thoroughly: This includes consulting a map to assess the length of the hike, water points on the trail and so on; double-checking your hiking gear; and keeping a sharp eye on the weather forecast.

Keep somebody informed: Tell someone about your plans, including where you plan to hike and when exactly you intend to return.

Gear up properly: Always carry a jacket, hat and sunscreen; wear comfortable shoes like takkies or hiking boots; keep a head lamp on your person; and carry enough food and water. A backpack is crucial for carrying essential gear.

Cellphone protocol: Ensure that you fully charge your cellphone and that you save WSAR’s emergency number (021 937 0300) in your contacts. If you’re in an area with poor reception, switch to flight mode to save on battery power. You’d also do well to install a GPS tracker on your cellular device.

Never hike alone: WSAR recommends hiking in a group of at least four people. That way, if one gets injured, another can stay with them while the others seek help.

Gather info: If you find yourself in an emergency situation, establish the following before contacting rescue services: the type of incident it is (eg. a mountain accident); the number of people involved and severity of injuries; the name of your location; and, if applicable, your GPS coordinates.

If you have any helpful hiking tips that you’d like to share, be sure to drop them in the comments section below.

Stay safe out there, folks!

World.title: Annual vehicle licence renewal: SA’s cheapest provinces
World.content:
When it comes to annual vehicle licence renewal, these are SA’s cheapest provinces right now. Image: File

Your annual vehicle licence renewal is one of those expenses that’s easy to forget about, but is always there to drain your bank balance at seemingly the most inopportune time. How much you pay for annual vehicle licence renewal in South Africa depends on two things: your vehicle’s tare (empty weight) and the province where it is registered.

And spoiler alert, there’s no single province that’s cheapest for annual vehicle licence renewal. North West, for example, has some of the lowest fees for lighter vehicles. While the Eastern Cape is particularly competitive across mid-weight bands. Unsurprisingly, at the other end of the scale, Gauteng is most expensive for many of the most common vehicle categories.

ANNUAL VEHICLE LICENCE RENEWAL IN SA

Cost aside, the good news is that annual vehicle licence renewal no longer has to be an awful queue-fest at your local licencing office. Government’s online NATIS site, allows registered motorists to view renewals, pay online and arrange delivery of their new disc. The Road Traffic Management Corporation (RTMC) standard transaction fee for the convenience is R72, with delivery generally taking three to five days.



Provincial authorities are allowed to set their own licence tariffs and update them on different schedules. Some fees have remained unchanged for years. Others have increased more recently. And some, like Gauteng, are gazetted for further increases …

ANNUAL VEHICLE LICENCE RENEWAL IN SA BY PROVINCE

WHICH PROVINCE IS THE CHEAPEST FOR ANNUAL VEHICLE LICENCE RENEWAL?

For a vehicle weighing between 751 kg and 1 750 kg, North West offers the lowest listed fee in every band. Its R552 fee for the 1 251 to 1 500 kg category, for example, is R138 cheaper than the Eastern Cape and R180 cheaper than the Western Cape.

For vehicles between 1 751 kg and 2 000 kg, North West and the Eastern Cape are almost neck and neck, at R762 and R768 respectively. Gauteng, meanwhile, charges R1 104 for a vehicle in the 1 751 to 2 000 kg band and R1 536 for one in the 2 251 to 2 500 kg band. These are the highest figures in those categories.



LATEST AND PROPOSED TARIFF CHANGES

Free State revised its annual vehicle licence renewal tariffs on 1 August 2026. Only the lightest band in this comparison remained unchanged at R450. The 1 001 to 1 250 kg band rose from R462 to R480, while the 2 251 to 2 500 kg band increased from R1 164 to R1 212. Meanwhile, Gauteng motorists should also keep an eye on proposed increases. A draft schedule has been reported, but proposed rates are not yet approved.

As ever, South African motorists have a 21-day grace period after the expiry date printed on their current licence disc. After that, late-renewal penalties and arrears may apply. The government advises motorists to renew before expiry rather than relying on the grace period.

But what do you think? How do you like to do your annual vehicle licence renewal? If so, please share your thoughts in the comments section below …

World.title: Tshwane water crisis: 833 SICK, minister says NO outbreak
World.content:
The Tshwane water crisis has left 833 people ill after residents consumed contaminated water in Bronkhorstspruit. Image: Pexels

The number of people who have fallen ill after drinking contaminated water in Bronkhorstspruit, Tshwane, has climbed to 833, including 328 children aged four and younger.

Health officials recorded 27 new cases in the 24 hours leading up to Monday, 26 October, while three patients remain in hospital.

Water and Sanitation Minister Pemmy Majodina, however, insists there is no outbreak.



MINISTER DENIES TSHWANE WATER OUTBREAK

Majodina made the claim during a visit to Bronkhorstspruit District Hospital alongside Deputy President Paul Mashatile.

“I’m still firm that there’s no outbreak. There’s no death. There is no one that is critical,” she reportedly said.

She maintained that most patients received treatment for dehydration before leaving hospital.



MASHATILE VISITS TSHWANE AMID WATER CRISIS

Mashatile inspected the Bronkhorstspruit Water Treatment Works on Monday to assess the damage and government’s response.

He raised concerns about private water tankers operating in the area, questioning where suppliers obtained their water.

“We are quite concerned about private suppliers of water with water tankers because we don’t know where they get that water from,” he reportedly said.



Mashatile said authorities would investigate the operators to protect residents from further contamination.

As the chair of the Inter-Ministerial Committee (IMC) on Water and Sanitation, I am in Bronkhorstspruit in the City of Tshwane Metropolitan Municipality, Gauteng Province, to receive updates on the condition of affected residents and the healthcare response following the… pic.twitter.com/OUTlEwfO0L — Paul Mashatile🇿🇦 (@PMashatile) October 26, 2026

WHAT CAUSED THE TSHWANE WATER CRISIS?

The City of Tshwane failed to adequately chlorinate water at the treatment plant between 24 September and 14 October.



Tests subsequently detected high levels of E. coli and coliform bacteria.

According to a report, a dispute over chlorine prices contributed to the shortage, with the municipality claiming its supplier increased prices by 400%.

The City has since secured additional chlorine and suspended the plant manager pending an investigation.



WHEN WILL WATER SUPPLY RETURN?

The plant remains closed as Rand Water assists with repairs.

Mashatile said the work could take several weeks but gave no reopening date.

Meanwhile, the City has deployed 36 water tankers to affected communities.



Authorities have urged residents to use approved alternative water supplies until tests confirm that tap water is safe to drink.

World.title: Orlando Pirates fan from Nigeria gets R40 000 from South Africans
World.content:
Orlando Pirates superfan, Miracle Ebubechi Michael, better known as Mimi or Anoda Mirakle, has become the centre of an wonderful display of ubuntu.

A crowdfunding campaign raised more than R40,000 to bring her to Johannesburg. She will get to watch the Soweto Derby on Saturday 31 October after it was sold out in eight hours last week.

MIRACALE UBURECHI IN MZANSI TO WATCH ORLANDO PIRATES LIVE IN THE SOWETO DERBY

According to reports, even football fans of Kaizer Chiefs and Mamelodi Sundowns also contributed.



The crowdfunding initiative was launched to cover her journey from Nigeria to Johannesburg. It has turned what might have remained a distant dream into a real possibility.

The Orlando Pirates Supporters Forum commited itself behind the initiative. The Zodwa Khoza Foundation has offered to cover accommodation for Mimi and her partner during their stay in South Africa.

Mimi’s visit is expected to extend beyond the highly anticipated clash between Orlando Pirates and Kaizer Chiefs at FNB Stadium.



Organisers have reportedly offered more. An itinerary will give her an opportunity to experience some of South Africa’s cultural landmarks. She will be escorted visit to Vilakazi Street in Soweto.

A formal visit to the Premier Soccer League offices is also part of the planned programme.

MIMI’S BOLD PROMISE IF KAIZER CHIEFS WIN

However, Mimi has added another layer of intrigue to her eagerly anticipated visit.



In the spirit of the banter that makes the Soweto Derby one of African football’s most entertaining rivalries, the Nigerian supporter has made a bold promise should Kaizer Chiefs emerge victorious.

“If Kaizer Chiefs beat Pirates in the Soweto Derby, I will walk all the way back to Nigeria on foot!” she declared in a viral social media video.

More than R40,000 has been raised, accommodation support has been offered, and a Nigerian football fan is preparing to experience a derby she has long wanted to witness in person.

World.title: Soweto Derby preview: Pirates vs Chiefs form, head-to-head
World.content:
Orlando Pirates and Kaizer Chiefs are set for Soweto Derby action on 31 October. Image: Mr Baggins (Flickr).

31 October marks another chapter in the fierce Orlando Pirates and Kaizer Chiefs rivalry.

The Soweto Derby clash takes place at the FNB Stadium on Saturday afternoon.

Here’s how Pirates and Chiefs compare heading into their clash in Johannesburg.



The Buccaneers are currently on a three-game domestic and continental winning streak.

This includes victories over Namibia’s African Stars across both legs of the CAF Champions League preliminary round.

Pirates are also unbeaten in the Premier Soccer League (PSL) this season.



The only blemish on their recent record was the MTN8 final loss to Mamelodi Sundowns on 10 October.

As cited by the PSL website, Teboho Mokoena and Iqraam Rayners scored for Masandawana.

Pirates have been hit hard by injuries this season, with the likes of Evidence Makgopa and Thalente Mbatha yet to return.



Kamogelo Sebelebele is in doubt, and the club is also being cautious about Oswin Appollis, according to Soccer Laduma.

Kaizer Chiefs FORM guide, latest news

The Amakhosi are facing the possibility of another season with nothing to show for it.

Kaizer Chiefs are down to fifth in the PSL and out of the CAF Confederation Cup in the preliminary rounds.



On Friday, Chiefs were beaten 2-3 on penalties by Zambia’s Red Arrows, as reported by SuperSport.

This leaves them effectively chasing the Nedbank Cup and Carling Knockout Cup.

In the PSL, the Glamour Boys’ last win was against the struggling Siwelele at the beginning of September.



They have just three wins after eight games and are in danger of slipping into the mid-table.

It has also increased the pressure on coach Fernando da Cruz, who could be axed by the end of the year.

Head-to-head results and prediction

The last time the PSL giants met, they played to a 1-1 draw, as cited by News24.



Sebelebele and Mmodi Pule scored on either side in the second half of their clash in April 2026.

Before that game, Pirates had the better of recent derby clashes.

This includes the 3-0 away win in February 2026 and the 3-2 home win in March 2024.



Pirates remain on track in the PSL, trailing Sundowns by a single point.

They have also advanced to the group stage of the CAF Champions League, with the draw set for Wednesday.

Chiefs, meanwhile, have struggled for wins in domestic and continental competition.



While derby clashes are often unpredictable, Pirates clearly have the superior form.

Our prediction is a one-goal win for the Buccaneers, as their PSL title defence keeps rolling.

For Chiefs, it should be more points slipping through their fingers.

Date: 31 October

Teams: Orlando Pirates vs Kaizer Chiefs

Venue: FNB Stadium, Johannesburg

Kickoff time: 15:30

World.title: Jay-Z to perform at Super Bowl LXI halftime show: NFL
World.content:
LOS ANGELES - Rapper Jay-Z will perform at the Super Bowl LXI halftime show this February in Los Angeles, the NFL announced.

Jay-Z's Roc Nation entertainment company has produced the star-packed Super Bowl halftime show each year since 2020, selecting the headliners, but the hip-hop mogul has not previously performed himself at the event.

"When we first reached an agreement with Roc Nation to produce the show, I had just one request: that Jay-Z take the stage himself one day, whenever the moment felt right to him," NFL commissioner Roger Goodell said in a joint statement.

"I couldn't be more excited for fans around the world to experience the artistry, creativity and cultural impact he will bring to the Super Bowl stage."

The announcement did not specify whether Jay-Z would be the sole headliner.

It came after Jay-Z -- who is married to pop megastar Beyonce -- performed two shows last weekend at Los Angeles' SoFi Stadium, which will serve as the venue for the Super Bowl on February 14.

Those gigs served as the culmination for a year-long tour celebrating the 30th anniversary of his debut album "Reasonable Doubt."

"From 'Reasonable Doubt' to standing on the Super Bowl halftime stage, this has been a journey," said Jay-Z, whose real name is Shawn Carter.

"Thirty years of music, work, and culture on the world's biggest stage. This run continues to be a dream come true."

In an indication of the level of star power Jay-Z could potentially bring with him to the halftime spectacular, he was joined on-stage in Los Angeles by John Legend, DJ Khaled, Dr Dre and Snoop Dogg.

World.title: Israel to give verdict on Netanyahu in pivotal election
World.content:
JERUSALEM - A deeply divided Israel will head to the polls on Tuesday for the first time since Hamas's October 7, 2023 attack, with voters delivering their verdict on veteran Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the country's rightward drift.

Israelis will cast their ballots in the shadow of three years of multi-front regional wars triggered by October 7, with the trauma still fresh and questions over accountability and security central to the campaign.

The close-fought vote comes as Israel looks increasingly isolated on the world stage, driven by a devastating military campaign in Gaza, soaring settlement construction and violence in the occupied West Bank, and a move towards hard-right religious nationalism.

The last polls to be published showed Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister, running neck and neck with his main centrist rival Gadi Eisenkot, a political novice and former military chief whose mild manner is seen as the antithesis of the incumbent.

Some 7.3 million people are eligible to vote, with more than half a million young people due to cast their ballot for the first time. Surveys show they overwhelmingly identify as centre-right or right-wing.

Tens of thousands of Israelis are estimated to have flown in from abroad to vote in an election seen as crucial to deciding the future character of their country.

"I think this is one of the most important election days in the history of the state of Israel," Uriel Brandler, a 58-year-old real estate agent, told AFP in Jerusalem the day before the vote.

"The country definitely needs a change for the better in every aspect."

World.title: Fainga'anuku named as loose forward for All Blacks northern tour
World.content:
WELLINGTON - All Blacks coach Dave Rennie on Tuesday confirmed a positional switch for Leicester Fainga'anuku, as the winger-turned-loose-forward returned to the New Zealand squad for their northern tour.

Fainga'anuku broke his leg and injured his ankle towards the end of the Canterbury Crusaders' Super Rugby campaign, and is yet to play for New Zealand under head coach Rennie.

During the Super Rugby season Fainga'anuku switched into the loose forwards under Rob Penney, causing a nuisance at the ruck while still offering his devastating running game.

Rennie praised the new additions to his severely injury-hit squad, saying they had shown "fantastic form" in domestic rugby.

"They bring a lot of quality and experience to the group," Rennie said.

"Playing Scotland, Wales and England on consecutive weekends is a tough assignment. These are all proud rugby nations with passionate home crowds.

"We will embrace the challenge and the opportunity to build on our Bledisloe Cup performances".

Hooker Codie Taylor will captain the team in place of the injured Ardie Savea.

Flyhalf Ruben Love is among the long list of names unavailable for the tour through injury, giving Richie Mo'unga more time to reacquaint himself with international rugby.

Also missing through injury are Samisoni Taukei'aho, Shannon Frizell, Tyrel Lomax, Leroy Carter, Luke Jacobson, Caleb Clarke and Ollie Norris.

World.title: Microsoft offers voluntary exit packages to 60,000 staff
World.content:
NEW YORK - Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, the company said on Monday, roughly a quarter of its workforce, as the tech giant seeks to cut costs while pouring money into artificial intelligence.

Staff on select teams in the United States, Canada, India and Britain at vice president level and below will be eligible, a Microsoft spokesperson said, while some groups of employees, including some working on data centres, sales and marketing, are excluded.

"The Voluntary Exit Offer reflects an important part of how we’re evolving our approach to change: creating greater flexibility and, where possible, more ways for employees to shape their next chapter," Amy Coleman, an executive vice president and chief people officer, told employees in a memo.

It's the second voluntary buyout offer that Microsoft has offered employees this year.

In April, the company reportedly offered around seven percent of its US workforce the option to retire early.

Around 30 percent of those eligible took the voluntary retirement plan, according to CNBC.

Microsoft had 223,000 employees globally at the end of June, down from 228,000 at the end of 2025, according to regulatory filings.

Around 27 percent of Microsoft's workforce is eligible for the new buyout offer.

The company is expected to report quarterly earnings later this week.

-Tech layoffs-

As major tech giants continue to spend heavily on AI-related investments, concerns persist about the impact of the technology on jobs.

Even industry insiders, such as Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, have warned of mass job losses.

Netflix will reportedly cut around 6 percent of its workforce, or 1,000 jobs, US media reported last week.

Auction site eBay laid off 1,000 employees earlier this month, adding to a previous round earlier this year which impacted 800 jobs.

In May, Meta laid off around 10 percent of its global workforce, impacting around 8,000 employees.

In April, Meta also said it would cancel plans to hire an additional 6,000 people and also shift 7,000 other employees into AI workflow-related roles.

Ride-hailing giant Uber said in September that it would lay off around 10 percent of its staff, impacting an estimated 3,000 or more employees.

And e-commerce giant Amazon announced 16,000 global job cuts in January.

Microsoft previously cut nearly 5,000 jobs in July that heavily targeted its Xbox gaming division.

Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet and Meta are collectively on track to pour roughly $700 billion into AI data centres, chips and computing infrastructure this year alone.

In July, Microsoft said it spent $41 billion overall between April and June and expected to increase its spending to $50 billion between July and September.

However, the company also adjusted its forecast for total spending in the 2026 calendar year to $175 billion, down from $190 billion previously.

Around two-thirds of its spending goes towards "short-lived assets," specifically chips, due to customer demand for "both AI and non-AI infrastructure," CFO Amy Hood said during a call with analysts.

World.title: KZN learners allegedly barred from exams to protect school’s 100% pass target
World.content:
DURBAN – The KwaZulu-Natal Department of Education is investigating allegations that learners at three schools in the province were barred from writing their National Senior Certificate (NSC) examinations.

In the first incident, a matric learner at Thokozamnganga High School in eNtshongweni, under the Pinetown District, was allegedly prevented from writing her history examination last week because she had not attended extra classes held on a Saturday.

In a second incident, six learners at Shallcross Secondary School in the uMlazi District were allegedly denied the opportunity to write mathematics literacy paper 1. The learners were reportedly told that their performance could jeopardise the school’s target of achieving a 100% pass rate.

At Ntwenhle High School, another learner was allegedly prevented from writing the accounting examination.

KwaZulu-Natal Education MEC Sipho Hlomuka condemned the alleged incidents, stressing that no learner should be denied the opportunity to write an examination.

“The denial of an opportunity to write an examination is a serious matter that cannot be taken lightly. Extra classes are intended to provide additional academic support to learners and must never be used as a punitive measure that compromises their right to complete their examinations.

“No learner should be made to feel that their future is at risk because they did not attend extra classes or because they may not achieve a distinction.”

The department said investigations were under way and would determine the appropriate action to be taken.

World.title: Tshwane must take responsibility for Bronkhorstspruit water crisis, says committee
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG – Parliament’s Portfolio Committee on Water and Sanitation says more people must be held accountable for the Bronkhorstspruit water crisis, after more than 800 people were treated for gastrointestinal illnesses after drinking contaminated water.

The crisis came to light after it emerged that water from the Bronkhorstspruit Wastewater Treatment Works had not been chlorinated and was therefore unsafe for consumption.

The Department of Water and Sanitation said the City of Tshwane had failed to notify residents in time not to drink or use the water.

Most affected are children, many under the age of four.

Committee chairperson Leon Basson said the incident appeared to point to wider problems with Tshwane's water treatment facilities.

“It seems that this problem in Bronkhorstspruit is not isolated. There are other problems with other purification plants in Tshwane,” he said.

Basson said the situation raised serious concerns about the municipality’s handling of drinking water and its response to the contamination.

Tshwane receives some of its water from Rand Water and Magalies Water.

Rand Water is currently helping the City with chlorination and managing the Bronkhorstspruit treatment plant.

World.title: Tshwane warned in 2023 over water treatment concerns, says Mahlobo
World.content:
PRETORIA - Deputy Water and Sanitation Minister David Mahlobo says the City of Tshwane was repeatedly warned about possible water contamination but failed to implement all the recommended corrective measures.

More than 800 people have reportedly fallen ill with gastroenteritis following failures to properly treat contaminated water supplied by the metro.

Mahlobo says Tshwane’s water treatment works were flagged in 2023 after concerns emerged in the government’s Blue Drop and Green Drop assessments, which monitor drinking water quality and wastewater management.

According to the deputy minister, the city submitted a corrective action plan and addressed some of the concerns but failed to resolve others.

He says further warnings were issued earlier this year after officials raised concerns about the quality of water leaving the treatment works.

Records indicate that between 24 September and 14 October, the city failed to carry out basic chemical treatment of water sourced from polluted water bodies.

The untreated water allegedly entered the supply system, contributing to hundreds of reported gastroenteritis cases.

The department has since opened a case over alleged professional negligence by some employees, with Mahlobo saying the incident created a public health hazard and raised concerns about the violation of human rights.

READ MORE | Tshwane water crisis: Parliament calls for wider accountability

“Our Blue Drop and Green Drop results have indicated that many municipalities are struggling, including Tshwane. The water treatment works of Tshwane; we did flag this water treatment works in the year 2023 when we released the results. They produced a corrective plan, they did certain things, they couldn't conclude others.

“Earlier this year, we also did the same and then also gave them warnings that the water that is coming out is not there, is not good,” Mahlabo added.

World.title: Your voting rights: How voters with disabilities can get assistance
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Voters with disabilities, including those who are blind or have visual impairments, have the right to receive assistance when casting their ballots, according to the Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC).

The IEC says voters may choose a companion aged 18 or older to assist them at the voting station.

However, the companion cannot be a candidate in the election or an election agent.

The provision is aimed at ensuring voters with disabilities can exercise their right to vote and participate in the electoral process.

Special voting will take place on 2 and 3 November, allowing eligible voters whose applications have been approved to cast their ballots ahead of Election Day.

Voters whose home visit applications have been approved can cast their ballots at home on 2 or 3 November.

This option is intended for voters who cannot travel to their voting stations because of physical infirmity or disability.

World.title: Closing ranks: Political traffic at Wamunyoro intensifies as Gachagua hosts Kalonzo, Wamalwa
World.content:
Wiper Party leader Kalonzo Musyoka with DCP party leader Rigathi Gachagua at his Wamunyoro residence in Nyeri on October 26, 2026. [Boniface Okendo, Standard]

The Opposition unity is now taking shape following intense political discussions between Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua and Wiper Patriotic Front (WPF) leader Kalonzo Musyoka.

Moments after Kalonzo and his delegation left Wamunyoro, Democratic Action Party leader Eugene Wamalwa and a section of the Luhya council of elders were ushered in for talks about when to announce the Opposition’s Presidential flagbearer, strict timelines of the electoral process, and internal affairs of the Opposition taking centre stage in the separate talks.

World.title: Kikuyu PCEA church loses 2.7-acre illegally acquired land
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Justice Jacqueline Mogeni, in her verdict, said the land in contention was public property and its registration in the name of the said church was irregular and fraudulent. [Courtesy, EACC]

The Presbyterian Church of East Africa (PCEA) has lost its 2.7-acre piece of land to a school.

This is after the Environment and Lands Court at Thika established that the land under the church's Ruguthi Women's Guild was a school playground and was illegally allocated.

Presiding Judge Jacqueline Mogeni, in her verdict, said the land in contention was public property, and its registration in the name of the said church was irregular and fraudulent.

According to her, the land had been reserved for use as a playground by Kanyiha, Lusigetti and Njumbi Primary Schools.

The verdict follows a case filed by the Law Society of Kenya, with the Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (EACC) participating as an interested party.

In a statement on Monday, EACC's head of Corporate Affairs and Communication Stephen Karuga said the anti-graft agency presented evidence demonstrating that the land had been reserved for public use and therefore, any allocation to third parties was irregular. Justice Jacqueline Mogeni, in her verdict, said the land in contention was public property and its registration in the name of the said church was irregular and fraudulent. [Courtesy, EACC]

"Our investigations established that the land was set aside in 1957 by the former County Council of Kiambu for use as a school playing field," Karuga said, adding, "the investigations further revealed that there was no letter of offer or acceptance, no evidence of payment of rent rates and no proof that the Women's Guild had paid any consideration to the council for the land."

According to Karuga, the judgement safeguards a vital public facility used by more than 1,300 pupils, ensuring that the playground remains available for learning, sports and recreation for the current and future generations.

As a result, the judge said the allocation, transfer and registration of the land LR. NO KARAI/350 and subsequent issuance of a title deed in 2001 was unprocedural, illegal, null and void.

"An order of Mandamus is hereby issued directing the 3rd respondent, the Land Registrar, Kiambu Chief Land Registrar, to forthwith cancel and revoke the Title Deed and all register entries in respect of the land issued to the 1st respondent on Dec 6, 2001, or at any subsequent date," the Judge said.

The judge further ordered that the said parcel of land be handed over to the Board of Management of the two schools and the Education Ministry.

"An order of permanent injunction is hereby issued restraining the 1st respondent, whether by herself, her church officials, agents, servants, assigns or anyone claiming through her, from entering into, taking possession of, fencing, depositing construction materials upon, transferring, charging, developing or in any other manner dealing or interfering with the land," she ordered.

World.title: Sakaja protests release of 14 suspects linked to Eastleigh collapsed building
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Sakaja demanded answers from Kamukunji Police on how the suspects were arrested in June but released on Sh50,000 bail without being charged in court. [GPS]

Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja has protested the release of suspects linked to the collapsed building in Eastleigh.

While pushing for the county to have prosecutorial powers, Sakaja demanded answers from Kamukunji Police on how the suspects were arrested in June but released on Sh50,000 bail without being charged in court.

Sakaja in statement posted on his X account (formerly Twitter) said City Hall had taken enforcement action against those involved after establishing change of user from a residential property to a commercial had been approved.

According to Sakaja, architectural plans required to authorise construction had not been approved.

The Governor said County officers arrested the suspects and handed them over to Kamukunji Police Station because county governments no longer hold prosecutorial powers they previously held.

“We enforced the law and arrested those involved. However, because we do not have prosecutorial powers, the suspects were handed over to Kamukunji Police Station. They were reportedly released on a cash bail of Sh50,000 without being taken to court,” Sakaja said.

“We want the police to explain why the suspects were released without being presented in court and why construction was allowed to continue. These are serious questions that must be answered,” he added.

A police occurrence book entry from Kamukunji Police Station indicates that 14 suspects were booked into custody on June 17, 2026, over the alleged offences relating to contravention of city planning laws.

Enforcement action and arrests were made severally by the county officials and most recently in July after failing to comply with the enforcement order below. However the suspects were released on a 50k bail at Kamukunji police on the very same day. Prosecution of the same was also denied. We have repeatedly asked for the resumption of the power to prosecute such violations of such county and county related laws after this was taken away from County governments in 2024 (one such letter to the office of the DPP is attached). Meanwhile, several such cases have either been rejected by prosecutors (who are independent of the County), dismissed by the justice system or have had minimal fines imposed. Fining a developer 50k for an illegal development with hundreds of millions without orders to stop and remove the offensive development is completely unreasonable. I raised this in the Senate a fortnight ago and we shall keep pushing for a review of this position. All of these instances, where enforcement action has been curtailed, blocked or interfered with, will be published to the public. October 25, 2026

The entry, recorded under OB No. 98/17/06/2026, names the suspects and states that they were booked by Nairobi City County officers before being placed in police cells.

A separate Kenya Police Service record indicates that 10 suspects were subsequently released on a cash bail of Sh50,000.

The entry, recorded at 9.44pm, states that the release was carried out on the instructions of the Officer Commanding Station (OCS), identified in the record as C.I. Onyapidi, through Corporal Awadh.

The record references receipt number 2039434 and states that the suspects left the station without complaints.

However, the documents do not, on their own, establish the specific charges against the suspects, the legal basis for the bail arrangement or whether they were subsequently presented in court.

The discrepancy between the 14 suspects recorded as booked into custody and the 10 named in the release entry also raises questions about the subsequent status of the other suspects. Sakaja demanded answers from Kamukunji Police on how the suspects were arrested in June but released on Sh50,000 bail without being charged in court. [GPS]

Sakaja said a June 2025 enforcement notice adds another dimension to the questions surrounding the property and the enforcement of planning regulations.

The notice, issued by Nairobi City County over alleged construction works undertaken without the required development permission, cited the Physical and Land Use Planning Act, 2019, and county by-laws.

It directed the recipient to stop the works and remove the development described as illegal, warning that the County could undertake the required action and recover the costs if the directives were not followed.

The notice also provided for an appeal to the County Physical and Land Use Planning Liaison Committee.

Sakaja clarified that approval to change a property’s use from private to commercial-cum-residential does not amount to approval of architectural plans authorising construction.

He said the County approved the change of use but did not approve the architectural plans, yet construction proceeded.

I have seen some people peddling a fake approval document alleging that the Eastleigh development was approved. It is telling that this is the same document that the Eastleigh developer used to get NCA approval. They allege that the development was approved in January of 2024. This is not true. The application for development as shown below was made in November of 2024, it could not have been approved in February of the same year. Also, there is a difference between a change of user approval and a development approval. The developer applied for change of use from residential to residential & commercial in August of 2024. Change of user was approved in October of 2024. Development approval has never been granted. The developer went on to build with impunity and without building approvals despite enforcement action by the county and arrests. — Sakaja Arthur Johnson (@SakajaJohnson) October 25, 2026

“If the building had been approved for construction, I would have named the officers who approved it so that action could be taken against them,” he said.

Sakaja, in his argument, said the current arrangement creates a gap between enforcement and prosecution, leaving counties dependent on other agencies after taking action against alleged offenders. Sakaja demanded answers from Kamukunji Police on how the suspects were arrested in June but released on Sh50,000 bail without being charged in court. [GPS]

Under his proposal, appropriately authorised county prosecutors would be able to pursue qualifying county offences through the courts, subject to the law and the constitutional authority of the Director of Public Prosecutions.

He said county prosecutors previously had a better understanding of technical offences involving planning, construction and other county regulations, enabling them to handle such cases more directly.

“We want to be able not only to enforce regulations and make arrests, but also to take offenders to court and prosecute them. When counties had prosecutorial powers, we had prosecutors who understood the nature and seriousness of county offences and could ensure that appropriate legal action was taken,” he said.

World.title: Pregnant woman rescued from collapsed Eastleigh building
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenya Red Cross workers after rescuing a man who trapped in the rubble.

A pregnant woman was on Saturday evening rescued from the multi-storey building that collapsed in Nairobi’s Eastleigh estate on Friday, October 23 and rushed to the Kenyatta National Hospital (KNH) for treatment.

She is the second person to rescued as earlier in the afternoon the Kenya Red Cross society announced the rescue of a man from the ill-fated building.

The man was also taken to KNH for treatment with the society saying that the rescue followed hours of work put in by the search and rescue multi-agency team.

“After hours of painstaking work alongside multi-agency partners, our search and rescue teams in Eastleigh brought a trapped man out of the rubble,” said Red Cross.

The rescue comes even as the fate of six people who were reported missing on Friuday remains unknown with rescue teams still continuing with the search at the site of the collapsed building along Yusuf Haji Avenue.

The society said that 66 of the 67 construction workers who were at the site had been traced and accounted for but the search continues for people who may have been near the site of the collapsed building.

The development comes as police announced that they had launched a manhunt for the for the owner and contractor of a building.

Police spokesperson Muchiri Nyaga said that officers had launched a probe in collaboration with relevant bodies to establish the cause of the collapse and determine criminal liability.

“Any individual or entity found culpable of negligence or of violating building regulations will face the full force of the law,” he said in a statement.

Nyaga called on members of public to stay completely clear of Yusuf Haji Avenue and 9th Street to give access to heavy excavators, specialised canine units and rescue personnel to perform their duties.

Earlier Saturday, at least 31 families reported their relatives missing as coordinated rescue efforts entered their second day.

No deaths have been reported so far.

The National Construction Authority (NCA) on Friday evening identified the developer, contractor, architect and structural engineer listed for the collapsed building.

The Authority has faced scrutiny over its oversight role, as Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja said the project had failed to comply with construction guidelines.

He said the county had forwarded relevant information to the Directorate of Criminal Investigations for further investigation.

In a statement, the NCA said the building was registered on July 30, 2025, as a proposed development on 9th Street in Eastleigh.

It identified 9th Street Plaza Limited as the developer and Stromax Holdings E.A. Limited as the contractor.

Emmanuel Mwangi Maina was listed as the project architect, while Joseph Muturi Mugu was named as the structural engineer.

World.title: Several feared trapped in Eastleigh building collapse
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Rescue efforts at the collapsed storey building in Eastleigh 9th street in Nairobi County. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

What was supposed to be a usually busy Friday afternoon in Eastleigh's 9th Street turned chaotic after an 18-floor building that was under construction came down, tumbling.

By Friday evening, rescue operations were still ongoing, with cries from people believed to have been trapped being heard from a distance as bulldozers and rescuers continued the search operation.

Two victims, a man and a woman, who were injured in the building had been rescued and rushed to hospital as the search continued.

Asha Jilo, one of the witnesses, said the building collapsed around 1:09 pm just after the afternoon prayers.

"Immediately after the building collapsed, we started contacting some people we know who work there, one of them was still available on the phone until around 3 pm, when his phone went offline," Jilo shared

On Fridays, Eastleigh is usually a hive of activities, being the main market day, but all the businesses were shut as police were battling rowdy youths, some of them believed to be opportunists.

The building, whose height was said to be about 15 floors, had not been cleared for occupation as required, raising questions about why the investors had allowed it to be taken.

It is said that the ground and first floors were already occupied by businesses, raising fears that the number of victims could be high. Rescue efforts at the collapsed storey building in Eastleigh 9th street in Nairobi County. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

At the time of the collapse, it is said that some construction workers were busy on the upper floors.

Governor Johnson Sakaja, who visited the scene after the collapse, was still gathering information about the building. The first priority was about saving lives.

“The building that collapsed is around 16 floors, and we have got information about the building, but what is more concerned right now is for us to save lives,” said Sakaja

Adding, “Equipment has already been mobilized, excavators and breakers, so we can be able to remove the big debris and save lives,’

The Governor said some developers engage qualified professionals to secure construction approvals before dismissing them and disregarding approved plans and safety standards.

He urged professional bodies to strengthen oversight, investigate such cases and take appropriate disciplinary action, stressing that developers must comply with approved designs, engage qualified personnel and obtain occupation certificates after safety inspections.

Rescue efforts at the collapsed storey building in Eastleigh 9th street in Nairobi County. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

Nairobi Regional Police Commander Issa Mohamud, who was at the scene, said that, according to reliable information, several people were trapped inside the debris, inside the big boulders, and the rescue effort is ongoing.

The city police boss said investigations will be carried out to ascertain who is responsible for any negligence.

“If there will be any death, that is negligence by murder. Whoever is the owner, whoever authorized the building, all of them will be charged properly. But that will come after thorough investigation is done,” he warned

Adding, “We will not excuse anybody on this matter. This has become now and then, and we will make sure that people face the law accordingly for any criminal negligence,”

World.title: Ruto hands over COMESA chairmanship, pushes for levy to fund regional programmes
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President Ruto and Zimbabwean President Emmerson Mnangagwa during the handover of the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa chairmanship at the bloc’s 25th Summit of Heads of State and Government in Harare, Zimbabwe, on Thursday, October 22, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has handed over the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) chairmanship to Zimbabwean President Emmerson Mnangagwa.

Ruto took over the one-year chairmanship from Burundi’s President Évariste Ndayishimiye at the 24th COMESA Summit in Nairobi on October 9, 2025.

His tenure focused on using digital technology to deepen regional integration, expand trade and promote inclusive growth.

He handed over the role on Thursday, October 22, during the 25th Comesa Summit of Heads of State and Government in Harare, Zimbabwe, where he urged the regional bloc to fast-track a market levy to finance its programmes and institutions.

“We cannot be ambitious in our plans and timid in our financing. Every programme we agree upon must be matched by the resources to deliver it. Otherwise, our communiqués will promise what our budgets cannot pay for,” Ruto said.

He urged the Comesa Secretariat to fast-track Article 168 of the COMESA Treaty, which provides for the Comesa Market Levy, as the organisation seeks sustainable and predictable financing.

The treaty establishes the levy to generate resources for financing the bloc’s activities.

Ruto said officials from finance ministries, central banks and other relevant agencies would meet to consider a draft COMESA Resource Mobilisation Strategy aimed at strengthening member states’ ownership of regional programmes and finding new ways to raise funds.

He called on member states to make financing central to their discussions, warning that the bloc’s institutions and integration agenda would depend on their ability to fund agreed commitments.

“Can we finance what we commit, and deliver what we finance?” he asked.

Ruto also urged African countries to channel more of their domestic financial resources into African institutions rather than leaving funds in foreign accounts while development projects lack capital.

He said Africa holds more than $4 trillion in domestic financial assets, arguing that regional financial institutions could mobilise more of these resources to support trade, infrastructure and development.

Ruto named the Trade and Development Bank (TDB), the African Trade and Investment Development Insurance (ATIDI) and ZEP-RE among the institutions that could mobilise capital for regional priorities.

He urged African governments to place more reserves with these institutions, finance more projects through them and support their bonds and guarantees.

The outgoing Comesa chairperson said the bloc needed stronger regional value chains and more trade among member states as global supply chains faced disruption and protectionism returned.

“Regional integration is no longer a dream we discuss. It is an economic and strategic necessity,” he noted.

Ruto said Comesa’s economic growth rose from 5.6 per cent in 2024 to 6.4 per cent in 2025, while inflation fell from 31 per cent to 13.2 per cent.

Exports among member states increased by 10.5 per cent to $14.7 billion, their highest level between 2020 and 2025, while exports to global markets rose by 6 per cent to $212 billion, he said.

He argued that African countries needed to process more raw materials locally instead of exporting them and importing finished products.

“To every partner who seeks our minerals, our markets and our young workforce, our offer is clear: invest with us, process with us, build with us,” Ruto added.

He called for partnerships based on mutual benefit and equal treatment, saying African countries should have a greater role in determining how their resources and markets contribute to economic development.

World.title: Judge certifies fresh bid to jail Sakaja, Charles Kerich over Sh76.7m debt as urgent
World.content:
Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja. [File, Standard]

The High Court has certified as urgent a fresh application seeking to have Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja, former Finance Executive Charles Kerich and two other county officials jailed over an alleged breach of a court-approved payment plan in a Sh106.7 million legal fees dispute.

Justice Francis Gikonyo certified the application by Kwengu & Company Advocates seeking to reinstate a three-month jail sentence previously imposed on Kerich and hold Sakaja, current Finance County Executive Committee Member Ibrahim Auma Nyangoya and Chief Officer for Finance Asha Abdi accountable for the alleged failure to pay Sh76.7 million.

World.title: Kenya confirms third Ebola case
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenya has confirmed a third case of Ebola involving a 65-year-old woman who is a close relative of the first two patients.

The Ministry of Health, in a statement, said the woman developed a fever, sore throat and malaise while in quarantine, prompting her isolation and testing.

Her samples tested positive for Ebola at both the National Virology Reference Laboratory and the Kenya Medical Research Institute (KEMRI).

According to the Health Director-General Patrick Amoth, the patient has been transferred to an infectious disease unit, where she is receiving supportive care and being monitored.

“Having been in quarantine, she was diagnosed early and is currently receiving supportive care, improving her chances of recovery while limiting the risk of further spread of the disease,” the statement read.

The second patient, on the other hand, is in stable condition and responding well to supportive care.

The latest case brings the number of confirmed Ebola infections in Kenya to three.

According to the Ministry, of the 130 contacts identified so far, 127 had been traced and placed in quarantine, with efforts ongoing to trace the remaining three.

World.title: Serbia’s leader concedes defeat to student-led movement in seismic political shift
World.content:
Belgrade, Serbia AP —

The long-serving strongman leader of Serbia, Aleksandar Vucic, conceded defeat on Sunday in an election that pitted him and his right-wing party against a diverse student-led opposition movement that spent two years protesting his government.

It was a seismic political shift in the Balkan country where Vucic, who had been endorsed by Russian President Vladimir Putin and who denounced the student movement as a foreign-led attempt to unseat him, led for 14 years.

High turnout and gathering tensions marked the highly contested parliamentary election that was a showdown between Vucic and his right-wing Serbian Progressive Party and university students who, accusing the government of corruption and dismantling democracy, had built a popular following across the country.

Serbia’s 6.4 million voters were electing lawmakers to the 250-member Parliament. In conceding the election, Vucic said his party projects that his opponents, the youth-backed Students’ List, will take between 135 and 140 seats while his SNS party will have around 105.

“The Students’ List has won,” Vucic told supporters at his party’s election-night event, though he blamed Serbia’s independent media as well as alleged interference by unnamed European countries and an “American deep state” for the loss.

Belgrade erupts in celebration

Vucic said that his SNS party won around 1.7 million votes compared to the Students’ List, which he said took around 2.2 million.

Supporters of the Students’ List immediately flooded onto the streets of Belgrade and other cities, honking horns, shouting and chanting: “Aleksandar is gone,” referring to Vucic.

The outcome, which Vucic announced only around an hour and a half after polls closed, came after tensions had built as voting progressed during the day.

Police in anti-riot gear cordoned off an area in central Belgrade around the election commission headquarters. Special police vehicles could be seen near a Belgrade park where Vucic’s loyalists have been camping for over a year, and large groups of black-clad men had congregated at various points throughout the city.

Protests over corruption lead to Vucic’s fall

Vucic was seeking to become Serbia’s prime minister after serving two near-full terms as president. He resigned the presidency last month to lead the campaign.

Support for the populist had eroded since 16 people were killed in 2024 when a concrete canopy collapsed at a train station in Novi Sad. That set off a wave of youth protests that blamed the collapse on high-level corruption, cronyism and rampant graft during renovation work at the station.

Despite the protests, Vucic retained considerable support among many of Serbia’s voters. Admirers viewed him as a capable leader who can steer the nation through global uncertainties — the image that was carefully crafted by the mainstream media.

Student movement

While the increasingly authoritarian Vucic has routinely outplayed Serbia’s fractured opposition in the past, the leaderless youth movement proved to be a tough opponent that rattled his firm grip on power in Serbia like no one else in the 14 years since his party took office.

The newly formed Students’ List movement was shaped by university students but none actually appeared on the election list. Instead, its candidates are little-known experts, athletes, farmers and artists.

This approach was meant to counter Vucic’s one-man rule and restore a sense of community and solidarity. The students’ message during the campaign focused on a non-partisan effort to rebuild Serbia’s economy and restore its democracy.

Candidates and supporters at the Students’ List headquarters in Belgrade celebrate victory at the news that Serbia’s ruling party, the Serbian Progressive Party, has conceded defeat in the parliamentary elections on October 25. ( Andrej Isakovic/AFP/Getty Images

The students have used youthful energy to attract voters who are disillusioned with local politicians. Vilified by pro-government media, they cycled and walked through the country to reach voters in rural areas — Vucic’s traditional strongholds.

The student victory echoed the recent electoral defeat of a Vucic ally in Hungary, where youth participation helped oust the autocratic Viktor Orbán after 16 years and bring in a new pro-European government. It was likely to resonate beyond Serbia as countries across Europe have faced angry youth and student protests.

The vote was closely watched in the EU

Monitors predicted that total turnout in the election could reach around 70%, unseen in Serbia since 2000. During the day, long queues formed at polling stations in Serbia and in cities around the world. Some in the Serbian diaspora were made to vote in the middle of the night after authorities tied voting hours to local Serbian time.

Recent Serbian elections had been marred by irregularities and the EU was closely watching the conduct of Sunday’s vote in a candidate nation for the bloc’s membership.

Independent election monitors reported dozens of cases of irregularities on Sunday such as photographing of ballots that suggested pressure on voters and attempted vote buying.

Both international and local election monitors had expressed concern about the safety and fairness of an election campaign marked by detentions, near-total government control over the media and reports of surveillance and cyberattacks against activists.

Local elections earlier this year in 10 municipalities in Serbia saw violent attacks on journalists and activists. The previous parliamentary vote in 2023 was followed by opposition protests alleging fraud.

World.title: Kamala Harris responds to her critics and Democrats who don’t want her to run again
World.content:
Clarksdale, Mississippi —

“Nice to meet you, Madam President,” Kamala Harris said, shaking hands with the Coahoma Community College student body representative on her surprise stop by the campus on Thursday afternoon.

Harris likes that disarming joke. She was the biggest political figure to come across this underfunded school in the Mississippi Delta, the grass so dry it crunched as she walked with a gathering of stunned students for a group picture.

“You don’t know how many people this uplifts,” said Don Green, who followed Harris that afternoon from the college to a rural health clinic in Clarksdale, most famous for being the site of the legendary Crossroads of the Blues.

Mike Cavanaugh, a sophomore at the University of Mississippi and president of the campus’ College Democrats, spoke ahead of Harris at a rally that day and answered her questions about voter registration during his brief chat with her on the photo line. “Young people are very excited,” he said.

“It didn’t have to be this way,” is one of the lines Harris used several times on the stump in Mississippi as she campaigned for Democrat Scott Colom, whose challenge to Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith is drawing a new burst of national attention and outside money.

“There are so many people who were devastated with the outcome of that election — for good reason, for really good reason,” Harris told CNN backstage before her speech at the rally and two days after her 62nd birthday. “That pain, it lingers, because every day we are witnessing events that we know didn’t have to happen. Could have been different.”

After the interview ended, Harris asked to go back on the record.

“The American people want leaders who aren’t just occupied with looking in the mirror. They want leaders who are looking at the people, you know?” she said. “And they can tell the difference.”

Much of the political insider world has been clear in not wanting Harris to run for president in 2028, or really not wanting to hear from her again, ever. Even before Democrats’ horror year of Joe Biden’s collapse, the contortions over Gaza that she’s still struggling with and Donald Trump’s return, Harris was never good about cultivating donors or keeping aides from fleeing her overly cautious style and the constant infighting that followed.

Yet with her stops in Mississippi and across the country, she’s hearing from many Democratic campaigns who believe having her around helps — and lots of voters who are turning out to show they agree. All told, she’ll end the midterms with more campaign appearances than Barack Obama, and after a late flurry that includes Wisconsin and Georgia this week, more than almost any potential top-tier 2028 candidate.

Several close to the former vice president and 2024 presidential nominee told CNN they believe when she keeps saying she’s thinking about running again, what that means is that after months of soaking up the superfans who bought tickets to her book tour, she hasn’t ruled it out.

But not killing the option is different from pursuing it, whether lining up staff or crafting a new agenda, and Harris acknowledged that her time-treading answers about not having made up her mind can only go on so long. But asked if that means six months or even a year, she said, “I don’t know.”

“I go back and forth. I honestly go back and forth,” Harris said of which way she’s leaning. “There’s so many factors.”

What Harris does know, two years after losing, is that she’s less interested in the game of inches that presidential primaries tend to be.

“I’ll be very specific,” she said. “If I run, my motivation is not to beat other Democrats. It’s to actually do the job.”

Privately, she’s been known to do her wry stare at comments from other Democrats who say she shouldn’t run – convenient, she says, since that would mean they didn’t have to run against her.

“I’m sure there are many who think that I should just sit at home and eat bonbons and cook Doug’s favorite foods,” she said, brushing off the Wall Street Journal article reporting that her husband, Doug Emhoff, had privately told some people that he preferred she didn’t run. “I could cook Doug’s favorite foods and do this.”

Harris said Emhoff was upset at his feelings being portrayed inaccurately. According to one person who has spoken directly with him, his more precise feeling is that the moves the two of them have been making were not done with a plan to run again.

“I feel so strongly and therefore am compelled, and maybe propelled, into doing this, because I know that I can help,” she added. “And how can I sit at home in the comfort of my home when I know there are things I can do to help? I don’t know any other life but that – that’s my point. I don’t know any life that is not about, ‘There’s a problem, what can I do to fix it?’”

Other Democrats could start campaigns in the next several weeks

When Harris talks about “turning pain into purpose,” that means one thing to frustrated voters in the final days of these midterm campaigns, like the retired plumber who shouted “You told us so!” as she ripped Trump’s record in the gym at Columbus High School.

It can mean another to the woman who was herself the candidate Trump beat, even as she kept up the smiles pouring drinks behind the bar at another stop in New Hampshire on Saturday. Around this time two years ago, Harris was calling around to make sure old friends would be with her to celebrate back on the quad at Howard University. She stopped her remarks on Thursday to call back to the man, “Yes, brother, I did.”

Supporters listen as Democratic presidential nominee US Vice President Kamala Harris delivers remarks, conceding the 2024 US presidential election to President-elect Donald Trump, at Howard University in Washington, on November 6, 2024. Evelyn Hockstein/Reuters

Harris did not, like Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro, Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker and Georgia Sen. Jon Ossoff, hit the Hamptons fundraising circuit this summer. She has not, as had been proposed in an internal memo circulated among her advisers, launched an extensive engagement tour championing Black voting rights in the wake of the Supreme Court’s Callais decision.

She spent much of the last year on an extended book tour that took her to 27 states and made her millions more than expected. She sold one of the X accounts she controlled to a partnership that netted her more money.

Yet she kept working the phones, whether calling a range of advocates and asking what she could have done differently in her abbreviated presidential run, or checking in with candidates like Texas Senate Democratic nominee James Talarico, to whom she offered some advice over how to manage the ongoing criticism from his former primary opponent, Rep. Jasmine Crockett, whom she endorsed before he won.

Her prospective opponents aren’t waiting on her.

Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear has discussed a plan to launch his campaign shortly after the December meeting of the Democratic Governors Association, when he’ll officially wrap up his stint as its chair. After months of public denials while maintaining a national travel schedule, Maryland Gov. Wes Moore has started telling people that after November he’s going to take another look at running for president.

Arizona Sen. Mark Kelly and former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg have been all over the country stumping for candidates, including in early states, as aides make sure to remind reporters each time they add more stops. New Jersey Sen. Cory Booker has quietly banked $20 million and started thinking through a South Carolina and Super Tuesday-focused strategy.

Operatives associated with multiple likely contenders are assembling opposition research files on expected opponents and asking around for suggestions of staff to hire. Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz, her former running mate, is already saying his advice for the future of the Democratic Party is “pick Pete Buttigieg” (which Harris said she hadn’t seen).

Harris’ motorcade is now just two cars, no sirens. She flies commercial. She pays for staff and security out of the limited fundraising she’s still doing off her old campaign email list, which left her and advisers having to pick between stops she was asked to make and forcing her to stack several virtual appearances into a day she’ll spend this week holed up in a hotel room with a computer instead.

“I have more access, you know? It’s like, the bubble is smaller, and that’s nice. Or there’s not a bubble,” she said.

As for candidates like Rob Sand, running for governor in Iowa, or Adam Hamilton, running for Senate in Kansas, who’ve said they don’t want her to come, Harris says she doesn’t take that personally.

“Oh, I want them to do whatever they need to do to win. I mean that sincerely,” Harris told CNN. “I have run for local, state, and national office. I am not naïve. And I want to win, and I respect whatever decisions they need to make in order to do that.”

Nor was she interested in drawing a line against candidates like Angie Nixon, the Democratic nominee for Senate in Florida who said she joined the Democratic Socialists of America specifically as part of launching her campaign, and who will be part of one of Harris’s virtual events this week.

Asked how big of a role the DSA should have in Democrats’ future, Harris said, “We are, as we say, a big tent, and I don’t think anybody should be kicked out.”

The lessons of Mississippi

Mississippi won’t be an early stop on the 2028 presidential calendar. But its electorate could offer a preview of what might await Harris in South Carolina, which is set to host the first Democratic primary again and where Black voters are critical.

“The conventional wisdom,” she said in Mississippi, is, “‘Those are red states, we can’t win there, therefore we won’t go there,’ as opposed to reconditioning ourselves to think about the fact that there are a lot of people who live here who actually care about the things we care about and deserve to be heard and deserve to have us spend our time and resources sitting with them and listening to them.”

Harris first connected with Colom in January, after Rep. Bennie Thompson, the lone Democrat sent to Washington from Mississippi, got them on the phone when she brought her book tour to Jackson. Colom’s campaign to unseat Hyde-Smith, in a state Harris lost to Trump by 23 points, has drawn increasing buzz and now outside spending from both Democratic- and GOP-aligned groups.

Still several Colom consultants initially opposed having Harris join campaign events, worried about nationalizing the race and bringing in a candidate known for losing. With some encouragement, Colom overruled them and called her directly to ask.

Georgia Sen. Raphael Warnock, who told CNN that he’s considering a presidential run and for months was a main engine of getting Democrats to focus on Colom’s race, drew 100 people when he came to the state two weeks ago. Harris had over 1,000 on their feet in the gym, with an RSVP list that had to be closed because of the fire marshal – even after a sudden decision to bar holding the event at a local college forced a last-minute venue change.

“In this community, it transcends the fact that she lost the last election,” Thompson told CNN while waiting for her to arrive at the community college.

Former US Vice President Kamala Harris speaks during a special lecture titled “American Leadership and the Future of Alliances” at the Asan Institute for Policy Studies in Seoul, South Korea, on October 14. Ahn Young-joon/AP

Black maternal mortality was a top issue for Harris when she was vice president. But when he’s campaigning with a focus on 400,000 people in the state without health insurance, rural hospitals closing and mothers dying waiting for a limited number of ambulances to be able to get them, Colom said he saw enormous value having Harris help draw a dozen reporters from across the state to a maternal health care clinic that’s struggling to cover costs.

“The question is: why does Vice President Harris care more about healthcare in our hospitals than our junior senator? If she cares more than our junior senator, I want to bring attention to that issue because that matters,” Colom told CNN after the rally. “You see how many people showed up, you see the excitement. People care about folks that are going to fight for the people.”

In Mississippi, as in Harris’ other stops, the memory of her loss cuts two ways.

“There’s people that think that she got the raw end of the deal,” said Chris Miller, the former chair of the Clark County Democrats in Nevada, who was an early supporter of her 2020 presidential campaign and attended the rally she did with the powerful Culinary Workers Union on behalf of her longtime supporter, state Attorney General Aaron Ford, running for governor. “There’s a feeling that if she wants to run, she should run.”

Patrick Gaspard, who was Obama’s first political director at the White House and has recently been informally advising a number of rising new voices in the Democratic Party including New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, was part of the Colom kitchen cabinet encouraging him to bring Harris in.

Videoing the crowd’s reaction to her on stage on his iPhone in Columbus on Thursday night, Gaspard said that has to be factored into any 2028 math, especially at a moment when voters around the country are making clear that they feel abandoned by the people who read tipsheets in green rooms.

“When Muhammad Ali was trying to regain the heavyweight crown, there were a lot of people who were saying they didn’t want him fighting again, they didn’t want him in the ring,” Gaspard told CNN. “They were saying that not because they were worried that Muhammad Ali would fall flat on his face — they were worried he would win.”

The story headline has been updated.

World.title: ‘He can barely walk’: Russians tell how vulnerable men are being targeted and coerced into signing up
World.content:
“They put him in the car and forced him to sign a contract…”

“Now he’s listed as missing… I haven’t fully accepted that he is most likely already dead.”

“It’s a paralyzing fear.”

All of these are quotes from people who say they have personal experience of forced military recruitment in Russia.

Their stories, told directly to CNN and backed up by human rights groups and a growing body of accounts from individuals and social media, paint a picture of a quiet shift underway in Russia’s war recruitment machine, now in its fifth year. We are obscuring their identities over their fear of reprisals.

Since a mass mobilization drive in 2022, which sparked a panicked exodus across its borders, Russia has relied mostly on large financial incentives to lure soldiers to fight. Evidence suggests that is now slowly giving way to coercion and deception.

Russia has repeatedly dismissed Ukrainian claims it is planning a new wave of mass mobilization, despite rising frontline casualties and falling recruitment numbers. And yet, as Russia escalates attacks, this “creeping mobilization” – as some are calling it – threatens to erode public acceptance of the war, just as the Kremlin needs it most.

Vulnerable targets

“I have (or rather I had) an uncle,” reads the message to CNN. “He is an old sick man, he has vascular problems and alcoholism, he can barely walk.”

In July, the person said, their uncle, an employee at a state defense company in his late 50s, was approached outside his apartment block by several men in civilian clothes and taken away in a car. They didn’t know where he was taken, but said that day “they slipped him a document to sign, supposedly a ‘notification that they were there.’ It turned out to be a contract (to join the military).”

The story, from a town in western Russia, fits an all-too-familiar pattern, said Artem Klyga, a Russian military lawyer based in Berlin, who advises Russians on their rights when it comes to military service. Since the start of the summer, he said, he has seen a surge in people reaching out to him about this kind of incident. “Now it’s a day-to-day practice,” he told CNN. Most cases he sees involve vulnerable men, often in debt or with health or alcohol problems. “They simply do not have a chance to say no, simply do not know their rights.”

“Call to Conscience,” a coalition of lawyers helping conscripts and reservists in Russia with advice around conscientious objection, told CNN they had seen a surge in reports of forced recruitment in July and August, with tactics “getting harsher by the day.”

In this case, after signing the document, the uncle returned home, his relative said, but a week later he disappeared. A few days after that he called to say he was at a training ground in Luhansk, in Russian-controlled eastern Ukraine. In late September came the news he was missing in action.

“I have trouble falling asleep, sometimes I have nightmares that they catch me,” the relative told CNN.

Ukrainian servicemen fire a Panzerhaubitze 2000 self-propelled howitzer towards Russian troops at a position in the Donetsk region on September 18. Anatolii Stepanov/Reuters

Another Russian who contacted CNN via a human-rights group said their brother was “detained” in mid-July “in a state of alcoholic intoxication, by unknown employees” – the relative’s assumption being that they worked for the local military recruitment office.

In this case, CNN has seen the military contract the brother ended up signing, as well as a video of what appears to be his last goodbye to his tearful mother before he gets into a white van. The relative also shared the written response from the local military prosecutor’s office to the family’s petition for the man to be released. It concludes he appeared at the recruitment office “of his own free will, without any coercion,” adding that “the contrary has neither been proven nor documented.”

Less than a month later came the news that he, too, was missing in action.

“He had a very difficult life, problems with alcohol,” the relative told CNN.

I am psychologically devastated; I always knew that rights in the Russian Federation are systematically violated, but I did not fully grasp what it is like to experience it.” Message to CNN from relative of recruit into Russian army

In June, Russia’s Penza region, about 375 miles south of Moscow, emerged as a particular hotspot for forced recruitment, according to social media accounts and human rights groups. Videos and accounts surfaced online of individuals being forcefully recruited off the streets.

In one video from June which CNN has geolocated to a military recruitment center in Penza, women crowd around a bus demanding the men inside be released. One woman points inside the bus: “What do you think, did they sign voluntarily or not?” she shouts at the camera. One of the men inside the bus seems to shake his head. “They forced you, they beat you,” shouts another woman. The Russian Ministry of Defense dismissed the reports of forced mobilization in Penza as fake.

Reports of violence in cases of forced recruitment are common, as is a disregard for medical exemptions. “The contract was signed under physical and moral pressure,” wrote one relative, who told CNN their uncle was taken in August. At the time he had a broken rib, they said.

‘Bring a friend’ bonuses

Another common feature of many of these stories: the individuals taking men on the street are not clearly identified, and are often in civilian clothes. This has raised concerns that they could be ordinary people trying to cash in on another type of military bonus – paid to anyone helping recruit new soldiers. One relative described them as “bounty hunters.”

“The recruiters know they are sending people to probable death for a reward, they have no compassion for either the contract soldiers or their relatives.” Message to CNN from relative of recruit into Russian army

CNN has not been able to verify this in specific cases, but regional authorities are making no attempt to hide the fact these payments exist.

“We will encourage those who provide assistance in attracting citizens to sign contracts,” announced Pavel Malkov, the governor of Russia’s Ryazan region, last August in a session of the regional parliament.

“We will provide a financial payment for each contract soldier. The bonus sum will vary from 50,000 to 300,000 rubles ($590 to $3,500), this is after tax.”

Staff at a recruitment stand for military contract service are pictured in a shopping mall in Moscow on October 10. Getty Images
