World.title: Mpika farmers urged to embrace climate‑smart farming
World.content:
Mpika District Commissioner David Siame has urged farmers in the district to embrace climate-smart agricultural practices to strengthen productivity, build resilience to climate change and improve rural livelihoods.

Mr Siame pointed out that agriculture remains a major source of food, income and employment for many households.

He however stressed that increasing climate variability requires farmers to adopt sustainable farming methods and technologies that can withstand changing weather patterns.

He said the Grow Zambia Agenda provides an important framework for accelerating economic transformation, with agriculture playing a central role in increasing production, creating employment and improving livelihoods.

The District Commissioner was speaking at the climate smart farmer preparedness workshop navigation of El Nino organized by the Solutions for Training in Agriculture and Resource Transformation (START) initiative in Mpika today.

He said that the initiative presents an opportunity for the district to promote crop diversification, strengthen value addition and improve farmers’ access to markets.

Mr Siame said achieving sustainable agricultural transformation requires farmers to have access to affordable inputs, appropriate financing, reliable climate information and improved agricultural technologies.

He also stressed the need to promote sustainable water management and irrigation systems to reduce dependence on seasonal rainfall.

The District Commissioner said climate-smart practices such as conservation farming, soil moisture management, crop diversification and the use of climate-resilient seed varieties are essential in reducing farmers’ vulnerability to drought and other climate-related risks.

He further emphasised the importance of timely weather forecasts and agricultural advisory services to help farmers make informed decisions on planting, crop selection and resource management.

Mr Siame also urged farmers attending the workshop to participate actively, share their experiences and identify at least three practical climate-smart agricultural practices to adopt or strengthen on their farms.

“We are encouraging you to share the knowledge acquired with fellow farmers in your communities to broaden the adoption of sustainable farming methods,” he said

The DC also commended the Start Initiative for its commitment to agricultural training and community empowerment, particularly its proposed Growing Future projects, which include community-based practical training and agricultural training centers.

“The initiative was encouraged to establish partnerships that support continued farmer training, practical demonstrations and technical mentorship,” he said

Mr Siame said that sustainable agricultural development requires coordinated efforts among Government, the private sector, civil society and farming communities.

He also added that climate preparedness must be integrated into household and community-level agricultural planning to improve productivity, strengthen resilience and enhance farmers’ living standards.

The workshop is expected to provide practical information on seasonal climate outlooks, improved farming practices, agricultural inputs and weather-index insurance.

And Mpika District Senior Agriculture officer (SAO) Sheila Mumba has called on farmers to adopt climate-smart and cost-effective farming practices to mitigate the effects of climate change and improve agricultural productivity.

Ms Mumba said erratic rainfall, prolonged dry spells and shifting growing seasons continued to pose challenges to farming communities, threatening crop yields, food security and rural livelihoods.

She said that climate-smart agriculture was essential to strengthening farmers’ resilience while supporting the attainment of national agricultural production targets.

Ms Mumba noted that government has prioritized climate-smart agriculture as a strategy for increasing crop production, in line with a presidential directive targeting the production of 10 million metric tonnes of maize, three million metric tonnes of soybeans, one million metric tonnes of wheat and one million metric tonnes of sugarcane by 2031.

Ms Mumba commended the START Initiative for organising the workshop in collaboration with the department in Mpika noting that the engagement would equip farmers with practical knowledge and strategies for adopting sustainable farming methods.

Meanwhile, START Initiative Board Chairperson Reverend Chrispin Suya has announced plans to introduce school vegetable gardens and community-based agricultural training programmes next year to equip youths and small-scale farmers with practical farming skills.

Mr Suya said the initiatives were aimed at transforming attitudes towards agriculture and promoting farming as a viable business and a source of employment, particularly among young people facing unemployment challenges.

He said that the Growing Future project would be introduced in selected local schools to teach learners crop planning, production, agribusiness and practical farming skills, adding that early exposure to agriculture would help nurture a generation of productive and entrepreneurial farmers.

Mr Suya said that START Initiative would also conduct targeted community training in commercial soybean production, modern fish farming and improved livestock management to help farmers venture into high-value agricultural enterprises.

He noted that the organisation was also seeking land to establish a practical agricultural training centre where youths and farmers could receive hands-on training in modern agricultural methods.

Mr Suya said the organisation further intended to promote integrated farming systems and circular bio-systems to help farmers reduce production costs through efficient resource utilisation.

The initiatives are expected to strengthen agricultural productivity, create employment opportunities and improve rural livelihoods.

World.title: Chipangali farmers urged not to plant tobacco
World.content:
The World Food Program (WFP), and the World Health Organisation (WHO) have expressed satisfaction with the utilisation of the Mutambala irrigation scheme Project in Chipangali District, Eastern Province.

The project is part of the alternative livelihood programme which seeks to discourage the growing of tobacco, and promote the growing of crops that do not contribute to the loss of soil fertility and environmental degradation.

Speaking during the tour of the Mutambala irrigation scheme in Wilikani village, World Health Organisation (WHO) National Professional Officer for tobacco control in Zambia Agatha Shula said she was elated with the work of the beneficiaries at the irrigation scheme who have shown great commitment and made progress in improving their wellbeing through the growing of alternative crops.

Ms Shula urged the beneficiaries to avoid growing tobacco which is harmful to human health and the environment.

“We are happy with how the project is doing here in Mutambala. We have seen that the approach of alternative livelihoods is being embraced. The issue with tobacco farming is very serious, it is a silent killer and affects our wellbeing,” Ms Shula said.

She emphasised that growing tobacco negatively affects soil fertility and causes environmental degradation.

Ms Shula has since called on the beneficiaries to be ambassadors of change in their communities by promoting alternative crops to tobacco.

And World Health Organisation African Regional Manager for Tobacco Control, William Maina, commended the beneficiaries for their work and commitment.

“What you are doing here is very encouraging, especially having a communal farm where you are all jointly working together to grow food. We want to encourage you to continue doing this work, and in the future, we will consider exchange visits so that others can come and learn from you,” Dr Maina said.

And Ministry of Health Tobacco Control Focal Point Person Chirispine Sichone emphasised on the negative effects of tobacco to human life, and urged the community to choose healthier alternatives.

He said the government is concerned with the health risks associated with tobacco evidenced by the passing of the tobacco control bill of 2025 which is awaiting presidential assent.

World.title: South Africa: Joburg Faces 3-Month Wait for Water Relief - South African News Briefs - October 27, 2026
World.content:
press review

Joburg Residents Face Up to 3-Month Wait for Water Relief

Johannesburg Water has said that residents may only begin to see relief from ongoing water shortages within the next three months, reports EWN. CEO Ntshavheni Mukwevho told residents at a community engagement in Crown Gardens that the city is implementing short-term interventions to improve pressure management and speed up responses to supply problems. However, he said sustained improvements would require long-term investment in water infrastructure. Meanwhile, Mayor Dada Morero maintained that the city's water challenges have not yet reached crisis levels.

Man To Seek Bail In Slain Runner’s Smartwatch Case



One of the three men arrested in connection with the possession and alleged resale of murdered runner Elizabeth "Tsontso" Moselakgomo's smartwatch is set to apply for bail in the Kempton Park Magistrates' Court, reports SABC News. Second-hand shop owner Kenneth Chibuzor faces charges including money laundering, theft and contraventions of the Second-Hand Goods Act. His co-accused, Stephen Sekhukhune and Danial Anthony Moat, face money laundering and theft charges. The State alleges the smartwatch changed hands several times after being acquired for R900. Moselakgomo's body was discovered in Rhodesfield, Ekurhuleni, on 12 September, three days after she was last seen leaving home for a run. Sekhukhune and Moat have been granted bail of R10,000 each.

Community Groups Seek Role In Migration Court Cases

Inter-Ministerial Committee on Migration chairperson Mammoloko Kubayi has said that community leaders and organisations want to join the government’s legal proceedings concerning asylum seekers and illegal migration, reports EWN. The cases include the Scalabrini Centre of Cape Town matter and conflicting Gauteng High Court judgments involving asylum seekers detained at the Lindela Repatriation Centre. Representatives from the Black Business Community, Bhinca Nation Organisation and Hlangana Mzansi want to present their lived experiences and highlight the socioeconomic challenges they associate with illegal migration. Kubayi said legal teams and senior counsel have offered to assist the groups on a pro bono basis.

World.title: Kenya: Police, Protesters Clash During Cost-of-Living, Fuel Demonstrations
World.content:
Cape Town — Nairobi police arrested several protesters on Monday as officers and demonstrators clashed in running battles across the CBD over rising fuel prices and the cost of living, The Eastleigh Voice reports.

Protesters gathered on Moi Avenue and Kimathi Street despite a heavy police deployment, carrying placards reading 'Remove taxes on fuel'. The protests followed the Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority's latest pricing review for the October-November cycle, which pushed petrol in Nairobi to Sh226.96 per litre, diesel to Sh227.76, and kerosene to Sh219.87.

In a letter dated October 22 and received at police headquarters the same day, the Coalition of Human Rights Defenders said the demonstration aimed to highlight the burden of fuel costs on households and businesses. Organisers estimated 500 to 900 participants, and pledged to keep the march orderly and respect the rights of other members of the public.

World.title: Pat McAfee invokes Charlie Kirk killing as Utah post sparks 'uncomfortable' GameDay visit
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

ESPN star Pat McAfee appeared to reference the killing of Charlie Kirk as he ripped the University of Utah over a social media post he says made him feel "very, very uncomfortable" before Saturday’s "College GameDay" broadcast.

McAfee said he saw a video on the university’s Instagram account shortly before going on air in Salt Lake City. The post asked students to do impressions of him, he said, and included comments calling him "corny" and "creepy."

The video has since been removed from the university’s social media accounts.

PAT MCAFEE HAS OFFICIALLY SURPASSED STEPHEN A SMITH AS THE FACE OF ESPN

The former NFL punter said he would not have minded if students had shared the remarks themselves, but he took issue with the university posting them before he walked in front of thousands of fans.

"The university puts that out, like as I’m about to go out and do an infomercial for the place, and then I’m walking in front of thousands of these people," McAfee said Monday on "The Pat McAfee Show."

"This is how the university feels about it. It’s an uncomfortable feeling."

McAfee said the post "set me off a little bit" and made him feel "a little weird." He then appeared to reference the September 2025 shooting of Kirk, the conservative activist who was killed during an event at Utah Valley University in Orem, about 40 miles south of Salt Lake City.

30% OF COLLEGE STUDENTS SAY VIOLENCE ACCEPTABLE WAY TO STOP SPEAKERS ON CAMPUSES, SURVEY FINDS

"Has anything like really scary happened at like a college gathering in the state of Utah recently?" McAfee asked. "Like, do we think we should be amplifying reasons for why people hate my guts as a university?"

Later in the segment, McAfee again pointed to "what happened 40 miles south of Salt Lake City a little over a year ago," saying the university’s post added to the hostility he faces just before he went on air to promote the school.

CHARLIE KIRK'S FAMILY ALLEGES UVU KNEW OF ROOFTOP SECURITY RISK BEFORE HIS ASSASSINATION: LEGAL FILING

"I was very, very uncomfortable," he said. "I think it made me not have the greatest morning."

The University of Utah apologized in a statement posted to its official Instagram account, saying its goal was to create "lighthearted engagement" about McAfee’s return to campus, but it "missed the mark."

"University staff are responsible for reviewing and posting content on official social media accounts and we take full accountability for that decision," the school said.

The university said officials had reached out to McAfee to express their appreciation and regret.

"We sincerely apologize for creating any perception that Pat was unsafe or unwelcome on our campus. Nothing could be further from the truth," the statement said.

The school added that McAfee and the entire "College GameDay" crew are always welcome at the university. It said ESPN’s pregame show has visited its campus seven times and that it has enjoyed a positive relationship with the crew.

McAfee said he knew some people believed the students’ comments were not particularly harsh, but he kept coming back to who posted the video.

"It was the university putting that out. It’s not like a blog. It’s the actual place that we’re at," he said.

WHY THE OVER 56.5 IS THE PLAY AS HOUSTON VISITS UNDEFEATED UTAH IN BIG 12 ACTION

The Instagram post was not the only part of McAfee’s visit that appeared to frustrate him. He also took issue with a student participating in his weekly "Kicking Is Easy" contest, which gives a contestant a chance to kick a field goal for $1 million.

McAfee said the student questioned why the prize was "only $1 million" after the potential prize reached $3 million for the previous week’s Notre Dame-BYU game.

"It’s my money! Only $1 million. It’s like, all right, I hate this place. I hate this place," he said.

McAfee said he hopes he never has to return to the university and joked that he might have COVID if "College GameDay" goes back.

Despite his frustrations, he praised Utah’s football team and called its student section "incredible." He also thanked the fans who attended Saturday’s broadcast.

Utah went on to defeat Houston 21-13 on Saturday.

World.title: Florida mom arrested after Vegas trip left 4 kids without overnight supervision: deputies
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

A Florida mother returning from Las Vegas was met by deputies as she stepped off a plane and arrested after authorities say she left her four children home alone while she traveled for work.

Body camera video shows deputies approaching Irene Miller as she exited the plane Friday morning, escorting her through the airport terminal and placing her in handcuffs.

The arrest came two days after one of Miller’s children called 911 to report that a dumbbell had fallen on her 9-year-old brother’s head, according to the Osceola County Sheriff’s Office.

FLORIDA AG SEEKS DEATH PENALTY FOR COUPLE WHO ALLEGEDLY HELD 4 CHILDREN IN ‘ROLLING PRISON’ FOR NEARLY 7 YEARS

Deputies responded to the Kissimmee home shortly after 8:30 p.m. on Oct. 21 and found four children, ages 9, 11, 12 and 14, with no adults present, the sheriff’s office said. Fire rescue crews took the injured boy to Celebration Hospital, where he was treated and discharged.

A deputy reached Miller by phone, and she said she was working in Las Vegas and planned to return Oct. 23, according to the sheriff’s office. Deputies learned she had left Florida on Oct. 18.

FLORIDA 3-YEAR-OLD DIES AFTER TRAGIC INCIDENT INVOLVING COMMON PLAY TOY AT BABYSITTER'S HOUSE

Miller told deputies she had arranged for a babysitter to travel from Tampa in the mornings to help the children get ready for school and check on them afterward. The sitter was not required to stay overnight, the sheriff’s office said.

Authorities contacted the children’s father, who agreed to take all four to his home while detectives made plans to meet Miller when her flight landed.

SAN JOSE GIRL, 8, DIES AFTER LIVING IN COCKROACH-INFESTED HOME AS MOTHER, STEPFATHER FACE CHARGES

Deputies arrested Miller, 50, on four counts of child neglect without great bodily harm and booked her into the Orange County Jail.

World.title: Brewers ride ridiculous, record-setting eight-run inning to dominant 3-0 World Series lead over Rays
World.content:
The Milwaukee Brewers moved one step closer to their first ever World Series title on Monday night, taking a 3-0 series lead with a dominant 10-1 win.

That's the short version of the story. The long version? The Tampa Bay Rays will be kicking themselves over a disastrous top of the fifth inning, and historians will one day use a clip of that inning, and the entire 2026 Brewers' postseason run for that matter, as proof of how powerful luck is in Major League Baseball.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Game three meant the series shifted to Tampa Bay, and Tropicana Field was packed to the rafters with Rays fans and a sizable contingent of Brewers supporters. But as has typically been the case this postseason, only those in Milwaukee blue and gold had much to cheer about.

MILWAUKEE BREWERS' DOMINANT BULLPEN AND CLUTCH OFFENSE PUT THE TAMPA BAY RAYS ON THE BRINK

At least defensively, the Rays put up a fight. In the top of the second, outfielder Chandler Simpson made a tremendous running catch in the left field corner, crashing into the fence to rob Sal Frelick of a hit. Then catcher Nick Fortes caught Garrett Mitchell trying to steal second base to end the inning. It was all downhill from there.

In the third inning, the Milwaukee superteam machine kicked into high gear. Jackson Chourio started things off with a ground ball single. Jake Bauers followed with a walk. That's when the Brewers' incredible penchant for outperforming on batting average on balls in play reared its gigantic head yet again.

Christian Yelich popped up a 71 mph blooper that fell in for an RBI single. William Contreras followed with another 79 mph blooper that fell in to drive in the second run of the game.

Still, a 2-0 game in the third inning wouldn't normally mean that much, but the Brewers had Robert Gasser on the mound. Who's Robert Gasser you might be wondering? Well, essentially the epitome of a league average pitcher, someone who had a 4.27 "expected" ERA in the regular season, then turned into a Cy Young candidate in the playoffs. Because baseball.

Gasser entered his game three start with just one run allowed in the playoffs, but the Rays couldn't muster even that on Monday night. Rarely getting swings and misses, Gasser relied on his best friend in October: the opposing team having exceptionally poor luck on batted balls put in play. Prior to Monday, opposing hitters had just a .185 BABIP against him. Then he went six shutout innings with just three strikeouts and only one hit allowed. How? Because the Rays had an .071 BABIP. Gasser will likely end his postseason with just seven hits on 55 balls put in play, an incredible .127 batting average allowed, when league average is around .300.

Gasser's start was the first time a lefty had gone six shutout innings while facing the minimum number of hitters in the World Series since Sandy Koufax.

Next time you want your favorite team to acquire the big name starting pitcher in free agency or at the trade deadline, just remember that one of the most effective starters on the team that won the World Series was Robert Gasser. That he did something that hadn't been done in the World Series by a lefty since one of the greatest pitchers in the history of the sport. In large part because of BABIP. There's no luck in baseball, because everything must have an explanation, no matter how absurd.

Gasser didn't need much support, obviously, but the Brewers unstoppable offense provided it anyway. In the fifth inning, Milwaukee put together one of the most absurd innings you'll ever see, and a near-perfect reminder of the immense amount of variance and randomness inherent in baseball.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

It started innocently enough, with Chourio once again singling with one out. Jake Bauers flew out for the second out, then Christian Yelich walked to put runners at first and second. Then, the play that will haunt Rays fans forever.

William Contreras grounded one in the hole between second and third, and third baseman Junior Caminero went to second base for the force out, unable to see that he had plenty of time to get Contreras at first. But Yelich beat the throw out, loading the bases for Brice Turang. Then, the floodgates opened.

Turang hit a grounder to short that Taylor Walls couldn't make the play on, scoring two. Then Garrett Mitchell slapped another single through the infield, directly where the shortstop typically plays. 5-0 Milwaukee. Cooper Pratt followed with a grounder that somehow clipped the foul line for a double, making it 7-0. Sal Frelick hit a soft line drive that fell in to left field to make it 8-0. David Hamilton, having an incredible postseason after a career of being a very bad hitter, drove in the ninth run of the game with a single. Finally, Jackson Chourio added his fourth hit of the game and second of the inning to make it 10-0. Why not?

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

That fifth inning was the first eight-run inning in World Series history. The Brewers went 9-18 with runners in scoring position, had a .471 BABIP and 16 hits against a typically strong Rays pitching staff. Tampa's BABIP? .130. That's only half of it. Per the league's Statcast page, Milwaukee's expected batting average in the game was .254. Their actual batting average was .390. Tampa's expected batting average was .236, and their actual was .107. And that's been Milwaukee's luck all postseason.

The Rays added a meaningless garbage time run in the bottom of the ninth, but Milwaukee takes a commanding 3-0 series lead, and is well on their way to the organization's first ever championship. Potentially as soon as Tuesday night's game four.

Should the Brewers close it out with a fully rested bullpen, they'd become the first team in the history of the sport to sweep both the NLCS and World Series. They're 10-1 in the playoffs thus far, with a chance to go 11-1 and win ten of nine straight to win a title. Baseball-ruining superteam indeed.



Not all of these results are down to luck, of course, and it's hardly a criticism of the Brewers' team or players to say they've had fortune on their side in the playoffs. Every team that wins the playoff tournament in Major League Baseball has luck go their way. The Dodgers in 2024 and 2025 had plenty of breaks, as did the Rangers in 2023 and Astros in 2022. And the Braves in 2021 and so on.

But there's an inescapable conclusion from this World Series, and the whole postseason, as a matter of fact: there is no way to "ruin" baseball. Or build a superteam. Or guarantee a championship. Because at the end of the day, the gaps between teams are so small that a few bounces either way over a short series can, and often does, determine the outcome. Having a rotation filled with Cy Young level pitchers is great and all, except that when it comes down to it, Robert Gasser can become Sandy Koufax over 15 innings. There's no way to predict who will get hot, who will be cold, and which teams will have luck on their side. Which is what baseball has always been, and always will be. No matter how much fake complaining owners do.

World.title: Cowboys, Dak Prescott get back on track at the expense of reeling Eagles in key NFC East win
World.content:
The Dallas Cowboys and Philadelphia Eagles NFC East bout on "Monday Night Football" in Week 7 wasn’t supposed to feature two 2–4 teams dealing with inauspicious starts to the season.

The NFL can be cruel in that way for some teams, but Week 7 turned into a situation where one team could get back on track in a division that seems up for grabs.

The Dallas Cowboys, who had quite a different narrative entering this contest on the road despite the same exact record as the team hosting them, did at least turn the ship toward the right direction on Monday night with a 38-21 win over the Eagles.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The narrative for Dallas was that they have the pieces, but is the coaching all there? Head coach Brian Schottenheimer’s name has been brought up in hot seat discussions, as the Cowboys lost back-to-back games in Primetime, and certainly didn’t want to make it a third against a struggling Philadelphia squad.

Nick Sirianni, despite winning a Super Bowl with this team recently, has also been on the wrong side of Philly fandom to begin this 2026 campaign, but there’s at least the injury excuse. Quarterback Jalen Hurts is out for the season, as he deals with blood clots. And though he was back on Monday night in a limited capacity, running back Saquon Barkley just hasn’t been healthy enough this year.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

With the Eagles losing four straight after a 2-0 start to the season, some fans have already resorted to the tanking conversation for a top draft pick. The Cowboys certainly are not at that stage – fans just think the coaching staff needs to get this group playing in sync on both sides of the ball.

For Dak Prescott and the offense, they continued to put points on the board, and they did so with a big lift from the run game. This isn’t a team that wants to pass the ball 45 times a game despite their veteran signal caller having done so many times throughout his career.

Javonte Williams produced 155 on the ground on 25 carries with a touchdown at the end of the game, weaving his way through the Philadelphia defense for big chunk plays, including a 34-yard burst through the line. That opens everything for this offense that proclaims itself the "G.O.T.I." – greatest offense there is.

CeeDee Lamb may have caught just five of his 12 targets, but two of those were touchdown grabs from Prescott. He finished the game with 74 yards, while his counterpart George Pickens had a touchdown himself on a 21-yard connection with his quarterback. And wide receiver three, Ryan Flournoy, totaled 70 yards on four grabs.

All was well for Dallas’ offense, but once again, the defense was questionable against McKee and the Eagles’ offense at home.

The first drive of the game brought hope to the crowd at Lincoln Financial Field, as the rabid fan base had been waiting for Barkley, the former Offensive Player of the Year, to return to the backfield after a hamstring injury. In just four plays, including a 29-yard run for Barkley, they remembered what it’s like to have a threat like him leading the way.

Barkley bounced outside on first-and-5 from Dallas’ eight-yard line for the Eagles’ first touchdown of the game, and it looked like they would compete against a Cowboys' defense that keeps trying to find its identity, or better yet, key stops. But the injury bug continued to halt Barkley from being 100%, as he tried battling through a back injury this time in this game. He was noticed stretching on the sideline and trying to keep his back loose with trainers, but to no avail.

Still, it was a back-and-forth battle in this latest chapter of a storied division rivalry, with long drives resulting in touchdowns on both sides. Dameon Pierce, who took over the lion’s share of carries, scored for the Eagles, while rookie Makai Lemon secured his first career touchdown to give the Eagles a 21-20 lead in the third quarter.

But as Prescott does, he responded with a touchdown of his own – the second for Lamb – and the Cowboys were eventually able to separate themselves after forcing an Eagles punt and DeMarvion Overshown making an incredible interception on a ball intended for Dallas Goedert while the Eagles were driving in the fourth quarter.

At 2-5 now, it may still be too early to say the Eagles’ season is a failure, but the cards they’ve been dealt are not pictures and they’re off suit.

The Cowboys, on the other hand, still have chips on the table and are in the hunt. At 3-4, they’re a game-and-a-half behind the New York Giants, who beat them in Week 1, for the NFC East lead.

And with winnable games against the Arizona Cardinals and Indianapolis Colts up next on the schedule, perhaps Schottenheimer's seat can cool down if they can put together their first win streak of the campaign.

World.title: John Harbaugh backs Cam Skattebo, rips NFL for controversial flag: 'That's the way you're supposed to run'
World.content:
Cam Skattebo shared his thoughts on a controversial unnecessary roughness call against him in the New York Giants’ win over the Houston Texans on Sunday.

His head coach, John Harbaugh, shared the same sentiment.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Skattebo ripped the NFL after officials assessed a 15-yard penalty against him after lowering his shoulder into Texans safety M.J. Stewart, delivering a forceful blow that sent him to the turf.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"I will say, man, the NFL loves to post me when I do stuff like that, but then also wants to take stuff from me," he said after a game where he ran for over 120 yards with a touchdown. "So, I mean, I’m going to run the ball like I want to run the ball, and if I’m going to continue to get flagged or it or fined for it, man, I guess I’m going to play for free."

On Monday during time with reporters, Harbaugh was asked about what he said to the official during his own heated exchange in the moment after holding back Skattebo, who was livid with the official as he came off the field.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"Did you see me after the play expressing my opinion? That’s how I felt about it," he said.

Harbaugh admitted he understood the idea of why a yellow flag landed on the turf at NRG Stadium after seeing the hit. The NFL is always trying to crack down on helmet-to-helmet contact, and the official thought that Skattebo led with the crown of his helmet when he hit Stewart.

Harbaugh saw it differently.

"I also understand human physiology and anatomy and the way the body works," he said. "Skat runs low. You have to run low.

"You have to run low to protect the football. You have to run low to protect your body. You can’t run in there and give tacklers your chest. When you run low, your head’s down there, too. You can’t move your head off your shoulders. It’s a physical impossibility."

Harbaugh added that he didn’t believe his running back was "trying to use his helmet as a weapon, as a battering ram." Skattebo certainly enjoys initiating contact. In fact, Skattebo was featured in multiple commercials during the broadcast where he is seen running through walls and other objects because, well, that’s his thing.

Ultimately, Harbaugh believes Skattebo’s running style is "the way you’re supposed to run."

World.title: Jay-Z to headline Super Bowl halftime show
World.content:
Jay-Z has helped select artists for the last several Super Bowl halftime shows.

Now, the 25-time Grammy winner and mogul will step into the performer role as the headliner for the 2027 show.

The NFL and Apple Music announced the news on social media during Monday night’s game between the Dallas Cowboys and the Philadelphia Eagles, confirming recent reporting about the halftime show from Puck that cited industry sources.

“GOAT’s out of the bag,” read the post, which featured a black-and-white video of Jay-Z in the stands with a goat on his lap as “Allow me to reintroduce myself,” the opening line of his song “Public Service Announcement (Interlude)” plays.

Jay-Z’s entertainment company, Roc Nation, has been a partner with the NFL and produced the halftime show since 2019.

“For several years, we’ve had the privilege of working closely with Jay-Z and Roc Nation, and I’ve seen the extraordinary impact he has had on the Super Bowl Halftime Show,” NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said in a statement. “When we first reached an agreement with Roc Nation to produce the show, I had just one request: that Jay-Z take the stage himself one day, whenever the moment felt right to him. I couldn’t be more excited for fans around the world to experience the artistry, creativity and cultural impact he will bring to the Super Bowl stage.”

Super Bowl 61 will take place Feb. 14 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, near Los Angeles. The game and the halftime show will air on ESPN, ABC and Disney+ and on mobile devices with NFL+.

Jay-Z, whose real name is Shawn Carter, just wrapped his 30 Tour, which celebrated the 30th anniversary of his debut album, “Reasonable Doubt.” His final two shows were at SoFi.

“From Reasonable Doubt to standing on the Super Bowl Halftime stage, this has been a journey,” he said in a statement Monday. “Thirty years of music, work, and culture on the world’s biggest stage. This run continues to be a dream come true.”

During the tour, which featured stops in Paris, London and Jay-Z’s hometown, New York City, he brought up several guests, including his wife, superstar Beyoncé.

It’s unclear whether Bey or any of Jay-Z’s many other famous friends and collaborators will make cameos during the halftime performance.

Many artists who have headlined the event have brought on major stars. But several, including The Weeknd and Rihanna, chose to shine solo when they appeared at the event.

Last year’s game, which was broadcast on NBC and Peacock, featured Bad Bunny as the headliner, with Lady Gaga and Ricky Martin making cameos. The performance was awarded seven Creative Arts Emmys this year, making it the most awarded halftime show in history. It was Bad Bunny’s first Emmy and Jay-Z’s third, with both artists serving as producers last year.

Kendrick Lamar, who headlined the 2025 show, also took home an Emmy after he tackled the gig.

Next year, said Apple’s vice president of music and international content, Oliver Schusser, fans can expect “an incredible show” from Jay-Z, whose “impact on global music culture is as profound as it is undeniable.”

World.title: How Democrats could win the House, how the GOP could hang on, and where to look for a wave
World.content:
Districts to watch: NC-14, KY-6

Another way to estimate the possible size of November’s swing is to look at the partisan shifts in elections held in 2025 and 2026, ever since Trump returned to office. These races include the 2025 governor’s elections in New Jersey and Virginia, other high-profile statewide elections and several special elections for the U.S. House.

Although Trump lost Virginia and New Jersey, the other recent elections have tended to occur in places that supported Trump in 2024. Averaging across all of these states and districts, Trump won them by an average of about 3.5 percentage points in 2024. In the 2025 and 2026 elections, however, those states and districts supported the Democratic candidate by an average of about 11 points. This amounts to a shift of 14.5 points in the Democrats’ favor.

If the Democrats are able to shift the vote in every district by such a historically massive margin in 2026, they could win as many as 263 seats to the Republicans’ 172. That would be the largest majority that either party has held in the U.S. House since the 1990 midterm elections.

Such a shift could put into play districts like Florida’s 27th District, represented by GOP Rep. María Elvira Salazar. Republicans in Florida left this district nearly unchanged when they redrew the state’s congressional map, believing that a district that Trump won by 14.6 points would be out of reach for the Democrats.

But it appears the race in this heavily Hispanic district is tightening, as polls show Latino voters nationwide turning against Trump and Republicans, with economic concerns weighing heavily on their minds. These voters were critical to Trump’s winning coalition in 2024, and indications that they are moving back toward Democrats are helping drive the party’s competitiveness in Republican-leaning, heavily Hispanic districts in states like Texas, too. Salazar outran Trump’s win margin by nearly 6 percentage points in 2024, and her survival in the 2026 election may require a similarly strong overperformance.

A 14.5-point national swing toward Democrats could also make North Carolina’s 14th District competitive. Republican Rep. Tim Moore’s district is one that North Carolina Republicans did not bother changing when they redrew their maps last year. Trump won the district by 15.1 points, and Moore himself won it in 2024 by 16.1 points.

Another district to watch is Kentucky’s 6th District. Republican Andy Barr has held this open Lexington-based seat since 2013, and Trump carried it in 2024 by 15 points. Barr is running for the U.S. Senate this year. Republican- and Democratic-aligned groups are spending heavily here, reflecting the importance of the race, as Republican Ralph Alvarado faces off against Democrat Zach Dembo.

The NBC News Decision Desk rates this race as lean Republican. In 2024, this district reported almost 90% of its votes by 8:40 p.m. ET. If Democrats are on track for a massive national shift, this district may provide one of the best pieces of early evidence.

National trends don’t mean every district shifts the same amount

To be sure, all of these scenarios assume that the partisan shift in 2026 will be the same in every district. This may be true on average, but some districts will have a larger shift than the national average and others will have a smaller one.

Demographics of a specific district may play a role in the size of the shift. For example, if Hispanic voters shift more dramatically toward the Democratic Party than non-Hispanic voters, then districts with higher concentrations of Hispanic voters will vote more favorably for the Democrats than the underlying partisanship of the district would predict.

Incumbency can also play a large role in causing a district to shift more or less than the national average. In 2024, the incumbent members of Congress outperformed their party’s presidential candidate by an average of 2.5 percentage points.

This year, there are slightly more Democrats seeking re-election than Republican ones. This means that the Democratic Party as a whole stands to gain more from the benefits of incumbency compared with the Republican Party.

On the other hand, there are more Republicans who represent districts with evenly divided underlying partisanship. For example, an “incumbency bump” matters a lot more to a Republican in a district Trump won by 5 points than to a Democrat in a district Harris won by 25 points.

Finally, redistricting has also played a key role in this year’s midterms. By redrawing districts in several states, Republicans stand to win as many as 10 more seats than if the map remained unchanged after 2024.

Redistricting impacts the role of incumbency, too. When the lines for a district are redrawn, incumbents are fighting for the votes of people whom they’ve never represented and who may be less familiar with their records. This tends to diminish the size of the incumbency advantage. Republican incumbents in Texas and other red states and Democratic incumbents in California must lean heavily on the “D” or “R” next to their names when they try to win the support of their new potential constituents.

World.title: NAACP decries viral videos of group wearing KKK robes in El Paso, Texas
World.content:
Police and the El Paso, Texas, branch of the NAACP are condemning a group of people, possibly including youths, who were shown wearing Ku Klux Klan-style white robes and hoods in viral social media videos.

The videos show the group walking on a neighborhood street, which police indicated is in El Paso. In one video, the person recording can be heard laughing and telling the group, “Y’all gotta yell something, güey.” (“Güey” is Spanish slang, most commonly used in Mexico, akin to “dude” in English.)

Carl B. Dwyer Jr., the NAACP’s El Paso branch president, denounced the display at a news conference Monday morning as deeply hurtful to Black Americans, for whom the KKK has been a real-life terror since the Civil War.

“Many believe that it’s just a joke,” he said after supporters joined in to sing “Lift Every Voice and Sing,” the hymn often referred to as the Black national anthem.

“It hurts,” Dwyer said. “It hurts.”

El Paso Police Chief Peter Pacillas said in a statement that the department was looking into whether the group, “reportedly including young people,” violated any laws, including disorderly conduct “or other applicable offenses.”

“Symbols and language associated with the Ku Klux Klan represent a history of terror, violence, and racial hatred,” he said. “They have no place in our community. Treating that history as a costume or a joke is unacceptable and contrary to the values of respect and safety that define El Paso.”

Artie C. Maxwell Jr., pastor of El Paso’s Mount Zion Baptist Church, also spoke at Monday’s news conference and provided historical context for a city that briefly sympathized with the Confederacy.

“We may think that it is a joke, but it’s not a joke when it comes to the lives that have come before us,” he said. “God, that many have died at the hands of those who have worn those costumes.”

Pacillas invited those with information about the incident to step forward.

“Free expression has limits when it crosses into conduct that threatens public order or the safety of others,” he said.

Dwyer urged local educators to remind students of history and its influence on the present.

“We’re calling on all of the superintendents, all of the school districts, please, speak up. Please, do something about this,” he said.

World.title: Judge further extends block on Trump administration’s removing trees at D.C. golf course
World.content:
A federal judge in Washington issued a longer-term injunction Monday blocking the Trump administration from removing or damaging any additional trees on the grounds of East Potomac Golf Links.

The order says the administration must provide written notice 10 business days before it makes “any irreparable modification to any forms or features of East Potomac Park” while the case proceeds.

In her order, U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes cited some of President Donald Trump’s Truth Social posts, which contradicted testimony from government employees.

“This started as a case about golf. That good walk spoiled. But it has become much more. It now forces the Court to reconcile assertions by President Donald J. Trump with the sworn testimony of multiple government employees and the argument of senior Department of Justice attorneys,” Reyes wrote.

Crews cut down trees on the East Potomac golf course as golfers continue to use the course on Oct. 10. Aaron Schwartz / Getty

The order displayed screenshots of Truth Social posts, including one on Oct. 18 in which Trump said Interior Secretary Doug Burgum, along with an architect, had “developed a plan to build a World Class Championship Golf Course” at East Potomac starting Nov. 15, even though Justice Department lawyers had earlier said there was no renovation plan.

In a follow-up post Oct. 19, Trump said work on the course would begin not on Nov. 15, but “IMMEDIATELY!” That post also said workers did not need approval for construction and called Reyes “a crazed lunatic.”

“Rarely, if ever, has the United States Department of Justice urged a federal court not to believe the sitting President,” Reyes wrote in her order Monday. “And yet, here we are.”

Golfers hit from a fairway near log sections cut from trees at the golf course on Oct. 12. Mark Schiefelbein / Getty

Reyes said during a seven-hour hearing this month that she believed it was most likely necessary to extend her order pausing the tree demolition because she had already found the government acted in “bad faith” when it abruptly chopped down more than 400 trees at the course over the Columbus Day holiday weekend.

“The Court earlier stated, ‘I am not the Lorax. I do not speak for the trees.’ The Court still does not speak for the trees. It speaks only for the rule of law,” Reyes wrote Monday.

Democracy Forward President and CEO Skye Perryman, who is representing plaintiffs in the case, praised Monday’s ruling in a statement.

“This is a big win that will rightly protect East Potomac park from further irreparable harm,” Perryman said. “We are grateful the court intervened to stop the Trump-Vance association’s greed and lawlessness while the case continues, and we are eager to argue the case in court.”

World.title: These factors could decide Netanyahu's fate in Israel's election
World.content:
Tel Aviv — After three years with their country at war on multiple fronts, Israelis have started casting ballots in a hotly contested election that will shape their next government. Polls show it is an incredibly tight race, and as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu fights to hold onto his job, there's no guarantee of a quick, definitive outcome for him or his political opponents.

Polls vary widely regarding the expected outcome. Right-leaning pollsters give an advantage to the right-wing and religious bloc led by Netanyahu, while left-leaning pollsters show an advantage for the so-called change bloc opposing the incumbent.

Most polls show neither side is likely to win a decisive majority of the 120 seats in Israel's parliament, the Knesset, which would enable it to unilaterally form a new government. The tight margins mean the voting may end in a stalemate, which could lead to protracted negotiations across ideological lines, the formation of a minority government, or even an election do-over.

"It looks like an indecisive outcome is the most likely outcome," said Yohanan Plesner, president of the Israel Democracy Institute.

This is the first election since the Oct. 7, 2023, attacks by Hamas, which authorities have acknowledged as Israel's most catastrophic security failure since the country's founding in 1948. Israelis are heading to the polls with their country still fighting in the subsequent multi-front war in Gaza, Lebanon and Syria, and after two direct rounds of conflict with Iran and Netanyahu advocating for a third.

Against that backdrop, there are a few key issues that could determine the election outcome, even if it does take days or weeks to shake out. But first, here's a look at the two main factions vying for the votes.

The Netanyahu camp

Netanyahu, Israel's longest serving prime minister and leader of the Likud party, is seeking to form another coalition similar to his current government, which relies on partnerships with ultranationalist and Jewish religious parties.

He has two main pitches to voters: First, that only he can form a government without the support of Israel's Arab parties, which he argues would be a danger to the country if they gain enough seats to influence Israel's engagement in its myriad conflicts.

Netanyahu's second argument to voters is that Israel's campaigns in Gaza, Lebanon, and especially Iran, are ongoing, and he needs more time to finish what his government started.

President Trump offered a full-throated endorsement of Netanyahu last week. He reiterated his administration's firm support for the war the two men launched jointly against Iran almost eight months ago, and warned that he could be disinclined to continue with it if Netanyahu doesn't hold onto power.

"If Israel has the wrong Leader, which would be anyone other than Bibi, America will have to do this work ourselves, and I am not inclined to do so," Mr. Trump said.

A campaign billboard depicting Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and President Trump is seen in Tel Aviv, Israel, on Oct. 26, 2026. JACK GUEZ/AFP/Getty Images

Since that endorsement, Netanyahu has argued that only he can work with Mr. Trump to ensure Iran does not obtain a nuclear weapon, which many Israelis see as an existential threat.

Netanyahu's campaign slogan, which rhymes in Hebrew, is: "Either right wing or Palestine, either right wing or a nuclear bomb."

Over the weekend, Netanyahu posted an AI-generated photo of a mushroom cloud over Tel Aviv on social media, with a caption reiterating his insistence that Iran poses an existential threat to Israel.

Netanyahu's supporters see him as a top-tier global leader.

"Bibi can handle the whole world," restaurant owner Benny Abraham told CBS News, using Netanyahu's nickname. "Bibi is charismatic. He has a strong voice. The world loves him."

"He's the king of Israel," Abraham added.

The (anyone but Netanyahu) "change bloc"

Running against Netanyahu is a diverse group of Arab, right, left and center parties that have one clear common denominator: They all want Netanyahu out of power.

The front-runner to lead the "change bloc," should its various parties collectively win enough seats to build a coalition, is former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot, who leads the centrist Yashar party.

Eisenkot lost his son and two nephews while they were serving in the military in Gaza. He was part of the Israeli war cabinet for much of the first year of the Gaza war, working alongside Netanyahu. About half of his party's candidates in Tuesday's election are women, in stark contrast to the male-dominated Netanyahu coalition.

Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot waves to supporters at a campaign rally on Oct. 25, 2026, in Tel Aviv, Israel. Erik Marmor/picture alliance/Getty Images

Eisenkot is framing himself as a humble veteran who wants to reunite Israel after years of division that he blames on Netanyahu.

Eisenkot responded Monday to Netanyahu's rhetoric about Iran posing a nuclear threat by accusing him of "relying on a campaign of fear-mongering, lies, and threats — including images of nuclear bombs in the heart of Tel Aviv."

"This time, it won't work for him," he said.

Eisenkot's key campaign promises include launching a state inquiry into the intelligence and security failure to prevent the Oct. 7, 2023, attack by Hamas — something Netanyahu has thus far blocked.

Uzi Aharoni, 73, an engineer from Tel Aviv, told CBS News he saw Eisenkot as the only real alternative to Netanyahu.

"Eisenkot is not left, he's not right. He's straight and honest. He's the kind of leader who will take care of us, the people of Israel, and not himself or his corrupt family," Aharoni said.

The Arab vote and the ultra-Orthodox draft

There are a few factors analysts believe could hand a victory to either side.

One thing polls can't predict well in Israel is voter turnout. Past elections have shown voters backing Netanyahu's Likud party, and Arab-Israeli voters, vary the greatest in their enthusiasm to come out on election days, so there could be room for turn-out surprises that significantly change the electoral math in favor of either side.

Arab Israelis, also referred to as Palestinian citizens of Israel, make up around 20% of Israel's population.

"The higher the Arab turnout, the less likely that Mr. Netanyahu, within the current coalition, can form another government," said Plesner at the Israel Democracy Institute.

More Arab voters will head to voting booths this year because of their strong desire to prevent Netanyahu from forming another government with far-right allies, who have made life difficult for them over the last four years, Jehad Abomoch, a cafe owner in the predominantly Arab city of Baqa al Gharbiya, told CBS News.

"The last four years were a real catastrophe, both socially and in terms of wars," he said, adding that many Arab Israelis feel that under Netanyahu, they have "no hope, no future."

There are also two new parties entering this election, and polls show each is hovering around the threshold of support required to gain seats in the Knesset. Whether either party ultimately crosses that threshold could also tip the scales — in either direction — toward a new coalition government.

Both parties are focused on challenging Netanyahu's alliance with ultra-Orthodox parties by demanding that ultra-Orthodox Jewish citizens be formally included in Israel's mandatory military service.

Ultra-Orthodox Jewish leaders of the Breslev Hasidic community take part in a rally against mandatory military conscription on Oct. 12, 2026, in Netanya, Israel. Amir Levy/Getty Images

It's a key issue that cuts right through Netanyahu's traditional support base and coalition partners.

Not all election outcomes are neat and tidy

In the event that neither bloc wins a clear majority in parliament, there are several paths forward to a new Israeli government.

One option is that parties or individual lawmakers could break election promises and switch sides, for which there is plenty of precedent in Israeli politics. There could be weeks of negotiating before a coalition is agreed on.

Another possibility is that the change bloc, if it wins a significant share of the votes but not quite a majority, could seek to form a minority government. To do that, the parties just need to win more seats collectively than the other side, even if it's not more than 50% of the 120 available. Arab parties could give the change bloc that plurality by either voting in favor of a minority government, or just abstaining and not voting against its formation.

If there's a stalemate and neither side can build a coalition government, the country will have to hold new elections. There is plenty of precedent for that scenario, too.

Between 2019 and 2022, Israel held five elections due to electoral deadlock.

Plesner told CBS News that, if all the politicians running effectively stick to their campaign promises and refuse to swap sides in the event of a stalemate "we will roll into another election."

"I'm sure that most politicians are not interested in that," he added.

World.title: DOJ takes steps to charge James Comey again
World.content:
The Justice Department took steps to charge James Comey with leaking classified information earlier this month, court records show, in its third attempt to bring criminal charges against the former FBI director and Trump foe.

Prosecutors are seeking to charge Comey with two counts of violating the Espionage Act by transmitting national defense information to a person not entitled to receive it. He has not been indicted by a grand jury or charged by criminal complaint, and was instead targeted through a criminal information filing.

In this case, the information was filed in order to preserve the statute of limitations before it expires, according to a Justice Department spokesperson. The official added that "this is an ongoing criminal investigation, and we will not comment further."

A criminal information does not require approval by a grand jury, or a finding by a magistrate judge of probable cause that there is evidence to establish that a crime was committed.

Comey's attorney, Patrick Fitzgerald, said Comey "steadfastly maintains his innocence."

The latest effort by the Justice Department stems from allegations that Comey gave national defense information to an unnamed individual for disclosure in a newspaper in October 2016.

According to court filings in the case, The New York Times published an article on Oct. 5, 2016, titled, "Yahoo Said to Have Aided U.S. Email Surveillance By Adapting Spam Filter." The article cited two unnamed government officials who spoke on the condition of anonymity.

The Justice Department alleges that it has uncovered evidence that Comey sought to "correct misinformation which had appeared in the press by way of Reuters the day before" and that Comey "directed staff" to speak with the Times reporter about the accuracy of the Reuters article.

Fitzgerald said the information "purports to charge Mr. Comey with crimes that he did not commit," adding that investigators looked into the matter twice during the first Trump administration and "determined that no charges should be brought against anyone."

In a separate video statement, Comey said, "well, they're back again" — a reference to the two prior attempts to charge Comey, including a dismissed indictment accusing him of lying to Congress and a still-pending indictment accusing him of threatening President Trump via a social media post of a photo of seashells arranged to say "86 47."

"It would almost be funny if it weren't such an appalling abuse of the Department of Justice, one that we cannot become numb to," Comey said. "Nothing's changed with me. I'm still innocent, I'm still not afraid of these people and I still believe in the independent federal judiciary."

Asked about the case late Monday, Mr. Trump told reporters he'd "just heard about it."

"I think he's a dirty cop, James Comey, but I know nothing about it," the president said.

In a statement posted to social media, the Justice Department said: "Filing a criminal information to toll the statute of limitations is a widely recognized practice in federal court and has been approved by multiple Circuit Courts of Appeals."

Former prosecutors and defense attorneys told CBS News they had not seen a criminal information filed in a felony case in this manner before, and called the maneuver highly unusual. The practice had been approved in other federal appellate court districts in some cases, but is less common in Washington, D.C.

Greg Rosen, a former federal prosecutor who helped lead Jan. 6 cases, told CBS News: "In years of practicing in D.C., I never saw one used this way, let alone in the third attempt by the same Department to charge the same man."

Michael Bromwich, a former Justice Department inspector general who is now a defense attorney, told CBS News that he has never encountered a situation where a criminal information was filed to pause the statute of limitations. Normally, such charging documents are filed when a defendant plans to waive their right to have a grand jury weigh charges and opts to plead guilty.

"I have never heard of proceeding by information to toll the statute of limitations. Most prosecutors you have ever dealt with have never heard of that. This seems to be a way to do an end-run around the statute of limitations and keep a case alive that deserved to die 9 years ago," Bromwich said. "This is just absolutely bizarro world stuff."

DOJ and Comey fought in secret over charging efforts

The criminal information were filed under seal in early October, and were unsealed by U.S. District Judge Trevor McFadden on Monday at Comey's request.

For much of this month, Comey's attorneys and federal prosecutors waged a behind-the-scenes fight over whether the Justice Department's effort to charge him should be dismissed.

In an Oct. 9 court filing, Comey's legal team argued the government "filed a faulty information under seal … in an effort to toll the applicable statute of limitations." The crime that the government is seeking to charge Comey under has a 10-year statute of limitations, which would run out in October of this year — but the ex-FBI director's lawyers say the statute of limitations applies to indictments and can't be extended if the government files a criminal information.

They also said Comey had "reason to believe that the government plans to use that information to seek an arrest warrant as soon as today, which could result in an after-hours arrest that would ensure Mr. Comey sits in jail over a holiday weekend."

"Mr. Comey has reason to believe multiple federal law enforcement officers have surveilled his whereabouts while traveling to a family members' residence and around his own neighborhood throughout the week," Comey's lawyers wrote on Oct. 9, just before Columbus Day weekend.

In an emergency court hearing, the government agreed to hold off on seeking an indictment for 30 days, attorneys for Comey later wrote.

The Justice Department argued that Comey's efforts to dismiss the criminal information was premature because no indictment has been returned.

"This is not the proper time for him to file pretrial motions or attempt to chip away at charging documents before he subjects himself to the Court's jurisdiction," the government said.

Further, the department said the law allows the government to proceed because it permits prosecutors to meet the deadline if the "indictment is found or the information is instituted."

In an unusual move, the criminal information filed by the department were signed by two senior officials — acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter and Principal Associate Deputy Attorney General Aakash Singh — as well as several special assistant U.S. attorneys who are not originally from the U.S. Attorney's office in Washington, D.C.

McFadden, the Trump-nominated judge overseeing the case, ordered the court docket to be unsealed Monday, writing: "Criminal charges against a former FBI director for his conduct while in office are of significant public interest."

He also said Comey "is aware of the criminal information and has offered to 'self-surrender,'" so there is no need to keep the case secret in order to help the government apprehend him.

The judge did not rule on the merits of the case.

Two prior investigations into FBI leaks

This is not the first time that the Justice Department has sought to investigate the disclosure of classified information in connection with a 2016 Times article.

Former U.S. Attorney John Durham of Connecticut, who was later appointed special counsel by Attorney General William Barr, investigated the matter in 2017, according to court filings in the case from Comey's defense team. At the time, he determined there were two sources for the article, including James Baker, the former FBI general counsel.

As part of that investigation, Baker said the FBI's chief of staff instructed him to provide the information and he understood it was being conveyed at Comey's instruction.

Durham ultimately did not recommend Baker or anyone else for prosecution.

Baker could not be immediately reached for comment.

The matter was later investigated a second time — in that case by the U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Columbia under an investigation code-named Tropic Vortex. That was closed in February 2020, also without charges, according to court papers.

Comey and Trump

The Justice Department filed the criminal information in early October, about a month before the midterm elections. It marks the latest overt investigative step taken by the Justice Department in a politically charged case, a maneuver that runs counter to longstanding norms.

Mr. Trump and Comey have had a contentious relationship for nearly a decade, dating back to when the president fired the former FBI chief early in his first term. His firing is what prompted then-Deputy Attorney General Rod Rosenstein to appoint Special Counsel Robert Mueller, whose investigation dogged Mr. Trump for much of his first term.

The two have exchanged barbs since then, with Mr. Trump calling Comey a "dirty cop" and repeatedly arguing he should be prosecuted, while Comey called Mr. Trump "morally unfit" to be president.

In September 2025, the Justice Department obtained an indictment against Comey that charged him with lying to Congress, alleging he falsely told lawmakers in a 2020 hearing that he had never authorized an FBI employee to serve as an anonymous source.

The indictment was personally signed by Lindsey Halligan, a former Trump White House aide who had been sworn in as interim U.S. attorney for the Eastern District of Virginia days earlier. Beforehand, staff in that office circulated a memo that argued charges should not be brought against Comey, CBS News has previously reported.

A judge dismissed the charges on the grounds that Halligan was improperly appointed.

Then, in April of this year, Comey was indicted in North Carolina on allegations that he threatened to kill Mr. Trump by posting to Instagram a photo of seashells arranged to form the numbers "86 47." (Mr. Trump is the 47th president.)

Comey has long denied wrongdoing, and his attorneys have argued the charges against him are politically motivated. They are currently seeking to have the North Carolina charges dismissed on several grounds, including that his prosecution is vindictive and selective. That matter is currently pending.

Comey isn't the only Trump foe to face criminal scrutiny. New York Attorney General Letitia James was also charged by Halligan's office with bank fraud last year. Her indictment was tossed out along with the first Comey indictment. Prosecutors presented her case to grand juries at least twice after that, but the grand jurors declined to re-indict her.

Attorney General Todd Blanche has long denied that the charges against Comey and other Trump adversaries are driven by politics. In an interview with CBS News earlier this year, he said the "86 47" indictment was driven by "local prosecutors" and "local agents."

Asked if Mr. Trump has called him up and ordered him to prosecute certain individuals, Blanche told CBS News he wouldn't discuss his conversations with the president, but "rest assured, he has much better, bigger and important things to do than to worry about me doing my job."

World.title: Judge continues to block Trump from cutting down trees at D.C. golf course
World.content:
A federal judge on Monday barred the Trump administration from removing trees from East Potomac Golf Links in Washington, D.C., in a colorful ruling that follows a weekslong controversy over President Trump's plans to overhaul the publicly owned course.

"The Court earlier stated, 'I am not the Lorax. I do not speak for the trees,'" U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes wrote. "The Court still does not speak for the trees. It speaks only for the rule of law."

In a 70-page preliminary injunction ruling, Reyes prohibited the government from "removing or damaging" any trees on the golf course while a lawsuit challenging the renovation plan works its way through the court system. The judge also required 10 days' notice before the government makes "any irreparable modification" to the course.

The judge had previously blocked tree removal through Monday.

In a Truth Social post, Mr. Trump called the ruling "unconstitutional" and said his administration would seek appeal. He added that the government would move forward with closing the course on Nov. 15.

"To have to give advanced notices to a judge who has no expertise in Golf, Architecture, Landscaping, Construction, or anything else having to do with building such a World Class Project, is not fair, appropriate, or Constitutional," the president wrote, arguing the project is "totally 'as of right.'"

Mr. Trump has sought to overhaul the golf course — which sits beside the Potomac River — for months, pitching a "World Class Championship Golf Course" fit to host high-profile professional tournaments instead of the current "dysfunctional" course. The D.C. Preservation League sued over the planned changes to the course, arguing the government violated the National Environmental Policy Act by failing to analyze the project's impacts.

Reyes has sparred with the government since it cut down hundreds of trees earlier this month with little notice to the court or plaintiffs. In a hearing two weeks ago, after more than 430 trees were felled, the judge told lawyers for the government that they had "lost credibility," and she was "furious" and "thoroughly unamused."

Mr. Trump said last week the course would close for construction beginning in November, and it would reopen in 15 months. He later said work would begin "IMMEDIATELY."

In her ruling Monday, Reyes argued Mr. Trump's statements about the renovation plans were tough to square with government lawyers' position that it's legally too early to challenge the plans in court because there was no final decision.

"Rarely, if ever, has the United States Department of Justice urged a federal court not to believe the sitting President," she wrote. "This started as a case about golf. That good walk spoiled. But it has become much more. It now forces the Court to reconcile assertions by President Donald J. Trump with the sworn testimony of multiple government employees and the argument of senior Department of Justice attorneys."

A golfer walks past the stump of a large tree at the East Potomac Golf Links, Monday, Oct. 12, 2026, in Washington. AP Photo/Mark Schiefelbein

Reyes said she was initially reluctant to intervene in the case, writing that she "would much prefer not to have to resolve Lorax v. Once‑ler redux" — a reference to an earlier court hearing in which Reyes invoked the Dr. Seuss character to explain why she wasn't interested in micromanaging the federal government's tree management efforts.

She said she only intervened "because the Government did what it assured all it would not do," by chopping down hundreds of trees on the golf course.

Reyes found that the D.C. Preservation League is likely to succeed in showing the Trump administration's plans for the golf course violate the legal requirement for an environmental review.

She also found that the tree removals were part of Mr. Trump's renovation plan, rejecting the government's argument that they were part of an unrelated maintenance effort.

The judge said she did not find statements by the Department of Interior's deputy chief of staff to be credible, including his description of the agency's tree management plan as "cleaning up" the course.

CBS News has reached out to the Justice Department and the Department of Interior for comment.

Mr. Trump has feuded with Reyes, calling her a "crazed lunatic."

Earlier this month, the Trump administration asked Reyes to recuse herself from the case, arguing that she had shown "open hostility" to the government and that her "histrionics in prior hearings have clearly demonstrated she is no longer impartial."

"To name just a few examples of bias, Judge Reyes has unfairly questioned Trump Administration attorneys' intelligence, allowed her disdain for the Trump Administration to influence how hearings unfold, and systematically disregarded basic separation of powers principles and Article III constraints on judicial authority," government attorneys wrote.

Reyes rejected that request and denied that she is biased, listing out compliments that she has paid government lawyers.

"So what happened? Not sudden onset bias," Reyes wrote in her denial. "Instead, the Government decided to remove over 500 healthy, non-invasive trees from East Potomac Golf Course. It waited until 4:55 p.m. on the Friday of a holiday weekend to give notice that it would begin removing trees within 15 hours. It removed nearly 430 trees in one day and would have destroyed hundreds more but for a rain delay."

World.title: Jay-Z to headline 2027 Super Bowl halftime show
World.content:
The man who has helped produce the Super Bowl halftime show is stepping into the spotlight: Jay-Z will headline the show himself.

The NFL, Apple Music and Roc Nation announced Monday night that Jay-Z will be the featured performer for the halftime festivities on Feb. 14 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

The announcement included a short video of Jay-Z sitting in SoFi Stadium surrounded by goats with the caption "GOAT's out of the bag."

After days of speculation, Jay-Z is set to return to the stadium where he closed his "Jay-Z 30" concerts over the weekend. The run began with three shows at Yankee Stadium in New York, continued in London and ended in Southern California.

Jay-Z's Roc Nation has partnered with the NFL since 2019 to advise on and help produce the league's entertainment presentations, including the Super Bowl halftime show. At the time, Jay-Z said he had told NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell, "If this is about me performing at the Super Bowl, then we can just end this conversation now."

Seven years later, Jay-Z is ready to perform after all.

Since then, the headlining halftime show performers have included Shakira and Jennifer Lopez, Rihanna, Kendrick Lamar and The Weeknd, among others.

Jay-Z, born Shawn Carter, has won 25 Grammy Awards and received 89 nominations, the second-most in history behind his wife, Beyoncé — who has performed at two Super Bowls. His catalog includes the albums "Reasonable Doubt," "The Blueprint" and "The Black Album," and hit songs such as "Hard Knock Life (Ghetto Anthem)," "99 Problems" and "Empire State of Mind," his collaboration with Alicia Keys.

His 1996 debut, "Reasonable Doubt," was inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame last year.

Jay-Z's career has extended into music publishing, artist management and sports. He co-founded Roc-A-Fella Records and founded Roc Nation in 2008, building it into an entertainment company that works with artists and athletes.

Jay-Z became the first rapper inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame in 2017 and joined the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2021.

Bad Bunny performed at last season's Super Bowl in February. His songs had sharp gains across streaming charts, playlists and music discovery platforms in the hours following the show.

The next morning, the Puerto Rican superstar held the top six spots on Spotify's Top 50 U.S. chart, with another song coming in at No. 8. Eleven other Bad Bunny songs were ranking in Spotify's Top 50 U.S. chart at the time.

World.title: Eric Bauza, actor who voiced Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, dies at 46
World.content:
Eric Bauza, the Emmy-winning actor who voiced iconic "Looney Tunes" characters Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, died on Sunday, according to his manager. He was 46.

"Eric was a unique and versatile voice actor who was loved by everyone he knew and worked with," said Judy Coppage, Bauza's manager. "His sudden passing is a shock to all of us, and he will be deeply missed. It's a profound loss for his family, the animation industry and his fans."

Bauza, who was born in Canada, died from hypertensive cardiovascular disease, according to the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner.

His family posted a brief statement on his Instagram page, adding that more details would come later.

Bauza had more than 400 acting credits listed on his IMDb page. In addition to voicing Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, Bauza is credited with voicing other "Looney Tunes" characters such as Porky Pig, Pepé Le Pew, Marvin the Martian, Elmer Fudd, Foghorn Leghorn, Tweety Bird and Road Runner. He also voiced characters in the most recent "Space Jam" film, alongside LeBron James.

Beyond "Looney Tunes," Bauza was known for his voice work on shows such as "Avatar: The Last Airbender," "Puss in Boots," "Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles," "Woody Woodpecker," "Bob's Burgers" and "Teen Titans Go!"

A statement from Warner Bros. Chairman Channing Dungey and Warner Bros. Pictures Animation President and CCO Bill Damaschke noted Bauza's impact on the "Looney Tunes" franchise.

"Eric Bauza was a unique voice talent who brought joy and laughter to millions around the world. During his 15 years at Warner Bros. Animation, he was the voice of Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck among countless other characters. He followed in the footsteps of giants like Mel Blanc," the statement said. "Eric said that carrying on the legendary legacy of the Looney Tunes was among the greatest honors of his life. In addition to his incredible talent, Eric was a treasured part of our animation family. Our hearts go out to his loved ones."

Bauza won Children's and Family Emmy Awards in 2022, 2023 and 2025 and was nominated in 2026. He was also nominated for five Daytime Emmy Awards from 2016 to 2021.

He joined CBS LA in August to discuss his latest film and the newest "Looney Tunes" installment, "Coyote vs. Acme."

"All of my work is based off of the original voiceover artist, the great Mel Blanc; he was the original. I like to call him the blueprint of these characters," Bauza said. "They're not just voices; these are personalities that we've been familiar with now for 90 years — it's like your oldest family members. So, that's my history with them."

Bauza said his favorite character to voice was Bugs Bunny, but as he got older, he felt more like Daffy Duck.

World.title: Dollar General overcharged people at checkout for years, FTC says
World.content:
The Federal Trade Commission and 20 states on Monday sued Dollar General, accusing the budget retailer of charging customers more for products than it advertised.

The chain, which operates 21,000 stores nationwide, allegedly mislabeled prices for years, "extracting millions of dollars in unlawful overcharges," the FTC alleged.

"Dollar General has betrayed the trust of millions of American consumers and imposed significant financial harm on communities and consumers who are already struggling to make their paychecks last," Christopher Mufarrige, director of the FTC's Bureau of Consumer Protection, said in a statement.

The FTC added that American consumers depend on Dollar General's advertised low prices to make ends meet on tight budgets, while prices that don't reflect advertised deals make it impossible for them to manage household finances.

The agency filed its complaint in the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Tennessee, Dollar General's home state.

"Our goal is 100% accuracy between shelf and register prices in every store," Dollar General said in a statement. "As with other retailers and despite our policies and procedures, occasional price discrepancies can occur.
