Helen McEntee, also of Fine Gael, is Minister for Foreign Affairs and Defence. Jim O’Callaghan is Minister for Justice, Martin Heydon is Minister for Agriculture, and Jack Chambers is Minister for Public Expenditure.

After the November 2024 election the Dáil split as follows: Fianna Fáil 48 seats, Sinn Féin 39, Fine Gael 38, Labour 11, Social Democrats 11, Independent Ireland 4, People Before Profit-Solidarity 3, Aontú 2 and the Greens 1, with independents holding the rest. Seat numbers have shifted since, including a May 2026 by-election in Galway West.

Sinn Féin, the left-wing nationalist party, leads the opposition because the two governing parties refuse to share power with it. Fianna Fáil and Fine Gael did not win the 88 seats needed for a majority on their own, so the government relies on friendly independents.

The next general election must be held no later than early 2030, five years after the Dáil first met in December 2024. Under the constitution, the vote must follow within 30 days of the Dáil’s dissolution.

The Legal Aid Row Clogging The Courts

The sharpest domestic fight is over legal aid, the state fund that pays lawyers for people who cannot afford one. New criminal legal aid rules took effect on 1 July 2026, and many defence solicitors have since withdrawn their services in protest.

Nationwide, the number of legal aid certificates fell by 93 per cent. In Dublin the total for July dropped to 60, from 3,344 in July last year.

Hundreds of criminal cases have been adjourned and courts have faced stoppages. Solicitors blame the rules on Justice Minister O’Callaghan, whom they accuse of refusing to negotiate.

The solicitors held a protest outside the Central Criminal Court in Dublin on 5 October, the first day of the new legal term. Solicitors in Cork have asked the Taoiseach to step in.

The row matters beyond Ireland because it tests whether a coalition with a thin majority can enforce spending reform against a well organised profession. It is a small case of a wider European question, how long governments can hold spending reforms under pressure.

Neutrality, Defence And Lebanon

Ireland is not a member of NATO, the Western military alliance, and has a long tradition of military neutrality. Irish troops can currently go abroad only under the “triple lock”: government approval, a Dáil vote and a UN mandate.

Minister McEntee’s Defence (Amendment) Bill drops the UN mandate requirement. It would also raise from 12 to 50 the number of personnel who can deploy without a Dáil vote.

The government says neutrality is unchanged and that oversight remains. Critics argue that joining EU missions without a UN mandate could drag Ireland into conflicts it would not otherwise choose.

The Dáil voted 79 to 71 on 21 October for the bill, which now goes to a parliamentary committee, and the government wants it law by the end of the year. The debate has a practical edge in Lebanon, where Irish troops serve in UNIFIL, the UN peacekeeping force, whose mandate runs only to 31 December 2026.

Budget 2027 And The Farm Vote

Harris and Chambers presented Budget 2027 to the Dáil on 6 October. It totals €8.5 billion (about US$9.5 billion at EUR/USD 1.1167), made up of €7 billion (US$7.8 billion) of extra spending and €1.5 billion (US$1.7 billion) of tax measures.

The standard rate income tax band rises by €2,500 (US$2,790) to €46,500 (US$51,930). The main tax credits rise by €125 (about US$140) each.

Farmers received targeted help. From 1 January 2027 the annual tax credit for Succession Farm Partnerships (farm-sharing agreements between generations) doubles from €5,000 (US$5,580) to €10,000 (US$11,170) for five years, and the three-year waiting period is removed.

Agriculture Minister Heydon also announced a €46.2 million (US$51.6 million) fertiliser aid scheme because of higher prices linked to the Middle East crisis. It combines €15.38 million (US$17.2 million) from the EU with the maximum national top-up of €30.8 million (US$34.4 million).

Ireland, The EU And Washington

Ireland chairs EU ministerial talks from 1 July to 31 December 2026 under the slogan “Strength with unity”. Its priorities are competitiveness, values and security, including continued support for Ukraine.

Lithuania takes over the chair on 1 January 2027. The role lets Dublin steer meeting agendas, though it does not let Ireland set EU policy alone.

What It Means for US Readers

Ireland is the European home of many large US technology and pharmaceutical groups, and a large share of its corporation tax comes from them. Corporation tax makes up about a quarter of all Irish tax receipts, so US tariff decisions and global minimum tax rules can move the Irish budget quickly.

For security watchers, the Lebanon mission and the triple lock debate show how far Dublin will move toward EU defence cooperation. For investors, the coalition faces no election before early 2030, which lowers the risk of a sudden change in tax policy.

What Is Not Known

It is not known how the legal aid dispute will end. The government has not announced a settlement, and the solicitors have not said when they will return to full service.

It is also unclear whether the Defence (Amendment) Bill will be amended in committee and pass before the end of the year. What role Irish troops will have in Lebanon after the UN mandate ends is not settled.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is the Taoiseach of Ireland in October 2026?

Micheál Martin of Fianna Fáil. He leads a coalition with Fine Gael and relies on independent members of the Dáil for a majority.

Who is the President of Ireland?

Catherine Connolly, an independent, took office on 11 November 2025. The role is largely ceremonial and the President does not run the government.

What is the triple lock?

It is the rule that Irish troops deploy abroad only with government approval, a Dáil vote and a UN mandate. The Dáil voted 79 to 71 on 21 October for a bill that removes the UN mandate requirement.

When is the next Irish general election?

It must be held no later than early 2030, five years after the Dáil first met in December 2024. An earlier vote is possible if the government falls.

What is Ireland’s role in the EU this year?

Ireland holds the rotating EU Council presidency from 1 July to 31 December 2026. It then passes the chair to Lithuania.

Sources: Department of Finance, Budget 2027; Department of Finance, Statement by Minister Harris on Budget 2027; Department of Defence, UNIFIL participation; Oireachtas (Parliament of Ireland), TDs; President of Ireland; Irish Presidency of the Council of the EU.

World.title: Your 2027 Marchamo Comes With a Sticker That Lasts 10 Years
World.content:
Your 2027 marchamo can be checked and paid starting Monday, Nov. 2. If your vehicle has a windshield, it’s also the last year you’ll need a new sticker for a while. The National Insurance Institute (INS) opens its marchamo lookup at 8 a.m. on Nov. 2. You have until Dec. 31 to pay without penalties.

The paper sticker is being replaced by an electronic tag that goes on the inside of your windshield and is designed to last up to 10 years. You still pay the marchamo every year. You just stop replacing the sticker. The tag uses passive radio-frequency identification, the same kind of chip found in many access cards. According to the INS, it has no battery and no GPS, so it can’t track where you drive. It only responds when an authorized reader scans it at close range to confirm your vehicle is cleared to circulate.

Clean the glass before you apply it, and get it right the first time. The tag is built to break apart if it’s peeled off, so it can’t be moved to another vehicle. If you apply it incorrectly or replace your windshield, you’ll need a new one from the INS. Cars, buses and trucks get the electronic tag first, and the INS has ordered 1.6 million of them. Motorcycles keep the traditional sticker for now while the INS tests how the tag holds up under harsher conditions.

Your proof of payment is going digital too. The circulation document will be emailed to the address you give when you pay, and you can also download it from the INS website or the INS Móvil app. Keep it on your phone, because you still have to show it if an officer asks. The mandatory insurance included in your marchamo, known as SOA, rises 5.4% for private vehicles, 4.5% for motorcycles and 12.4% for buses. It drops for taxis, light and heavy cargo vehicles and special equipment.

Across all vehicle types, the weighted average SOA premium rises about 4% to ₡46,700 ($102), an increase of ₡1,811 ($4), according to the Superintendency of Insurance (Sugese). That average isn’t what every owner pays. Your amount depends on your vehicle type. Superintendent of Insurance Tomás Soley linked part of the increase to a 15% rise in the number of people injured in traffic crashes between 2024 and 2025. The SOA pays for medical care and disability benefits for people hurt in crashes, not for repairs to your vehicle. Coverage stays at ₡6 million ($13,100) per injured person.

Don’t expect your total bill to rise by the same percentage. The SOA is only one part of the marchamo, which also includes the vehicle property tax, any unpaid traffic fines and other charges. You can pay on the INS website, at INS branches and service points, through authorized agents or by phone at 800-TELEINS.

The electronic tag was first planned for 2024. It was delayed by procurement problems, including a tender that was declared void, and by privacy and cybersecurity concerns raised by experts. Every vehicle owner in Costa Rica has until Dec. 31 to pay. Checking your amount soon after Nov. 2 gives you time to spot unexpected charges, such as unpaid fines, before the deadline.

World.title: US Embassy Helped Mother Get Son Out of Costa Rica Community, She Says
World.content:
An American mother says she watched her son grow thinner and more distant over more than two years in a religious community in Pérez Zeledón, and that she was able to bring him home this year only with help from relatives and U.S. Embassy staff. The community, known as EarthWaking Village, is under investigation by the Judicial Investigation Agency (OIJ) over alleged fraud against foreigners, and a Canadian woman says she lost about $350,000 there.

Four Americans, including the community’s alleged leader, were detained in an Oct. 6 raid and released under precautionary measures. None has been charged. The mother, who spoke to local media under a pseudonym, said her son was 24 and going through a difficult period in 2023 when he came across a book describing the community as a remote place where residents grew their own food and lived apart from the pressures of the outside world.

He traveled there for what was presented as a memorable experience, she said, and stayed after members persuaded him to remain. At first, she said, the family saw little cause for concern. The first warning sign was that he began pulling away from relatives. She said he was told not to speak with his family because his new family was in the village.

According to her account, the alleged leader, identified by authorities by the surname England, presented himself as a spiritual authority through whom members believed God spoke. She said staying in the community required members to hand over their money and belongings to the group and to him.

She visited in April 2024 and said she attended ceremonies in which the leader claimed to drive demons and egos out of residents. She said she saw him mistreat people and that he tried to pressure her as well. She stayed less than two weeks and could not persuade her son to leave.

Back home, she continued paying his phone bill and health insurance so he would not lose contact or coverage. She said he ran his credit cards to their limits on the leader’s instructions, after being told he would never return to the United States and that the money was not his, and that she paid the charges to keep him out of debt.

Late in 2025, she said, she learned that residents had begun fasting intermittently as a way to cleanse their souls, and that her son had lost about 10 kilograms (22 pounds). When she returned to Costa Rica in December 2025, she said, he looked pale, gaunt and very ill, and everyone she saw in the village was very thin. She said she contacted the U.S. Embassy to report that people there were sick, going hungry and in danger.

In late February 2026, with help from relatives and embassy staff, she got her son out. He returned to the United States and spent five months in a mental health facility, where he was diagnosed with psychosis induced by a psychedelic substance, she said. She said she does not know what substance he took. He was discharged earlier this month.

Her account could not be independently verified. On Oct. 6, OIJ agents, prosecutors and the investigations department of the U.S. Embassy raided properties in Platanillo and Barú. They detained England, 44; Hallman, 44, described as his partner; McDow, 63; and Gingras, 62. Investigators have counted 11 foreign alleged victims, including U.S. and Canadian citizens, and estimate the losses at about $600,000, a figure they have described as preliminary.

According to the investigation, recruits paid for supposed land purchases, received a certificate as apparent proof and were then asked for more money to administer the lots. Some were allegedly urged to apply for credit cards with the highest possible limits, leaving the debt in their names, and some who had already paid were later told they did not qualify to stay.

The four were released under six-month precautionary measures that require them to report to prosecutors every 15 days, surrender their passports and remain in Costa Rica, among other conditions. The group has said it is not a sect. Javier Chaverri Ross, a lawyer who represents several of the alleged victims, has said he believes there are more victims than those counted so far. The investigation remains open, and the four remain in the country under court supervision.

World.title: Camalote man charged after police discover 4.5 grams of crack cocaine during house search
World.content:
Camalote man charged after police discover 4.5 grams of crack cocaine during house search

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police have formally arrested and charged 40-year-old Joel Fuentes of Camalote Village, Cayo District, following the discovery of 4.5 grams of crack cocaine during a search of his residence.

According to ASP Stacy Smith, officers attached to the GI3 unit executed a search warrant at Fuentes’ home on Monday, October 19, 2026.

During the search, officers reportedly discovered a transparent plastic bag containing 4.5 grams of suspected crack cocaine.

Fuentes was subsequently arrested and charged with possession of controlled drugs with intent to supply.

World.title: Three San Pedro residents charged following discovery of 278 grams of cannabis and 10 grams of cocaine
World.content:
Three San Pedro residents charged following discovery of 278 grams of cannabis and 10 grams of cocaine

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Three residents of San Pedrito, San Pedro Town, have been formally arrested and jointly charged with possession of controlled drugs with intent to supply following the discovery of 278.1 grams of cannabis.

The accused have been identified as Sheildy E. Rodriguez Jacome, Euthrofio Oscar Lisbey and Joel Amalio Herrata.

According to police, Detective Constable Arley Castillo formally arrested and charged the three individuals on October 25, 2026.

All three were cautioned by police and elected to remain silent.

During Monday’s police press briefing, ASP Stacy Smith further confirmed that Jacome was additionally charged with possession of controlled drugs with intent to supply following the discovery of 10.7 grams of cocaine during a search of her person.

Police have not disclosed further details surrounding the circumstances of the arrests.

World.title: Orson Gardiner, Nadia Palacio charged after police discover 7.4 grams of crack cocaine during house search
World.content:
Orson Gardiner, Nadia Palacio charged after police discover 7.4 grams of crack cocaine during house search

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police have formally arrested and jointly charged two residents of the Cayo District following the discovery of 7.4 grams of crack cocaine during a search of their residence.

According to ASP Stacy Smith, the arrests followed the execution of a search warrant on October 20, 2026, by officers attached to the Special Tactics Response Team.

The operation was conducted at a residence on Hibiscus Street, where officers reportedly discovered the suspected controlled substance.

The accused were identified as a 47-year-old man surnamed Orson Gardiner and a 37-year-old woman surnamed Nadia Palacio.

Both individuals were jointly charged with possession of controlled drugs with intent to supply.

World.title: Cahal Pech Village Resort is hiring a front desk agent and a bartender
World.content:
Cahal Pech Village Resort is hiring a front desk agent and a bartender

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Cahal Pech Village Resort and Tours in San Ignacio is recruiting for two positions: a front desk agent and a bartender.

The resort is seeking a front desk agent who is experienced with the RoomMaster property management system and knowledgeable about tours in the Cayo District and across Belize. The ideal candidate is organized, professional and focused on guest service.

The resort is also looking for a friendly, energetic and innovative bartender who can bring fresh ideas to the bar and keep guests engaged.

Interested persons are asked to send their CV to [email protected].

World.title: BermudAir launches nonstop flights from Fort Lauderdale to Belize ahead of winter tourism season
World.content:
BermudAir launches nonstop flights from Fort Lauderdale to Belize ahead of winter tourism season

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Belize welcomed another major boost to its international air connectivity on Monday, October 26, 2026, as BermudAir officially launched its inaugural nonstop flight from Fort Lauderdale, Florida, to the Philip Goldson International Airport.

The new service provides travelers in South Florida with another direct connection to Belize as the country prepares for the busy winter tourism season.

The Belize Tourism Board (BTB), alongside its tourism partners, organized a special welcome for arriving passengers, featuring live music from the Kriol Culture Heritage Brukdown Band in celebration of Kriol Heritage Month.

Visitors were also treated to local delicacies and welcome drinks courtesy of Travellers Liquor.

A ribbon-cutting ceremony marked the occasion, with Nicole Usher, Chief Executive Officer in the Ministry of Tourism, Youth, Sports and Diaspora Relations, and Director of Tourism Evan Tillett joining senior BermudAir representatives.

The airline was represented by Seth Bailey, Vice President of Commercial, and Andrea Spiegel, Chief Marketing and Communications Officer.

The Fort Lauderdale route is the first of several new nonstop services BermudAir plans to introduce to Belize.

Additional flights from Boston, Raleigh-Durham, Orlando Sanford and St. Petersburg/Tampa Bay are scheduled to begin in December 2026.

BTB is also hosting American journalists, content creators and travel advisors to showcase Belize’s tourism attractions and promote the destination to travelers across the U.S. East Coast.

The expanded air connections are expected to create additional opportunities for Belize’s hotels, tour operators, restaurants and other tourism-related businesses.

World.title: Government confirms Alexis Rosado’s immediate resignation from ICJ team
World.content:
Government confirms Alexis Rosado’s immediate resignation from ICJ team

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Ambassador Alexis Rosado has resigned as Belize’s Co-Agent before the International Court of Justice, following growing public pressure over his continued service while facing criminal proceedings.

The Government of Belize announced the resignation on Monday, October 26, confirming that it takes effect immediately.

Earlier Monday, Opposition Leader Tracy Taegar Panton publicly called on Rosado to voluntarily step aside until the criminal proceedings against him are resolved.

Panton argued that temporary withdrawal from public responsibilities during serious criminal proceedings should not be viewed as a declaration of guilt but as a measure of accountability.

Her statement questioned whether Rosado should continue representing Belize in such an important international legal matter.

The Government’s announcement confirmed that Rosado had resigned but did not explain his reasons for stepping down or establish whether the decision was connected to Panton’s appeal.

Rosado faces criminal proceedings involving allegations of sexual offences against a minor. He is entitled to the presumption of innocence, and the allegations have not been proven in court.

The Government said it would make no further comment on the matter out of respect for the judicial process.

It also sought to reassure the public that Belize’s cases before the ICJ remain on track.

With written submissions already filed, the legal proceedings will continue under Ambassador Assad Shoman and the remaining legal team.

The Government reaffirmed its commitment to protecting Belize’s sovereignty and territorial integrity in accordance with international law.

World.title: Belize Network of NGOs backs calls for Alexis Rosado to step down, demands accountability in public office
World.content:
Belize Network of NGOs backs calls for Alexis Rosado to step down, demands accountability in public office

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): The Belize Network of NGOs (BNN) has joined calls for Ambassador Alexis Rosado to step down from his role as Belize’s Co-Agent before the International Court of Justice (ICJ), insisting that public officials must be held to the highest standards of integrity and accountability.

In a press release dated October 26, 2026, the organization said individuals entrusted with public responsibilities must protect public confidence, particularly when facing serious criminal charges or allegations.

BNN cited Section 121 of the Belize Constitution, which addresses standards of conduct and integrity in public office.

The organization argued that Belize needs standardized protocols allowing for the temporary removal of public officials from their duties while serious criminal matters are being determined by the courts.

According to BNN, such measures should not be interpreted as declarations of guilt but as safeguards for public confidence.

The organization specifically supported calls for Rosado to step aside from Belize’s ICJ team.

Rosado has been facing criminal proceedings involving allegations of sexual offences against a minor. He remains entitled to the presumption of innocence.

The statement came on the same day the Government of Belize officially confirmed Rosado’s resignation as Co-Agent, effective October 26.

BNN’s release did not acknowledge the resignation, and it is unclear whether the organization issued its statement before the Government’s announcement.

The organization emphasized that public accountability must apply consistently to individuals serving in official capacities, regardless of their positions or responsibilities.

BNN also reaffirmed its commitment to good governance, transparency and protecting the integrity of public institutions.

World.title: 16-year-old student pulls fake gun on teacher at Julian Cho Highschool because he didn’t do his homework
World.content:
16-year-old student pulls fake gun on teacher at Julian Cho Highschool because he didn’t do his homework

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police in Punta Gorda are investigating an incident involving a 16-year-old student who allegedly pulled out an imitation firearm during a confrontation with a teacher over homework at Julian Cho Highschool in Punta Gorda.

According to ASP Stacy Smith, the incident occurred on October 20, 2026, when a teacher questioned the student about an assignment he had failed to submit.

When the student could not produce his homework, the teacher reportedly requested his demerit card.

Police say the student then allegedly reached into his pencil case, removed what appeared to be a firearm and subsequently placed it back inside the case.

With encouragement from his classmates, the student eventually surrendered the object, which was determined to be an imitation firearm.

Smith confirmed that the teacher has not made a formal police report. However, the Community Policing Unit in Punta Gorda has become involved in addressing the incident.

She explained that possession of an imitation firearm with criminal intent can constitute a criminal offence and that the student, being 16 years old, is of an age at which criminal liability may apply.

Police have not announced any charges, and the matter remains under investigation.

World.title: Criminalise gun couriers
World.content:
CHAMPAGNIE... it was also my expectation and hope that the National Security Council would have looked at specific criminalisation of couriers or shippers who are used to import illegal firearms into this country

Senior attorney Peter Champagnie, KC — who has been strident about the shortcomings of the 2022 Firearms Act since inception — on Monday welcomed amendments proposed by the National Security Council but is urging criminalisation of couriers or shippers who import illegal firearms into the country by virtue of lax inspection protocols.

His call comes in the wake of Sunday’s announcement by the Office of the Cabinet that the National Security Council (NSC) has recommended that individuals convicted of illegal possession of a firearm should now face a new minimum mandatory sentence of 20 years imprisonment instead of the current 15-year minimum.

The NSC also proposed that adults who groom children to use, store, transport, or acquire illegal guns will face a new criminal offence under the pending amendments to the Act “to address the gap whereby gangs seek to recruit and enlist minors in the commission of gun crimes”.

Additionally, the NSC agreed that further consideration should be given to how cases involving children found with illegal firearms are handled and assured that concerns raised regarding imitation firearms will be “clearly addressed to distinguish between toy guns and guns designed to realistically imitate a weapon”.

The council also said the review would include concerns surrounding firearms with expired licences. In the meantime, however, it said before the new provisions take effect, the Government will provide a gun amnesty and cash buy-back programme, giving anyone holding an illegal gun the opportunity to surrender it. The Ministry of National Security and Peace has been directed to have the draft legislation ready by the end of November 2026 for wider consultations.

On Monday, Champagnie, in an interview with the Jamaica Observer, applauded the pending changes but said, “It was also my expectation and hope that the National Security Council would have looked at specific criminalisation of couriers or shippers who, because of the lack of diligence that is applied to scrutinise and inspect shipments, are used to import illegal firearms into this country.”

“As I understand it presently, as it relates to Customs and what obtains, the worst that can be expected if a shipment is contaminated by illegal weapons or anything illegal is that there is perhaps a penalty or a hearing, or there is a suspension of that person’s licence or revocation. But I do believe that it needs to go further in the way of criminalisation, because what the National Security Council needs to also focus on is not just the tail end of the problem; that is to say, persons who are in possession of illegal firearms, but also the source of these firearms, because we do not manufacture firearms here; they have to come from somewhere other than Jamaica. And I think there needs to be stiffer penalties, or indeed penalties, in relation to that. Not just mere trafficking; it has to also reach the shippers and couriers, that is my view,” the prominent defence attorney said.

“They could easily create a mandate where shippers or couriers are required to containerise their shipment in a sterile era where it is video-recorded and presented, and where they would have to show that they took all reasonable steps to ensure that their cargo or the shipment is not contaminated,” Champagnie suggested.

Making it clear that he was speaking in a personal capacity and not on behalf of other legal bodies, Champagnie said he had no quarrel with the proposal to increase the statutory mandatory minimum from 15 to 20 years.

“That is the supremacy of Parliament. I can’t say that they have no authority for so doing and indeed, I have been on record over the years to say that this idea of giving someone who is caught with an illegal weapon three years or 18 months or even a fine is unacceptable. So I support the statutory mandatory minimum, and if they want to increase it, then that’s their right. However, I do believe that there needs to be a holistic approach with the Firearms Act to facilitate guilty pleas,” Champagnie maintained.

“There must be some incentive for persons wanting to plead guilty, and there must be some exceptional circumstances where a person found in possession of a firearm must be allowed to have a kind of discretion for that person to receive a sentence below the statutory mandatory minimum, and in those circumstances, there is authority for it in other jurisdictions where exceptions are specifically laid out. But certainly, in relation to the hardcore criminals and those that use imitation firearms to commit offences, they must expect severe penalties,” he argued.

Champagnie, in the meantime, said legislation which addresses the appeal process in circumstances where a sentence is excessive should also be revisited.

“We must also bear in mind that the prosecution now has the right to appeal if a sentence is given that is considered to be woefully inadequate for the circumstances, and there have been cases that have settled that. So, I would want that to be also considered, and I look forward to the actual details of the report and the recommendations beyond what has been issued by way of a press release, because one is not able to fully appreciate all of the nuances and the extent of the recommendations until we actually are able or in a position to examine the actual paper that is in the way of recommendations,” he told the Observer.

He said the planned silent protest on September 23 and a sit out by some attorneys as part of the push for a review of the Act had not been in vain.

“When the attorneys sought to bring some kind of pressure for the Government to re-examine the Firearms Act, the first comment that was made was that the legislation was up for review next year, and therefore we should await that period. I note, however, that there is a shift now, where there seems to be an intention to have recommended changes effected within this year. That is good, but what it demonstrates is that we are able to pivot and we are able to move with alacrity if the need arises,” he said in urging the authorities to ensure that practitioners from both the private and public bar are at the discussion table.

“I don’t think ever before in our legal history, we have had a situation where a legislation, in the way of the administration of the criminal justice system, has received universal comments in the way of shortcomings by not just the private bar but also the public bar, the prosecution, and in some instances the judges, as it relates to it facilitating guilty plea, and that is a major, major point to be made,” he argued.

“Anyone who is involved in the practice of law day to day will tell you that there are real issues. There are real issues also with licensed firearm holders who run the risk of getting 20 years just by being in possession of a licensed firearm and being caught for instance in a physical confrontation with another person even when they are not using it, so these are fundamental issues that I think need to be examined,” he said.

Section 14(3) of the Act dictates that a person commits a felony if they are in possession of a firearm or an imitation firearm at the time of committing, or when being apprehended for, any specific serious offence listed in the First Schedule of the provision.

World.title: Waiting in pain for 5 months
World.content:
Garfield Granston, who broke his spine in May, is seen at Black River Hospital.

THE wait continues for 57-year-old Garfield Granston — who broke his spine in May — to receive a procedure which remains stalled by an out-of-service machine at Kingston Public Hospital (KPH).

His stepdaughter, Elexso Smith, told the Jamaica Observer on Monday that the family has endured five long months awaiting a surgery date, but KPH has not delivered a clear timeline, leaving Granston at Black River Hospital (BRH) where he was initially admitted.

Granston’s ordeal began on May 15, 2026 when he fell from a tree and was rushed to BRH in his home parish of St Elizabeth. There, doctors determined that he had sustained fractures in two places along his spine and would require surgery.

The family was subsequently told that the hospital lacked the facilities to perform the procedure, and her stepfather was referred to KPH — Jamaica’s largest public multidisciplinary Type-A facility — with the hope of receiving the treatment he needed.

The procedure required 10 pedicle screws, 10 set screws, and two rods, at a total cost of $854,000. Faced with that bill, Smith said the family sought assistance from the Ministry of Health and Wellness, which provided a $554,000 subsidy, while they covered the remaining $300,000.

Smith shared that after the bill was cleared, she was certain that her stepfather would soon receive surgery. But when they took the receipt to Granston’s surgeon, another obstacle outside of her family’s control presented itself.

“Before we pay the money at KPH, and before we got help from the health ministry, the doctor was very harsh, because he was arguing saying that we have to pay the money before we can do surgery. When we get the receipt, and gave it to the doctor he said: ‘One more problem. The machine broke down’,” Smith told the Observer.

“Every time he is to go up there [KPH] they’re always putting him off or if he’s sent up there they send him back down [to BRH]. From the last time he went up there on the 30th [of June] he has not been back there. And then when they [BRH] call up there they say he mustn’t come, or there is no bed space,” she claimed.

The most recent update was delivered by doctors at Black River Hospital, notifying Smith and family that the surgery would not be possible until a bedsore that Granston had developed during his five-month stay completely healed.

She argued that the “cut”, slightly positioned above his lower back, was small, and should not, in her estimation, cause further delay.

Smith added that her stepfather’s care regimen has been stressful on the family, who argue that caring for him in his current state is significantly more difficult than if he were recovering from surgery.

“Sometimes we say that it would have been better if he was at home, you know, so you can spend a little time with him and do what you have to do. It’s really hard for us; you have to buy pampers and every little thing. If he did the surgery and can sit upright, we could push him in a wheelchair and help him to use the bathroom. So right now it’s just really hard,” said Smith.

Meanwhile, Granston remains at BRH where he receives treatment for pain but continues to bear the discomfort of his injuries.

“They’ve just been giving him pills. Right now, he’s been complaining about pain in his belly. About two weeks ago he had to do a test and we’re still waiting on those results. So it has just been hard on him, and hard on everyone,” Smith said.

Tired of waiting while her stepfather languishes in pain, Smith has called on KPH to provide a clear timeline for when his distress will end.

“I just want to find out what’s really happening with this surgery situation. It’s been months and nothing. We’re not hearing nothing at all. So we just want KPH to state what their position is with this surgery as soon as possible,” said Smith.

World.title: Bad Sekki jets to NY
World.content:
Bad Sekki.

For Jamaican comedian and social media personality Karlando “Bad Sekki” Bailey, the bright lights of New York City’s Times Square have long represented more than just a popular tourist attraction. They have been the setting for a video he has imagined creating for years, and come November, that dream could finally become a reality.

The popular content creator is now preparing for his first trip to the country, with plans to visit four cities, reconnect with family, and explore opportunities to further develop his craft.

But amid the excitement of travelling overseas for the first time, there is one particular moment Bailey is eagerly anticipating — standing in the heart of Times Square, surrounded by its towering digital billboards, and delivering a line he has long rehearsed in his mind.

“A just one video idea me have weh me really wah do from when, where I am in Time Square saying ‘New York’. That’s the main thing I am looking forward to,” Bailey shared.

The moment, although seemingly simple, carries considerable significance for the comedian, whose journey from working as a security guard to establishing himself as a popular Jamaican content creator has been marked by persistence, humour, and an ability to connect with audiences through everyday experiences.

His upcoming adventure, dubbed Bad Sekki Goes to America, will run from November 16 to December 2, 2026, documenting his experiences across four US cities while offering his followers a glimpse into a new chapter of his life.

For Bailey, the opportunity comes after a disappointing experience in March 2025, when his initial application for a US visa was denied. He subsequently shared the setback with his followers, generating encouragement from supporters who were eager to see him eventually realise his ambition.

Determined not to allow the rejection to derail his plans, Bailey reapplied in 2026 and was granted a visa in October.

“I felt happy and really thankful that I got it. I tried last year and didn’t get it,” he said, reflecting on the moment he received the good news.

According to Jason McNeish, who is spearheading the organisation of the trip, travelling to the United States has been one of Bailey’s long-standing aspirations.

“It has been a dream of his to travel and go to the US. He applied for his visa in 2025, which was denied. He reapplied in 2026 which was approved,” McNeish explained.

And while Bailey was ready to board a plane almost immediately after receiving his passport, McNeish said the team wanted to ensure that his first international experience would be memorable and beneficial to his career.

“He wanted to go the next day after he got the passport but we wanted to make it a whole trip. He will be visiting four cities so it took a longer time to plan,” he said.

The itinerary is being developed to combine entertainment, cultural exploration, family connections, and professional development, allowing Bailey to experience the United States both as a visitor and as a creative professional.

A major component of the trip will be content creation, with Bailey expected to document his experiences and share them with the audience that has supported his rise in Jamaica’s digital entertainment space.

New York, in particular, is expected to provide a backdrop for his signature brand of comedy, as he explores unfamiliar surroundings and captures the reactions and experiences that have become central to his appeal.

However, the trip will not be limited to sightseeing and social media videos.

McNeish revealed that plans are also being explored for Bailey to visit professional studios and gain exposure to international production environments, with the possibility of connecting with representatives associated with streaming giant Netflix.

“We are making it a full experience, he’s going to of course connect with family and more importantly for me he is going to get some professional development as well, so we are looking at visiting a few studios…” McNeish said.

He was careful to point out, however, that the proposed Netflix engagement has not been finalised. Discussions are ongoing with an agent affiliated with the company in the hope of arranging an opportunity during the visit.

The emphasis on professional development reflects an ambition to use the trip as a stepping stone towards expanding Bailey’s creative possibilities beyond the Jamaican market.

For the comedian, however, some of the most meaningful moments may come away from the cameras.

Among those eagerly anticipating his arrival is a cousin with whom he grew up, and who was one of the few people aware that he had decided to make another attempt at securing a visa.

“She was the first one I called. She was so happy for me because she was the only one I told that I was going to look about it,” Bailey recalled.

The planned reunion adds a personal dimension to an adventure that is already shaping up to be a significant milestone in his life.

The Bad Sekki Goes to America project will seek to capture those moments alongside the humour, excitement, and inevitable surprises of experiencing a new country for the first time.

World.title: Kane, Putellas taste Ballon d’Or glory
World.content:
LONDON, England (AFP) — Harry Kane became England’s first Ballon d’Or winner in 25 years in his native city of London on Monday, beating out stiff competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe.

Alexia Putellas claimed the women’s prize for a third time to extend Spain’s domination of the award, thanks to her role in leading Barcelona to last season’s UEFA Champions League before moving to London City Lionesses.

The first-ever Ballon d’Or ceremony on English soil got off to an inauspicious start as the London traffic caused a delay of nearly an hour, with many of the star names arriving late.

But there was a happy ending for the hometown hero as Kane collected the crowning glory of his career to date.

The 33-year-old Bayern Munich forward struck a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for club and country last season, propelling the German giants to a league and cup double. He also scored six times as England finished third at the World Cup.

“Without you guys [his Bayern Munich teammates] and the rest of the team it wouldn’t be possible, the way you guys push me, the way we compete.

So thank you very much,” Kane said after collecting the award. Kane’s medal collection is limited to German domestic triumphs since he arrived at Bayern in 2023.

He was on the losing side for Tottenham in the 2019 Champions League final against Liverpool, and twice tasted bitter defeat in the final of the European Championship with England.

But his remarkable goalscoring consistency has earned him the highest individual award in football.

“Making the move to Bayern Munich was a big step in my career,” Kane told AFP earlier.

“Some people saw it as a risk but for me, it was always about improving and seeing if I could get better around the teammates, the team, the club — and it has pushed me onto another level.

“Being a number nine for Bayern and England, you are expected to score goals — and to do that the number of times I did last year is something I’m really proud of,” he added.

Winner in 2021 and 2022, Putellas’s third Ballon d’Or caps her return back to the top of the women’s game after an anterior cruciate ligament injury derailed her rise four years ago.

Putellas succeeds Spain teammate Aitana Bonmati, the winner the past three years who was sidelined by a leg break for most of last season.

“Ever since I suffered the injury I’ve been trying to enjoy every moment as if it were my last, because you never know if it’ll happen again,” Putellas told AFP in an interview last month.

“I never felt that the [Ballon d’Or] trophy was ‘mine’… Having already experienced it once, I’m able to enjoy it even more now,” she said.

Yamal made the boldest fashion statement of the contenders with a pink flower on the front of his black suit.

The Barcelona winger scooped up the first award of the night for young talent of the year for the third-consecutive time.

But the 19-year-old fell short of becoming the youngest-ever Ballon d’Or winner after he failed to produce his best form during Spain’s World Cup success.

Mbappe got the better of Yamal with two goals as Real Madrid edged Barcelona 2-1 in El Clasico on Sunday. But his wait to win the Ballon d’Or goes on despite his prolific year for France and Real Madrid.

Luis de la Fuente beat out Paris SaintGermain’s Luis Enrique and Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta to be named men’s coach of the year, after leading Spain to World Cup glory.

“I’m really privileged to work with a team of such high quality on a professional and human level,” de la Fuente said.

Barcelona’s Pere Romeu scooped the prize for women’s coach of the year. Arsenal’s Bukayo Saka won the Socrates award for his humanitarian work.

Paris Saint-Germain missed out on securing any of the main individual awards despite winning a second-consecutive Champions League, but did have the consolation of winning men’s club of the year.

Spanish duo Unai Simon and Cata Coll were named best men’s and women’s goalkeeper, respectively.

World.title: BAD BUNNY!
World.content:
Jamaica and Manchester City Women’s striker Khadija “Bunny” Shaw .

REGGAE Girlz superstar Khadija “Bunny” Shaw has spent her career defying expectations, and she reached another incredible milestone by being recognised as the third-best player in women’s football globally.

On Monday, Shaw finished in the top three of the Women’s Ballon d’Or Rankings, as announced at the awards ceremony in London, England. The Jamaican, who was tipped as one of the favourites, ended behind winner Alexia Putellas of Spain who was recognised for her quadruple-winning season with FC Barcelona last season.

Shaw is the only Jamaican to have ever been nominated for the Ballon d’Or, male or female, and she created further history by becoming just the fourth player from outside Europe to finish in the top three. She is also only the third North American player to achieve the feat, joining USA’s Megan Rapinoe, who won the award in 2019, and Alex Morgan, who finished third that same year.

Shaw had a remarkable season in England, guiding Manchester City to the Women’s Super League (WSL) and the FA Cup, ending their four-year title drought.

She finished with 21 goals to win the WSL Golden Boot for a third-straight season and was named WSL Player of the Season, Professional Footballers Association (PFA) Player of the Year, and Football Writers Association (FWA) Footballer of the Year.

Shaw improved on her ranking after finishing 24th in the 2023 race and 15th in 2024.

Despite not winning the overall award, the Reggae Girlz captain says she’s overwhelmed by the achievement.

“To be named as the third-best player by those who voted is a huge honour for me, and I’m extremely grateful for the recognition,” Shaw said. “[Manchester] City are a special club, and for them to trust me with leading our front-line week in, week out, is something I take immense pride in.

“I would like to thank my teammates and the staff for supporting me, on and off the pitch, so I can perform at my best. Recording a historic double last season was a campaign that will always hold a special place in my heart. This recognition would not be possible without them.”

Jamaica Football Federation (JFF) President Michael Ricketts told the Jamaica Observer that Shaw deserves to be recognised as one of the world’s best.

“Bunny has been on the world stage for a number of years and we’re just super excited and happy that she would have achieved so much during her footballing career,” he said. “Bunny is one of our local players who would have ascended to the position of being a superstar, and she would have come up through a local parish programme and, of course, our national programme.

“It gives us more reason to be delighted and proud of the achievements of a local superstar. It has reached the level now that nothing that Bunny achieves is surprising because she seems to be head and shoulders above [other players], especially in Concacaf and certainly matching up with those worldwide. So, we are again basking in another historic achievement and I really want to personally, and certainly on behalf of the entire JFF, to extend again for the umpteenth time another congratulatory remark to the great Khadija “Bunny” Shaw. We are just super excited and we’re here to give her as much support as we can.”

Reggae Girlz Head Coach Hubert Busby says Shaw has further cemented her status as a legend in Jamaican culture.

“I think it’s well documented of what an impact, not just her but the women’s team, senior women’s team, has had on young girls in Jamaica and in the Diaspora. And to see one of our own highlighted when you’re watching these awards with the best of the best players and the distinguished guests who are there, it is remarkable just to know how far she’s come in this time,” he told the Observer.

“I just think she’s going to go from strength to strength. I still think she’s got a few more years left in her so we just continue to be revelled in her accomplishments. And, let’s not forget, she definitely is a national treasure, for sure.”

Shaw joined Erling Haaland and Kevin De Bruyne as the only Man City players in history to finish in the top three of the Ballon d’Or.

World.title: Excelsior booted from Champions Cup, deducted six points in Manning Cup
World.content:
Wolmer’s Boys’ Jude Davis (left) plays the ball while coming under a challenge from Excelsior High’s Tristan Bethune during their ISSA Walker Cup game at the Stadium East Field on Saturday. (Photo: Garfield Robinson)

Defending Manning Cup champions Excelsior High were found guilty of using an ineligible player at an ISSA Disciplinary Committee hearing on Monday.

As a result, they were stripped of their Walker Cup top-four spot and, by extension, kicked out of the all-island Champions Cup, where Wolmer’s Boys will replace them.

Excelsior lost the semi-final to eventual champions Kingston College but, prior to that, had defeated Wolmer’s in the quarter-final.

The top four schools from the urban Walker Cup and the top four from the rural Ben Francis Cup will contest the Champions Cup. JC, who were kicked out of the Walker Cup final after using an ineligible player in the semi-final, retained their spot in the Champions Cup as they had already qualified for the Champions Cup before using the ineligible player.

Excelsior will also lose six points in the Manning Cup in Group 2, which they led with 12 points.

The latest controversy comes amid growing scrutiny of ISSA’s player-registration and eligibility procedures, following the disciplinary action against JC.

The situation also raises fresh questions about the association’s player-verification procedures and the responsibility of schools to ensure that their players meet competition eligibility requirements.

World.title: Perrin Gayle moves on from NCB Retail Banking, Foundation
World.content:
Perrin Gayle

National Commercial Bank Jamaica Limited (NCB) on Monday announced that Perrin Gayle has moved on from his roles as executive vice president of its retail banking portfolio and CEO of the NCB Foundation, effective Monday, October 26, 2026.

In a press release, the financial institution said Gayle decided to pursue another interest.

Kevin Ingram, Senior Assistant Vice President and Head of Branch Sales, will provide interim leadership for retail banking, while Belinda Williams, Head of Group Corporate Affairs Unit, will assume responsibility for the NCB Foundation, the release noted.

Gayle joined NCB in January 2025.

“We thank Perrin for his leadership and contribution to Retail Banking and the NCB Foundation, his service to our customers and communities, and his support for the team. We wish him every success in his next chapter,” said Sheree Martin, Chief Executive Officer of NCB.

World.title: Fi Wi Land: From their first steps, Jamaica’s sea turtles must be protected
World.content:
Once abundant along the island’s shores and in its surrounding waters, Jamaica’s sea turtles now face mounting threats to their survival. From habitat loss caused by coastal development, tourism and beach erosion to poaching and natural predators, these marine creatures face numerous challenges, particularly during the vulnerable nesting and hatching seasons.

In this week’s episode of Fi Wi Land, host Carlysia Ramdeen and National Environment and Planning Agency (NEPA) Environmental Coordinator Ricardo Miller explore the importance of protecting Jamaica’s sea turtles and the role everyone can play in their conservation.

They discuss what to do when encountering nesting turtles or newly hatched babies, why disturbing nesting sites can have serious consequences, and how simple, responsible actions can give hatchlings a better chance of survival.

Discover how you can help safeguard these threatened marine creatures for future generations as the Jamaica Observer, in association with NEPA, presents Episode 2 of Fi Wi Land.

Catch the latest episode on the Jamaica Observer’s YouTube channel and other digital platforms.

World.title: Inside von der Leyen’s Commission shake-up
World.content:
Ursula von der Leyen’s plan to slim down and reorganize the European Commission moves a step closer, with outside advisers calling for a stronger center, fewer bureaucratic silos and potentially far-reaching changes to some of Brussels’ most powerful departments.
