World.title: Croatia is the Leading Charter Power, But Earns Less Than Greece – Why?
World.content:
October the 26th, 2026 – Croatia is the world’s leading charter power, yet it earns less than Greece does from the same sector. The big questions is why?

Croatia is the number one charter power in the world with nearly five thousand vessels in its fleet. In the first eight months of this year, more than 431 thousand charter guest arrivals and more than 2.7 million overnight stays were recorded. However, market saturation has led to charter prices, especially for sailing yachts, falling by 50 percent or more during the peak season. As Alenka Juricic Bukarica reports for Glas Istre, this is not only the case this year. At the same time, competition in other Mediterranean countries is growing, especially in Greece, which last year had just over 3,000 vessels in charter. That is still fewer than Croatia, but with a clear upward trend.

Rising operating costs in recent years have also significantly changed conditions on the Croatian charter market, particularly for smaller vessels, and have negatively affected the return on investment and, consequently, the interest of new investors. Croatia is no longer perceived as a cheap destination, and there has also been a change in the structure of guests: instead of professionals, charter is increasingly chosen by people who are not normally involved in sailing, which increases demand for skippers and hostesses. Ultimately, people from the industry say that in some cases better prices can be achieved on the market in September than in the peak season…

in typical croatian style, there’s a paradox…

The current situation on the Croatian charter market was recently analysed by Ani Trstenjak, head of the Yacht Rent charter agency, and Daniela Gračan from the Faculty of Tourism and Hospitality Management (FMTU) in Opatija. Nautical charter has become, they emphasise, an important part of the tourism economy. It has attracted domestic and foreign capital and created a business ecosystem that includes vessel owners, charter companies, marinas, service providers, intermediaries and numerous providers of supporting services.

However, the success that for decades was measured by fleet growth, number of bookings and total revenue is opening an increasingly uncomfortable question – can Croatian charter continue to grow in the same way without endangering its own profitability.

“Market analysis by the vessel rental platform Yacht-Rent.com for 2026 points to an interesting paradox. Namely, Croatian sailing yachts and catamarans are among the cheapest compared to competing markets, while at the same time achieving high occupancy. Croatian charter does not primarily suffer from a lack of demand, but from a structural problem where demand is increasingly difficult to convert into revenue and profit. At the same time, it is clear that revenue is necessary to cover operating costs, financing, maintenance, depreciation and fleet renewal,” Trstenjak explained.

She clarified that Yacht-Rent’s market analysis for this year compares prices and bookings of vessels across six Mediterranean markets. It covers the operating season from 1 April to 2 November 2026, and expresses prices per person (berth) per week so that different vessel sizes can be compared on a comparable basis. According to that analysis, Croatia has the lowest average weekly price per berth among the compared markets for both sailing yachts and catamarans.

an exceptionally demanding market

Specifically speaking, sailing yachts in Croatia achieve an average weekly price per berth of €355, compared to €454 in Greece and €494 in Turkey. The price in Croatia is 22 percent lower than for a sailing yacht in Greece and 28 percent lower than in Turkey. At the same time, Croatian sailing yachts have an average of 19.4 booked weeks, slightly more than 19 weeks in Greece and significantly more than 17 weeks in Turkey. The estimated gross seasonal revenue per berth in Croatia amounts to €6,887, compared to €8,626 in Greece and €8,398 in Turkey.

The situation with catamarans is similar to that of sailing yachts. The average price of €706 per berth per week in Croatia is 16 percent lower than in Greece and 14 percent lower than in Turkey. Catamarans in Croatia are on average booked for 18.8 weeks during the season, which is close to 19.2 weeks in Greece, but significantly more than 15.4 weeks in Turkey. Despite this, the estimated gross seasonal revenue per berth in Croatia amounts to €13,273, while in Greece it reaches €16,147. Turkey achieves €12,659 in seasonal revenue per vessel.

“These data shows that Greece in the observed sample manages to combine high utilisation with a higher price. Croatia, on the other hand, achieves high capacity utilisation with a significantly lower price,” pointed out the head of the Yacht Rent agency. Adding that Croatian charter today operates on a highly competitive Mediterranean market, she also recalled that a guest can today easily compare prices, year of construction, equipment and capacity of vessels, rental conditions, additional costs and available destinations. And when vessels are very similar to each other, price becomes one of the most important decision criteria. However, she stresses, price is not the cause of the crisis, but its symptom.

higher and higher costs

Although not all segments of charter are equally price-sensitive, Trstenjak explains that luxury crewed vessels, differentiated service, special routes and a top customer experience can have greater pricing power. A standard sailing yacht comparable to dozens of other vessels at the same destination has significantly less room to raise its price independently. Charter companies today face high costs for berths, servicing, spare parts, insurance, labour, cleaning, administration, sales and distribution. Financing, depreciation and the need for fleet renewal, berth prices and insurance also play a significant role. All of this leads charter firms to accept a lower price in order to still rent out the vessel. In the short term such a decision can be rational, our interlocutor says, if the booking covers the additional costs of the rental and contributes to covering fixed costs. However, in the medium or long term, such a decision can be disastrous.

“When discounts become a permanent way of doing business, a serious problem arises that Croatian charter has been facing since 2023. Revenue may cover part of the costs, but it very likely no longer leaves enough funds for equipment renewal, major services, vessel replacement and return on capital. A company can therefore have high turnover, positive operating profit and at the same time an insufficient return on the capital invested in charter management. Every charter company wants to have enough vessels to attract guests, expand its offer and increase turnover.

But when a large number of investors make similar decisions, total supply can grow faster than demand. The number of available vessels increases, but the number of guests and attractive periods does not necessarily grow at the same speed. Therefore, an individual discount may be rational, but collective reliance on discounts can reduce the profitability of the entire market because supply does not adjust quickly enough,” Trstenjak says.

capital investment

She also addressed the problem of charter management, i.e. the fact that many Croatian citizens or companies, as well as foreigners, have in recent years seen the purchase of a sailing yacht or catamaran as a profitable form of capital investment. For the vessel buyer, the charter company handles the rental business, while the owner can use it for part of the year and collects income from the rental. Maintenance costs of the boat are borne by the owner. In such a model, the vessel owner expects a return on capital, the charter company wants to achieve the highest possible margin, while the guest wants the best price-quality ratio.

“If the vessel was purchased with excessively high expectations regarding rental price and number of booked weeks, a change in market conditions can seriously endanger the profitability of the investment. The owner expects a return, while the charter company has to choose between a lower price and the risk of unfilled periods,” our interlocutor warned. She concludes that the Croatian charter market has matured and that it is actually very important to make better use of the season and develop the offer outside the main summer months. At the same time, marinas, anchorages and the preservation of the sea must not be neglected, because it is precisely the quality of the destination that attracts guests. “The future of the charter sector does not depend only on further growth, but on how sustainable and profitable that growth will be,” concluded Ani Trstenjak.

a charter loss of €35 million…

The HUP Nautical Sector Association presented the Blue Book of Croatian Nautics and an initiative for the establishment of a National Nautical Council that should define a common development vision until 2040 at the Biograd Boat Show.

According to HUP’s analysis, entrepreneurs in nautics last year achieved €2.8 billion in business revenue and €1 billion in export revenue, employing 18,323 people. Business revenues rose 9.4 percent and exports 14.8 percent compared to the previous year. The analysis is based on HUP’s register of more than 3,200 mapped economic entities in activities related to nautics. In the period from 2021 to 2025, exports grew 70.8 percent, from €597.1 million to more than €1 billion. The share of gross investments in fixed assets in business revenues simultaneously increased from 11.7 to 18 percent. In the Blue Book, however, a warning was issued about pressure on the profitability of charter, which last year recorded a net loss of €34.7 million. “For the further growth of Croatian nautics, safer investment conditions, faster procedures and the availability of qualified workers are needed.

The Blue Book shows that revenue per employee in the sector from 2021 to 2025 rose by 43 percent, from €108.5 thousand to €155.1 thousand, which confirms the potential for creating greater added value. We want more design, production and servicing to take place in Croatia and for a larger part of the value created to remain in the domestic economy, while preserving the sea and the coast,” said Irena Weber, Director General of HUP. Luciano Beg, president of the HUP Nautical Sector Association, also pointed out that in addition to counting berths and overnight stays, the success of nautics should be measured by the production of vessels and equipment, overhauls, innovations, exports and quality jobs, and that this requires a long-term vision and better coordination between the economy, state institutions and the scientific community.

World.title: “I Won’t Shoot My Own People” – How Perišin Escaped the JNA in a MiG
World.content:
October the 26th, 2026 – Rudolf Perešin refused to shoot at his own people, instead escaping the JNA and flying to Austria.

On the 25th of October 1991, pilot Rudolf Perešin, then a member of the Yugoslav Air Force, defected in a Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-21 fighter from the JNA base in Bihać to Klagenfurt, Austria. Index writes that with that act, he became one of the symbols of resistance and the struggle for Croatia’s independence. After landing in Austria, the public forever remembered his statement: “I am a Croat and I won’t shoot at my own people.”

His MiG-21 was never returned to the Yugoslav People’s Army. It remained in Austria, and Perešin soon joined the Croatian Army and the Croatian Air Force. He became commander of the 1st Fighter Squadron and took part in numerous combat missions during the Homeland War.

During the military-police operation Flash, which took place on the 2nd of May 1995, Perešin’s aircraft was hit in the sky above western Slavonia. He managed to eject, but landed in territory controlled by enemy forces and was killed. His remains were found only two years later – on the 4th of August 1997. He was buried with full military honours on 15 September 1997 at Mirogoj Cemetery in Zagreb. Rudolf Perešin has remained a lasting symbol of courage, patriotism and professional honour of Croatian pilots. His legendary MiG-21 is today exhibited in Zagreb as a reminder of one of the most important moments in the history of the Croatian Air Force.

The aircraft in which Perišin defected was displayed in a museum in Klagenfurt until 2019, when it was returned to Croatia.

World.title: He Survived a Shipwreck and Built a Church – 900 Years Later, Croatia Officially Protected it
World.content:
October the 25th, 2026 – A merchant surviving a shipwreck and then building a church in gratitude that Croatia officially chose to protect almost 1,000 years later is the story behind a construction on an island few know about.

It’s believed that the Church of Saints Cosmas and Damian (Crvka sv. Kuzme i Damjana) on the island of Ugljan dates from the 11th or 12th century. It is located in a peaceful cove, right by the sea, not far from the hamlet of Guduće. Olive groves, dense pine forests, beautiful coves, old fishing villages, crystal-clear sea and views of the Zadar archipelago are what await visitors to Ugljan.

As Ivana Vasarevic writes for Putni Kofer, it’s widely known as one of Croatia’s greenest islands, which also carries the flattering nickname “the garden of Zadar.” It’s just 22 kilometres long, has a little over 5,600 inhabitants, is separated from the mainland by the Zadar Channel, and is connected to the neighbouring island of Pašman by a bridge across the Ždrelac passage. Among Ugljan’s main attractions is the fortress of St. Michael above Preko; nearby is also the islet of Galevac, known for its Franciscan monastery, while in Muline you can visit the remains of an ancient oil mill where the Liburnian olive oil was once produced.

TODAY IT IS CONSIDERED THE OLDEST PRESERVED CHURCH IN THE SETTLEMENT OF UGLJAN

The island’s special charm comes from its small stone churches. One of them was recently declared a cultural asset by the Ministry of Culture and Media of the Republic of Croatia. It is the Church of Saints Cosmas and Damian, located in Ljokine Cove, not far from the hamlet of Guduće, on the southwestern side of the island. This modest stone building stands right on the shore and is the oldest preserved church in the settlement of Ugljan: it is believed to date from the 11th or 12th century.

Besides its exceptional historical value, the Church of Saints Cosmas and Damian is also interesting because of the unusual legend that has accompanied it for centuries. According to the story, a merchant and sailor named Toricella was shipwrecked in the waters around Ugljan. He managed to save himself and swim to the shore in Ljokine Cove, and on that spot he decided to build a votive church. He dedicated it to Saints Cosmas and Damian, early Christian martyrs and physicians, in gratitude for his rescue.

THE ROOF OF THE SIMPLE LITTLE CHURCH WAS COVERED WITH BROKEN STONE SLABS

Although the shipwreck story cannot be historically confirmed, the name Toricella also appears in old documents. The little church is first mentioned on 6 August 1512 in the will of F. Toricella from Bergamo in Italy. In it he stipulated that a piece of land should be given for use to the priest who celebrates a sung Mass in the little church on the feast of Saints Cosmas and Damian. According to the interpretation of don Marko Dokoza, a priest who for years led tours of Ugljan’s little churches as part of Open Doors Days, Toricella was only later identified with the seafarer from the shipwreck legend.

The original church was a very simple, square stone building, 4.8 metres long and 2.8 metres wide. Its walls were about 80 centimetres thick, and at the rear it had a lowered semicircular apse. The roof was covered with broken stone slabs, and there were two small windows in the side walls. The interior had a half-barrel vault, while the simple architectural details reflected the modesty and age of the building.

PAINTINGS DEPICTING SAINTS COSMAS AND DAMIAN AND THE BLESSED VIRGIN MARY WITH THE CHILD

At the beginning of the 20th century the little church was significantly enlarged. A new nave, ten metres long and 3.8 metres wide, intended for gatherings of the faithful, was added to its front part. Today its interior contains an altar, pews and paintings depicting Saints Cosmas and Damian as well as the Blessed Virgin Mary with the Child. On the façade a small round window stands out, and above it a stone bell-gable with a bell made in the workshop of Jakov Cukrov in Split.

Saints Cosmas and Damian, to whom the church is dedicated, were twin brothers and physicians who helped the sick free of charge. Their feast day is celebrated on the 26th of September. For centuries that date held special significance for the inhabitants of Ugljan: according to records in the parish chronicle, numerous pilgrims from all the settlements on the island, as well as from the neighbouring areas, used to come to the little church on that day.

IN THE NEARBY HAMLET OF GUDUĆE YOU CAN ALSO SEE A UNIQUE MOSAIC BENCH

The tradition, of course, lives on today. Mass is still celebrated in the little church, during which blessings are invoked upon Ugljan sailors and ships all over the world. Thus this small place of worship has remained connected with the sea and seafarers, just as in the legend of its origin. The Church of Saints Cosmas and Damian on the island of Ugljan is also interesting as an excursion destination.

It is located in a peaceful cove, and a gravel road through a pine forest leads to it. In the nearby hamlet of Guduće you can also see an unusual mosaic bench created back in 2019 by the retired Božica Kliman, known as Boška. On its front side is a depiction of the Church of Saints Cosmas and Damian itself, along with a magical sunset, a squid and a lighthouse — colourful reminders of the islanders’ unbreakable connection with the sea and fishing.

World.title: New fee added to packages sent from outside EU from November
World.content:
From November 1, a handling fee of €2 will be added for each item of goods contained in a shipment ordered from online stores outside the European Union, regardless of the shipment's value.

"The calculation logic for the handling fee is indeed the same or similar to that of the customs duty on small consignments. The amount of the fee depends on the number of goods lines listed on the declaration. If we take the example of 100 pairs of jeans, which are identical goods, they can be entered on a single goods line on the customs declaration," Kaari Lainevool, service manager at the Tax and Customs Board's customs administration department, explained to ERR.

A customs duty of €3 applies to shipments worth up to €150. If the contents of a package has to be declared on three goods lines, for example, the total customs duty is €9 and the new handling fee is €6.

Customs duty on more expensive shipments depends on the goods, but the €2 handling fee will also be added for each goods line in these shipments.

Tõnu Väät, executive director of the Estonian E-Commerce Association, said the additional cost may discourage buyers from ordering cheap goods: "The same product that I used to order and that cost, for example, €6 – if I add €3 to that and another €2 from November, then it is no longer worth ordering."

He added that some Estonian retailers have already noticed an increase in sales figures following the introduction of the customs duty in July.

"For example, several electronics retailers selling phone chargers, headphones, phone cases, screen protectors and other similar products have said that their sales have increased by 10-20 percent in recent months," Väät explained.

However, customs statistics do not show how much people in Estonia have reduced their orders from outside the European Union.

The Tax and Customs Board said the volume of small consignments declared in Estonia fell by 80 percent in July and August. However, some packages are cleared through customs in other European Union member states and arrive in Estonia as intra-EU shipments. As a result, they are not reflected in Estonian customs statistics.

The new handling fee will cover the costs of checking shipments, including risk analysis and package inspections.

Depending on the online store, buyers may pay the handling fee either when completing their purchase or only when importing the goods. The decisive factor is the date of declaration: the fee will also apply to packages ordered or arriving in Estonia before November if the customs declaration is submitted on November 1 or later.

World.title: Retailers say electronic price tags will not lead to sudden price rises
World.content:
Supermarket chains in Estonia have said the increased use of electronic price tags, which reduce the need for paper, will not be used to suddenly increase prices during peak demand, despite customer concerns.

Observant customers have noticed electronic price tags in various grocery stores for some time now. Selver, for example, has introduced electronic tags for fruit, vegetables and bakery products.

"This certainly makes work more efficient and convenient, and you do not have to print and replace tags. At the same time, it has to be considered very carefully, because the investment is significant," said Selver communications manager Mariann Järvela.

Completely replacing paper tickets with electronic screen tags would cost millions of euros for a major retail chain.

Rimi supermarket chain said its smaller stores have made the switch already. The company's head of sales and business operations, Jelena Litvinovitš, said the investment has not paid off.

"Unfortunately, this technology really is still very, very expensive. To be honest, we are waiting to see whether it might become cheaper, but not yet. The risk is that if we do not find a solution in the coming years, the batteries will run out and then we will have to consider what to do with these price tags," she said.

Electronic price tags in Rimi supermarket. Source: ERR

Electronic tags can be changed in seconds, and customers are concerned prices will rise suddenly during peak demand.

For example, it is theoretically possible to take a packet of coffee from the shelf at one price, and then find it has risen at the checkout. Stores promise that this will not occur.

"I can confirm that there is no such risk at Rimi. It would certainly raise a lot of questions and negative emotions among customers. One of the reasons is that we have not found a good solution for how to change prices during the day and how to explain this to customers," Litvinovitš said.

"Yes, in theory it is possible and it would certainly bring greater profits. We know that it is used elsewhere in the world, but we ourselves have not found a good explanation or ways to do it," she added.

Grocery stores are not the only ones using automated solutions. For example, electronics retailer Euronics introduced electronic price tags in 2023, citing savings on labor costs. The company paid half a million euros for the tags three years ago.

"In the more distant future, we will probably reach a point where there are no paper price tags, but that is probably still some way off. In the near future, there are many advantages, but there are still quite a few disadvantages as well," said Nele Peil, head of the Estonian Traders Association.

Electronic price tags in Rimi supermarket. Source: ERR

World.title: Court rejects eastern border bunker procurement tender appeal
World.content:
The Supreme Court of Estonia on Monday rejected a company's appeal challenging the tender to procure concrete bunkers to be installed along Estonia's eastern border.

The court decided on Monday not to hear a cassation appeal by Nordic Shield Group AB, in which the company sought to challenge a tender organized by the Estonian Center for Defense Investments (RKIK) for the procurement of concrete bunkers.

RKIK's Baltic Defense Line project manager Armin Siilivask told ERR that Monday's court decision means the procurement process can now proceed.

"Now that the court has made its decision, our aim is to continue with the procurement according to the planned schedule, so that we can, if possible, reach the signing of a contract as early as March next year. To do this, the necessary procurement procedures must be carried out: conducting bidding rounds, holding negotiations, carrying out checks and evaluations and, if everything goes smoothly, signing a contract with a suitable bidder," Siilivask said.

Nordic Shield Group's appeal focused on the tender's production quality standard and the required ISO certificate.

RKIK said the certificate submitted by Nordic Shield Group did not meet the requirements set out in the tender conditions.

Estonia's aim is to install 600 concrete bunkers along its eastern border by the end of 2027 as part of the Baltic Defense Line. RKIK announced a tender for the procurement of the bunkers in 2025.

World.title: Elering launches tender for €30M crisis management center
World.content:
The center will be built adjacent to Elering's head office on Kadaka tee in Tallinn, and must meet state defense security requirements. It is expected to be completed within two years.

Hannes Kont, head of Elering's crisis preparedness unit, said that due to the changed security situation, Elering has launched a highly extensive crisis preparedness program, within the framework of which investments are being made in infrastructure security. The establishment of a new crisis management center forms one part of this.

"We must ensure that system dispatchers can monitor and control the situation via secure data channels at any given moment. Looking at what is happening in Ukraine and at the threat assessments issued by the state, the necessary level of security has become considerably more precise and higher. We must do this in a much more secure environment than before," Kont said.

"What those technological solutions are, how we at any moment have a literally microsecond-level overview of the state of both the electricity and gas infrastructure — those details we will certainly not disclose," Kont went on, citing security concerns.

Kont said Elering wants to conclude the construction contract by the beginning of next year at the latest. Tender participants must submit a preliminary bid with a deadline of 20 months. "Naturally we are in a hurry, but we will see what the market offers. Our ambition is to sign the contract by the start of 2027, which means the crisis management center could be completed by the end of 2028 or the start of 2029."

Elering is a state-owned transmission operator which runs Estonia's electricity and gas transmission systems. Security concerns have driven investment in critical infrastructure. The center is part of a wider crisis preparedness program.

World.title: US act 30 Seconds to Mars to give first Estonian concert in over 10 years
World.content:
American rock act Thirty Seconds to Mars are to perform in Estonia next spring.

The group, whose nucleus is brothers Jared and Shannon Leto, will play the Unibet Arena Kvartal in Tallinn on May 22.

This will be their third appearance in Tallinn, though the first in over a decade – the band were last in concert here in 2014.

The May 2027 performance forms part of the "A Beautiful Lie vs This Is War" concert tour, featuring songs from the band's two albums of the same names.

Tickets go on sale on Friday, October 30 at 10 a.m., with presales for members of promoter Baltic Live Agency's Concert Club able to make purchases a day earlier.

Founded in 1998 in Los Angles, Thirty Seconds to Mars is known for songs such as "The Kill (Bury Me)," "From Yesterday" and "Kings and Queens." The band combines alternative rock with electronic elements in its music and has released six studio albums over the course of its career.

2005's "A Beautiful Lie" brought worldwide fame, and the band has sold more than 15 million albumsIt also holds a Guinness World Record for 300 shows in a single album cycle.

Allegations of sexual misconduct on the part of Jared Leto, who is also an actor, appeared in the media in summer 2025 though no police report or formal complaint has been filed in connection with the accusations, which Leto denies.

World.title: Minister: Defense plan decisions must be reviewed, light fighter jets eyed
World.content:
This includes weighing up the procurement of light fighter jets for the Estonian Defense Forces (EDF).

The latest status of the national defense development plan was that it had reached the Government Office for approval, but you nonetheless found some changes needed to be made. Is that right?

As far as I know, the 10-year national defense development plan was issued by the Ministry of Defense back in the spring, if not early spring. And during that time, there have indeed been some changes in air defense, which had already begun to emerge in the war in Ukraine last year; the picture is now likely clearer, and for that reason alone. This is not a question of my having reviewed anything, but rather the Defense Forces as a whole have become better informed, and some things have also developed further based on the example of the war in Ukraine. So these changes stem from that.

The latest status of the national defense development plan was that it had reached the Government Office for approval, but you nonetheless found some changes needed to be made. Is that right? As I understand it, the plan was in fairly final form at the Government Office, awaiting approval alongside the state budget strategy (RES), and upon becoming minister, drawing on the commander's advice, you reopened it and saw things needed to be added and changed?

As far as I know, the 10-year national defense development plan was issued by the Ministry of Defense back in the spring, if not early spring. And during that time, there have indeed been some changes in air defense, which had already begun to emerge in the war in Ukraine last year; the picture is now likely clearer, and for that reason alone. This is not a question of my having reviewed anything, but rather the Defense Forces as a whole have become better informed, and some things have also developed further based on the example of the war in Ukraine. So these changes stem from that.

So, keeping the shipping lanes in the Gulf of Finland open and procuring additional air defense capabilities – most recently, you spoke about the need to acquire light fighter jets. Is that right?

For us this is not just the shipping lanes in the Gulf of Finland, but the sea routes toward the west as a whole. The Gulf of Finland is actually a secondary issue in that respect. But without these maritime connections, we would certainly die out very quickly – 80 percent of our trade currently takes place by sea, and the same is true for the Finns. So we must look at this as a whole together with our allies, to ensure that these connections remain under our control at all times.

Now, as for air defense and air-to-air defense, meaning those same jet aircraft, what Russia has come up with over the past year is essentially cheap cruise missiles, or jet-powered drones. And one of the most effective means currently in use against them is aircraft, jet aircraft. Whether we take the route of acquiring light jets such as the Hawk, L-39 or something similar, or instead look toward unmanned jets, is another matter. But I do think we should consider how to bring our air-to-air defense capability into play, so to speak. However, resources are limited, and we have to consider what we would have to sacrifice to do all of this.

In your assessment, is acquiring light fighter jets a genuinely realistic prospect at present? Are you proposing that this be added to the national defense development plan and that the necessary funding be found?

I think that this is realistic. But it is not only realistic, it may also be needed. How else are we to counter such threats? However, to do that, we will first need to review the broader air defense picture. What do we want to develop there, what do we have, and how would these aircraft, however many there might be, fit into it? It also depends on the circumstances: imagine that we are in a full-scale war. What airfields or runways would we be able to use for this? Maybe at some point we would no longer have them, so then the question arises of where the aircraft would take off from, or whether we would have to use something else, some other locations. And finally, how many of these aircraft should there be, at what point would we use them, and where would they operate? All of this is not yet entirely clear to me.

When did the commander of the Defense Forces provide his additional input on the national defense development plan?

I think it was a few weeks ago. I cannot say exactly right now. But it was during my time as minister, meaning within the past month. And it was sent to the minister of defense, not the Government Office.

And what did he recommend? Is that a matter between the two of you, or can you make it public?

That is actually where the issue of jets comes from, at least in part. But it also touched on other matters.

And now, as I understand it, you are due to give a presentation on this to the National Defense Council, which reports to the president?

Yes, I will be discussing these issues at the National Defense Council. Not in the form of proposals yet, but I will raise the issues we are working on. That said, I am not ready to present concrete proposals.

When might those concrete proposals be ready?

I really cannot say right now, but sometime this year.

World.title: EKRE wants to reduce election deposit for candidates
World.content:
EKRE's parliamentary group wants to reduce the deposit political parties pay to participate in elections from €946 to €220 per candidate and from €118,250 to €27,500 for a full candidate list.

EKRE believes the current amount is too high and has put forward a proposal to change the law.

"Under the current rules, the deposit per candidate is equal to the monthly minimum wage in the year the elections are announced, which as of October 2026 is €946. Since a party may field up to 125 candidates, submitting a full candidate list requires a payment of €118,250. Such an amount is an excessive obstacle for new and small political forces that lack state funding and accumulated financial reserves. This effectively restricts opportunities to participate in elections and reduces political competition," the proposal states.

The bill submitted by EKRE seeks to decouple the deposit from the monthly minimum wage and links it to the subsistence threshold for a person living alone or the first member of a family, as agreed in the State Budget Act under the Social Welfare Act.

"The monthly minimum wage is determined by labor market and wage policy considerations, and its increase is not linked to the conditions for participating in elections, meaning that the deposit also increases without a deliberate decision by the legislator," the party believes.

"The subsistence threshold is significantly lower and more stable: since January 1, 2026, it has been €220 per month. As a result of the amendment, the deposit would decrease from €946 to €220 per candidate and from €118,250 to €27,500 for a full candidate list, or by approximately 77 percent. This would preserve the deposit's deterrent effect against clearly unjustified candidate lists while ensuring that new political forces are not placed at a disadvantage."

However, while still in office as Chancellor of Justice, Ülle Madise said there was no reason to consider the election deposit disproportionate.

She explained that the fee's main purpose is to avoid a situation where too many voters are left without representation because they voted for a list or candidate who does not pass the election threshold and cannot enter the Riigikogu.

World.title: Experts look to math teaching changes to ease Estonia's engineer shortage
World.content:
Despite growing interest in engineering, Estonia faces a shortage of more than 800 young engineers in the next decade as 40 percent retire. Changes to math teaching may help.

Interest in engineering has grown sharply, but according to OSKA, the Estonian Qualifications Authority's labor market forecasting system, the sector will still be short more than 800 young engineers over the next decade as 40 percent retire. There are no quick solutions, but efforts are being made to alleviate the shortage by changing how mathematics is taught.

Interest in studying at Tallinn University of Technology's (TalTech) School of Engineering has increased by 25 percent over the past three years. According to Fjodor Sergejev, dean of the School of Engineering, students are enrolling in a variety of programs, from energy and construction to mechanical and industrial engineering, but there will not be enough graduates to fill the gap.

"We need replacement workers because many engineers from previous generations are retiring and need to be replaced, but we also need to ensure the development of the sector, and for that we need even more engineers. Even the substantial demographic support we currently have is unfortunately unable to meet all our needs, because the replacement demand is indeed very high, in some fields even numbering in the thousands."

Cathy-Liis Põlluveer, president of the Estonian association of engineers (Eesti Inseneride Liit), also acknowledged the shortage: "We currently have a situation where it depends somewhat on the field, but when an engineer, particularly an experienced engineer, is being sought and a recruitment competition is held, there is practically no queue of applicants or diversity among candidates. Instead, engineers are being sought like needles in a haystack."

According to Anneli Leemet, an analyst at OSKA, demand will grow most for electrical and energy engineers, mechanical engineers and electronics engineers. Leemet said the issue is not only meeting the numerical demand but ensuring engineers have a diverse range of skills.

Cathy-Liis Põlluveer. Source: Personal collection.

One possible solution experts see is strengthening mathematics education in basic schools (grades 1–9) — making mathematics teaching more relevant to everyday life, more integrated with other subjects, and delivered in a way that supports all children's motivation to learn. According to Tiina Kraav, a lecturer in mathematics education at the University of Tartu, there are no quick solutions, but mathematics teaching is being continuously developed.

"Making mathematics more interesting to learn, making mathematics learning more visible, making mathematical thinking more visible to students, making mathematics learning more creative, improving how problem-solving skills are taught in the classroom, getting students to talk about what they think and how they think when solving mathematics problems – all of this will certainly help in the longer term," Kraav said.

Põlluveer believes subjects that help connect natural sciences and mathematics could be beneficial.

Priit Laats, a teacher of technology education, arts and technology at Tartu Raatuse School, confirmed that schools are increasingly moving toward theme-based learning: "For example, in the first stage of basic school, there is integrated learning. It is theme-based, with Estonian, mathematics, nature studies and creative subjects all together all the time. In fact, other grades should already be structured in a similar way. But again, who is going to develop all of this? It is a huge amount of work. If I take how I, in turn, support mathematics, we introduce 3D modeling as early as fourth grade: the spatial world, shapes, symbols, symmetry, reflection, all the faces and planes – it is all mathematics all the time, and we do this right through ninth grade."

OSKA will publish a new cross-sector study of labor and skills needs in engineering in early November, which will show that competition for hybrid competencies is increasing in the labor market. This means engineers must have in-depth specialist knowledge combined with digital, data analysis, artificial intelligence, business or management skills.

World.title: Mbappe dropped by Chinese brands for ‘offending national sentiments’
World.content:
Beijing – Kylian Mbappe was dropped Tuesday by two major brands in China after a video circulated online in which the French football superstar apparently joked about former leader Mao Zedong.

In China jokes about Mao, the country’s founding leader who died in 1976, are considered disrespectful and remain a social taboo.

“Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments,” drinks giant Dongpeng said in a statement, adding that “with immediate effect we are terminating all cooperation with Kylian Mbappe”.

Adverts showing AI-generated images of the 27-year-old France captain drinking a Dongpeng sports drink were regularly shown in China during this year’s World Cup.

Mengniu, China’s largest dairy producer, also cut ties with the Real Madrid forward, who until this incident was hugely popular among Chinese fans with millions of followers on social media.

Mbappe is fondly nicknamed “Guigui”, the Chinese translation of “Turtle”, due to his popularity as a character in a Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles meme.

“With immediate effect our company is terminating all cooperation with Kylian Mbappe,” Mengniu said in a statement.

“Mengniu firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any words or actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people,” it added.

The announcements came after a video emerged online with Mbappe saying that the funniest internet meme he had seen was of his face photo-shopped onto that of “some guy — I think he’s a Chinese dictator”.

This was an apparent reference to a meme of Mbappe superimposed on an image of Mao, one of several using the footballer’s face and other historical figures.

The authenticity of the video could not immediately be verified by AFP Fact Check.

“Dongpeng Beverage ends cooperation with Mbappe” was the top-trending topic on Chinese social media site Weibo.

One Weibo user said that the “extremely serious wrong remarks… crossed the red line. They are completely unacceptable”.

Others urged Dongpeng to remove Mbappe’s image from their energy drink bottles.

Dongqiudi, one of China’s biggest online football outlets, said in a statement on Monday evening that Mbappe’s remarks were “offensive to China and the Chinese people” and “have hurt the feelings of Chinese football fans and the Chinese people”.

– China furore –

Mbappe in September addressed a previous meme depicting him as a military dictator, in an interview with French sports newspaper L’Equipe.

“There’s a part of it that’s funny. You can tell that, for some people, it’s all in good fun. But there is another part that’s a bit less funny because of the damage such people have caused throughout history,” he said.

“Being compared to individuals who murder others, or who have brought misery to millions upon millions of people — well, I don’t think I’ve ever done anything like that in my life,” he said.

The furore in China came a day after Mbappe lost out to Harry Kane for the Ballon d’Or, the most prestigious individual award in football.

Global sports stars that have commented on sensitive topics such as Taiwan, Tibet and Hong Kong have previously caused controversy in China and been dumped by sponsors there.

Former NBA player Dwight Howard referred to Taiwan as a country in 2023 as he appeared in a video with the island’s vice president and current president Lai Ching-te, sparking fury on Chinese social media.

Beijing claims Taiwan is part of its territory and has threatened to use force to bring it under its control.

Houston Rockets general manager Daryl Morey posted a tweet in 2019 supporting Hong Kong protests, leading to China suspending sponsorship deals with the NBA and pulling games off Chinese television for a year.

World.title: Cavs edge T’Wolves in overtime despite superb Edwards
World.content:
Los Angeles – The Cleveland Cavaliers ended the Minnesota Timberwolves’ perfect start to the NBA season, winning 127-125 in an overtime thriller despite 47 points from Anthony Edwards.

Donovan Mitchell and James Harden led the scoring for the victorious Cavs, with 26 and 19 points apiece, as Cleveland moved to 2-1.

“Tough win for us, especially early in the season,” said Harden, who added four rebounds and nine assists.

The Timberwolves, having won their opening three games, led for much of the night, with a 15-point advantage in the first half.

Edwards, only cleared to play late after being listed as questionable with a right knee injury, had made an electric start, with 11 points in the first quarter.

But the Cavaliers rallied to pull level in the third quarter, and then had to come from behind again after slipping to a seven-point deficit in the fourth.

Harden’s driving floater with 10 seconds remaining tied the game, and a blocked Edwards layup with four seconds left sent it to overtime at 113-113.

With just a minute left in overtime, Edwards tied the game again with a trey so close to the arc that a video replay was required.

But Mitchell re-established Cleveland’s lead with a go-ahead midrange jumper, and when Minnesota’s Jonathan Kuminga missed a free throw with 30 seconds left, the Cavaliers pulled clear.

Harden made two more free throws, leaving the Timberwolves requiring three points, but Edwards’ clutch effort bounced off the rim.

Peyton Watson poured in two more free throws for Cleveland to bury the contest.

“We made a lot of mistakes on both ends of the basketball in that first half… second half, we did a better job,” said Harden.

Elsewhere, the Oklahoma City Thunder improved to 4-0 with a hard-fought 125-114 win over the Phoenix Suns.

Ajay Mitchell led the scoring with a career-high 30, supported by Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, who added 26.

“This league is about winning games, and that’s all that matters,” said Gilgeous-Alexander.

“We were just ready to go. Guys were ready to go. Guys were ready to step up,” added the reigning NBA Most Valuable Player.

– ‘Perfect night’ –

The Houston Rockets also stayed perfect with a 120-110 win over the Atlanta Hawks.

It is their first 4-0 start since 2014, with star Kevin Durant rested for the entire fourth quarter in an ultimately comfortable win.

Giannis Antetokounmpo recorded his first triple-double with new team Miami even as the Heat (0-4) suffered a 113-109 loss to the Dallas Mavericks.

Antetokounmpo, a two-time league MVP who left the Milwaukee Bucks this summer, scored 29 points with 14 rebounds and 11 assists.

Mavericks teen star Cooper Flagg also scored 29, with 11 assists, six rebounds and a career-high five steals.

The Grizzlies also improved to 4-0 with a 110-105 win over the Utah Jazz, while Brandon Miller scored 39 points as the Charlotte Hornets beat the Washington Wizards 110-103.

And the Golden State Warriors earned their first victory of the season with a 134-114 triumph over the Denver Nuggets.

Stephen Curry made 8-of-8 field goal attempts for 24 points.

“Just staying patient. We’ve been working on some offensive approach where I know I get a lot of attention, trying not to force things,” he said.

“I didn’t know it was going to be a perfect night like that, but glad it all came together.”

World.title: Tech firms track Wall St rally on mixed day for Asian markets
World.content:
Hong Kong – Tech firms rallied Tuesday following a healthy run-up on Wall Street as traders welcomed AI titan Anthropic’s IPO filing that revived optimism over the sector after stuttering in the second half of the year.

However, the main gains were concentrated in South Korea and Japan, with other Asian stock markets putting in a mixed performance as traders gear up for a slew of key earnings and central bank decisions this week.

In submitting its plans to list its shares, Anthropic, one of the world’s leading artificial intelligence companies, reported first-half revenue surged about 1,300 percent year-on-year, but also flagged safety risks.

The sale is seen as a crucial test of whether the AI boom can deliver profits, and a disappointing reception could dent enthusiasm further, with traders already questioning the vast sums invested in the sector as well as several companies’ financial positions.

The filing lays out risks specific to an industry that has faced a string of reports in recent months of AI systems behaving in unexpected and harmful ways.

“If the use of our AI models results in harm, whether through use by malicious actors or misuse by other third parties, or if our model guardrails or safeguards fail to prevent such misuse,” the firm’s business could suffer, it said.

Still, Wall Street-listed tech firms rallied, pulling the Nasdaq and S&P 500 higher along with the Dow.

Seoul briefly jumped more than four percent, thanks to strong gains in chipmakers SK hynix and Samsung, while Tokyo added around two percent on the back of spikes in Kioxia, Advantest and SoftBank.

“Sentiment towards technology has improved as investors assess Anthropic’s IPO filing at the start of a week packed with corporate earnings and the Federal Reserve’s rate decision,” wrote Fiona Cincotta at FOREX.com.

“Anthropic revealed steep losses and impressive revenue growth in its filing… laying out ambitions to build AI systems capable of reshaping the global economy, even at a high cost.

“The listing plan remains in place, even as other firms have stepped back owing to recent market volatility.”

There were also gains in Sydney, Taipei and Manila, but Hong Kong, Shanghai, Singapore, Wellington and Jakarta all retreated.

Investors are now awaiting earnings this week from Magnificent Seven members Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon as well as SK hynix and Samsung.

The Fed is expected to keep interest rates on hold when it announces its decision on Wednesday, though CME Group’s FedWatch tool says there is a 70 percent chance of a hike when it meets in December.

Oil prices extended Monday’s drop as senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan held talks with Iran in an attempt to stop the Middle East war from reigniting, with Tehran saying the discussions were “very good”.

Officials from the three Mecca pact countries flew to Iran as part of efforts to “de-escalate between the parties to the current crisis”, a Saudi foreign ministry statement said.

The talks followed warnings by the United States, Iran and Israel that hostilities could restart in the eight-month war, with some observers suggesting the period between next Tuesday’s US midterm elections and the new Congress taking office was particularly fraught.

Also in view are elections in Israel, where voters will deliver their verdict on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the country’s rightward drift.

World.title: Jay-Z to perform at Super Bowl LXI halftime show: NFL
World.content:
Los Angeles – Rapper Jay-Z will perform at the Super Bowl LXI halftime show this February in Los Angeles, the NFL announced Monday.

Jay-Z’s Roc Nation entertainment company has produced the star-packed Super Bowl halftime show each year since 2020, selecting the headliners, but the hip-hop mogul has not previously performed himself at the event.

“When we first reached an agreement with Roc Nation to produce the show, I had just one request: that Jay-Z take the stage himself one day, whenever the moment felt right to him,” NFL commissioner Roger Goodell said in a joint statement.

“I couldn’t be more excited for fans around the world to experience the artistry, creativity and cultural impact he will bring to the Super Bowl stage.”

The announcement did not specify whether Jay-Z would be the sole headliner.

It came after Jay-Z — who is married to pop megastar Beyonce — performed two shows last weekend at Los Angeles’ SoFi Stadium, which will serve as the venue for the Super Bowl on February 14.

Those gigs served as the culmination for a year-long tour celebrating the 30th anniversary of his debut album “Reasonable Doubt.”

“From ‘Reasonable Doubt’ to standing on the Super Bowl halftime stage, this has been a journey,” said Jay-Z, whose real name is Shawn Carter.

“Thirty years of music, work, and culture on the world’s biggest stage. This run continues to be a dream come true.”

In an indication of the level of star power Jay-Z could potentially bring with him to the halftime spectacular, he was joined on-stage in Los Angeles by John Legend, DJ Khaled, Dr Dre and Snoop Dogg.

World.title: Jordan strikes militant groups in Syria after church attack
World.content:
Amman – The Jordanian military said it had struck “terrorist organisations” in neighbouring Syria on Monday in retaliation for a deadly jihadist attack on a church last week, hours after authorities arrested three men they accused of the killings.

It said air force jets had “destroyed several terrorist positions” and killed and wounded “numerous members” of groups linked to the perpetrators of the church attack.

Syrian authorities reported civilian casualties from the raids, with health officials in Daraa province saying six people, including three children and a woman, were killed.

Syria’s civil defence agency reported seven deaths in total, six people in Daraa and one in neighbouring Sweida province.

On Friday, gunmen killed nine people during a funeral service at the Greek Orthodox St George’s Church in the village of Hammoud in Karak governorate, southern Jordan.

Karak is home to a significant Christian community in Muslim-majority Jordan, where Christians make up between two and three percent of the population.

Major General Abdullah al-Maaytah, Jordan’s director of public security, on Monday named the three detained suspects as Hazza Zaidan Mohammed, Meshal Zaidan Mohammed and Ahmad Sami Hussein.

The trio, two of them brothers and the other related by marriage, were cornered at an abandoned house where they had barricaded themselves inside and opened fire on security forces.

“All three terrorists have been injured. They have been taken to hospital and are still receiving treatment,” Maaytah told a press conference.

– ‘We will show them’ –

One of the suspects was in critical condition, Jordan’s state broadcaster Al-Mamlaka reported. There were no casualties among the security forces, it added.

“This country must remain an oasis of security and stability, and we affirm that Jordan will remain impervious to anyone who dares to challenge it,” Maaytah said.

Under Jordanian law, murder is punishable by death by hanging.

A number of weapons and a large quantity of ammunition were seized from the three suspects, the Public Security Directorate said.

Jordan’s King Abdullah II said in a post on X that security forces “chased them to the very end”.

“We vowed the terrorists would not escape punishment, and no proponent of dark ideologies that divide Jordanians will be tolerated,” he wrote.

Earlier, the king visited wounded victims of the church attack in hospital, dressed in military fatigues and carrying a pistol on his hip.

“We will show them,” he vowed.

Interior Minister Mazen al-Faraya told Al-Mamlaka on Monday that the attackers were all Jordanians and “had been holed up in a building in one of the villages near the site of the attack”.

“There is no indication of any external contacts or collaboration with foreign parties,” he said.

Government communications minister Mohammad al-Momani said “we stand ready and will strike with an iron fist, without mercy or leniency, against anyone who attempts to undermine Jordan’s security”.

Attacks on houses of worship in Jordan are rare. In 2016 an attack in Karak targeted a security centre and police patrols, leaving 10 people dead.

On Friday, Prime Minister Jafar Hassan ordered a three-day period of national mourning for the victims of the church attack, with flags to be flown at half-mast over government and public institutions.

Eight of the nine victims were laid to rest on Sunday next to the church in a funeral that drew a huge crowd amid a large security presence, AFP images showed.

The ninth person, Mohammed al-Qasous, was buried in south Amman on Monday.

World.title: Kane beats Yamal and Mbappe to taste Ballon d’Or glory
World.content:
London – Harry Kane became England’s first Ballon d’Or winner in 25 years in his native city of London on Monday, beating Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe.

Alexia Putellas claimed the women’s prize for a third time to extend Spain’s domination of the award, thanks to her role in leading Barcelona to last season’s Champions League before moving to London City Lionesses.

The first ever Ballon d’Or ceremony on English soil got off to an inauspicious start as the London traffic caused a delay of nearly an hour, with many of the star names arriving late.

But there was a happy ending for the hometown hero as Kane collected the crowning glory of his career to date, becoming the first Englishman to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001.

The 33-year-old Bayern Munich forward struck a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for club and country last season, propelling the German giants to a league and cup double.

He also scored six times as England finished third at the World Cup.

“I love to represent my country and to bring this trophy back to them and have an English winner I think is something that’s really, really special, especially here in London,” Kane told AFP. “What a crazy night and I’m really, really happy.”

Despite being England and Tottenham’s all-time record goalscorer, Kane’s medal collection is limited to German domestic triumphs.

He was on the losing side for Spurs in the 2019 Champions League final against Liverpool and twice tasted bitter defeat in the final of the European Championship with England.

But joining Bayern in 2023 and his remarkable goalscoring consistency have earned him the highest individual award in football.

“Making the move to Bayern Munich was a big step in my career,” Kane told AFP earlier. “Some people saw it as a risk but for me it was always about improving and seeing if I could get better around the team-mates, the team, the club and it has pushed me onto another level.

“Being a number nine for Bayern and England you are expected to score goals and to do that the number of times I did last year is something I’m really proud of,” he added.

– Putellas back on top –

The winner in 2021 and 2022, Putellas’s third Ballon d’Or caps her return to the top of the women’s game after an anterior cruciate ligament injury derailed her rise four years ago.

Putellas succeeds Spain team-mate Aitana Bonmati, the winner the past three years whose season was quashed by a leg break.

“This is a consequence of all that we achieved last season,” said Putellas.

“I am really grateful for having been (at Barcelona) 14 seasons as a player, it is something incredible. It was like a perfect story.”

Yamal made the boldest fashion statement of the contenders with a pink flower on the front of his black suit.

The Barcelona winger scooped up the first award of the night for young talent of the year for the third consecutive time.

But the 19-year-old fell short of becoming the youngest ever Ballon d’Or winner, finishing third, after he failed to produce his best form during Spain’s World Cup success.

Mbappe finished second but his wait to win the Ballon d’Or goes on despite being the top scorer in the World Cup, Champions League and La Liga as his goals did not lead to collective triumphs for France or Real Madrid.

Luis de la Fuente beat out Paris Saint-Germain’s Luis Enrique and Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta to be named men’s coach of the year after leading Spain to World Cup glory.

“This is recognition for a job very well done over many years,” De la Fuente told AFP. “I believe Spanish football, both in terms of coaching and the game itself, serves as an example of excellent youth development, which ultimately paves the way for future success.”

Barcelona’s Pere Romeu scooped the prize for women’s coach of the year.

Paris Saint-Germain missed out on any of the main individual awards despite winning a second consecutive Champions League, but did have the consolation of men’s club of the year.

Spanish duo Unai Simon and Cata Coll were named best men’s and women’s goalkeeper.

World.title: Australia warns of ‘unprecedented’ AI threat
World.content:
Sydney – Artificial intelligence poses an “unprecedented” threat as foreign governments turn it loose to hack computer networks and critical infrastructure, Australia’s cyber security agency warned on Tuesday.

The Australian Signals Directorate said rapidly advancing artificial intelligence models could be of huge benefit if harnessed for good, even using some AI tools to compile its own annual “cyber threat” report.

But recent months had also shown how AI was helping criminals and state-sponsored hackers launch attacks at “greater scale than ever before”, the directorate said in the report.

“AI has been the defining force in the cyber threat landscape over the past year, allowing malicious actors to find vulnerabilities faster and exploit them at unprecedented scale, speed and sophistication,” the report read.

“In recent weeks, new threats have emerged from the unintended actions of AI agents and model testing.”

Global worries about the power of advanced AI tools are mounting after a string of hacking incidents involving models from leading developers such as OpenAI and Anthropic.

The report documented a stark increase in cyber security incidents.

The Australian Signals Directorate issued more than 4,400 warnings about potentially malicious activity over the past year — an 80 percent increase compared to the prior 12 months.

“State-sponsored cyber actors continued to target Australian organisations primarily to gain access to sensitive or non-public information.

“This activity extends beyond government networks, and includes critical infrastructure entities, private businesses and individuals.”

The report said hackers linked to China, Russia and North Korea had targeted Australia or its allies in recent times.

Defence Minister Richard Marles said the nation could not ignore the AI revolution.

“AI is here and it’s real. People need to engage,” he told reporters.

“There’s no turning the clock back in relation to that. Malicious actors are using AI to find vulnerabilities in systems.”

Marles urged Australians to update their computers and “harden their systems”.

Governments and firms have in recent days been rushing to fix critical flaws in a programming language that runs a large share of the world’s websites.

The vulnerability was found using a powerful model from OpenAI.

World.title: NBA inks deal with Kalshi and Polymarket, citing safeguards
World.content:
Los Angeles – The NBA on Monday announced commercial partnerships with Kalshi and Polymarket that the basketball league said will help safeguard against illegal activity on the wildly popular online prediction markets.

Kalshi and Polymarket will be officially designated the league’s “preferred prediction market exchanges,” and will be able to use NBA marketing materials for their promotions.

In return, the deal gives the NBA control over what specific trades the websites can offer, and obliges the companies to share information “relating to investigations and suspicious trading.”

It comes as prediction markets have exploded in popularity, benefiting from looser regulations that allow them currently to operate nationwide.

They are technically distinct from traditional sports betting, as there is no central sportsbook that sets odds. Instead, users place monetary wagers directly against one another via online exchanges.

Some states have questioned the difference. New York attorney general Letitia James this summer sued Kalshi, accusing it of running an illegal gambling operation.

Individual NBA stars including four-time NBA champion LeBron James and Giannis Antetokounmpo already have endorsement deals with Polymarket and Kalshi respectively.

Victor Wembanyama has been an outspoken critic, calling it “very sad to see some players promoting” sports gambling.

The NBA has been hit by multiple illegal gambling scandals in recent years.

In October 2025, Miami Heat guard Terry Rozier was among those arrested in a far-ranging FBI probe into illegal gambling.

Rozier, who has denied wrongdoing, was accused of providing inside information on injuries and game absences to bettors. He allegedly told co-conspirators he would exit early with a supposed injury from a March 2023 game when he was with the Charlotte Hornets.

This June, former Milwaukee Bucks player Malik Beasley was indicted on illegal gambling charges. In one example, Beasley is alleged to have informed a former teammate that he intended to underperform with respect to rebounding in a game.

Under the new deal, the NBA would be able to prevent markets that are especially susceptible to manipulation.

“Protecting the integrity of the game is our top priority,” Scott Kaufman-Ross, NBA head of media distribution and partnerships, said in a statement.

“As this category develops, we believe it is important to work constructively with regulators and operators to help ensure that appropriate safeguards are in place.”

The deal includes explicit prohibitions against league and team personnel trading on NBA-related markets.

The NBA also expanded its existing agreement with sportsbook partner DraftKings to include prediction markets.

Prediction markets have drawn broader controversy over allegations that insiders have used privileged information to make fortunes wagering on politics and even war.

World.title: 10L people, 20k vehicles, Rs 10k cr loss: Why traders' body want Rahul's Nov 1 rally postponed
World.content:
Delhi traders have urged Rahul Gandhi to postpone the November 1 rally, warning of potential losses of Rs 10,000 crore

10 lakh people, up to 20,000 vehicles

21 markets at risk

'We hear you': Rahul Gandhi

Traders reported losses after Oct 10 protest

The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) has urged Congress leader Rahul Gandhi to postpone the partyâs proposed November 1 rally at Delhiâs Ramlila Maidan, warning that it could disrupt business across 21 major wholesale and retail markets during the peak festive shopping season and cause losses of up to Rs 10,000 crore.The tradersâ body has asked Congress to defer the rally until November 10, after Bhai Dooj, or shift it to an alternative venue away from commercial areas. The Congress has claimed that the rally could draw 10 lakh people.In a letter to Rahul Gandhi, a copy of which was also sent to Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal raised concerns about possible barricading and road closures on October 31 and November 1. He said traders were worried about whether customers would be able to reach shops during the crucial festive period, news agency PTI reported.According to the CTI, a gathering of 10 lakh people could bring between 15,000 and 20,000 vehicles into Delhi. These could include 10,000 to 12,000 buses and 5,000 to 7,000 smaller vehicles, such as cars, minibuses and tempo travellers.The organisation questioned where these vehicles would be parked, claiming there was no authorised parking facility for even 200 vehicles in the immediate vicinity of Ramlila Maidan.It also warned that congestion could spill into the narrow lanes of Old Delhi, many of which are only 10 to 12 feet wide. A single truck getting stuck in these lanes could trigger traffic jams lasting several hours, it said.The CTI identified 21 markets that could be affected by the rally, including Chandni Chowk, Sadar Bazaar, Khari Baoli, Bhagirath Palace, Chawri Bazaar, Kashmere Gate, Karol Bagh, Daryaganj, Paharganj, Jama Masjid and Lajpat Rai Market.The body cited the October 10 event at Jantar Mantar, claiming that a gathering of around 3,000 to 4,000 people had disrupted movement across central Delhi and caused traders losses of Rs 3,000 crore.It projected that the November 1 rally could bring commercial activity across Old Delhi to a standstill, with losses potentially reaching Rs 10,000 crore.The CTI has proposed Burari Ground or Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium as alternative venues if the rally cannot be postponed. It has urged the Congress leadership to consider the concerns of traders and minimise disruption to business during the festive season.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi expressed solidarity with Delhiâs traders, alleging that government restrictions had disrupted business by shutting metro services, sealing roads and locking down the capital.Linking the disruption to his allegations of âvote choriâ, Rahul demanded that Prime Minister Narendra Modi sack Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, whom he referred to as âAccused No. 4â.âTo every trader in Delhi: We love you and hear you. The Govt shut the metro, sealed our roads and locked down our capital. With a stolen vote nothing is safe - your shop, your savings, your childrenâs future. Tell Modi to sack accused no. 4, Gyanesh Kumar and the protests will stop in 30 seconds,â Rahul said.Delhi traders sought Prime Minister Narendra Modiâs intervention over losses allegedly caused by the October 10 protest called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), demanding compensation from those responsible for the disruption.The Automotive Parts Merchants Association (Regd.), Delhi, said customers stayed away from markets for four to five days before and after the protest call, resulting in heavy business losses.The association had said October, November and December were crucial for traders because of the festive season, including Navratri, Dhanteras and Diwali. It warned that repeated disruptions during this period could threaten the livelihoods of shopkeepers and their employees.The trade body called for a transparent assessment of the losses and sought full compensation from the principal organisers and participants responsible for the disruption, arguing that traders should not bear the financial burden.It said shop earnings were used to support tradersâ families and employees, pay rent, fund childrenâs education and cover medical expenses for elderly parents.The association also flagged the absence of basic emergency arrangements, including ambulances, fire services and first aid, at protests, warning that such gaps could lead to serious accidents.

World.title: Centre to train 10,000 healthcare workers in drug de-addiction by 2029
World.content:
NEW DELHI: With the Centre targeting a drug-free India by 2029, the health ministry has launched a nationwide capacity-building programme to train 10,000 healthcare professionals in the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of substance use disorders, including addiction to alcohol, opioids and other drugs.

Union health minister J P Nadda launched the programme on Monday under the Vision Document on Narcotic Control 2026-2029, stressing that tackling substance abuse requires coordinated action by healthcare, social welfare and law enforcement agencies. The ministry aims to train 2,000 personnel in the current financial year, followed by 3,000 in 2027-28 and 5,000 in 2028-29.

The programme will be implemented through six central government institutions under the Drug De-addiction Programme, with the National Drug Dependence Treatment Centre (NDDTC), AIIMS, serving as the coordinating centre.

The other institutions are NIMHANS, Bengaluru; PGIMER, Chandigarh; Central Institute of Psychiatry, Ranchi; Dr Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital, Delhi; and AIIMS Bhubaneswar.

The training will combine live online sessions, self-paced courses and in-person programmes. Doctors and medical officers will undergo a 12-week online training course featuring lectures and clinical case discussions, while nurses, community health officers, auxiliary nurse midwives, counsellors and psychologists will have access to specialised modules.





The curriculum will cover substances ranging from alcohol and cannabis to opioids, sleeping tablets and inhalants, as well as addiction among vulnerable groups, including women and adolescents.

More than 800 nominations have already been received through the health ministry and the National Health Mission for online and offline training. Around 150 personnel from de-addiction centres supported by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment are also expected to undergo in-person training over the next two months.

Nadda said fragmented efforts among government departments had created gaps in coordination and service delivery. Effective implementation of the narcotic control strategy, he said, would require clearly defined responsibilities, sustained inter-ministerial coordination and collective accountability. He also stressed the need to strengthen de-addiction centres through training, institutional support and adequate resources.
