At the launch, Nadda released the second edition of

Substance Use Disorder: Manual for Physicians (Management of Addictive Disorders)

. First published in 2005, the revised manual incorporates advances in the understanding and treatment of addiction and is intended to help doctors manage substance use disorders in both specialised facilities and general healthcare settings.

The initiative follows the Vision Document on Narcotic Control unveiled by Union home minister Amit Shah in June 2026. Besides enforcement against drug trafficking, the strategy assigns the health ministry the task of expanding access to evidence-based addiction treatment by strengthening the skills of medical and allied healthcare personnel.

Officials said the programme would draw on the clinical expertise and training infrastructure of the six institutions to improve the availability and quality of addiction care across states and Union territories.

World.title: 'Veto should be held by all permanent members': India at UN
World.content:
Parvathaneni Harish called for comprehensive Security Council reforms, arguing that all permanent members of an expanded Council must have equal rights and responsibilities

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India has called for comprehensive reforms of the United Nations Security Council (UNSC), saying all permanent members of a reformed Council must have the same rights and responsibilities, including the power of veto.Delivering India's statement at the United Nations, India's permanent representative Parvathaneni Harish said the veto should be exercised with restraint and must not become a tool for narrow political interests, particularly on matters concerning international peace and security.India also opposed proposals to create a separate category of permanent members without the veto or with fewer powers, arguing that such an arrangement would deepen existing inequalities within the Council."India's position on the veto is principled and well known. It is aligned with the Common African Position. We reiterate that as long as the veto exists, it must be held by all permanent members of a reformed Council. Fairness and justice demand that all permanent members enjoy the same rights and responsibilities," news agency ANI quoted Harish as saying."A new category of permanent members, with or without the veto, would only further complicate a discussion that is already difficult, and would further entrench the very inequity we are seeking to correct.Periodic elections and the concept of permanency are fundamentally contradictory," Harish added.Harish said the veto had been used 331 times on around 200 resolutions during the UN's history. He noted that most vetoes, or threats to use them, had come from three of the five permanent members -- China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States."The record of the Veto is stark. Over the life of this Organisation, the veto has been exercised 331 times on around 200 resolutions. We also note that two out of the five permanent members have not exercised a veto for over three and a half decades, and most of the vetos or threats of vetos have emanated from only three of the P5," he said.He also questioned the effectiveness of accountability measures introduced in 2022, under which the UN General Assembly holds a debate whenever a permanent member exercises its veto. The continued use of the veto since the mechanism was adopted showed that it had not brought the expected change, he said.He also highlighted what he described as an âeffective or de facto vetoâ in the Council's working methods. Under the practice of consensus, a single member can block presidential statements, press statements and decisions of sanctions committees, sometimes without providing an explanation, he said."The veto is not only what is cast in the open. There is also the 'effective or de facto veto' that every Council member, elected and non-elected, holds over presidential statements, press statements and the decisions of sanctions committees, where the unwritten rule of consensus allows a single member to hold or block a proposal, most often without explanation," Harish said.

World.title: Collegium moots Justice Koshy as CJ of Delhi HC
World.content:
File photo: Delhi high court

The Supreme Court Collegium led by CJI Surya Kant on Monday recommended appointment of Justice P Sam Koshy, at present a judge of Telangana HC, as CJ of Delhi HC. It also recommended names of Justices Manash Ranjan Pathak, Tapabrata Chakraborty and Sudhir Singh as chief justices of HCs in Gujarat, Telangana and Uttarakhand, respectively.

World.title: More violence in Arunachal as anti-dam protests spread
World.content:
PASIGHAT/ITANAGAR: A 12-hour bandh against a proposed hydropower project in Arunachal Pradeshâs Upper Subansiri district turned violent Monday, with mobs damaging vehicles and NHPC equipment and wounding two security personnel as anti-dam protests spread from Siang basin to Subansiri valley, report Kangkan Kalita and Joken Ete.

The latest flashpoint was Daporijo town, 220km west of Pasighat by road. NHPC equipment, a company vehicle and two police vehicles were damaged during the bandh called by All Tagin Studentsâ Union and other organisations against Menga dam, part of the proposed 1,605MW Subansiri Upper Hydroelectric Project. Police conducted a flag march in Daporijo and appealed for peace.

Remove central forces, say protesters; depends on restoration of peace: Government

Constable-driver Hibu Lasha and a CRPF man were wounded. Both were shifted to Ziro for treatment,â Upper Subansiri SP Pawan Kumar Yadav said.

The bandh began at 5am over opposition to the proposed Menga dam and an alleged attempt to detain ATSU president Tadak Pakba. Backed by student unions and community groups from the Subansiri basin, the agitation grew out of fears that the project would threaten their land, livelihoods, and future.

Earlier, Pasighat recorded widespread arson, vandalism and clashes with security forces when protesters laid siege to the East Siang district headquarters from Friday night to early Saturday over the proposed 11,200 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP), with its main reservoir planned near Geku village, about 35km downstream from Upper Siang district headquarters Yingkiong.





The Siang flows from Tibet into the ancestral land of the Adi community inhabiting Siang, Upper Siang and East Siang districts, while Upper Subansiri is home to the Tagin community. The Adi and Tagin people are closely related.

Tension continued in Upper Siang, where protesters demanded the release of people arrested for the violence and four activists placed under preventive detention. They also demanded the withdrawal of central security forces and an immediate halt to the pre-feasibility survey for the project.

World.title: On Accession Day, Mehbooba blasts Sheikh Abdullah, says his pro-Pak politics turned Kashmiris suspects
World.content:
SRINAGAR: PDP president

Monday launched a scathing attack on National Conference founder Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah, accusing him of fuelling anti-India sentiment despite having championed Jammu & Kashmirâs accession to India and providing what she called âHindutva forcesâ an opportunity to target the regionâs special status.

Addressing a party convention at the PDP headquarters here on the occasion of Accession Day (Oct 26), Mehbooba said the people of J&K had willingly joined India and that the countryâs initial leadership had maintained good relations with the region and its people.

âThe first prime minister of the country, Jawaharlal Nehru, had said J&K would be a show window for the world. I do not know what happened between Sheikh Abdullah and the central leadership that Sheikh Abdullah, who was flagbearer of accession, turned against it and began saying we now wanted Pakistan, a plebiscite and separatism,â the former CM said.

She said Sheikh Abdullahâs politics strengthened âHindutva forcesâ across the country, giving them an excuse to target J&Kâs special status and intensify their campaign for âone nation, one flag and one Constitution.â

âSheikh Abdullah was the real flag-bearer of bringing Jammu & Kashmir, a Muslim-majority region, into India. But he became unhappy and launched the plebiscite movement. From 1953, he spent 22 years pursuing that politics.





As a result of it, the people of Jammu & Kashmir came to be viewed with suspicion by the country,â she said.

âLook at J&K today. It is one of the most militarised regions in the world. There are seven to eight lakh troops including security personnel, paramilitary forces deployed here,â Mehbooba said.

She said Sheikh Abdullah returned to the political mainstream in 1975 after reaching an accord with the Centre and abandoned the slogans he had raised for 22 years, including those relating to a plebiscite and Pakistan.

However, she said, the people of J&K continued to pay the price for his politics of 22 years.

âEven after 80 years, J&K continues to suffer,â she said.

Mehbooba said recently at the United Nations, the president of Turkey, who has nothing to do with J&K, raised the issue. As usual, Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif also raised it. âIn response, our govt said J&K is an integral part of India,â she said.

Mehbooba said J&K will be discussed in Punjab and Uttar Pradesh elections, but no one talks about the people of J&K.

âInstead, they talk to us through agencies like the NIA and CBI, through the UAPA and the Public Safety Act (PSA),â she said.

âIndia is a great country with a rich culture and heritage, its people are great. But the people of J&K continue to be treated as they were in 1947,â she said. âIn 2019, they pushed Jammu & Kashmir into further decline by taking away our rights and abrogating Article 370,â she said.

The 79th Accession Day is being celebrated across J&K on Monday. On Oct 26, 1947, Maharaja Hari Singh, the then ruler of the princely state, signed the Instrument of Accession, formally agreeing to Jammu & Kashmirâs accession to India, which came into effect on Oct 27, 1947.

World.title: SC to UP police: Educate officers on investigation
World.content:
Supreme Court slams UP police for "slipshod investigation", orders Rs 6 lakh compensation for man held six years without evidence.

Appalled at the way UP cops carried out probe: SC

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a severe indictment of Uttar Pradesh police for carrying out a âslipshod investigationâ that resulted in a man being in custody for six years when there was no evidence against him, Supreme Court Monday said the state cannot shirk its responsibility to protect citizens and directed it to pay a compensation of Rs 6 lakh to him.âThis is a classic case of how an investigation should not be proceeded with, resulting in the prosecution putting into jeopardy a personâs life and liberty,â SC noted at the outset of its verdict.On Sept 30, in a separate matter, the top court had slammed UP police for not naming the accused in a road accident case.It would be better if investigations in all criminal cases were handed over to CBI if the state police works with an agenda and does cover-up jobs, court had said, noting the accused had not been named despite the complainant catching him on the spot and handing him over to police.In the present case, a bench of J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said there was no evidence to implicate the person in a kidnapping and murder case. It noted he was never named in the FIR and police made him an accused on the basis that he was seen in CCTV footage. SC said it was âappalled at the manner in which investigation was carried outâ. âIt is unfortunate that despite no evidence against the petitioner, he was imprisoned for six years as an undertrial.Based on a slipshod investigation, a haphazard prosecution was carried out, which resulted, fortunately, in the acquittal of the accused. We cannot but deprecate the manner in which the probe was carried out and prosecution conducted,â SC said. âState police would do well to educate their officers in the process of investigation.âMaking the state accountable for policeâs misdeed, the court said six years have been erased from the manâs life on the strength of a concocted story built on mere surmises and conjectures, and the state has to pay compensation.âThe state cannot shirk from its responsibility to protect its citizens, especially when a person arraigned in a criminal case is presumed innocent until proven guilty. The investigation and prosecuting agencies exist not merely to, and by whatever means, bring in a conviction. They should recognise themselves to be essential stakeholders in the justice delivery system, ensuring justice, not only to the victim, the de facto complainant and the injured but also to the accused,â the SC bench said.

World.title: 17 remand prisoners escape from sub-jail in Theni district; combing operations lead to arrest of four: IGP
World.content:
In a coordinated escape bid, as many as 17 remand prisoners broke out of the Thekkampatti sub-jail near Andipatti in Theni district at around 11 p.m. after attacking prison warders on Monday (October 26, 2026).

The district police have sounded an alert and deployed a large posse of personnel at check-posts.

Inspector General of Police (South Zone) Vijayendra Bidari rushed to the spot and held an inquiry with Theni Superintendent of Police Praveen Gowtham and others.

Preliminary inquiries revealed that all 17 inmates were locked in a cell. At around 10.30 p.m., a few of them had called the warder on duty, claiming that an inmate had suffered a seizure (epilepsy) and seeking assistance. The staffer opened the cell and went inside, where the other inmates assaulted him and escaped.

As the news spread, the police stepped in and deployed more personnel in and around the sub-jail.

The IGP said, “One of those who escaped, identified as Praveen Kumar, was secured within a few hours; three other persons were also nabbed by the teams, taking the total number of arrests to four.”

“As many as 17 special teams have been formed. Combing operations are under way to secure all the remaining accused,” he added.

Another officer who is part of the special team told The Hindu on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) that the inmates hailed from various districts, including Chengalpattu, Salem, Kanniyakumari, Sivaganga, Madurai, and Theni. They were being held in connection with different criminal cases.

The public can contact 9498101570 or 9176104100 if they have any information about the prisoners who escaped.

Who are the 17 inmates?

The names of the escaped inmates are as follows: Lingam, Raja Sinkandar, Karuppasamy, Silambarasan, Thirupathi, Maenchi Sundram, Sabari, Pon Muthu, Nijanth, Karthik Raja, Mugilan, Selva, Tharun, Rajkumar, Praveen, Muthu Ilango, and Rajuveen.

A police officer monitoring the combing operations in Theni said that one of the accused was apprehended in a forest area within a few hours. Subsequently, three others were also nabbed within the next hour. The names of the four rearrested prisoners were given as Praveen Kumar and Silambarasan of Theni district and Raja Sikandar and Rajkumar of Madurai district.

Keralam police alerted

The Keralam police were alerted, and combing operations were under way in some forest areas, too, said a senior officer.

The special teams formed to nab the prisoners have shared their pictures with officers at different locations across Tamil Nadu and Keralam. Searches were under way in the forest areas along the Western Ghats and in the neighbouring Idukki district in Keralam, too.

The police identified the warden injured in the attack by the inmates as Thangapandi, a Grade II constable. He has been admitted to the Theni Government Medical College and Hospital. Two others were also undergoing treatment, the senior officer said.

Though the exact locations from where the four prisoners were rearrested by the special teams were not disclosed immediately, the senior officer said that, based on the confessions of the accused, the teams were in the process of apprehending the remaining prisoners who had escaped.

“Once the remaining 13 prisoners are also secured, we will conduct a thorough inquiry,” said Director General of Police Mahesh Kumar Aggarwal.

Drones used to nab prisoners

The police are also using high-definition drones to nab the escaped prisoners.

A discreet probe involving the jail staff, who were on guard duty at the four prison blocks, revealed that the 17 accused were detained in the second block. They were all booked for criminal offences, including cases involving ganja, attempted murder, and theft.

The officers said that the CCTV footage showed that the 17 persons had used the pathway meant for prisoners and, after attacking a few other personnel at the main gate, had fled under the cover of darkness.

Checks stepped up

Following the escape incident, the prison authorities have directed all prison staff across the State to remain alert and instructed them to exercise extra vigilance when taking prisoners to court hearings on Tuesday.

World.title: Cyclone Arnab to trigger heavy rains in parts of Jharkhand, government asks districts to remain alert
World.content:
Cyclone Arnab, which is expected to make landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast on Wednesday (October 28, 2026), is set to bring heavy rainfall in parts of Jharkhand for three days, prompting the State government to ask district administrations to maintain vigil, officials said.

Cyclone Arnab live updates

A 'yellow' alert (be updated) of heavy rain has been issued for Ranchi, Khunti, Simdega, Gumla, Lohardaga, Saraikela-Kharsawan, East and West Singhbhum for 24 hours starting from 8.30 a.m. on October 28, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said.

The rain intensity is likely to increase thereafter, with IMD issuing an 'orange' alert (be prepared) for seven Jharkhand districts — Garhwa, Palamu, Latehar, Lohardaga, Gumla, Simdega and West Singhbhum — for 24 hours till 8.30 a.m. on October 30, according to a weather bulletin.

"A heavy rainfall alert has also been issued for Chatra, Koderma, Hazaribag, Ramgarh, Ranchi, Khunti, Saraikela-Kharsawan and East Singhbhum from 8.30 am on October 29 for 24 hours," it said.

The weather department has also issued warnings for thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds for three days beginning Wednesday (October 28, 2026).

"The very severe cyclonic storm Arnab over west-central Bay of Bengal moved nearly westwards and lay centred at 5.30 am on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) over the same region. It is very likely to move west-northwestwards till evening of October 27," Ranchi Meteorological Centre Deputy Director Abhishek Anand said.

"The district administrations have been directed to remain vigilant and prepared to deal with adverse conditions," an official said.

The Ranchi district administration has asked its officials to be vigilant over the situation.

"Waterlogging is likely in low-lying areas and on roads in Ranchi due to heavy rainfall. Kutcha houses, shanties, and structurally weak buildings may sustain damage. Rivers, lakes and large drains could overflow. There is a possibility of flood-like conditions in low-lying areas," the administration said in a statement.

It is also anticipated that standing crops in fields could be damaged due to the accumulation of water, it added.

Keeping the possibilities in mind, Ranchi Deputy Commissioner Manjunath Bhajantri has issued instructions to all officials concerned to keep a constant watch on the situation and ensure necessary preparations.

World.title: Theni jailbreak: Human error led to escape of prisoners, says DGP-Prisons Sandeep Rai Rathore
World.content:
A ‘human error’ led to the escape of 17 inmates from the Theni district jail on Monday (October 26, 2026) night, Director-General of Police, Prisons, Sandeep Rai Rathore, said.

While four of the escaped prisoners were already secured, an intensive combing operation was under way in Theni district and adjoining areas to apprehend the others. The State authorities were in touch with their counterpart in Keralam to mount vigil on all roads leading to the inter-State borders.

The inmates, five of whom were involved in a sensational murder case in Vikramangalam police station limits in Madurai district, overpowered jail warders and escaped through the main entry.

“There was a clear breach of security protocol as the prisoners managed to pass through a three-tier barrier manned by security personnel. Some prison staff were carried away by the claim that an inmate had suffered epilepsy and was battling for life. Their focus was on shifting him to the hospital. The prisoners took advantage of this gap and escaped,” Dr. Rathore told The Hindu on Tuesday (October 27).

Prison guards suspended

Nine prison guards in different ranks were placed under suspension.

The DGP said a detailed inquiry had been ordered into the lapses and circumstances that led to the escape of the prisoners, and firm action would be taken against the staff found guilty of dereliction of duty. Parrying questions on the possibility of some prison officials colluding with the accused prisoners, he said any such nexus would be known only after the inquiry.

Security audit under way

Dr. Rathore said a security audit of all prisons in Tamil Nadu was ordered soon after the escape of a Nepali prisoner in Puzhal central prison recently. It came to light that the electrified fence had been defunct for quite some time.

“A gap analysis is under way in all prison complexes across the State. Prisons are hardened targets where foolproof security arrangements should be in place…there should be no room for any complacency,” he said.

“Soon after the escape of prisoners was reported, we alerted senior officers in South and Central Zone to conduct vehicle checks and enhance surveillance in railway stations, bus stands, etc. We are working in coordination with the DGP of Keralam in the search operations,” Dr. Aggarwal said.

World.title: Four new faces join Omar Abdullah’s Cabinet in J&K
World.content:
Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah-led government, on Tuesday (October 27, 2026), inducted four new faces into the Council of Ministers, including an old hand from Srinagar, Ali Muhammad Sagar, and a female face Shameema Firdous, taking the total strength of Cabinet to nine in the Union Territory.

J&K Lieutenant-Governor Manoj Sinha administered the oath of office and secrecy to Mr. Sagar, Ms. Firdous, Mir Saifullah, and Altaf Kaloo at Lok Bhavan in Srinagar. One Minister, Satish Sharma, an Independent candidate from the Jammu province, was dropped from the present Cabinet. Ruling National Conference (NC) ally Congress has decided to stay away “till Statehood is restored”.

#WATCH | Srinagar | Jammu & Kashmir Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha administers the oath of office to newly inducted ministers as CM Omar Abdullah expands his Cabinet Mir Saifullah, MLA Trehgam Kupwara, Ali Mohammad Sagar ,MLA Khanyar Srinagar, Shameem Firdous, MLA Habba Kadal Srinagar and Altaf Ahmad Wan, MLA Pahalgam inducted as ministers — ANI (@ANI) October 27, 2026

Mr. Sagar (68), who represents the Khanyar constituency, is an old hand in the NC and has served as a Minister in the past too. Mr. Sagar and his son Salman Sagar, managed to win two seats from Srinagar district in the 2024 elections.

Ms. Firdous, who represents Srinagar’s Habba Kadal constituency, is the second female Minister in the Cabinet after Sakina Itoo from south Kashmir’s Kulgam. The NC won seven out of eight seats from Srinagar district in the 2024 Assembly elections.

The induction of Mr. Kaloo gives additional representation to south Kashmir, while Mr. Saifullah adds to the representation of north Kashmir, a stronghold of the party.

Under Section 53 of the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019, the Council of Ministers in the UT cannot exceed 10% of the 90-member Assembly. For the past two years, CM Abdullah had only five Ministers in the Cabinet.

World.title: Tribal, Dalit advocacy groups in Keralam allege policy discrimination against SC, ST students in nursing admissions
World.content:
Tribal and Dalit advocacy groups have approached the Keralam government, flagging alleged systemic irregularities and discriminatory scheduling against Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST) in the centralised allotment process for professional degree nursing and allied health science courses for the 2026-27 academic year.

Adivasi Gothra Mahasabha State coordinator M. Geethanandan and Adishakthi Summer School coordinator Mary Lydia have urged the Health Minister, SC/ST and Backward Classes Welfare Minister and the Director of Medical Education in formal petitions to address the alleged lapses in the ongoing process that have purportedly disenfranchised marginalised aspirants from higher-tier seat upgrades.

The controversy centres on the sequencing of seat allotments undertaken by the LBS Centre for Science and Technology in Thiruvananthapuram. After the conclusion of the ninth allotment round for B.Sc. Nursing and Allied Health courses on October 16, the agency issued an urgent notice directing SC and ST rank holders to report at LBS facilitation centres before 11 a.m. on October 17 for in-person spot allotments. The official notification apparently included a binding condition that stated that any candidate who accepted an allotment in the SC/ST spot round would be barred from participating in any subsequent admission allotments.

The candidates, who had been already admitted elsewhere, were additionally required to furnish a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from their existing colleges on short notice. Under the impression that regular centralised allotments were drawing to a close, multiple eligible candidates opted to secure seats permanently under their reserved quota, the complainants alleged.

However, the agency published a fresh notice on October 23, which announced a tenth round in the form of an online special allotment, providing candidates until 1 p.m. on October 26 to pay fees and finalise admissions.

Notably, the October 23 notice reiterated the exclusionary clause, officially shutting out all students who had taken seats in the October 17 spot round from submitting higher options in the tenth round or in any subsequent eleventh round that may follow. The community leaders lamented that opening higher-preference seats to general pools, while freezing out reserved category students who had been steered into premature spot rounds, would defeat constitutional safeguards and penalise the very candidates the quota is meant to protect.

Administrative apathy alleged

The petition also highlighted the alleged administrative apathy regarding reporting timelines. The complainants pointed out that LBS officials scheduled deadlines across the Puja holiday period without sufficient transit time.

“In one particular incident, an ST candidate from the Kani tribal community in Thiruvananthapuram had to retrieve original certificates from an institution in Kannur on October 22 and travel the entire length of the State to register admission in another district on the exact same day. The student was forced to borrow substantial sums to hire a private taxi across districts simply to avoid forfeiting the seat,” they stated.

The petitioners demanded that the government and the LBS Directorate immediately lift the restriction that bars spot-allotment recipients from participating in subsequent rounds, and ensure that SC and ST aspirants are guaranteed the full measure of seats that are legally reserved for them.

World.title: New privacy law will shut down news rooms, change the concept of news: Digital News Publishers Association
World.content:
The Digital News Publishers Association (DNPA), a group of 21 publishers from across the media spectrum, including ones owned by the Ambani and Adani groups, said the Central government’s new privacy law will “shut down news rooms and usher in an era of censorship”.

DNPA urged a Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant to issue notice to the Union government on their plea for a stay of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025.

The Supreme Court issued notice to the Centre and listed the case for detailed hearing on November 17.

“We cannot pass ex parte orders of stay,” Chief Justice Kant said.

Senior advocate Madhavi Divan and advocate Anuj Tiwari, appearing for DNPA, said the association was not asking for a stay but wanted the Centre to address the court on their plea for an interim stay of the privacy law.

“If I (publishers) are left to the mercy of the data principal, it will close down news rooms… They are changing the very concept of news,” Ms. Divan submitted.

The CJI welcomed suggestions from DNPA on how to balance the rights of innocent citizens against the misuse of Press freedom by the media while protecting the latter’s right to disseminate information to the public.

“You (DNPA) are the best person to tell us… How do we ensure that a balance is struck?” Chief Justice Kant addressed Ms. Divan.

The senior counsel said the privacy law was not meant for journalists at all. The very objectives of the law did not intend to fetter journalistic freedom exercised by traditional and recognised media houses, who were already regulated by bodies like the Press Council of India.

“If we report inaccurately, we will suffer… Now they are saying we have to ask them before publishing?” Ms. Divan challenged.

DNPA has argued that the law was completely in contravention with the law laid down by the Supreme Court in its privacy judgment, which held the right inviolable and fundamental to human dignity and life.

“They impermissibly restrict the fundamental right to information and freedom of speech and expression,” the petition said.

The law “failed to provide any exemption in favour of journalistic activity as a distinct class of processing, entitled to constitutional protection under Article 14 and 19(l)(a) of the Constitution of India and threaten the full spectrum of Journalistic activity carried out by journalists, ground reporters, citizens, whistleblowers, RTI activists, and other stakeholders, and strikes at the core of our democratic framework and runs contrary to the basic tenets of the Constitution of India”.

It said publishers, editors, reporters and correspondents were, as a consequence of the law, brought within a regime of notice and prior consent, compelled erasure, and verifiable consent.

“Such a power is capable of being turned to the identification and targeting of journalistic sources and is thus constitutionally infirm,” the petition said.

World.title: Regional trade deficit widens sharply
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan’s trade deficit with nine neighbouring countries widened by 26.62 per cent to $4.97 billion during the first quarter of 2026-27 compared to $3.93bn in the corresponding period last year.

The widening gap reflects a contraction in Pakistan’s exports to regional markets, largely due to reduced shipments to Afghanistan and Bangladesh.

Trade with Afghanistan, including exports, has remained suspended since Oct 10, 2025, further weighing on overall export performance.

Imports from China rose sharply during the July-September quarter, contributing significantly to the widening imbalance. Consequently, the bilateral deficit with China widened by $858.808 million, accounting for approximately 82.18pc of the increase in the combined deficit with the nine countries.

Gap with nine neighbours rises 26.6pc to $4.97bn in July-September

Exports to China rose marginally, while exports to Nepal also grew in percentage terms, though the increase remained negligible in dollar value.

In contrast, shipments to Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka declined, according to the latest data compiled by the State Bank of Pakistan.

Exports to nine countries—Afghanistan, China, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, India, Iran, Nepal, Bhutan and the Maldives—fell 6.72pc to $944.24mn in July to September of FY27, down from $1.01 billion in the same period last year.

By contrast, imports surged 19.79pc to $5.92bn in 3MFY27 from $4.94bn in the same months of the previous fiscal year.

Further analysis showed that imports from China grew 19.76pc to $5.82bn in 3MFY27, up from $4.85bn over the same period last year. Pakistan’s exports to China grew 17.95pc to $663.57m in 3MFY27 from $562.56m in the same months of the preceding fiscal year.

Imports from India increased by 68.90pc to $61.74m in 3MFY27 from $36.55m over the last year. Meanwhile, no exports to India were recorded in the first quarter of FY27.

Exports to Afghanistan fell 88.34pc to $18.86m in 3MFY27, down from $161.76m last year. Imports stood at $0.25m in 3MFY27, compared with $4.52m in FY26, a decline of 94.40pc.

Pakistan’s exports to Bangladesh declined by 2.96pc to $174.77m in 3MFY27 from $180.12m over the last year. Imports dipped 36.11pc to $13.88m in 3MFY27 from $21.73m over the last year.

Published in Dawn, October 27th, 2026

World.title: Pakistan reaffirms solidarity with Kashmiris on Black Day, calls for end to rights violations
World.content:
The country’s top leadership on Tuesday reaffirmed Pakistan’s support for the people of Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir (IIOJK) as the country observed Kashmir Black Day to mark the anniversary of the arrival of Indian forces in Srinagar on Oct 27, 1947.

In a statement issued on the occasion, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said the arrival of Indian forces in Srinagar 79 years ago marked the beginning of a “tragic chapter” in the history of Jammu and Kashmir, which continued to cast a long shadow over the region.

He expressed deep concern over the prolonged incarceration of Kashmiri political leaders, activists and human rights defenders.

“Pakistan’s position on Jammu and Kashmir remains clear, consistent and principled,” he said, adding that lasting peace and stability in South Asia could not be achieved without a just and peaceful resolution of the dispute in accordance with relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions and the aspirations of the Kashmiri people.

Paying tribute to the sacrifices of the Kashmiri people, PM said countless men, women and children had made immense sacrifices in pursuit of their rights, adding that their memory would always be honoured.

He reaffirmed the government and people of Pakistan’s unwavering solidarity with the people of occupied Kashmir.

According to a statement issued by the Presidency, President Asif Ali Zardari said the people of IIOJK had endured decades of conflict, restrictions and denial of their fundamental rights since Oct 27, 1947.

He said, “continuing restrictions on fundamental freedoms, heightened militarisation, arrests and reports of human rights violations remained a matter of serious concern and underscored the need for sustained international attention”.

Dar calls for resolution in line with UN resolutions

In his message, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said the people of IIOJK continued to be deprived of their fundamental rights under Indian occupation, nearly eight decades after Indian forces entered Srinagar.

He said the Kashmiri people’s struggle for the right to self-determination, recognised by the United Nations, remained unfinished, adding that Pakistan stood firmly with them in their pursuit of freedom, dignity and the right to determine their own future.

Dar added that India’s unilateral measures of Aug 5, 2019, had further aggravated the situation in the disputed territory, intensified the suffering of its people and could not alter the occupied region’s disputed status.

He called on the international community to fulfil its responsibilities towards the Kashmiri people, take sustained notice of the human rights situation in IIOJK and urge India to end rights violations and allow them to exercise their right to self-determination.

He paid tribute to the sacrifices of the Kashmiri people and reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to extending them political, diplomatic and moral support.

Dar said a just, peaceful and lasting resolution of the dispute in accordance with relevant UN Security Council resolutions and the aspirations of the Kashmiri people was essential for peace and stability in South Asia. He added that the dispute could not be resolved through unilateral actions or the use of force.

World.title: Israelis to decide Netanyahu’s fate in pivotal election today
World.content:
A deeply divided Israel will head to the polls on Tuesday for the first time since the October 7, 2023, attack, with voters delivering their verdict on veteran Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the country’s rightward drift.

Israelis will cast their ballots in the shadow of three years of multi-front regional wars triggered by October 7, with questions over accountability and security central to the campaign.

The close-fought vote comes as Israel looks increasingly isolated on the world stage, driven by a devastating military campaign in Gaza, soaring settlement construction and violence in the occupied West Bank, and a move towards hard-right religious nationalism.

The last polls to be published showed Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, running neck and neck with his main centrist rival Gadi Eisenkot, a political novice and former military chief whose mild manner is seen as the antithesis of the incumbent.

Some 7.3 million people are eligible to vote, with more than half a million young people due to cast their ballot for the first time. Surveys show they overwhelmingly identify as centre-right or right-wing.

Tens of thousands of Israelis are estimated to have flown in from abroad to vote in an election seen as crucial to deciding the future character of their country.

“I think this is one of the most important election days in the history of the state of Israel,” Uriel Brandler, a 58-year-old real estate agent, told AFP in Jerusalem the day before the vote.

“The country definitely needs a change for the better in every aspect.” Netanyahu, 77, has served as Israel’s prime minister on and off for more than 19 years.

The wily political operator focused heavily on his security credentials during his campaign, playing on his relationship with US President Donald Trump and insisting he is the only one who can keep Israelis safe.

In the years since October 7, Netanyahu led multiple wars that have seen Israeli forces reduce Gaza to rubble, occupy southern Lebanon and for the first time attack arch-foe Iran with US help.

At home, Israelis have faced bombardment from Iran, Hamas, Lebanese group Hezbollah, and Yemen’s Houthi rebels.

‘Not afraid to take action’

Zipporah Bennett, an 85-year-old retiree, said she was voting for Netanyahu “because he has had the experience of navigating the country through a lot of difficult seasons”.

“He has the full support of the American government,” she said, “and I believe he’s a man who’s not afraid to take action.” Netanyahu returned to power in December 2022, bringing into his coalition far-right ultra-nationalists who have since seen their political clout skyrocket.

The opposition has scorned the premier for his backing of ultra-Orthodox parties fighting to keep exemptions for religious Jewish students from drafting into the military, which faces personnel shortages.

But one of the biggest criticisms levelled at Netanyahu is his failure to take responsibility for the October 7 attack, the deadliest day in the country’s history.

Eisenkot, 66, has pledged to establish an independent state commission of inquiry into the security failures that led to the attack, something Netanyahu’s government has resisted.

Seeking to unseat the premier is an informal bloc of parties led by Eisenkot’s Yashar and spanning from the right to the centre-left.

Eisenkot has vowed to prevent the creation of a Palestinian state and expressed support for Israeli settlements, but has promised to crack down on violent settlers.

Neither Eisenkot nor Netanyahu have publicly said they would partner with the predominantly Arab lists, which represent some 21 percent of Israel’s population and who could become kingmakers if the results are as close as expected.

Final results could take days to trickle in and it is highly unlikely that any single party will come close to the 61 seats needed for a majority in the 120-member parliament.

Cobbling together any coalition could take weeks or months, with possible new elections on the horizon if negotiations fail.

World.title: Jordan strikes militant groups in Syria after church attack
World.content:
The Jordanian military said it had struck “terrorist organisations” in neighbouring Syria on Monday in retaliation for a deadly attack on a church last week, hours after authorities arrested three men they accused of the killings.

It said air force jets had “destroyed several terrorist positions” and killed and wounded “numerous members” of groups linked to the perpetrators of the church attack.

Syrian authorities reported civilian casualties from the raids, with health officials in Daraa province saying six people, including three children and a woman, were killed.

Syria’s civil defence agency reported seven deaths in total, six people in Daraa and one in neighbouring Sweida province.

On Friday, gunmen killed nine people during a funeral service at the Greek Orthodox St George’s Church in the village of Hammoud in Karak governorate, southern Jordan.

Karak is home to a significant Christian community in Muslim-majority Jordan, where Christians make up between two and three per cent of the population.

Major General Abdullah al-Maaytah, Jordan’s director of public security, on Monday named the three detained suspects as Hazza Zaidan Mohammed, Meshal Zaidan Mohammed and Ahmad Sami Hussein.

The trio, two of them brothers and the other related by marriage, were cornered at an abandoned house where they had barricaded themselves inside and opened fire on security forces.

Members of the Syrian civil defence group known as the White Helmets take part in rescue operations in the aftermath of airstrikes, in Daraa Governorate and As-Suwayda Governorate, Syria, in this handout image released October 27, 2026. — AFP

“All three terrorists have been injured. They have been taken to hospital and are still receiving treatment,” Maaytah told a press conference.

‘We will show them’

One of the suspects was in critical condition, Jordan’s state broadcaster Al-Mamlaka reported. There were no casualties among the security forces, it added.

“This country must remain an oasis of security and stability, and we affirm that Jordan will remain impervious to anyone who dares to challenge it,” Maaytah said.

Under Jordanian law, murder is punishable by death by hanging.

A number of weapons and a large quantity of ammunition were seized from the three suspects, the Public Security Directorate said.

Jordan’s King Abdullah II said in a post on X that security forces “chased them to the very end”.

“We vowed the terrorists would not escape punishment, and no proponent of dark ideologies that divide Jordanians will be tolerated,” he wrote.

Earlier, the king visited wounded victims of the church attack in hospital, dressed in military fatigues and carrying a pistol on his hip.

“We will show them,” he vowed.

Interior Minister Mazen al-Faraya told Al-Mamlaka on Monday that the attackers were all Jordanians and “had been holed up in a building in one of the villages near the site of the attack”.

“There is no indication of any external contacts or collaboration with foreign parties,” he said.

Government communications minister Mohammad al-Momani said “we stand ready and will strike with an iron fist, without mercy or leniency, against anyone who attempts to undermine Jordan’s security”.

Attacks on houses of worship in Jordan are rare. In 2016 an attack in Karak targeted a security centre and police patrols, leaving 10 people dead.

On Friday, Prime Minister Jafar Hassan ordered a three-day period of national mourning for the victims of the church attack, with flags to be flown at half-mast over government and public institutions.

Eight of the nine victims were laid to rest on Sunday next to the church in a funeral that drew a huge crowd amid a large security presence, AFP images showed.

The ninth person, Mohammed al-Qasous, was buried in south Amman on Monday.

World.title: Unbeaten Pakistan look to maintain winning run against Sri Lanka
World.content:
LAHORE: Sri Lankan pacer Eshan Malinga bowls during a net practice session at the Gaddafi Stadium on Monday.—Courtesy PCB

LAHORE: Buoyed by Shadab Khan’s extraordinary rescue act against England, unbeaten Pakistan will look to maintain their winning momentum when they face Sri Lanka in the fifth match of the One-day International tri-series at the Gaddafi Stadium on Tuesday.

Pakistan have secured their place in Saturday’s final after winning all three matches, but the fixture offers captain Shaheen Shah Afridi’s side another opportunity to assess combinations and address concerns over the top order before the title decider.

Sri Lanka, meanwhile, will be keen to strengthen their position after beating England by two wickets earlier in the series. A victory on Tuesday would confirm their place in the final alongside Pakistan, while a Pakistan win would keep England’s hopes alive ahead of their last league match against Sri Lanka on Thursday.

The hosts enter the contest after one of the tournament’s most dramatic victories. Chasing England’s 242, Pakistan slumped to 154-9 before Shadab struck an unbeaten 113 off 96 balls, with 13 fours and five sixes, to secure a one-wicket win with 17 balls to spare.

His unbroken 89-run stand with Haris Rauf set a record for the highest 10th-wicket partnership in a successful ODI chase, surpassing the previous mark of 64 set by West Indies’ Deryck Murray and Andy Roberts against Pakistan in the 1975 World Cup.

The innings marked Shadab’s maiden ODI century and came after a difficult period in which his performances had attracted criticism. Speaking after the match, he acknowledged his recent struggles but said he had continued to work on his game.

“Obviously, I didn’t really have good performances in the recent past,” he said, adding that he had kept trying to do his best as a professional.

Shadab also credited Haris for his contribution to the partnership. “I think Haris deserves more credit than me,” he said, explaining that the two batters guided each other through the tense closing stages.

The partnership nearly ended when Shadab was given out lbw on 97. With Pakistan needing 20 runs, Haris urged him to review the decision; UltraEdge revealed an inside edge and the decision was overturned. Shadab later recalled Haris asking him: “Are you going to take the review home with you?”

SAIM RELEASED FROM SQUAD

The dramatic comeback also exposed Pakistan’s top-order frailties. Saim Ayub, who scored six against England, has since been released from the squad at his own request to return to domestic cricket and work on his batting form. Sahibzada Farhan has been named as his replacement.

The move follows another squad change a day earlier, when left-arm wrist spinner Sufiyan Moqim was released, with the Pakistan Cricket Board citing the nature of the Lahore pitches. Left-handed batter Maaz Sadaqat was added as cover for players carrying minor niggles and remains with the squad.

The team management will be looking for greater consistency from the top order, including Babar Azam and Fakhar Zaman. Avoiding another early collapse will be crucial against a Sri Lankan side that has shown it can compete in tight matches.

Pakistan’s previous meeting with Sri Lanka offers encouragement. They won by 37 runs, with Salman Ali Agha scoring 107 off 90 balls, including nine fours and a six, before Shaheen led the bowling effort with three wickets.

Shaheen has taken seven wickets in three matches in the tri-series. Against England on Sunday, he became the fastest Pakistan fast bowler to claim 150 ODI wickets when he dismissed Tom Banton in the opening over.

The left-armer has also taken 20 wickets in seven ODIs at the Gaddafi Stadium. Four more would take him past Wasim Akram’s tally of 23 at the venue and make him its leading ODI wicket-taker.

Pakistan hold the advantage in the overall ODI head-to-head record. Of the 161 previous matches between the sides, Pakistan have won 97 and Sri Lanka 59, while one ended in a tie and four produced no result.

Pakistan rested from training on Monday after Sunday’s exhausting contest, while Sri Lanka practised at the Gaddafi Stadium. The hosts will hope the recovery time helps them regain energy after the emotional demands of their narrow victory.

With Pakistan already through to the final, Tuesday’s match will test whether Shadab’s heroics can inspire a more assured performance from the top order. Sri Lanka, meanwhile, have the chance to secure their place in Saturday’s title clash and leave England’s qualification hopes dependent on the final league fixture.

Published in Dawn, October 27th, 2026

World.title: Rate hike divides business community
World.content:
KARACHI: Foreign investors welcomed the State Bank of Pakistan’s (SBP) 50bps rate hike to 12 per cent on Monday, but the business community called it counterproductive for stabilisation, industrial growth and export competitiveness.

M. Abdul Aleem, Secretary General of the Overseas Investors Chamber of Commerce and Industry, acknowledged the SBP’s move, saying it was needed to contain inflationary pressure and safeguard macroeconomic stability amid global energy price risks.

However, with large-scale manufacturing growth recovering to 1.9pc in July-August FY26 and private-sector credit expanding 14.1pc year-on-year, it is equally important to sustain the emerging momentum in investment and economic activity, he said.

As inflationary pressures are significantly influenced by external energy prices and domestic supply constraints, he emphasised that monetary tightening must be complemented by targeted supply-side reforms, fiscal discipline, competitive energy tariffs, broader tax-base coverage and predictable taxation and regulatory policies.

Foreign investors back SBP’s move to curb inflation, while industry says it will hurt exports and growth

In contrast, FPCCI President Atif Ikram Sheikh said raising the policy rate to an uncompetitive 12pc would further inflate borrowing costs for manufacturers already grappling with unprecedented high overheads, soaring utility tariffs and liquidity constraints.

Instead of curbing inflation — driven largely by supply-side bottlenecks, energy costs and fiscal anomalies rather than excess demand — tight monetary policy has crippled domestic manufacturing, he said, urging the government and the State Bank to recalibrate the framework and bring the policy rate to single digits to make credit affordable for trade, SMEs and large-scale manufacturing.

High interest rates also place an unmanageable debt-servicing burden on the exchequer and private borrowers, creating a cycle of fiscal distress and stagnant output, he said, asking the SBP to align rates with regional benchmarks.

KCCI President Talat Mahmood warned that the hike would further raise the cost of doing business, discourage private-sector investment and undermine growth. He said Pakistan needs to strengthen its productive capacity, attract investment, generate employment and accelerate export-led growth but the policy rate hike will send the wrong signal to businesses planning to invest and expand.

SITE Association of Industry President Abdul Hadi said the move would further aggravate industry problems at a time when factories are operating far below capacity and barely surviving.

The business community has long demanded a single-digit policy rate, but industry’s real problems have again been ignored, he said, adding that high rates will not only make fresh funding harder but also increase the burden on existing loans.

He said the rate hike would burden manufacturers, forcing formal businesses to shut down or scale back, as costlier borrowing would hit new investment, expansion and production.

Korangi Association of Trade & Industry President Sheikh Umer Rehan said the hike could hurt industry, business growth, and recovery, adding that inflation could also be curbed by cutting energy costs, fixing taxation, improving the business climate, and implementing effective industrial policies.

Pakistan Textile Exporters Association Chairman Rehan Naseem Bharara said the rate hike would raise working-capital costs, constrain investment and weaken global competitiveness at a time when industry is already grappling with expensive energy and financing.

World.title: Minister blames closure of border for LPG price hike
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The National Assembly was apprised on Monday that closure of Pakistan-Iran border was one of the main reasons of sky rocketing price of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) in the country.

“Closure of Pak-Iran border is one of the main reasons of high prices of LPG and now we are trying to get the fuel from sea route,” said Federal Minister for Petroleum Ali Pervez Malik while responding to a calling attention notice in the house.

The notice, which was jointly moved by Ms Aliya Kamran, Shahida Begum and Naeema Kishwar Khan, invited the attention of minister to a matter of urgent public importance regarding unprecedented increase in the prices of LPG causing grave concern among the public.

A mover of the bill Aliya Kamran said in remote and northern areas of the country the LPG was selling at Rs 700 to Rs 800 per kg against its official price, set by Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) of Rs 280 per kg.

LPG is largely consumed fuel in remote and far flung areas of the country where pipe gas is not available. The consumption of LPG and its price increase in winter.

Naeema Kishwar questioned that why the government has suspended trade with Iran through border.

On this the minister said 50 to 60pc LPG was imported from Iran and rest of the required fuel we get from Qatar. He said due to United States-Iran war LPG supply from Qatar has been suspended.

He said the government was reviewing the whole system and that it has a policy to acquir the gas from other sources abroad.

The minister also agreed the official price of LPG, prescribed by Ogra was Rs 280 per kg. However, it has been observed that even during surplus supply of LPG, the gas is nowhere sold at the government rate.

World.title: Flu cases double at Karachi hospitals in over a week amid seasonal shift
World.content:
• JPMC, CHK report more cases over past 10 days than first half of month

• Experts advise frequent hand washing, avoiding close contact with sick people and staying hydrated

KARACHI: The city is seeing a spike in the number of flu cases over the past eight to 10 days, senior health experts shared on Monday, urging people to take precautionary measures to cope with changing weather conditions.

“We have been seeing patients with flu-like symptoms for over a month but their numbers have just doubled over the past week, rising from 30 to 40 per day to 70 to 80 now, with the gradual seasonal shift towards winter, especially the drop in night-time temperatures,” said Dr Irfan Siddiqui, heading the emergency department of Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre (JPMC).

He said, “At the initial stages [of illness], people generally turn to clinics in their neighbourhoods, and it’s only when the disease takes a serious turn that they report to a hospital’s emergency department”.

He added that the large number of cases at one of the city’s key tertiary care hospitals indicated that a far greater number of people are being affected in the city and the number of patients visiting the hospital was just the tip of the iceberg.

JPMC, CHK report more cases over past 10 days than first half of month

The spike in flu cases, he said, was seasonal and that people with weak immune systems, the elderly and children, were more vulnerable.

Another factor contributing to the spike, he pointed out, was the general public’s reluctance to adapt their eating habits to changing weather conditions, which could make them more susceptible to illness.

Most flu patients currently reporting to the hospital, he said, were aged between 18 and 32 years and belonged to the labour class. A significant number of them were heavy smokers and drug users. “Patients are generally presenting with severe illness and taking a longer-than-usual time for recovery,” he added.

Dr Siddiqui emphasised the need to practise good hygiene and maintain healthy habits. He advised people to wash their hands frequently, stay at home when ill, avoid close contact with sick people, stay hydrated and get adequate sleep. He also advised against consuming cold drinks and water.

“Getting a flu shot every year [early fall] is the most effective step to reduce the risk of seasonal flu and potential complications. But the vaccine is costly and available only at private healthcare settings.”

As at JPMC, the number of flu patients reporting to Dr Ruth Pfau Civil Hospital Karachi (CHK) has doubled in just over a week.

“The cases have jumped from eight-10 [a day] to 30 to 40. This includes people of all age groups, though younger people aged 20-30 are dominant,” said Dr Imran Sarwar, additional medical superintendent and head of the emergency department at CHK.

“Perhaps it’s more contagious this time as we are getting three to five patients of the same family,” he said, adding that flu treatment was symptomatic, with only a few complicated cases requiring admission.
