The students adopted a new strategy. Rather than limiting their demonstrations to the capital, they began organising marches, cycle rides and meetings with local residents across the country.

This strategy was important for several reasons:

The protests spread beyond the capital. The movement built ties with residents of smaller towns and regional communities;

Students positioned themselves as representatives of society as a whole. They won support from university staff, teachers, ordinary citizens and people from a wide range of professions;

The movement built its own communications network. Citizens critical of the government ensured that the flow of information no longer depended solely on traditional media.

By this stage, the student protests had become one of the largest popular movements in Serbia’s recent history.

Miloš Vučević

15 March 2025: the historic rally in Belgrade

The rally on 15 March 2025 marked a pivotal moment for the movement. Hundreds of thousands of people gathered in Belgrade.

The independent organisation Archive of Public Gatherings estimated that between 275,000 and 325,000 people took part. Serbia’s Interior Ministry gave a significantly lower figure. The discrepancy itself became a subject of debate.

Why was this event important?

First, it showed that the students enjoyed support well beyond university campuses;

Second, the government faced a challenge not only from the traditional opposition, but also from a broad coalition of citizens united by a common demand for justice and state accountability;

Third, the movement had grown so powerful that the question of Serbia’s political future could no longer be ignored.

Once again, the protest showed that calls for a change of government were coming from beyond political parties. A sense emerged across society that the existing system could be changed.

Spring and summer 2025: when the demands turned into a political struggle

On 5 May 2025, the student movement called for snap parliamentary elections. This broadened the scope of the protests. Vučić’s government, meanwhile, said the demonstrations aimed to destabilise the state and alleged that foreign powers were involved. The student movement rejected these accusations, identifying its main goals as fighting corruption, establishing independent institutions and holding fair elections.

Tensions continued to rise throughout this period. Reports emerged of arrests, clashes and acts of violence against protesters. Government opponents accused the authorities of controlling the media and weakening democratic institutions — allegations the government denied.

One of the movement’s most significant decisions was to create a political alternative from within the protest movement.

Students began selecting candidates to represent them in the parliamentary election. They formed an electoral list called “Student List — Students Win”. The aim was to broaden the movement’s representation by including people from different professions and social groups.

On 9 September 2026, Vučić called a snap parliamentary election for 25 October. He made the announcement amid a prolonged political standoff, as the student movement was already preparing to contest the election.

22 октября 2026 года: сотни тысяч сторонников движутся к предвыборной финишной прямой

За несколько дней до выборов, назначенных на 25 октября, студенческое движение провело в Белграде масштабный заключительный митинг. Сторонники из разных городов страны направились в столицу.

Согласно данным, опубликованным накануне выборов, между студенческим списком и правящей партией развернулась упорная борьба. Вучич предрекал победу, хотя и признавал, что она достанется нелегко.

Это стало кульминацией движения, которое продолжалось почти два года: протест, начавшийся с требований справедливости после гибели 16 человек, теперь стремился обеспечить себе большинство в парламенте.

25 October 2026: Vučić concedes defeat

On election night, something that many in Serbian political circles had long considered unthinkable happened.

Vučić announced that his political camp had lost the election and that the Student List had won. He estimated that the Student List would secure between 135 and 140 seats in parliament, while his own camp would get around 105.

According to Reuters, preliminary projections gave the Student List 138 seats in the 250-member parliament, compared with 104 for Vučić’s Serbian Progressive Party. The Student List had therefore secured a parliamentary majority. Voter turnout stood at around 70%, one of the highest levels since 1992.

According to Serbian political sociologist Gazela Pudar Draško, writing in The Washington Post, the student movement had taken the protests to a new level: citizens had moved beyond simply expressing discontent and begun taking direct part in political change. Students across the country had created an alternative model of political mobilisation by building relationships with local communities and making decisions collectively.

Radomir Šajčić, a professor at the University of Belgrade, commented on the victory at the students’ campaign headquarters. “Tonight we celebrate our victory, and tomorrow we will start building the future!” he said, Reuters reported.

The end of Vučić’s rule

World.title: Two teenagers arrested in Tbilisi over alleged plot to attack school: what we know
World.content:
School attack plot in Georgia

Two 14-year-olds have been arrested in Tbilisi on suspicion of planning an attack on a school and acts of violence against pupils. They attend different schools and communicated with each other through social media.

According to the prosecutor’s office, the teenagers had already chosen a specific school and planned their actions.

One of the teenagers has already been remanded in custody. The court is due to hold a hearing on the second suspect today.

What we know about the case

The Georgian outlet Sando Tskaro was the first to report the teenagers’ arrests. According to its report, police detained 14-year-old S.T. on the afternoon of Thursday, 22 October.

The following day, 23 October, police arrested the second teenager at his home. The first suspect exercised his right to remain silent, while the second denies the charges against him.

Police searched both teenagers’ homes. They seized a number of items, including a starter pistol, ammunition, pepper spray, gloves, a helmet and a knife.

The father of the first suspect, S.T., told Sando Tskaro that he did not know who the teenager was with whom his son had allegedly planned to commit the crime.

According to the father, the teenagers communicated through video calls on Telegram and TikTok.

He said they had discussed the 2011 terrorist attacks in Oslo. They had also talked about films based on real events that depicted acts of violence.

The prosecutor’s office has largely confirmed this account. It issued an official statement only after the information had already appeared in the media.

According to the statement, the teenagers met in April and May 2026. They chose a specific school in Tbilisi, studied its layout and began preparing an attack.

The prosecutor’s office says the teenagers planned to place a dummy explosive device outside the school. This would have allowed them to enter the building undetected, cause a disturbance and use weapons to injure people inside.

“They acquired various items and created all the necessary conditions to commit the crime. However, they failed to carry out their plan because law enforcement officers uncovered their activities,” the prosecutor’s office said.

Defence lawyer’s position

Gia Darchia, the lawyer representing one of the teenagers, told Radio Liberty that the prosecution had no evidence in the case.

According to Darchia, the case file contains only two days’ worth of messages from October, none of which mentions organising anything.

According to the defence, the items seized from the suspects’ homes as evidence were intended for personal use. They included souvenirs given to them by their parents and ordinary household objects. The lawyers argue that any claims that the teenagers were “preparing to commit a crime” are therefore entirely “unserious”.

“These people did not know each other. They had never even seen each other and had made no attempt to meet. What is more, they had never been to the school they allegedly planned to attack.”

The lawyer says his client would not even recognise the second suspect if someone showed him to him. He notes that his client had never seen a photograph of the other teenager, who used an avatar on social media. He also stresses that the teenagers never communicated via video calls.

The defence lawyer says the investigation began after the second suspect published a social media post calling for violence. However, the case file contains neither a screenshot nor any other visual evidence that the post existed. The lawyer argues that neither the investigative materials nor interviews with the suspects indicate any links between the teenagers and radical groups. Nor had anyone observed any suspicious behaviour on their part.

“They had no intention of blowing anything up or harming anyone. There is no basis for talking about any kind of organised activity,” he says.

The lawyer representing the second suspect has declined to comment to the media at this stage.

Authorities have opened a criminal case under Article 225, parts 1 and 2, of the Criminal Code. The article covers organising group actions involving violence, looting, damage to or destruction of other people’s property, and the use of weapons. It also covers preparing to take part in such actions.

The article provides for a prison sentence of six to nine years.

School attack plot in Georgia

World.title: ‘Georgia without Ivanishvili’: Opposition launches new wave of protests – photos and video
World.content:
New wave of protests in Georgia

On 25 October, thousands of people gathered in Tbilisi for a major opposition-organised protest under the slogan ‘Georgia without Ivanishvili’.

Waving flags and blowing horns, protesters gathered outside Tbilisi State University before setting off on a mass march towards Rustaveli metro station.

With this rally, the opposition announced the start of a new wave of protests in Georgia. The next rally is scheduled for 28 November.

The date is symbolic: exactly two years earlier, the ruling Georgian Dream party publicly announced that it was suspending EU accession talks.

The announcement sparked ongoing pro-European protests, with demonstrators demanding fresh, free and fair parliamentary elections.

Key messages from opposition leaders

The rally’s organisers, leaders of the pro-Western opposition, addressed the demonstrators.

“This day, 28 November, represents a defeat for all of us as long as Bidzina Ivanishvili remains in power. The postponement of our integration into the European Union is a defeat for all of us. The indefinite delay of a brighter future for our children is a defeat for all of us,” said Nika Gvaramia, one of the leaders of the Coalition for Change.

“Ivanishvili’s group is trying to formally strip us of one of the most important achievements secured by the United National Movement – multiparty elections in Georgia. They now seek to legally establish a one-party dictatorship,” said Levan Tsutskiridze, leader of the Freedom Square party.

“It may seem that Bidzina Ivanishvili is making such a brazen decision that we should all despair. In fact, the opposite is true. By banning any alternative, Ivanishvili is acknowledging a crisis of his own legitimacy. He is admitting that he no longer trusts the Georgian people – that he fears the free choice of Georgian citizens, and quite rightly so,” said Tamar Chergoleishvili, leader of the Federalists movement.

Young people and other protesters were also among the speakers.

“Look at one another – you are surrounded by people who refuse to give up, who continue to fight for a better future for our country,” student Luka Mishveladze told the crowd.

Background

The 25 October rally was part of Georgia’s pro-European protest movement, which has been ongoing for nearly two years. The demonstration was announced and organised by the opposition.

The date was no coincidence: on 24 October 2024, Georgia held crucial parliamentary elections, with the country’s European future at stake.

The election results remain disputed both domestically and internationally. The vote marked the beginning of a major political crisis in Georgia, leading to strained relations with Western partners, sanctions and the suspension of multimillion-dollar aid packages.

The protests were met with violent police crackdowns, including beatings, torture and arrests of activists. Several packages of repressive laws were adopted, while pressure on the media and civil society intensified, including measures that effectively blocked access to funding.

Western institutions adopted numerous resolutions criticising these developments.

The political crisis entered a new phase when the ruling Georgian Dream party moved to ban pro-Western opposition groups it deemed unacceptable.

Almost all the parties that organised the 25 October rally and announced a new wave of protests were among those facing a proposed ban.

World.title: German Kronen eyes Azerbaijan as market for food processing equipment
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 27. The German company Kronen views Azerbaijan as a potential market for the supply of equipment for processing vegetables, fruits, and salad products, Stephan Zillgith, the Managing Director of the company, said at the German-Azerbaijani Business Forum in Baku on Tuesday, Trend's correspondent reports from the event.

According to him, the company specializes in manufacturing equipment for washing, cutting, and drying vegetables, fruits, and salad products. Its machines are used in the food industry, the foodservice sector, and on cruise ships.

Zillgith noted that Kronen’s equipment is also used in the production of plant-based alternatives to meat products. He said this sector represents a new and promising market for the company.

He added that the company’s equipment can also be used in the baking industry, specifically for cleaning and slicing apples.

According to Stephan Zillgith, the equipment’s capacity ranges from 100 kilograms to 5 metric tons of product per hour, which allows the company to offer solutions to both small businesses and large manufacturers.

He also noted that the company supplies equipment to more than 120 countries around the world.

“We hope that Azerbaijan will become the 121st country where our equipment will be available,” Zillgith noted.

World.title: Azerbaijani society is demonstrating unity on all issues - President Ilham Aliyev
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 27. Today, Azerbaijani society is demonstrating unity on all issues, President Ilham Aliyev said in his speech at the 7th World Forum on Intercultural Dialogue.

Reaffirming that there are no internal risks in Azerbaijan, the head of state noted: “All the potential risks are coming from beyond our boundaries, and ideological risks are as dangerous as physical risks. Therefore, we must always be alert. We must be fully committed to protecting our identity, statehood, independence, and way of life.”

World.title: Azerbaijan aims to raise digital literacy to 70% by 2030 - agency
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 27. The goal is to raise the digital literacy of the population in Azerbaijan to 70% by 2030, the Head of the Digital Competencies Development Department at the Innovation and Digital Development Agency (IDDA), Vusala Gurbanova, said at the event on "Digital skills: today's results, tomorrow's opportunities" held in Baku on Tuesday, Trend’s correspondent reports from the event.

According to her, improving the country's digital development indicators in international rankings is one of the key priorities. The formation of a digital society and the development of a digital economy help strengthen Azerbaijan's position in international rankings.

Gurbanova remarked that this year, Azerbaijan improved its standing in the Global Innovation Index, rising from 94th to 85th place, an advancement of 9 positions among 139 countries.

"Our main goal is to strengthen our position in international rankings by creating a digital society and developing our digital economy," she emphasized.

The department head noted that the intensification of efforts in this area in recent years has contributed to Azerbaijan's progress in international rankings. She expressed hope that the country's position in the Global Innovation Index would continue to improve next year.

According to Gurbanova, Azerbaijan ranks 74th out of 193 countries in the E-Government Development Index. Expanding digital services and enhancing the digital skills of the population are of great importance for improving these indicators.

Touching upon the current level of digital literacy in the country, he also noted that, according to an assessment conducted by IDDA from 2023 through 2024, the digital literacy level of the population stood at 25%. The assessment covered various groups, ranging from households to schoolchildren, university students, teachers, and other segments of the population. The analysis was conducted with the participation of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU).

"We aim to increase the digital literacy of the population to 70% by 2030," Gurbanova explained.

She emphasized that achieving this goal requires expanding initiatives for the development of digital skills, increasing access to modern technologies for various population groups, and integrating digital knowledge into daily life.

According to the department head, enhancing digital literacy is significant not only for developing the ability to use technology but also for expanding the digital economy and strengthening the country's international competitiveness.

World.title: Swiss Bühler aims to strengthen its position in Azerbaijan's food industry
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 27. The Swiss company Bühler intends to strengthen its position in the Azerbaijani market, with a particular focus on food security, the development of local production, and reducing dependence on imports, Tolga Çeltekligil, Head of Sub-region South West Asia and East Africa at Bühler Group, said during the German-Azerbaijani Business Forum in Baku on Tuesday, Trend's correspondent reports from the event.

According to him, the company is interested in participating in the implementation of Azerbaijan’s national strategies, particularly in the areas of food security and the development of the processing industry.

Çeltekligil noted that one area of cooperation is the development of grain storage facilities and infrastructure serving the Middle Corridor, including the ports of Alat and Baku, as well as the Baku Grain Terminal.

He also emphasized the importance of reducing food imports and increasing local production. According to the company representative, developing local production will expand opportunities for Azerbaijani producers and diversify the country’s industry.

Furthermore, Çeltekligil noted that Bühler supplies equipment to various sectors of the food industry, including grain processing, pasta production, breakfast cereals, plant-based products, and pet food.

World.title: Kraken secures initial approval to enter Kazakhstan's crypto market
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 27. International cryptocurrency platform Kraken has received in-principle approval from the Astana Financial Services Authority (AFSA), marking a step toward entering Kazakhstan's digital assets market, according to Kazakhstan's Ministry of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Development.

The approval was announced following a meeting between Kazakh Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov and Kraken Co-CEO David Ripley on the sidelines of the AI & Digital Bridge 2026 international forum in Astana.

During the meeting, the sides discussed prospects for developing the digital assets market, introducing modern financial technologies, improving regulatory approaches, and applying international experience in Kazakhstan's digital economy.

Following the meeting, Kazakhstan's Ministry of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Development and Kraken signed a memorandum of cooperation aimed at developing the digital assets market and introducing blockchain technologies in the country.

The in-principle approval is one of the key stages in the licensing process and creates the conditions for the company to begin operating within the regulated jurisdiction of the Astana International Financial Centre (AIFC) once it meets the established requirements.

The approval confirms the interest of one of the world's major international cryptocurrency platforms in entering the Kazakh market and creates new opportunities for further development of the country's digital assets industry.

The memorandum provides for cooperation on improving digital asset regulation, developing digital financial markets, integrating traditional banking infrastructure with the digital assets market, introducing blockchain technologies, and implementing educational initiatives to improve public financial literacy.

Particular attention is being paid to cooperation with the AIFC to strengthen Kazakhstan's position as a regional crypto hub and create favorable conditions for attracting leading international participants in the digital assets industry.

“The entry of major international players such as Kraken into the Kazakh market is an important step in developing the domestic digital assets industry. Our task is to create a transparent, competitive and secure environment in which international companies can introduce advanced technological solutions, while citizens and businesses gain access to modern financial services. The signing of the memorandum with Kraken creates additional opportunities to exchange international experience, develop blockchain technologies and strengthen Kazakhstan's position as a regional crypto hub,” Deputy Minister of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Development Gizzat Baitursynov said.

In turn, Ripley noted that Kazakhstan demonstrates significant potential for developing the digital assets industry and is creating favorable conditions for international market participants.

"Receiving AFSA's in-principle approval is an important step toward Payward, the parent company of Kraken, entering the Kazakh market. We highly value the constructive dialogue with government authorities and look forward to further cooperation in developing a secure, transparent and innovative digital assets ecosystem,” Ripley said.

The Ministry of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Development said it would continue working to establish a favorable regulatory and technological environment for the digital assets industry, attract international market participants and expand the practical application of blockchain technologies in the country's economy.

For reference, Kraken is one of the largest international cryptocurrency platforms. Founded in the United States in 2011, it provides retail and institutional clients with services for buying, selling, holding, and trading digital assets.

Kraken is operated by the Payward group of companies and serves markets in North America, Europe, and other regions. The platform supports a wide range of digital assets and fiat currencies and offers professional trading and institutional services.

World.title: Representatives of all ethnic groups and religions fought as one iron fist during Second Garabagh War - President Ilham Aliyev
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 27. We enjoy a very high level of solidarity, mutual respect, and mutual understanding, and we are all united around our national ideas. One of them is Azerbaijanism, which embraces all the peoples of Azerbaijan, President Ilham Aliyev said in his speech at the 7th World Forum on Intercultural Dialogue.

Emphasizing that this unity manifested itself during the most challenging periods in Azerbaijan’s independent history, the head of state noted that during Armenia’s military aggression and occupation, as well as the Second Garabagh War, representatives of all ethnic groups and religions fought as one iron fist, which became a symbol of Azerbaijan’s victory.

World.title: Azerbaijan's digital skills programs graduate over 11,000 people - ministry
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 27. More than 11,000 people have graduated from the digital skills development programs in Azerbaijan so far, Rashad Bayramov, advisor to the Minister of Digital Development and Transport, said at the event on "Digital skills: today's results, tomorrow's opportunities" held in Baku on Tuesday, Trend’s correspondent reports from the event.

According to Bayramov, the rapid development of technologies is not limited to the creation of new technological opportunities, but also has a serious impact on the labor market, accelerates various processes in society, and changes the requirements for the workforce. Therefore, for the successful implementation of digital transformation, along with the development of technological infrastructure, it's also important to increase investments in human capital.

He noted that evaluating digital development only as an investment in infrastructure means a one-sided approach to the issue. In addition to the creation of new technologies, it is necessary to train specialists with appropriate knowledge and skills for their adoption, proper application, and contribution to the welfare of society.

"Here we are talking not only about the training of IT specialists. Increasing the digital literacy and skills of people working in various fields, and ensuring their effective use of new technologies, are also among the main goals," he remarked.

The ministerial advisor emphasized that the development of human capital constitutes one of the key priorities within the concept of digital development and the relevant action plans signed by the President of Azerbaijan.

He added that extending digital skills development programs to the country's various regions is crucial for broadening access to knowledge and opportunities in this field.

"The agency hosting today's event has implemented over 20 programs, not only in Baku but across nearly 40 regions of the country, with more than 11,000 individuals completing these programs," Bayramov pointed out.

According to him, the presence of international technology companies in Azerbaijan and the establishment of training centers create additional opportunities for the development of local talent, enabling them to acquire practical knowledge and experience. In this regard, the operations of companies such as Andersen, EPAM, and Starship are particularly significant.

Bayramov mentioned that one of the primary objectives is to create conditions for young people and professionals to apply the knowledge they have gained within a real-world work environment and to participate in product development through their work at various companies. This helps in the development of their professional skills and their adaptation to the requirements of the labor market.

The advisor also pointed out that the development of human capital is a long-term process. According to him, it is not possible to fully meet existing needs in this area within a short timeframe, and investments made today will yield results in the future.

He emphasized that expanding digital transformation and enhancing the digital literacy of the population cannot be achieved solely through the efforts of government institutions.

"The role of government institutions alone is not sufficient for the digital transformation of society and the enhancement of digital literacy. In this regard, the collaborative efforts of government bodies, the private sector, and media organizations are of great importance," Bayramov concluded.

World.title: Azerbaijan Business Development Fund assets stand at about $558.8M
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 27. The assets of the Azerbaijan Business Development Fund total approximately 950 million manat ($558.82 million), the head of the investment department at the Azerbaijan Business Development Fund, Mikayil Aliyev, said during the German-Azerbaijani Business Forum in Baku on Tuesday, Trend's correspondent reports from the event.

According to him, the fund supports projects in various sectors of the economy, including the food industry, pharmaceuticals, the production of construction materials, and green energy.

He noted that cooperation with German companies is already underway within the framework of a number of projects, including in the fields of barley malt processing, soft drink production, and the manufacture of biaxially oriented polypropylene (BOPP) film. German companies are supplying equipment for these projects.

“The fund pursues three main objectives: supporting economic growth and diversification, attracting foreign direct investment to Azerbaijan, and investing in competitive projects aimed at reducing dependence on imports.

The fund's maximum investment in a single project is $20 million. Typically, the fund acts as a minority shareholder with a stake of up to 30%, and its participation in projects usually lasts from five to seven years," Aliyev said.

He also noted that Azerbaijan offers investors various government incentives and special economic zones. In particular, Aliyev highlighted the opportunities available in industrial parks, the Alat Free Economic Zone, and through the investment incentive mechanism.

World.title: Walsh back at fullback in Kangaroos team to face Cook Islands
World.content:
Reece Walsh appears to be the frontrunner to wear the number one jersey for the Rugby League World Cup knockout stages after being named to start against the Cook Islands.

The Brisbane game-breaker opened Australia's campaign against New Zealand before veteran James Tedesco had his turn in their win over Fiji.

Both were among their team's best players, giving Kangaroos coach Kevin Walters a selection headache.

Despite his impressive showing that included three try assists, it appears Sydney Roosters premiership captain Tedesco may have paid the price for the Kangaroos' below-par showing in their 36-22 win over Fiji last Sunday.

He has been named on the bench, with Walters turning back to Walsh for his side's final pool game.

With the unbeaten hosts needing to stiffen their defence across the park, Tom Dearden has won the race to partner Cameron Munster in a third halves pairing, with Sam Walker relegated to the reserves.

Walker has been in the headlines since the Fiji match, with his Roosters outfit withdrawing their contract offer.

Walters has recalled rested forwards including skipper Isaah Yeo and his battle-hardened Penrith teammate Liam Martin, who will line up in the second row alongside Jacob Preston, who came off the bench against Fiji.

After coming off the bench against Fiji, who made easy metres through the middle in a gallant defeat, Pat Carrigan and Tino Fa'asuamaleaui are back in the starting pack.

David Fifita and Keaon Koloamatangi have been demoted for the clash in Townsville.

Centre Bradman Best did enough in his first Kangaroos match to keep his spot ahead of Latrell Mitchell.

Ethan Strange, who replaced the injured Mitchell Moses in the squad, is set to make his Test debut after being named on the six-man bench in the number 14 jumper.

Robinson ruled out of tournament for Jillaroos

Julia Robinson scored one of Australia's 15 tries against England, but the Jillaroo will miss the rest of the tournament with a dislocated wrist. (Getty Images: Janelle St Pierre)

The Jillaroos also named their team for their next game at the Rugby League World Cup, with star centre Julia Robinson ruled out of the tournament.

Robinson dislocated her wrist in Saturday's 78-0 win over England. Scans ruled out a fracture, but confirmed ligament damage.

The Jillaroos will face Wales in Sydney on Sunday. Robinson was replaced in the extended squad by Canberra's Sheridan Gallagher.

Jess Sergis comes into the centres, while Jesse Southwell was named at five-eighth alongside Tarryn Aiken. Makenzie Weale and Sariah Paki move from the bench into the starting forward pack.

World.title: Four charged over suspected arson attack on home with family inside
World.content:
Two men and two women have been charged in connection with a house fire in Cobden in February.

Earlier this month, police released CCTV footage showing the moments before flames engulfed the south-west Victorian home in a suspected arson.

The householder was still at home at the time of the blaze along with his two children, aged five and 16.

All three escaped without injury.

This morning, detectives executed search warrants in Camperdown and Cobden.

A 34-year-old Cobden woman was charged with 15 offences including criminal damage by fire, possessing a drug of dependence, possessing ammunition, and possessing a prohibited weapon.

A 44-year-old Camperdown woman has been charged with attempting to pervert the course of justice, trafficking methamphetamine and conspiracy to commit an offence.

A 34-year-old Camperdown man has been charged with attempting to pervert the course of justice, conspiracy to commit an offence, committing an indictable offence while on bail and trafficking methylamphetamine.

A 50-year-old Camperdown man has been charged with weapon and drug offences.

All four have been remanded to appear at Warrnambool Magistrates’ Court tomorrow.

World.title: Gaza ceasefire hasn't stopped Israel committing genocide, UN inquiry finds
World.content:
Israel has continued to commit genocide in Gaza since last October's ceasefire, a United Nations commission has found.

The UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry also found Israeli forces had committed crimes against humanity and war crimes in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including extermination, persecution, torture, rape and other forms of sexual violence.

The report, released the day before Israel's general election, said the country's forces had targeted Palestinians in Gaza and that the situation in the West Bank had "deteriorated gravely" since the October 7, 2023, Hamas attacks in Israel.

It also comes as Israel presses on with a massive military operation in the West Bank city of Hebron, which has displaced more than 3,000 people, according to municipal authorities.

Israel's military said it had arrested 40 people throughout the West Bank and searched more than 400 sites since the start of the operation in Hebron. (Reuters: Ammar Awad)

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu launched the operation after Palestinian gunmen killed two soldiers on Friday, local time.

The war in Gaza started after Hamas-led attacks on Israel in 2023, when militants killed 1,200 people and took 251 hostages.

Israel responded with a campaign that has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians and displaced nearly all of Gaza's population, according to its health ministry.

Last September the UN commission, chaired at the time by 2026 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Navi Pillay, found Israel was committing genocide in Gaza.

Israel rejected the report, labelling it "distorted and false", and has continuously denied allegations of war crimes and crimes against humanity.

In June the commission released another report accusing Israel of deliberately targeting and killing Palestinian children in Gaza, which Israel condemned as full of "errors and distortions".

In the West Bank

The report released overnight mainly focused on the actions of Israeli forces since October 2023, but also found "sustained settler violence" in the West Bank had formed part of Israel's "widespread and systemic attack" against Palestinian people.

The report said 254 Palestinians had been killed by air strikes in the West Bank between October 7, 2023 and the end of September this year. That compares to six deaths by air strikes from 2008 until the October 7 attacks, the commission found.

The report also accused Israeli prison guards of crimes in the West Bank. It found a pregnant detainee in Damon prison was subjected to multiple beatings and strip searches, including an instance involving a female guard touching her genitals while "humiliating" her. The woman was also unable to produce breastmilk for her baby as a result of malnutrition in detention, the report said. Another case of a female detainee being denied sanitary pads and access to a toilet was also detailed.

It found that sexual violence had been used to displace Palestinian people, while accusing Israeli forces of deliberately killing and injuring children in the West Bank.

Military operations since January last year have led to the largest displacement of Palestinians in the West Bank since 1967, with more than 34,000 Palestinians displaced as of August, the report said.

Commission chair Srinivasan Muralidhar said Israel's actions in the West Bank were part of "a broader strategy to exterminate and displace Palestinians" while imposing "unliveable" conditions in the area.

Israel's foreign ministry said the report was "a propaganda document detached from reality" and accused it of "delegitimising the Jewish state and legitimising jihadist terrorism against its citizens".

The Israeli mission in Geneva said the latest report was part of a "misinformation campaign to demonize the State of Israel".

"The attempt to destroy the Jewish state … continues today through efforts by actors such as the UN Commission of Inquiry to undermine Israel's legitimacy and deny its fundamental right to exist and defend itself," ambassador Daniel Meron said in a statement.

Mr Muralidhar said Israel's "excessive and discriminatory application of lethal force" against Palestinians over generations stemmed from its "colonising policies".

"Attempting to equate Palestinian statehood with a threat to the existence of Israel is blocking any viable attempts to realise Palestinians' right to self-determination," he said.

In Gaza

The report found Israeli authorities had continued to commit "genocidal acts with the genocidal intent to destroy, in whole or in part, the Palestinians in Gaza", since the commission made its first accusation of genocide in September 2025.

It said much of the killing and harm was a direct result of Israel's expansion into Gaza.

Measuring Israel's expansion across the Middle East ABC analysis reveals the extent of Israel's expansion on four fronts: Lebanon, the West Bank, Gaza and Syria.

When the ceasefire was declared in October 2025, the IDF held roughly 51 per cent of the territory — the boundary of that was referred to as the "Yellow Line".

The report said that line had become a "steadily encroaching de facto border", rather than a temporary ceasefire demarcation, and that Israeli-controlled areas had expanded to at least 60 per cent of Gaza.

From the ceasefire signing until early April, at least 196 Palestinians — including 43 children — had been killed near the Yellow Line, the commission said.

It found that Israeli forces continued using heavy munitions, drones, quadcopters, artillery and sniper fire in densely populated areas during the truce.

The commission also made findings against the Palestinian Authority, which oversees parts of the West Bank, saying its targeting of Palestinians with dissenting views including journalists and human rights defenders had resulted in killings.

Mr Muralidhar said despite "an increase in unnecessary and disproportionate" force since the October 7 attacks, the authority had failed to properly investigate the killings.

There was no immediate reaction from the Palestinian Authority.

World.title: Mother grieves for son killed in 'skid car' crash as driver is jailed
World.content:
A court has heard the driver of a dangerously modified "skid car" that was involved in a fatal crash is glad to be in jail.

This story contains photos and the name of an Aboriginal person who has died, used with the permission of his family.

Charlie Ernst Keogh, 27, pleaded guilty to dangerous driving causing death after smashing into a power pole in Tamworth on March 10, 2025.

Logan Power, 18, died after being thrown from the vehicle.

Keogh was yesterday sentenced in Tamworth District Court to three years and two months in jail.

He will be disqualified from driving for three years once released.

Judge Peter McGrath told the court a psychiatrist's report showed Keogh had genuine remorse for his actions.

The report quoted him as saying: "I feel like shit, I feel like crying every day, I can't bring my mate back."

" I don't blame [the Power family] for hating me, I'm glad I'm in jail, it gives them some closure for what I've done. "

Logan Power's friends and family wanted to make sure he was never forgotten. (ABC New England: Peter Sanders)

Modified 'skid car'

The court heard that Keogh was driving at no less than 92 kilometres an hour in a 50km/h zone at the time of the crash.

Judge McGrath told the court that Keogh had modified the vehicle into a "skid car".

That involved clamping the rear brakes and adjusting the differential to make it better at performing burn-outs, but overall more difficult to control.

The court heard forensic examination found the rear brakes were not working during the crash.

"[Keogh] was aware that, in his own words, it took longer for the car to slow down, due to clamping the rear brakes," Judge McGrath said.

"He'd intended to modify the car back, but hadn't got around to it.

"Mr Keogh put not just Logan, but Logan's brother and his own partner [who were also in the car] at risk."

'Nothing will bring him home'

Mr Power's friends and family filled the court, with some having to sit in the jury box.

All wore shirts depicting the young man, with many weeping as Holly Power read about the loss of her son.

"As a family, we've had to watch one another suffer while finding a way to survive our own pain," Ms Power said.

"No matter how much we wish, beg, or pray, nothing will bring him home.

"Logan, my beautiful boy, my Logi Bear, you should be here."

Holly Power spoke emotionally about the loss of her son. (ABC New England: Peter Sanders)

Genuinely sorry

When handing down his sentence, Judge McGrath said the court accepted Keogh pleaded guilty at the earliest possible opportunity and was "deeply and genuinely" sorry for his actions.

"His recognition that he killed his mate and wakes every morning with sorrow for what he's done … that will last longer than any sentence of imprisonment," Judge McGrath said.

"But I won't let it undermine the criminality of taking someone's life driving dangerously like he did.

" Any sentence I impose on Mr Keogh won't bring back Logan. "

Keogh will be eligible for parole on February 29, 2028.

World.title: Chilling final moments of murdered WA woman revealed in court
World.content:
WARNING: The following story contains details that may distress some readers.

A woman has described in chilling detail how she stabbed her ex-girlfriend multiple times in a drug-fuelled attack in her home after the woman allegedly tried to give her toddler illicit drugs.

Hannah Louise Glover was giving evidence in the trial of James Anthony Sorgiovanni, 29, who is accused of murdering Tara Morrison in Busselton in 2024.

Glover, 30, had also been charged with murder but pleaded guilty part-way through the trial, following the evidence of a woman who said Glover had confessed to the killing while the pair were in prison.

On Tuesday, Glover detailed the final moments of Tara Morrison's life in chilling detail to a packed WA Supreme Court room.

According to Glover, Tara Morrison (pictured) was restrained by Mr Sorgiovanni while she stabbed her. (Supplied: Facebook)

The 30-year-old's testimony was direct and largely emotionless, and she only shed tears when she spoke about her daughter.

Drug-fuelled murder

She told the court she had been using drugs on the night of the killing, along with Ms Morrison and Mr Sorgiovanni, including methylamphetamine and GHB, also known as 'fantasy'.

Glover told the court that Ms Morrison came to her home in April 2024 with clothing and groceries, and the plan was for her to stay at the house.

However, Mr Sorgiovanni was unhappy with the idea because he was jealous, she said.

Hannah Louise Glover and James Anthony Sorgiovanni had both been on trial for the murder of Tara Morrison, but Glover pleaded guilty. (ABC News: Anne Barnetson)

Glover said that at the time, they had "run out of money from buying so much drugs".

Infant daughter present

She said she had heard her daughter cry, and claimed she discovered Ms Morrison holding the toddler in her room, trying to give her GHB.

She stopped this from happening and settled her daughter, she said, before Mr Sorgiovanni asked: "What are you going to do about it?"

Police outside home where Tara Morrison was murdered in April 2024. (ABC News: Jacqueline Lynch)

Glover told the court Ms Morrison walked into her bedroom, and Mr Sorgiovanni "grabbed her by the arms". Glover then stabbed her.

The trio then moved to an area near the front door of the house, where she stabbed Ms Morrison a further three times in the neck.

Ms Morrison broke free, the court heard, but Glover attacked her again in various locations in the house as Mr Sorgiovanni restrained her.

"You did all the stabbing," the prosecutor said.

Glover agreed, and said she thought she had stabbed Ms Morrison "10 to 15" times.

'It's done'

She told the court that when she left Ms Morrison, she was slumped and not moving.

"She was trying to breathe," Glover told the court.

Glover said she saw Mr Sorgiovanni subsequently stab Ms Morrison "in the chest area", before telling her "it's done".

She told the court she washed herself in the bathroom before finding her daughter was awake.

Woman admits murder after court told of victim's final moments Hannah Louise Glover pleads guilty to stabbing Tara Morrison to death in Western Australia's South West after a murder trial hears about her prison confessions.

Glover said she then asked Mr Sorgiovanni: "What the f*** did we just do?"

Glover told the court she only used one knife, contrary to what the court had heard previously.

She said she did not know how Ms Morrison's body ended up in her daughter's wardrobe.

Glover testified that, at the time, she weighed 48 kilograms and would not have been able to move the body.

'Frame' claim denied

Under cross-examination from defence lawyer Lisa Boston, Glover denied she was giving evidence in order to get a reduced sentence.

She said it was about "justice being served" and "the whole truth coming out".

Glover denied trying to "frame" Mr Sorgiovanni and that Ms Morrison died as a result of "a frenzied attack" by her alone.

She also refuted Ms Boston's suggestion Mr Sorgiovanni had tried to pull her away and hold her in a "bear hug".

World.title: Tasmania Devils' inaugural VFL captain axed after pub incident
World.content:
The Tasmania Devils have axed VFL captain Robbie Fox, following an incident at a Hobart pub, the ABC understands.

Fox, 33, is understood to have been removed from the Granada Tavern, in Hobart's northern suburbs, after becoming drunk and disorderly at the venue two weeks ago.

It's understood Fox was abusive toward some staff at the venue, and at one point a bottle was thrown.

The Granada Tavern was contacted but declined to comment.

The ABC understands Fox was removed from the Granada Tavern following an incident two weeks ago. (ABC News: Owain Stia-James)

The incident has contributed to the Devils parting ways with their inaugural skipper, opting not to offer him a fresh contract for the 2027 season.

In a statement, Devils VFL boss Aaron Pidgeon said "the club's expectations regarding player behaviour, and adherence to our standards" were part of the decision not to offer him a new deal.

Fox is also employed by the Devils as the club's strategic projects and impact lead, and it's understood he will remain in the role.

Robbie Fox is a former Sydney Swans AFL player. (Supplied: Facebook/Tasmania Football Club)

The veteran defender, who hails from Burnie, was recruited to the Devils after playing 105 games with the Sydney Swans, including the 2022 and 2024 AFL Grand Finals.

In an injury-affected season, he played 13 games this year for Tasmania in the VFL, leading the club to a top four finish and a home semi-final.

World.title: Giant, spiked hail falls as 'very dangerous' storms hit Queensland
World.content:
A series of "very dangerous" storms have brought hail up to seven centimetres in size to parts of south-east Queensland.

The Bureau of Meteorology issued a severe thunderstorm warning for Logan, parts of Ipswich, Gold Coast, Brisbane City and Scenic Rim Council areas.

Storms brought hail to parts of the south east on Tuesday. (Supplied)

The bureau warned the thunderstorm is likely to produce damaging, locally destructive winds and large, possibly giant hailstones, as well as heavy rainfall that may lead to flash flooding.

Hail stones measuring between three and seven centimetres have been recorded at Yamanto, Flinders View, Ripley and Mudgeeraba between 2:30pm and 3:30pm, the bureau confirmed.

Loading...

A severe thunderstorm warning is also in place for parts of the Central Highlands and Coalfields, Wide Bay and Burnett and Southeast Coast forecast districts.

Giant hail is considered anything larger than 5cm in diameter, according to official definitions used by the bureau.

In 2020, 14-centimetre hailstones were recorded around the Brisbane area.

Giant hail can cause significant injuries and damage cars, windows, homes and even crops which end up in its path.

Gold Coast chief lifeguard William Ashley said people should stay out of the water during storms as beaches close.

"Water is a very good conductor of electricity so we don't want to encourage anyone into the water during the storm," he said.

Three rescued from floodwaters

Police have urged motorists to avoid driving through floodwaters after three people became stranded in separate incidents across the Darling Downs over the last 24 hours.

A 60-year-old man became stuck in floodwaters at Talgai, north of Warwick, around 9:15pm on Monday night.

Police said he managed to free himself and was rescued by Queensland Fire and Rescue Swiftwater crews.

Loading...

In a separate incident an 18-year-old woman allegedly drove into floodwaters in Warwick early on Tuesday morning and later returned a roadside breath test reading of 0.179 per cent.

A 57-year-old man who became stuck in floodwaters at around 2:30am at Ellengowan was brought to safety by swift water rescue crews just before 7am.

World.title: Music mogul Jay-Z picks himself to perform at next Super Bowl
World.content:
Jay-Z, the American music mogul behind Empire State of Mind, 99 Problems and entertainment company Roc Nation, that helps produce Super Bowl half-time shows, will himself be next year's featured performer at the NFL showpiece in California.

The NFL, Apple Music and Roc Nation announced Jay-Z will headline the 2027 Super Bowl half-time festivities on February 14 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

Jay-Z attending a NFL game between Washington Commanders and the Dallas Cowboys at Northwest Stadium. (Reuters: Peter Casey-Imagn Images)

NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said he had one request when the league first reached an agreement with Roc Nation: that Jay-Z take the stage himself "whenever the moment felt right to him".

"From Reasonable Doubt to standing on the Super Bowl half-time stage, this has been a journey," Jay-Z said in a statement.

"Thirty years of music, work, and culture on the world's biggest stage.

"This run continues to be a dream come true."

After days of speculation, Jay-Z is set to return to the stadium where he closed his celebration of the 30th anniversary of Reasonable Doubt, the mogul's 1996 debut album.

The concerts included three sold-out shows at Yankee Stadium and sold-out performances in London and Paris ahead of a stop at SoFi Stadium over the weekend.

Jay-Z's Roc Nation has partnered with the NFL since 2019 to advise on and help produce the league's entertainment presentations, including the Super Bowl half-time show.

At the time, Jay-Z said he told Mr Goodell: "If this is about me performing at the Super Bowl, then we can just end this conversation now."

Inside SoFi Stadium at Inglewood, California, ahead of the Super Bowl 2022. (Getty Images: Gregory Shamus)

Seven years later, Jay-Z is ready to perform after all.

Jay-Z, born Shawn Carter, has won 25 Grammy Awards and received 89 nominations, the second-most in history behind his wife, Beyoncé — who has performed at two Super Bowls.

His catalogue also includes the albums The Blueprint and The Black Album, and hit songs such as Hard Knock Life (Ghetto Anthem), 99 Problems and Empire State of Mind, his collaboration with Alicia Keys.

NFL half-time entertainment The NFL announces the Jonas Brothers will be the half-time entertainment when Melbourne hosts the Rams and 49ers to launch the season in September.

Last year, Reasonable Doubt was inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame.

His recent concerts brought out a rotating cast of guests.

At SoFi Stadium, his daughter Blue Ivy played piano on The Story of O.J. and Dead Presidents, while Scarface, John Legend and DJ Khaled joined him on opening night. Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg and Too $hort appeared during Saturday's finale.

Earlier in the run, Beyoncé, Rihanna, Eminem and Nas were among the guests at Yankee Stadium.

Bad Bunny and Lady Gaga perform during this year's Super Bowl half-time show at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images)

Jay-Z has built a career as an executive and entrepreneur. The Brooklyn rapper co-founded Roc-A-Fella Records and founded Roc Nation in 2008, building it into an entertainment company that works with artists and athletes.

He became the first rapper inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame in 2017 and joined the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2021.

He is also a four-time Emmy winner.

Kendrick Lamar performs during the 2025 Super Bowl half-time show at Caesars Superdome in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Getty Images: Patrick Smith)

Roc Nation will executive produce the half-time show, with Hamish Hamilton directing.

The half-time show has collected Emmys in recent years. Bad Bunny's performance in February won a record seven, including best live variety special, while Kendrick Lamar's show last year won for music direction.

AP

World.title: The documentary we didn’t need? The One About Matthew Perry plays it too safe
World.content:
★ ★ CultureTV & radioReview The documentary we didn’t need? The One About Matthew Perry plays it too safe Kylie Northover October 27, 2026 — 6:01pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

The One About Matthew Perry ★★ When an “authorised” celebrity docuseries boasts exclusive access to private archives and immediate family, we can be confident it’s going to lean towards hagiography, and this three-part series about Matthew Perry does just that. It’s less a deep dive and more a surface skim that provides little insight into the Friends star, who died of a drug overdose in 2023, aged 54. Directed by filmmaker Emmy Award-winner Mary Robertson (whose most recent series include Quiet on Set: The Dark Side of Kids TV and The Fall of Diddy), The One About Matthew Perry follows the well-worn path of celebrity documentaries that are afraid to offend. While pitched as a “celebration of Perry’s life”, in reality it’s a fawning, straightforward biography that stretches back to his childhood, mostly told by his half-sister Mia Perry Bowick, and two of his longtime mates, David Pressman and Roger Castillo. Perry as Chandler Bing, with Courtney Cox as Monica Geller in Friends. NBCUniversal via Getty Images We get the requisite childhood photos and footage, memories of Pressman, Castillo and others (among them Hank Azaria), but intriguingly, none of his castmates from Friends – Jennifer Aniston, Courteney Cox, Lisa Kudrow, David Schwimmer and Matt LeBlanc – take part. Perry’s sister puts this down to it being still too painful and raw for them to publicly revisit his death, but we’ll obviously never know.



By the end of the three-episode series though, it’s hard not to wonder if this is because perhaps they didn’t have only glowing things to say about the late actor. It’s not until past the two-hour mark that a negative thing is uttered, when a former girlfriend reveals Perry had been cheating on her for a year. Related Article Review What to stream this week: Connie Britton’s weird comedy-thriller, plus five more picks For fans of Friends, there is very little of the sitcom that made Perry a star. There’s a telling quote from Perry early on (and which he wrote about in his 2022 memoir, Friends, Lovers, and the Big Terrible Thing) in which he declares he asked God to “make me famous. You can do anything you want to me; just make me famous”. This invocation obviously came true with the role of Chandler Bing – and the rest of his life. We’re told Perry was “complex” and flawed” but given nothing below those surface descriptions. Even his addiction, we’re told, is caused by the opiates he was prescribed after a jetski accident; it’s not until the final episode that his struggle with depression is mentioned, his reason for using the Ketamine that would end his life.



There is his opiate-induced colon perforation, which almost killed him, his successful addiction advocacy, and a slew of former girlfriends and other talking heads, most of whom tell us that Perry was the comedic genius of his generation. Perry with Mia Perry Bowick, who presents much of the docuseries. Courtesy of Netflix But for fans who have read Perry’s memoir – by all accounts a much less unctuous account of his life – there are not many revelations. Unless you count the fact that his Friends castmates held hands as they walked to his coffin at his funeral, which sounds straight from the hands of the sitcom’s scriptwriters, frankly. But there are some shocking statistics. Perry reportedly spent more than $7 million on 15 stints in rehab throughout the years, 30 years in therapy, and attended some 6000 AA meetings. This series is one for the hardcore fans, but I venture even they might find the three-hour duration at least an hour too long. The One About Matthew Perry is now streaming on Netflix.

World.title: Sam Walker’s bumper Roosters offer is off the table. Now he’s lost his Kangaroos spot
World.content:
SportNRLNRL 2026 Sam Walker’s bumper Roosters offer is off the table. Now he’s lost his Kangaroos spot Christian Nicolussi October 27, 2026 — 5:47pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

Kevin Walters says his decision to pick Tom Dearden over Sam Walker in the halves for Australia this weekend had nothing to do with the Sydney Roosters messy contract stand-off with their premiership-winning halfback. Less than 24 hours after the Roosters sensationally withdrew their $4.2 million deal extension over three seasons to Walker, Australia’s coach omitted him from his starting team. Dearden and Cameron Munster will be given a shot against the Cook Islands in Townsville on Saturday. Loading “But that [contract situation] had nothing to do with it,” Walters told this masthead about his decision. “Sammy is a man, he can handle that situation – there are a lot of players here who haven’t settled their careers beyond next season, so he’s not the only one.



“Their managers are the ones who are looking into it. The players get updates, so they’re not really talking directly with clubs or coaches, and even if they are, it’s all part and parcel of being a rugby league player. “I don’t see it being difficult or that much of a sideshow. It is their futures, which is an important part of their lives, and it’s unavoidable at this time of year. Sam Walker scores against Fiji. Getty Images “Sam has been great around the camp, he trained well on Tuesday. You wouldn’t know what’s happening on the outside with his contract situation. “[As for Dearden], I saw a bit from Tommy in the first game when he came on as a half to replace Mitchell [Moses] and I liked the way he played.



“He was five-eighth last week, he played well and had some good moments, but this week I feel like it was the right time to give him an opportunity at No. 7.” Walters, meanwhile, confirmed he had flirted with the idea of using James Tedesco on the wing after handing the No.1 jersey back to Reece Walsh for Saturday’s clash. Sam Walker and James Tedesco are out of the Australian starting side to play against the Cook Islands. Getty Images Walsh was a standout at fullback against New Zealand, while Tedesco returned serve on Sunday against Fiji when he set up several tries in the Kangaroos’ victory and kept the players calm when it looked like a boilover might be on the cards early in the second half. “I’ve gone back to Reece, it’s for this week,” Walters said. “I thought about trying to find a slot for ‘Teddy’ maybe on the wing, but that would have been an injustice to him.



“He hasn’t played a lot there, and we’ve already got two good wingers here. I didn’t want to change that. He’ll be in the squad, and if required, he’ll play a role off the bench. Teddy is a pretty good guy to have on the bench; just his energy and the way he plays, there’s nobody more competitive than him in the team.” Ethan Strange will be the only debutant for Australia, with the Canberra playmaker named in the No.14 jersey. Hours after making his debut for Australia on Sunday night, Sam Walker’s talks over re-signing with the Roosters broke down. Getty Images Melbourne hooker Harry Grant, one of 11 Kangaroos set to become free agents on Sunday, said his contract situation would not prove a distraction. Grant said more players than usual were prepared to test their value on the market because of the uncertainty around the size of the salary cap when the new broadcast deal kicks in from 2028, and the addition of two clubs in the shape of the Perth Bears and PNG Chiefs.



Penrith back-rower Liam Martin, another Kangaroo yet to sign an extension with his club, said the players were teasing each other about which areas they were looking at on real estate sites. “It’s good to have that banter,” Martin said. “What the group does well is not let it distract us, once we’re training, we’re on and focused on the job at hand, but during downtime, we can have that laugh.” Martin said his preference was to remain at Penrith. “Fingers crossed I can work out a deal and stay,” he said. “I absolutely love being there – it’s still my No. 1 choice to stay.” Walker’s Roosters teammate Salesi Foketi, meanwhile, said he hopes the Tricolours can find a way to keep the star halfback. Up to seven clubs are said to be circling Walker, with the 24-year-old set to become one of the hottest players on the market from Sunday, while the Roosters may even opt to let him go next season if he can find a deal for 2027.



Related Article Rugby League World Cup ‘There was no refund’: Why Ethan Strange was happy to trade Thai villa for Kangaroos camp Foketi on Tuesday said that would be a sad development. “The club’s very good and Sammy’s very good,” Foketi said after Tonga World Cup training in Sydney. “Sammy goes out and competes and that’s just the kind of person he is on and off the field.” Asked if it would be a disaster for the Roosters to lose their premiership-winning half, Foketi replied: “Disaster? Jeez, that’s a big word. “Yeah, honestly, I’m not too sure. I’m just focused on the World Cup at the moment and taking it day by day, as I do,” he said. ”Everyone’s irreplaceable. Everyone plays the game in their own way, everyone’s unique in that way.”

World.title: V’landys subpoenas former NSW minister in bid to unmask his critics
World.content:
NationalNSWDefamation V’landys subpoenas former NSW minister in bid to unmask his critics Chris Barrett Updated October 27, 2026 — 5:38pm ,first published 4:04pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. NRL boss Peter V’landys has launched an extraordinary bid to uncover what critics of his have said about him privately by having a subpoena served on former NSW government minister Brad Hazzard. The sports administrator is attempting to get his hands on confidential submissions to the so-called Hazzard report into racing as part of his defamation battle against an Australian racing website. Peter V’landys (left) and Brad Hazzard. Jamie Brown A retired former state attorney-general and health minister, Hazzard interviewed dozens of participants in the $3.3 billion racing industry after being commissioned by the Minns government to undertake a review. He has now been brought into V’landys’ bitter legal dispute with racing site The Thoroughbred Report and its owner Vicky Leonard over an article that questioned whether his stewardship of the NRL was distracting him from his long-time job as chief executive of Racing NSW.



The subpoena issued to Hazzard directs him to turn over any communications he had with Leonard and associates of hers about V’landys as well as submissions made to him that mention V’landys. The move could potentially have major ramifications for other government reviews if the names of people who spoke to the former minister are revealed in the court action. Vickey Leonard is defending defamation proceedings brought against her and her website by V’landys. Renee Nowytarger A furious Hazzard is challenging it, as is the state government, who were represented by separate lawyers during a brief appearance in the NSW Supreme Court on Tuesday. Hazzard told this masthead the integrity of his review was based around an expectation that the identities and comments of those who took part would be protected.



“As a former NSW health minister and attorney-general, I agreed to undertake a review of the Thoroughbred Racing Act for the NSW government. At all times, the review process was predicated on those making submissions feeling confident that their submissions would be treated confidentially,” he said. “I expected and believed that the process would be respected by all in the industry and until receipt of the subpoena I believe that is precisely what had happened.” V’landys has transitioned from racing to running the NRL full-time. Oscar Colman V’landys is overseas and declined to comment. V'landys viewed the story in The Thoroughbred Report as a call to arms against him because it included a link at the bottom encouraging readers to have their say on Hazzard’s review.



He claims in the defamation suit that it contained misinformation about the shape of the racing industry under his leadership and wrongly suggested the time he dedicated to running rugby league was taking away from his responsibilities. Leonard herself subpoenaed the Australian Rugby League Commission in pursuit of documents relating to V’landys and also sought access to his medical records, before being forced to abandon those efforts in May. Brad Hazzard was NSW health minister during the COVID-19 pandemic. James Alcock Hazzard was appointed by the government in August last year, three months after the proposed sale of Rosehill Gardens racecourse for housing was voted down, and tendered his report in July. It is yet to be made public.



Hazzard said it was up to the government to decide when to release it but said he was now “concerned that what was a respectful review has been dragged into somebody else’s defamation proceedings”. V’landys’ subpoena to Hazzard does not call for the ex-minister to provide the court with his full report. Jockey Chad Schofield rides Tempted to victory this month in The Everest, the showpiece of Sydney’s spring carnival. Getty Images There has been much speculation within racing about its contents, as well as about who is paying for V’landys’ defamation proceedings, which prominent barrister Sue Chrysanthou SC is fronting for him. Racing Minister David Harris has been asked in parliamentary hearings whether Racing NSW was footing the bill.



“Personally, I don’t know,” Harris said when asked in a hearing in August. Upon further questioning, he added that such issues were matters for the board of Racing NSW, which operates independently of government. Related Article Wests Tigers Court bid launched to blow up Wests Tigers power base The serving of Hazzard with a subpoena comes nearly a year after this masthead revealed that V’landys had become aware of aspects of a confidential meeting between the former minister and members of the NSW Trainers Association. An angry V’landys subsequently turned down an invitation to a barbecue from NSW Trainers Association chairman, businessman and Melbourne Cup-winning owner Richard Pegum, who he put on the board of the NRL-owned PNG Chiefs team. Hazzard said at the time he would never break the trust of those he gathered information from, stressing his independence.



His report could have implications for Racing NSW’s wide-reaching commercial and regulatory powers, which are underpinned by state legislation. V’landys has been on long-service leave from Racing NSW since July, when he stepped in as acting NRL chief executive to replace the departed Andrew Abdo. He will officially leave racing in five weeks after 22 years in charge, having become full-time executive chairman of the Australian Rugby League Commission last month. World.title: Four things to know as Israel’s polls open in defining test for Netanyahu
World.content:
WorldMiddle EastWorld elections Four things to know as Israel’s polls open in defining test for Netanyahu Matthew Knott Updated October 27, 2026 — 5:27pm ,first published 3:30pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month.
